title: fix(vta): provision mediator ACL during DIDComm enable and update
body:
### Summary

- Add `--setup-acl` support to DIDComm enable and update commands.
- Carry `setupAcl` through the Trust Task extension.
- Provision the VTA mediator ACL before the forwarded self trust-ping.
- Reuse the candidate connection during live mediator updates.
- Preserve the previous mediator during its drain period.
- Delay promotion of the new outbound mediator by 5 seconds for DIDComm-carried updates so the response can still leave through the old mediator.
- Add transient and live cross-mediator handshake coverage.
- Update runtime service-management documentation.

The 5-second promotion grace period is a temporary workaround for a messaging SDK limitation: inbound subscribers do not currently receive the source mediator/transport identity, so the response cannot be explicitly routed back through the mediator that delivered the request. Source-aware reply routing should replace this workaround.

## Testing

Validated the existing mediator-backed transport harness with:

```bash
cargo test -p vta-service \
  --features transport-harness \
  transport_harness_tests
```

This CI-filtered suite now includes the live DIDComm mediator ACL regression. The regression is located in `test_support.rs` inside the existing `transport_harness_tests` module, so it is executed by the current CI job rather than requiring a separate integration-test command. 

### Follow-Up

`didcomm enable` currently persists the new DIDComm configuration but does not initiate a service restart. The persistent DIDComm service therefore starts only after a later process restart. Restart and readiness coordination will be handled in a separate follow-up PR.

title: chore(vetting-pcs): depend on published predicate-credential-system
body:
## Summary

`predicate-credential-system` is now published on crates.io (v0.1.0, from [OpenVTC/predicate-credential-system](https://github.com/OpenVTC/predicate-credential-system)). This switches `vti-vetting-pcs` and `vtc-service`'s optional `vetting-pcs` feature from the vendored path dependency to a normal version dependency, and removes:

- `vendor/predicate-credential-system/` (the vendored copy)
- `vendor/0001-pcs-application-contexts.patch`
- `vendor/PROVENANCE.md`

Also drops the now-stale "vendored, temporarily" comments in `Cargo.toml`, `vti-vetting-pcs/Cargo.toml`, `vti-vetting-pcs/src/lib.rs`, `vtc-service/Cargo.toml`, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Synced with `main`

This branch was 137 commits behind `main`, including a large architectural migration (#1834/#1835, "the community's REST-only admin surfaces are signed Trust Tasks") that moved a whole class of admin REST routes — schemas, relationships suspend/restore, rooms, community branding/join-discovery, join-requests query/vetting, and later the policy log and DID log — onto the Trust-Task spine. It's merged in through `863dba15`, in two rounds (`main` kept moving while this was in progress).

Several of the conflicts were **not** real 3-way conflicts — git's auto-merge silently kept this branch's pre-migration content wherever this branch's own commits happened not to touch the exact same lines, with no conflict marker at all. Caught and fixed by diffing every touched file directly against `main` after resolving markers, rather than trusting a clean `git merge` result:

- `vtc-service/src/routes/mod.rs`, `vtc-service/src/routes/schemas.rs` — silently kept retired REST routes; a whole new module (`vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/surface_tasks.rs`) was missing from the tree entirely.
- `vtc-service/src/schemas/accepts.rs` — a visibility widening the new module needs was dropped.
- `vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs`, `trust_tasks/conformance.rs`, `trust_tasks/error_code_census.rs` — census/witness tables silently kept old baseline counts and omitted `main`'s new entries for the migrated verbs (this recurred on the second sync round too — same pattern, smaller scope).
- `vtc-service/tests/openapi_response_census.rs`, `tests/trust_task_manifest.rs` — stale exception-list entries these tests' own guard-rails caught once actually run.
- 24 further files this branch never touched at all were taken wholesale from `main`.
- `vtc-service/admin-ui/openapi.json` / `src/lib/wire.ts` regenerated from source (`UPDATE_OPENAPI=1 cargo test`, `npm run wire:generate`) rather than hand-merged, verified to match exactly what the build serves.

**`main` is moving fast enough that a perfect sync isn't practical** — it gained 3 more commits during the final test run alone (`afcf2470`, `1f5ff9bf`, `05692732`). This branch is current as of `863dba15`; a final short sync immediately before merge is worth doing if `main` has moved further by then, but chasing it commit-by-commit in this PR isn't a good use of anyone's time.

**CI has not run on this PR at all**, on any commit — a `CLOWarden` check suite is stuck `queued` and no GitHub Actions check-suite exists for this branch, unlike every other open PR in this repo. That looks like an org/repo-level permissions gate unrelated to this change; worth a maintainer's attention separately. Verification here is from local testing only (see below).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build -p vti-vetting-pcs --all-features`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs` — full suite, **4 clean runs across both sync rounds** (1617 lib tests + ~85 integration test-result blocks each time, 0 failed; 3 real bugs found and fixed along the way, all from the silent-staleness pattern above)
- [x] `cargo test` (admin-ui, vitest) — 498/498 passing
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --test openapi_snapshot` — checked-in `openapi.json` matches the build exactly

title: fix(vtc-service): a raised document limit only for a known issuer, within a large-document budget
body:
Ports the webvh hardening from affinidi-webvh-service#239 and #244 to vtc-service.

- A type's raised `maxDocumentBytes` is granted only when the document's unverified in-band `issuer` holds a VTC ACL entry. Anyone else gets the default limit.
- Each grant is charged against a per-address budget of 5 per minute. The address is the client IP over HTTPS (the admission limiter's address) or the sender VID on the messaging transports. A service-wide cap of 60 per minute bounds freshly minted VIDs and IP pools.
- After proof verification the charge is settled. A failure, or a verified issuer that differs from the claimed one, doubles that address's next cost. Penalties survive a full budget map: only idle, unpenalised entries are evicted, and a new address is otherwise refused.

Checks: clippy, the `size` unit tests, `openapi_tests`, `conformance` and `trust_task_manifest`.

title: fix(vti-common): step-up gate reads the session's level, not the token's
body:
A step-up (\`auth/passkey/login/finish/0.2\`, \`purpose: stepUp\`) elevates the session row and mints no new token; the spec has the caller's existing tokens pick the elevation up at introspection. \`check_fresh_step_up\` nonetheless required \`claims.acr == "aal2"\` from the JWT, so a session that signed in at aal1 (SIOPv2, DID-signed authenticate) kept an aal1 token for its whole life and could never satisfy any \`StepUpAuth\` / \`elevation::verified\` gate.

In the VTC admin console this showed as "passkey verification did not complete" when enabling console signing, after the passkey ceremony had succeeded. It equally blocked \`acl/grant\` and \`acl/change-role\` for SIOP sessions.

The gate now checks the row's \`acr\` and the live elevation window. The window remains the authority: only a step-up writes it.

Tests: new regression test (aal1 token, elevated row passes); existing \`step_up_refuses_aal1_even_with_a_live_window\` still passes. \`vti-common\` 592 pass; \`vtc-service\`/\`vtc-client\` pass except the 4 known \`admin_ui::tests\` under \`VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1\`. \`vta-service\` tests and clippy not run locally.

title: Which ToIP deliverable type a repo-driven registry is (question for ToIP staff)
body:
## Summary

Carried over from [cred-spec #52](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/issues/52), which flagged it as a question for ToIP staff and never got an answer: which ToIP deliverable type a repo-driven registry is, and whether the CTWG glossary's process and tooling can be borrowed wholesale.

Why it matters: a ToIP specification moves Working Draft → Implementers Draft → Approved Deliverable under the JDF process, and this registry deliberately does not, because a vocabulary has to be able to add an entry the week a community needs it. But the registry's content is licensed under OWFa 1.0 (LICENSE.md) and contributions under the OWF CLA plus DCO (CONTRIBUTING.md), copied from the Trust Tasks registry, and it is published under a ToIP-controlled host. Someone at ToIP should confirm that a continuously published, PR-governed registry fits an existing deliverable category (the glossary is the precedent), or say what it should be called and what process applies.

## Ask

A short answer from ToIP staff, recorded here and then in README.md, on: the deliverable category; whether the IPR mode in LICENSE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md is the right one for that category; and whether anything about the release process (GOVERNANCE §8) needs to change to fit it.

title: Relationship policy discovery: both communities must admit an edge, neither can find out
body:
## Summary

Forming an edge between two communities requires **both** communities' policies
to admit it, and there is no way for either side to learn the other's policy
before trying. The first signal that an edge is inadmissible is a rejection,
after one half has already been published.

Raising this as an interoperability question rather than a purely local one: the
failure is symmetric and neither party can fix it alone, which is the shape of
thing a specification usually settles.

## Detail

A cross-community edge needs two independent permissions:

- The **public** community must accept a half whose subject is an opaque
  pairwise identifier belonging to a non-member.
- The **private** community must permit its member to name an outsider in a
  credential at all.

Each is a reasonable policy position, and either may be "no". Nothing published
by either community says which.

A concrete instance from our implementation. Our default relationship policy has
two branches:

```rego
# Pairwise: membership comes from the session.
allow if {
    input.action == "publish"
    input.authenticated_member.is_current
    input.identifier_form == "pairwise"
}

# Attributed: both named parties are community members.
allow if {
    input.action == "publish"
    input.identifier_form == "attributed"
    input.issuer.is_current
    input.subject.is_current
}
```

The public member's half is *attributed* — that is the whole point of a public
community — and its subject is an outsider, so `input.subject.is_current` is
false and the publish is denied. The pairwise branch would admit an opaque
subject, but only when the publisher's own identifier is pairwise, which is
exactly what the public community has declared it does not use.

So the edge fails, correctly, under a policy that is defensible on its own
terms. What is missing is any way for the other party to have known that before
publishing their half — and by then the private member has already issued a
credential naming someone who cannot reciprocate.

## Why it matters

Both parties behave conformantly and the edge still fails, which makes this an
interoperability property rather than a local configuration choice. It also
fails asymmetrically in time: whichever party publishes first has already
disclosed something.

The information needed is small — whether a community accepts non-member
subjects, and which identifier forms it will publish under. Those are properties
a community can state without revealing anything about its membership, which
matters because the communities most likely to refuse are the private ones.

## Requested clarification

1. Should a community publish enough of its relationship policy for a
   counterparty to determine, before publishing, whether an edge is admissible?
2. If so, is that a discoverable field on the community profile, and is it in
   scope for this specification or for the Trust Task layer?
3. Is there an intended ordering for edge formation that avoids one party
   disclosing before the other's admissibility is known?

**Proposed answer**: publish the relevant predicates — accepted subject forms,
accepted issuer identifier forms — as a discoverable field on the community
profile. It is cheap, it reveals nothing about membership, and it turns a failed
publish into a pre-flight check. We will implement this locally either way; the
question for the group is whether it should be interoperable, since a
locally-invented field helps nobody else.

## Context

Raised while implementing the VRC path in
`OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure`. Set out as item X4 in the
["Across communities" section of the DTG conformance
review](https://docs.fpp.storm.ws/dtg-conformance-infographic.html). Related:
#21, #22, and the two companion cross-community questions filed alongside this
one.

title: feat(social-recovery): add the social-recovery task family (4 specs)
body:
This is the `social-recovery` family, split out per your review of #672 — one PR for the
categories, then one PR per family with its schemas. **CODEOWNERS routes this to the
`social-recovery` reviewers only.**

## What is here

- **4 specs**, each with a `payload.schema.json`.
- Categories used: **`key-management`** — all of them already in your enum. **This family
  does not depend on #672**, so it can be reviewed and merged independently of the
  category discussion.
- Additions only. The assembler stages the diff and **refuses to run if anything
  outside `specs/social-recovery/` changed, or if any path already exists upstream** — the
  clash check is exercised against a planted file each run, so a silent pass cannot
  be mistaken for a clean one.

## Validation

**596 specs validate against your own `spec.meta.schema.json`** — your
existing corpus plus these 4 — using **your unpatched 17-category schema**,
not a version of it we edited. 0 failures. Every spec declares `errorCodes`.

Payload schemas are draft 2020-12, `$id` on `https://trusttasks.org/spec/<slug>/<version>`,
`additionalProperties: false`, and reference `$defs/Ext` from
`_framework/0.2/framework.schema.json` — your convention, not one we invented.

## Why this family first

It is small, and it is one of only three of our families that is already
**lowerCamelCase-clean**, so it does not carry the §4.10 casing work we owe you on
the rest. **Please treat it as a shape template**: if the file layout, the spec
structure, the schema conventions or the commit/PR format are wrong, correcting them
here costs you one review instead of twenty-eight. We will not open the remaining
families until you have had a chance to say.

## Known-open, stated rather than hidden

- 🟡 **Worked examples are not yet round-trip verified against our implementation.**
  We tested this and the honest result is that some examples describe an intended
  API rather than the one our code accepts today. Where that is true of a spec in
  this family we would rather fix the example than quietly ship it — tell us if you
  want those corrected before merge or tracked separately.
- 🟡 **`ext` passthrough is declared but not universally implemented** on our side.
  The schemas model it per your `$defs/Ext`; our runtime honours it for some
  operations and not yet all.
- The `Security & Privacy` sections follow your house structure. Our earlier
  submission cited internal `src/...` paths in some spec bodies; **0 of your 592 do
  that**, so they are removed here.

## Casing

On your `sourceClass` point: **your conclusion was right and we are conforming.**
§4.10 items 3 and 4 govern it (your citation of §8.3 was the error-code table), and
we confirmed you hold your own corpus to it — zero unexplained snake_case enum values
across your 592 payload schemas. This family needed no changes. The rest is measured
and in flight; see the discussion on #672.

## Open questions for maintainer review

The `🟡 NEEDS-REVIEW:` convention this description promised is now actually in the
specs, under an **Open Questions for Registry Review** heading in each. Thank you for
catching that it was missing — it should have been there from the start.

It was missing for a reason on our side, now fixed: our own validator treated any spec
containing the marker as a failure, so the convention could not be used without turning
our own gate red. That encoded the wrong reading of our rule. A `NEEDS-REVIEW` marker
does not mean "we did not finish it" — it means "complete as far as we can take it, and
flagged for the reviewer who has to decide."

- **`social-recovery/buddies/list`** — in our reference implementation this is a
  same-device, owner-local read: a Settings-screen listing of the operator's own recovery
  buddies, not a request one party sends about another party's data. We documented it as
  the code behaves, but whether it belongs in a peer-facing registry at all is a call we'd
  like your judgment on.
- **`social-recovery/status/get`** — declares a `deviceNotFound` error code our
  implementation never emits (`localDeviceDid` is only checked for list membership, never
  looked up against an owner record). Flagged rather than silently resolved either way.
- **`social-recovery/buddies/add`** — same pattern: declares a `selfEnrollment` code our
  implementation never emits; nothing compares the buddy DID to the requester's own.

A fourth candidate was deliberately **not** marked: `buddies/list` publishing each buddy's
`publicKeyHex` is an intentional disclosure whose rationale is already in the spec text.
It is a decision, not an open question, and padding this list would cost you attention
rather than save it.

## Still red, and named rather than left to look handled

`bindings match specs`, both drift checks and `cargo test` are failing because no
generated client binding (Rust/TypeScript/Go/Dart) declares these four operations'
TYPE_URIs — codegen has not been run for this family. That is a generator run, not a
spec change. We are running it; this note is here so the red is not mistaken for a
spec defect.

title: feat(vtc-client)!: every VTC call is a signed Trust Task
body:
Every `vtc-client` and `cnm` call to the VTC is now a signed Trust Task over the resolved transport (TSP > DIDComm > HTTPS `POST /v1/trust-tasks`). The REST routes that were kept only for them are deleted.

## vtc-client

- The fallback from Trust Task to bearer REST is gone. `document()` sends over the session when there is one; otherwise it signs with the operator's key and posts to `/trust-tasks`. With no session and no key the call returns `NotAuthenticated`.
- New `VtcClient::with_key(base, vtc_did, HolderKey)`: an HTTPS client that signs every task and holds no bearer token.
- Removed: `with_token`, the `tt` / `get_json` / `post_json` helpers, and `resend_vetter_grant` (admin resend has no signed form).
- Moved to signed tasks:
  - `list_members`, `list_join_requests` (paginated `members/list`, `join-requests/list`)
  - `approve_join` / `reject_join` (`join-requests/decide`)
  - `remove_member`, `update_member_extensions`, `member_credentials`
  - `list_policies`, `get_policy`, `upload_policy`, `activate_policy`. `activate_policy` reads the revision first to get the `purpose` the task requires.
  - `install_did_log` (`did/register`)
  - `grant_vetter`, `show_vetter`, `revoke_endorsement` (`endorsements/revoke`)
  - `audit_verify`
- Still on bearer REST until #1835 merges: `list_vetter_grants`, `auto_grant`, `configure_auto_grant`, `branding`, `set_branding`, `requested_attributes`, `set_requested_attributes`, `vetting_revocations`.

## cnm

- `connect_for_tasks` now signs its HTTPS client with the profile key (`with_key`).
- These commands now use the resolved transport and honour `--transport`:
  - `cnm audit verify`
  - `cnm did-log install`
  - `cnm vetting vetters grant|revoke`
  - `cnm vetting bootstrap-pgp` (roster read and grants)
- The other vetting commands keep a bearer connection until #1835.
- `cnm vetting vetters resend` is removed. A vetter can still resend their own grant with the signed self-resend.
- Not changed: `cnm consent` (`cnm-cli/src/consent.rs` belongs to the other session). It still sends a signed document, but always over HTTPS.

## VTC routes deleted (their Trust Task is served on main)

- `GET /members`, `PATCH /members/{did}`, `DELETE /members/{did}`, `GET /members/{did}/credentials`
- `GET /join-requests`, `POST /join-requests/{id}/decide`
- `GET /policies`, `POST /policies`, `GET /policies/{id}`, `POST /policies/{id}/activate`
- `POST /admin/did/register`
- `GET /audit/verify`
- `POST /vetting/vetters`, `POST /vetting/vetters/show`

The openapi snapshot and `wire.ts` are regenerated. The response schemas the console types its signed calls with are registered as components.

## Routes kept

- Their Trust Tasks are not on main until #1835: `GET /vetting/vetters`, `GET`/`PUT /vetting/auto-grant`, `GET /vetting/revocations`, `GET`/`PUT /community/branding`, `GET`/`PUT /community/requested-attributes`.
- `POST /vetting/vetters/{did}/resend`: missing spec (below). The console still uses it.
- `POST /credential-exchange/request`: documented exception.

## Missing specs

- Admin resend of another member's vetter grant. `vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.1` only covers the signer's own grant.
- The `vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1` response doesn't say whether the call created a grant or returned an existing one; REST used 201 vs 200 for that. `grant_vetter` now calls `show` first to fill in `created`, which is informational only.

## Tests

- Suites that drove the deleted routes now use signed documents, through the extended `common::legacy` shim or `common::signed`.
- The auth-plumbing suites (cookie session, idle timeout, audience, smoke) now point at `GET /auth/whoami`.
- The census and manifest tests are updated for the removed routes.

Local run:
- clippy with `-D warnings`: clean
- fmt: clean
- `vtc-service --lib openapi_tests conformance`: pass
- `--test trust_task_manifest`: pass
- `vtc-client`: 32 pass
- `cnm-cli`: 90 pass

CI covers the rest.

title: feat(spec-meta): add 10 category values for domains the taxonomy has no home for
body:
## What this changes

Two files, and they have to move together:

1. `specs/spec.meta.schema.json` — ten values added to `#/properties/category/enum` (17 → 27).
2. `website/assets/data.js` — the matching ten `window.TT_CATEGORIES` entries.

Nothing else. No specs, no bindings, no version bumps, no CHANGELOG entry.

This is the first of the split series you asked for. The families and their specs
follow as one PR per family, so `CODEOWNERS` can route each one by slug.

## Why both files

`scripts/build-registry.mjs::checkCategoryTaxonomy()` fails the build on any enum
value with no `TT_CATEGORIES` entry — *"its specs would render without a
name/color and crash the spec page"* — and warns on the reverse. So the enum
patch alone would break `main`, and the `data.js` entries alone would be dead
weight. `CLAUDE.md` in this repo records this shipping for real once, when
`chat/message/1.0` went out broken on the live site.

We reproduced that check locally against a clean clone before opening this, in
four arms: pristine/pristine silent, patched-enum + unpatched-`data.js` failing on
exactly these ten, patched/patched clean, and unpatched-enum + patched-`data.js`
warning rather than failing. The third arm alone would not have told us whether
the check discriminates.

We also assert something the build does not: every `color` we set resolves to a
`--tt-<color>` token `tokens.css` actually defines, because `catColor()` emits
`var(--tt-${cat.color})` and an undefined token renders nothing rather than
failing. All ten use the existing six-token palette.

## The ten values

| Value | Family it serves | Why no existing value fits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `temporal-coordination` | `calendar` | Negotiating *when*, between parties |
| `automation` | `scheduler` | Scheduled or triggered execution with no human in the loop |
| `media` | `media` | Custody and delivery of recorded audio/video/image/book assets |
| `communications` | `call` | Real-time synchronous session setup — offer/answer, participants |
| `collaboration` | `canvas` | Concurrent multi-party editing of shared state |
| `matchmaking` | `matchmaking` | Mutual-interest discovery and introduction |
| `privacy` | `data-subject` | Data-subject rights against a controller |
| `storage` | `files` | Document custody on behalf of another party |
| `task-management` | `todo` | Human work tracking and assignment |
| `prediction` | `forecast` | A claim about the future plus the record that settles it |

**`privacy`** has a regulatory anchor (GDPR data-subject rights) the registry has
no home for today. `consent` covers a subject *granting* permission; it cannot
express a subject compelling a controller who would rather not comply.

**`prediction`** is the only temporally-directional value here. `reputation`
scores the past and `provenance` records it; neither can hold the claim half.

## Where we think you are right

You flagged `communications`, `matchmaking` and `media` as overlapping the
existing `chat`, `messaging` and `data-exchange`. We would rather discuss those
three than defend them, and we are happy to drop or merge any of them. If you
want the smallest possible first step, `privacy` and `prediction` are the two you
said make a good case, and this PR is easy to reduce to just those.

Separately, and this one is ours to fix rather than yours: all 36 `bridge/*`
specs we proposed declare `category: messaging`, and you are right that this
repo's `messaging` means operator-facing control of a mediator or relay, not an
application-level protocol bridge. That is a genuine misclassification on our
side. We will pick a better category for `bridge` in its own PR rather than
smuggle it through this one.

## Provenance

These ten values are not a taxonomy proposal in the abstract. Each one is the
category a family needed while implementing the Trust Task framework against this
registry, and every one of them is declared by specs we are submitting in the
follow-up PRs. If a value ends up with no family behind it, it should not land —
`checkCategoryTaxonomy()` would warn about it as dead weight, correctly.

title: feat(vtc-service)!: git-ns admin reads are signed Trust Tasks
body:
## Summary

The six git-ns admin-console reads that only ever had bearer REST are now signed Trust Tasks, served on the document dispatcher (`vtc-service/src/git_ns/admin_reads.rs`) over every transport, matching the pattern #1835/#1840 set for the rest of the admin surface. Specs merged in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#686, released in trust-tasks-rs 0.24.7 (bumped from 0.24.6).

| Route removed | Trust Task |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/git-ns/rights` | `git-ns/right/list/0.1` |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/rights/issued-by-departed` | `git-ns/right/issued-by-departed/0.1` |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/jobs` | `git-ns/bridge/job/list/0.1` |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/projection` | `git-ns/projection/show/0.1` |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/accounts` | `git-ns/account/list/0.1` |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/activity` | `git-ns/activity/list/0.1` |

Authority: the community-administrator capability alone for `right/list`, `right/issued-by-departed`, `projection/show` and `account/list` (each spans every namespace); the community-administrator capability or a namespace's own `git.ns.admin` for `bridge/job/list` and `activity/list` — the same split `namespace/list`/`repo/list` already use. Each of the six pages: `limit` clamped to 1..=500 (default 100), an opaque `cursor` bound to the request's own filters so a mid-page filter change is refused `malformedRequest`.

`routes/src/routes/git_ns.rs` (the whole REST surface) is deleted; its response types and tests moved into `git_ns::admin_reads` / `git_ns::tasks` and `git_ns/tests.rs`. `admin-ui/src/plugins/repos/api.ts` now signs all six with the console key (`postSignedRead`); `admin-ui/openapi.json` and `wire.ts` regenerated.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

- No `cnm` subcommands for the six new tasks yet (table in `docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md` marks them `—`).
- The admin console still fetches one page (default 100/500) of each listing — no "load more" UI for `nextCursor` yet.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt` — clean
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib -- openapi_tests conformance` — 11 passed
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --test trust_task_manifest` — in progress at push time; CI covers it
- [x] `admin-ui`: `npm run lint` (wire:check + tsc) and `npx vitest run` — 498 passed

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.24.7
body:
### Added

- **git-ns**: Administrator reads as Trust Tasks ([#686](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/686))

* feat(git-ns): administrator reads as Trust Tasks

  Six VTC git-ns console REST reads had no Trust Task equivalent: the admin
  console's Repos plugin (rights, jobs, projection, accounts) and activity
  feed were served only over a bearer admin session, with no signed,
  transport-agnostic path.

  New specs:

  - git-ns/right/list/0.1 — the whole-community rights picture (recorded and
    v0.1 role-derived grants), each row's subjectMember/granterDeparted.
    A new spec rather than a git-ns/view revision: the role-derived rows are
    not RightRecords (no granter, no grant time) and the administrative
    membership facts are not member-facing, so folding them into view/0.5's
    shared RightRecord would widen every other consumer of that component.
  - git-ns/right/issued-by-departed/0.1 — recorded rights grouped by a
    departed granter, alongside the community's cascade_on_departure policy.
  - git-ns/bridge/job/list/0.1 — the bridge job queue, scoped to administered
    namespaces like git-ns/namespace/list and git-ns/repo/list.
  - git-ns/projection/show/0.1 — what is published to the Trust Registry,
    and how many records the next reconciliation pass will change.
  - git-ns/account/list/0.1 — every member's linked forge account,
    community-wide, since git-ns/view only returns the caller's own.
  - git-ns/activity/list/0.1 — rights changes, drift and bridge jobs
    interleaved into one timeline, scoped like the namespace/repo listings.

  All six declare proof REQUIRED, an Authorization section naming either the
  community-administrator capability (rights, issued-by-departed,
  projection, accounts — matching the REST handlers' SuperAdminAuth gate) or
  namespace-administrator standing (jobs, activity — matching the namespace
  and repo listings' pattern), and a cursor/limit paged list shape.
  git-ns/_shared/0.5 adds AdminRightRow and RightOrigin, the row shape right/list
  and right/issued-by-departed share.

  Regenerated all four bindings (Rust, TypeScript, Go, Dart).

- **auth**: Proxied authenticate and session-key refresh ([#687](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/687))

## `vta-sdk`

## [0.56.2](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.56.1...vta-sdk-v0.56.2) — 2026-09-29 ### Added - **vta**: Clear a context's DID with vta/contexts/update-did/1.1 ([#1828](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1828)) * feat(vta): clear a context's DID with vta/contexts/update-did/1.1 Once a context had a DID it could be replaced but never removed: update-did/1.0 requires a non-empty `did`, and contexts/update only sets one. `webvh/dids/delete` refuses a DID a context still acts as and says "reassign it first", so a context's last DID could not be retired short of assigning another the operator did not want. Serve update-did/1.1 (trust-tasks `feat(vta/contexts/update-did): 1.1`) beside 1.0 through one handler. `did: null` clears — the record comes back with `did` absent, and clearing a context with no DID succeeds. Needs a trust-tasks-rs release carrying update_did::v1_1; see the TODO on the floor in Cargo.toml. - **trust-tasks**: Advertise the acceptance window over trust-task-discovery 0.3 (VTI-TRN-047) ([#1817](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1817)) Both VTI node types refuse a document more than ten minutes (plus 60 s of skew) past its issuedAt (VTI-OPS-024). A sender holding a document before delivery has to know that window to decide when to issue a new attempt instead, and until now the only way to know it was to share the constant. trust-task-discovery/0.3 (trust-tasks #677, trust-tasks-rs 0.24.4) lets a responder state it. - Raise the trust-tasks-rs floor to 0.24.4, the first release carrying discovery 0.3, and trust-tasks-capability-client with it. Only those two lockfile entries move. - vti-common: `trust_task::acceptance::AcceptanceWindow` and `VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW` (ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW + DEFAULT_SKEW). This is the one value the consumers apply (`freshness_policy()`), the responders advertise (`advertised()`, rounded down so it is never wider, VTI-TRN-047), and the push engine judges staleness by (`past_max_age`, `refuses`). `trust_task::discovery` has the pattern grammar and the 0.1/0.3 response builders, so both nodes answer the same way. - VTA: serves trust-task-discovery/0.3 next to 0.1, answering each in the version it was asked. The window goes at response level, since the VTA applies one window to everything it dispatches. The 0.1 frameworkVersion was "0.2", a stale copy of the framework crate's default. It answers identified callers only, as the VTA does, and lists the routing table itself (DISPATCHED_URIS plus the rooms and git-ns registrations). - Registrations: TASK_TRUST_TASK_DISCOVERY_0_3 in vta_sdk::trust_tasks and its task list, ReadOnly in retry_safety, the VTA dispatch table and its conformance witness (built from the real builder, not a literal), and the VTC DISPATCHED_URIS and its declared-URI census. - Push engine (VTI-TRN-045): its two staleness predicates now read VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW, the same value the nodes advertise, where before they combined two separate constants. It still reads no advertised window. A lookup would be a request/reply exchange, and every push is one-way. None of the recipients (approvers' devices, wallets, requesters) serves discovery. The window only matters when the recipient cannot answer. The engine never sees an `expired` refusal, so 0.3's "re-ask after an unexpected refusal" would have no trigger. ## [0.45.2](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-service-v0.45.1...vta-service-v0.45.2) — 2026-09-29 ### Added - **vta**: Vta contexts update --clear-did, offline ([#1830](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1830)) The offline binary's `contexts update` could set a DID but not clear one, the one CLI left behind by #1828. `--clear-did` conflicts with `--did` and clears through update_context_did(None), as pnm's does. - **vta**: Clear a context's DID with vta/contexts/update-did/1.1 ([#1828](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1828)) * feat(vta): clear a context's DID with vta/contexts/update-did/1.1 Once a context had a DID it could be replaced but never removed: update-did/1.0 requires a non-empty `did`, and contexts/update only sets one. `webvh/dids/delete` refuses a DID a context still acts as and says "reassign it first", so a context's last DID could not be retired short of assigning another the operator did not want. Serve update-did/1.1 (trust-tasks `feat(vta/contexts/update-did): 1.1`) beside 1.0 through one handler. `did: null` clears — the record comes back with `did` absent, and clearing a context with no DID succeeds. A string `did` must be a DID; 1.1 is parsed into the generated `update_did::v1_1::Payload`, whose `PayloadDid` holds the pattern, and 1.0 keeps its original body. 1.0 is listed as superseded by 1.1, and the legacy `PUT /contexts/{id}/did` now names 1.1 as its successor. - vta-sdk: `TASK_CONTEXTS_UPDATE_DID_1_1` (retry-safe); `update_context_did` sends 1.1; new `clear_context_did`. - pnm / cnm: `contexts update-did --clear`, and `contexts update --clear-did` (conflicts with `--did`), both on update-did so a context admin can do it. - The delete blocker offers both fixes and names update-did rather than contexts/update (super-admin only); its text also carried a run of literal spaces from an unjoined line wrap. Needs a trust-tasks-rs release carrying update_did::v1_1; see the TODO on the floor in Cargo.toml. - **trust-tasks**: Advertise the acceptance window over trust-task-discovery 0.3 (VTI-TRN-047) ([#1817](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1817)) Both VTI node types refuse a document more than ten minutes (plus 60 s of skew) past its issuedAt (VTI-OPS-024). A sender holding a document before delivery has to know that window to decide when to issue a new attempt instead, and until now the only way to know it was to share the constant. trust-task-discovery/0.3 (trust-tasks #677, trust-tasks-rs 0.24.4) lets a responder state it. - Raise the trust-tasks-rs floor to 0.24.4, the first release carrying discovery 0.3, and trust-tasks-capability-client with it. Only those two lockfile entries move. - vti-common: `trust_task::acceptance::AcceptanceWindow` and `VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW` (ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW + DEFAULT_SKEW). This is the one value the consumers apply (`freshness_policy()`), the responders advertise (`advertised()`, rounded down so it is never wider, VTI-TRN-047), and the push engine judges staleness by (`past_max_age`, `refuses`). `trust_task::discovery` has the pattern grammar and the 0.1/0.3 response builders, so both nodes answer the same way. - VTA: serves trust-task-discovery/0.3 next to 0.1, answering each in the version it was asked. The window goes at response level, since the VTA applies one window to everything it dispatches. The 0.1 frameworkVersion was "0.2", a stale copy of the framework crate's default. It is now "0.6", the MAJOR.MINOR of the 0.6.0 that 0.3 writes, so one responder no longer names two framework releases. - VTC: serves trust-task-discovery/0.3 for the first time. It answers identified callers only, as the VTA does, and lists the routing table itself (DISPATCHED_URIS plus the rooms and git-ns registrations). - Registrations: TASK_TRUST_TASK_DISCOVERY_0_3 in vta_sdk::trust_tasks and its task list, ReadOnly in retry_safety, the VTA dispatch table and its conformance witness (built from the real builder, not a literal), and the VTC DISPATCHED_URIS and its declared-URI census. - Push engine (VTI-TRN-045): its two staleness predicates now read VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW, the same value the nodes advertise, where before they combined two separate constants. It still reads no advertised window. A lookup would be a request/reply exchange, and every push is one-way. None of the recipients (approvers' devices, wallets, requesters) serves discovery. The window only matters when the recipient cannot answer. The engine never sees an `expired` refusal, so 0.3's "re-ask after an unexpected refusal" would have no trigger. The module docs and docs/05-design-notes/retry-and-idempotency.md say so. What remains of the spec's divergence F.3 is the producer side only.

title: feat(git-ns): administrator reads as Trust Tasks
body:
## Summary

Six VTC git-ns console REST reads had no Trust Task equivalent — the admin console's *Repos* plugin (rights, jobs, projection, accounts) and its activity feed were served only over a bearer admin session (`vtc-service/src/routes/git_ns.rs`), with no signed, transport-agnostic path. This adds one spec per route:

| REST route | Trust Task |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/git-ns/rights` | [`git-ns/right/list/0.1`](specs/git-ns/right/list/0.1/spec.md) |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/rights/issued-by-departed` | [`git-ns/right/issued-by-departed/0.1`](specs/git-ns/right/issued-by-departed/0.1/spec.md) |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/jobs` | [`git-ns/bridge/job/list/0.1`](specs/git-ns/bridge/job/list/0.1/spec.md) |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/projection` | [`git-ns/projection/show/0.1`](specs/git-ns/projection/show/0.1/spec.md) |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/accounts` | [`git-ns/account/list/0.1`](specs/git-ns/account/list/0.1/spec.md) |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/activity` | [`git-ns/activity/list/0.1`](specs/git-ns/activity/list/0.1/spec.md) |

## Design notes

- **`git-ns/right/list/0.1` vs. a `git-ns/view` revision.** A new spec, not a `git-ns/view` 0.6 bump: the role-derived rows the console shows (v0.1 `[hooks.git-trust] grant_on_role` grants) are not `RightRecord`s — no granter, no grant time, no expiry — and `subjectMember`/`granterDeparted` are administrative facts a member's own view has no business carrying. Folding either into the shared `RightRecord` component would widen every other consumer of it across the `git-ns/*` family. `specs/git-ns/_shared/0.5` adds a new, additive `AdminRightRow` (+ `RightOrigin`) component instead, shared by `right/list` and `right/issued-by-departed`.
- **Authority follows the REST handlers' actual gates.** `right/list`, `right/issued-by-departed`, `projection/show` and `account/list` require the **community-administrator capability**, matching their handlers' `SuperAdminAuth` — none of them is namespace-scoped, so `git.ns.admin` on a namespace is explicitly not enough (each Authorization section says so and why). `bridge/job/list` and `activity/list` scope to **administered namespaces** (community administrator sees all; a namespace admin sees their own), the same pattern `git-ns/namespace/list` and `git-ns/repo/list` already use — `activity/list` mirrors the existing handler's per-namespace filtering exactly, and `bridge/job/list` tightens beyond the REST handler's current unscoped `AdminAuth` to match the family's established security posture.
- **`git-ns/activity/list/0.1` vs. an `audit/list` filter.** Kept as its own spec rather than a filter on `audit/list`: the feed interleaves two different stores (git-ns audit rows *and* the bridge job queue) into one timeline, which `audit/list`'s filters have no way to express, and its authority (namespace-administrator standing) differs from `audit/list`'s community-wide audit-read capability.
- **Paging.** All six use the registry's common `cursor`/`limit` request, `nextCursor` response shape (as `vtc/registry/sync-jobs/list` and `vtc/registry/records/list` do) rather than the unpaged shape `git-ns/namespace/list`/`git-ns/repo/list` use — these six enumerate collections that grow unboundedly (rights history, job queue, member roster, activity log), unlike a namespace or repository count.
- All six declare `proof: REQUIRED`, an `## Authorization` section, and the four `## Security & Privacy` sub-headings, with valid and invalid (`payload.invalid-examples.json`) examples.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run validate` — clean, no new errors or warnings from these six specs
- [x] `npm run check-bindings` — Rust/TS/Go/Dart agree with the registry
- [x] `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs -- specs::git_ns` — 120 passed, 0 failed
- [x] Regenerated all four bindings (Rust, TypeScript, Go, Dart) in this PR

title: feat(spec-meta): a specification declares its own maximum document size
body:
## ⚠️ Framework-level change

Adds an optional front-matter member, **`maxDocumentBytes`**, so a specification can state the largest document of each variant a consumer serving it is expected to accept. This is the registry half; the framework text (Specification Requirements **item 21**, plus one sentence in Parser Hardening) is proposed in the canonical repository: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#26. `SPEC.md` is not edited here.

```yaml
maxDocumentBytes:
  request: 360448      # bytes of the serialized document, proof included, no transport envelope
  response: 65536      # each variant optional; at least one declared
  rationale: ...
```

### Why

SPEC §12.4 tells a consumer to bound what it parses at "a body-size limit appropriate to the Trust Task specification's payload", and §7.3 item 19 already notes that a transport-layer limit is the wrong place to choose one. No specification could say what its limit was, so a consumer serving many tasks picks one cap for all of them. The VTC does this with 64 KiB on `/trust-tasks`, which refuses registering a credential schema or moving website content. Raising the cap for every task so the largest ones fit would open all the others to bodies they have no use for. With this member, each task states its own bound and the spine enforces it per type.

### Semantics

- The bound is two-sided. A consumer **MUST NOT** refuse a document within the bound on size alone, and **SHOULD** refuse a larger one with `malformedRequest`, before parsing where it learns the `type` first.
- The two variants are independent: an absent one never inherits the other's bound.
- With no declaration, the consumer's own limit applies, as it does today.
- The meta-schema allows 1 KiB to 16 MiB. Anything bigger belongs in a chunked transfer.

### What changes

- `specs/spec.meta.schema.json`: the member.
- `trust-tasks-codegen`:
  - emits `Payload::MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES: Option<usize>` on the request and `Response` impls;
  - emits `schema_index::max_document_bytes_for(type_uri)` (bare URI for the request, `#response` for the response), for a dispatcher that knows the type before it parses;
  - refuses a `response` bound on a spec with no `$defs.Response`.
- `trust-tasks-rs`: the trait constant, defaulting to `None`. It is additive and has a default.
- `check-bindings`: compares Rust's constants against the front matter, re-derived independently.
- `CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md`: when and how to declare it.

**Rust only for now**, the same as `ERROR_CODES` today. The TS, Go and Dart generators do not emit it yet, and no spec in this PR declares it. The first users are in the stacked PRs below.

### `"variant": "response"` fixtures

These came in through #677, which has merged. This branch no longer carries a copy of that change: the rebase dropped it because it was already upstream.

### Stacked on this

- Admin, community, schemas, vetting, relationships, join-requests and rooms specs: #680
- Website chunked transfer: #682

### Checks run locally

Run on the stacked branches, which contain this one. All passed:

- `npm run build`, `check-bindings`, `check-dart-packages`
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets`, `cargo doc --all-features`, and `cargo clippy -D warnings` (default and `--all-features`)
- TS `tsc --noEmit`, `npm test`, `npm run smoke`
- Go `build`, `vet`, `test`, `gofmt`
- Dart `analyze --fatal-infos`, `test`

title: feat(vta/services): rollback 1.1 with a mediator drain window
body:
Adds `vta/services/rollback/1.1`: an optional `drainTtlSecs` for the mediated transports (`didcomm`, `tsp`). It is the same member, with the same rules, that `vta/services/update/1.1` added in #656.

**Why.** A rollback of a mediated transport can move it off its current mediator, and that mediator then drains. Rollback 1.0 gives the operator no way to set how long the drain lasts, so the agent can only use its default. The VTA's CLI (`services didcomm rollback --drain-ttl`) and SDK already accept an operator-chosen window. Without a member for it on the Trust Task, a rollback that starts a drain ignores that choice and always uses the default.

**Rules (same as update 1.1):**
- Refused with `malformedRequest` for `rest` and `webauthn`.
- If absent, the agent uses its default. The agent may raise a value below its floor to the floor. It must do so when the request arrived through the mediator being replaced.
- A mediator that carries both mediated transports drains once for both, and the result reports a single `drainUntil`.
- New in this version: when the rollback leaves no mediator draining, `drainTtlSecs` is accepted and has no effect. Whether a rollback drains depends on stored state the operator may not be able to see.

A 1.0 request is a valid 1.1 request. The response is unchanged, because the shared `RollbackResult` already carries `drainingMediator` and `drainUntil`. Includes `payload.invalid-examples.json`.

**Checks run locally:** `npm run validate`, `npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings` (592 specs, all four languages agree), `cargo test --workspace` (plus `trust-tasks-rs --all-features`, which includes the new `rejects_invalid_examples`), `go test ./...`, `dart analyze` + `dart test`, the TS `npm test` + `tsc` + `smoke`, `test:infra` and `test-ceremonies`. All pass. Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings are regenerated in this PR.

title: docs(specs): operational examples sign for authentication
body:
## What

VTI-KEY-022 (#637) moved a Trust Task document's proof default from
`assertionMethod` to `authentication`, reserving `assertionMethod` for
attestations and approver decisions — the closed list: `auth/step-up/approve-response`,
`task-consent/decision`, `confirm/response` (their `#response` variants sign
for `authentication`). #637's own docs sweep (6d48962a) updated the
top-level examples that existed at the time. This PR catches the ones that
didn't: newer minor versions created after that sweep, and a couple it missed.

## Changed (`assertionMethod` → `authentication` on an operational document's
top-level `proof`, non-normative examples only)

- `SPEC.md` — Example 1 (§4.2, a complete Trust Task document), Example 5
  (§8.2, an error response), Appendix A.4 (an example conforming document).
  `SPEC.md` is generated from the canonical `trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec`
  repo; this fix should also land there so the next regeneration doesn't
  revert it.
- `specs/acl/swap-key/0.1/spec.md` — the `linkProof` example (a challenge-bound
  consent proof, functionally an authentication signature, not an attestation).
- `specs/did-management/did/publish/0.1/spec.md` — the request example.
- `specs/git-ns/right/revoke/0.3`, `right/ratify/0.1`, `right/break-glass-notice/0.1`,
  `right/break-glass/0.1`, `right/grant/0.3`, `bridge/job/0.4`,
  `namespace/reseat/0.3`, `drift/resolve/0.3`, `account/unlink/0.1`,
  `repo/create/0.3` — minor versions published after #637's sweep that copied
  the old `assertionMethod` examples forward.

No normative text contradicted the rule in any of these files; only the
JSON examples were stale. No `verificationMethod` fragment named an
assertion-specific key, so none needed renaming.

## Left unchanged (real attestations / approver decisions / out of scope)

- `specs/task-consent/decision/0.1`, `specs/auth/step-up/approve-response/0.1–0.5`,
  `specs/confirm/response/0.1` — the closed list; normatively require
  `assertionMethod`.
- Embedded W3C Verifiable Credentials: `specs/vault/credentials/get/0.1`,
  `specs/vault/credentials/receive/0.1`, the role credential in
  `specs/vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1` (its two top-level Trust Task proofs
  were already fixed by #637; the remaining `assertionMethod` there is the
  delivered VC).
- Embedded/nested signed artefacts: the vetting card (`specs/vetting/session/0.1`,
  `specs/vetting/request/0.1`, `specs/vetting/_shared/0.1/vetting-card.schema.json`)
  and the witness proof (`specs/webvh/witness/publish/0.1`,
  `specs/webvh/witness/sign/0.1`) — these are attestations embedded in
  `payload`, not the Trust Task envelope's own proof.
- `specs/keys/derive-and-sign-document/0.1` — a generic document-signing
  service where `proofPurpose` is a caller-supplied payload member for a
  document the producer hands over; not the framework's own default.
- DID-document verification-relationship references (`specs/vta/_shared/0.3`,
  `specs/vta/webvh/dids/**`) — these name the `assertionMethod` DID-document
  relationship, unrelated to a Trust Task proof's `proofPurpose`.
- `specs/vault/sign-trust-task/0.1` and `0.2` — untouched; PR #667 is open
  against these files.
- `specs/provision/integration/{0.1,0.2,0.3}/payload.invalid-examples.json` —
  already a deliberately-invalid conformance fixture demonstrating this exact
  rule (`"note": "DataIntegrityProof.proofPurpose must be authentication."`).
- Interop test fixtures (`trust-tasks-go/proof/testdata`,
  `trust-tasks-ts-proof/test`, `trust-tasks-dart-proof/test/fixtures`) —
  byte-exact signed fixtures pinned by cross-library tests; changing the
  string would invalidate the signature they carry.

## Bindings

Regenerated all four (`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`,
`npm run build-ts-bindings`, `npm run build-go-bindings`,
`npm run build-dart-bindings`). Only the Rust crate had a diff — its codegen
embeds each spec's fenced request/response examples verbatim as conformance
tests, so the ten touched git-ns/did-management specs' Rust conformance
fixtures picked up the new `proofPurpose` string. TS, Go and Dart generate
from the JSON Schemas, which didn't change, so they have no diff.

## Checks run locally

- `npm run validate` — clean (591 specs; existing warnings are pre-existing
  debt unrelated to this change)
- `npm run check-bindings` — all four bindings agree
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs` — pass
- `go test ./...` in `trust-tasks-go` — pass
- `npm install && npm test` in `trust-tasks-ts` — pass

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.3.14`) | `0.3.13` → `0.3.14` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.3.13` → `0.3.14` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

feat(git-ns): administrator reads as Trust Tasks (#686)

* feat(git-ns): administrator reads as Trust Tasks

Six VTC git-ns console REST reads had no Trust Task equivalent: the admin
console's Repos plugin (rights, jobs, projection, accounts) and activity
feed were served only over a bearer admin session, with no signed,
transport-agnostic path.

New specs:

- git-ns/right/list/0.1 — the whole-community rights picture (recorded and
  v0.1 role-derived grants), each row's subjectMember/granterDeparted.
  A new spec rather than a git-ns/view revision: the role-derived rows are
  not RightRecords (no granter, no grant time) and the administrative
  membership facts are not member-facing, so folding them into view/0.5's
  shared RightRecord would widen every other consumer of that component.
- git-ns/right/issued-by-departed/0.1 — recorded rights grouped by a
  departed granter, alongside the community's cascade_on_departure policy.
- git-ns/bridge/job/list/0.1 — the bridge job queue, scoped to administered
  namespaces like git-ns/namespace/list and git-ns/repo/list.
- git-ns/projection/show/0.1 — what is published to the Trust Registry,
  and how many records the next reconciliation pass will change.
- git-ns/account/list/0.1 — every member's linked forge account,
  community-wide, since git-ns/view only returns the caller's own.
- git-ns/activity/list/0.1 — rights changes, drift and bridge jobs
  interleaved into one timeline, scoped like the namespace/repo listings.

All six declare proof REQUIRED, an Authorization section naming either the
community-administrator capability (rights, issued-by-departed,
projection, accounts — matching the REST handlers' SuperAdminAuth gate) or
namespace-administrator standing (jobs, activity — matching the namespace
and repo listings' pattern), and a cursor/limit paged list shape.
git-ns/_shared/0.5 adds AdminRightRow and RightOrigin, the row shape right/list

title: feat(auth): proxied authenticate and session-key refresh
body:
## Summary

webvh#238 kept three REST auth routes because no Trust Task covered them: the VTA-proxied SIOPv2 login (`POST /api/auth/challenge` + `POST /api/auth/`) and the session-key-bound refresh (`POST /api/auth/refresh`). This PR closes both gaps so webvh can delete its last REST auth routes.

- **`auth/authenticate/0.3`** — adds an optional proxied form. `payload.principal` names the VID being authenticated as when it differs from the document's `issuer`; `payload.delegationEvidence` carries whatever the auth service's own policy requires as evidence that `issuer` (the delegate, e.g. a holder's VTA) may act for `principal`. The resulting `Session.subject` is `principal`; the new `Session.actor` (shared `_shared/0.3` Session schema) records the delegate, so audit and revocation never conflate the two. The ordinary (self-authenticating) form from 0.2 is unchanged, including the `sessionKey` binding.
- **`auth/refresh/0.2`** — accepts a `proof` made by the session key bound at login (`auth/authenticate/0.2`/`0.3`), required in addition to the refresh token whenever the located session carries one (`sessionKeyProofRequired` otherwise). Adds an absolute session lifetime rule: refresh MUST NOT advance `Session.expiresAt` past `Session.absoluteExpiresAt`, refusing with `sessionLifetimeExceeded` once reached — the session key is never accepted as approval/step-up authority, only as a binding check layered on the bearer token.

Both specs add an `## Authorization` section (framework 0.6.0, required for consequential tasks), the four Security & Privacy sub-headings covering delegation abuse, stolen session keys and refresh-token theft with valid/invalid examples, and `## Changes from` sections.

All four bindings (Rust, TypeScript, Go, Dart) regenerated and cross-checked.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run validate`
- [x] `npm run check-bindings`
- [x] `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs -- specs::auth` (81 passed)
- [x] `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate -- specs::auth::authenticate::v0_3 specs::auth::refresh::v0_2` (8 passed, including `rejects_invalid_examples`)

title: feat(vtc-service)!: the community's REST-only admin surfaces are signed Trust Tasks
body:
## Summary

VTC batch 3, part 2 (stacked on #1834). The community's REST-only admin surfaces from trust-tasks #680 move onto the Trust Task spine (`trust_tasks::surface_tasks`). Authority is the signer's ACL row, read at execution, and matches each bearer route:

| task | authority |
|---|---|
| `vtc/community/{branding,requested-attributes,join-discovery}/show/0.1` | any entry (the route took any session) |
| `vtc/community/{branding,requested-attributes,join-discovery}/update/0.1` | `Admin` |
| `vtc/schemas/{register,list,show,delete}/0.1`, `vtc/schemas/accepts/{register,list,show,delete}/0.1` | `Admin` |
| `vtc/vetting/vetters/grants/list/0.1`, `vtc/vetting/auto-grant/{show,update}/0.1`, `vtc/vetting/revocations/list/0.1` | `Admin` |
| `vtc/relationships/{suspend,restore}/0.1` | the edge's issuer or an `Admin`; anyone else gets `notFound` |
| `vtc/join-requests/vetting/show/0.1`, `vtc/join-requests/query/0.1` | `Admin` |
| `vtc/rooms/list/0.1` | `Admin` (host admin view, outside `rooms/*` per I5) |

Notes:
- **Suspend/restore**: the issuer is the document's signer, so the issuer's own proof replaces the route's `pop` authorization. A pairwise-DID edge is suspended by a document that DID signs.
- **Schemas**: `delete` now refuses with `inUse` (a SHOULD the old route skipped) when an Accepts criterion's DCQL names the type, with `details.criterionIds`. `accepts/register` refuses in the spec's order: `invalidQuery`, `unregisteredType`, `unregisteredStatementType`, `invalidVetting`, `notPublishable`.
- **Listings** page in memory with an offset cursor (`o<n>`). A cursor from anywhere else is refused.
- **Error codes**: every declared code is witnessed in `tests/surface_verbs_spine.rs`, except `accepts/register:notPublishable`. That one is baselined (UNWITNESSED 8→9) because no schema-valid payload reaches it; the reason is in the census.
- **Console**: every call on these surfaces is a signed document: vetting (grants, auto-grant, withdrawals, join vetting facts, criteria), branding, join discovery, rooms. Response shapes the removed routes described are kept in the openapi components, so the console's wire types are still generated.

## Routes

Removed: `GET`/`PUT /v1/community/join-discovery`, `POST`/`GET /v1/schemas`, `GET`/`DELETE /v1/schemas/{type_uri}`, `POST`/`GET /v1/schemas/accepts`, `GET`/`DELETE /v1/schemas/accepts/{id}`, `POST /v1/relationships/{id}/suspend`, `POST /v1/relationships/{id}/restore`, `GET /v1/join-requests/{id}/vetting`, `POST /v1/join-requests/query`, `GET /v1/rooms`.

Kept because `vtc-client` still calls them: `GET`/`PUT /v1/community/branding`, `GET`/`PUT /v1/community/requested-attributes`, `GET /v1/vetting/vetters`, `GET`/`PUT /v1/vetting/auto-grant`, `GET /v1/vetting/revocations`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`, fmt
- [x] new/changed targets: `surface_verbs_spine` (new), `relationships`, `endorsements`, `join_requests`, `join_didcomm`, `vetting_journey`, `trust_task_manifest`; lib `spine_proof_tests` (86), `error_code_census`, `trust_tasks::tests`
- [x] openapi snapshot and `wire.ts` regenerated; admin-ui `npm run lint`; vitest 498/498
- [ ] CI

title: feat(vtc-service)!: console signing keys are auth/signing-key Trust Tasks
body:
## Summary

VTC batch 3, part 3 (stacked on #1835). The console's signing keys move from `/v1/admin/console-keys` to `auth/signing-key/{enroll,list,revoke}/0.1` (trust-tasks #680) on the Trust Task spine (`trust_tasks::signing_key_tasks`). All of enroll's normative items 4–8 are implemented:

- **4. The approval digest covers the whole document.** No delegation is written without a passkey gesture of `identityDid` bound by `bound_step_up::operation_digest` to the type and the **whole** payload (`signingKeyDid`, `identityDid`, `scope`, `deviceLabel`, `expiresAt`), recomputed over the document as received. A changed label or another key finds no gesture (tested).
- **5. Step-up only on the requester's authenticator; standing is not an oracle.** The gesture is asked for inline, only of the requester (`bound_step_up::request_for_enrolment`). It offers every registered console passkey, as an unauthenticated passkey login already does, so the first answer is the same for an administrator and for a DID nobody has heard of (tested). Nothing reaches the identity's devices. Standing (a live `Admin` row) is checked after the gesture, and only a passkey registered to `identityDid` can record it.
- **6. Capped expiry.** Every delegation has an expiry, at most 30 days away. A requested `expiresAt` is capped, and absent means 30 days. `ConsoleKeyDelegation.expires_at` is no longer optional.
- **7. Console-only scope, never accepted for `assertionMethod`.** The stored delegation carries `scope: console`. The spine refuses any approval type (`auth/step-up/approve-response`, `task-consent/decision`) whose proof is by a key a delegation names, whatever the delegation's state. The console now answers bound step-ups **unsigned** with `evidence.kind = webauthn` (approve-response 0.4 allows this), with the passkey as the only gate. An unsigned answer is heard only when it is an approval carrying a *console session passkey* of the subject. It is checked before the pending step-up is touched. A member's step-up passkey is still only accepted beside the member's own signature, and a denial always needs one.
- **8. Per-identity cap and rate limits.** At most 5 active keys per identity (`tooManyKeys` with `details.maxActiveKeys`). Enrolment attempts are limited per identity (10), per enrolling key (5) and overall (120) in each 10-minute window, answered `unavailable` with `retryAfter`. Per-source-address limiting is the HTTPS door's governor.
- Also item 1 (`keyNotIssuer`), item 2 (the key rules before anything about the identity: `selfDelegation`, `keyHoldsStanding`, `alreadyEnrolled`, `keyRevoked`, `expiryInPast`), item 9 (the key rules are re-checked, the cap checked, the gesture spent and the row written under one lock), and item 12 (audited against the identity, naming the key).
- **Revoke** is accepted from the key itself, from its identity, or from an unrestricted admin. A context-scoped admin revoking a peer's key, like an unknown key, gets `notFound`. A repeat revocation reports the original `revokedAt`. **List** returns the signer's identity's own keys (its own row, or the identity an active delegation names).
- **Console**: enrolment signs with the new browser key, runs the bound gesture (`postSignedWithStepUp`), and re-sends the identical document. List and revoke are signed by this browser's key. `answerStepUp` sends unsigned.

## Routes

Removed: `POST /v1/admin/console-keys`, `GET /v1/admin/console-keys`, `DELETE /v1/admin/console-keys/{console_did}`. None kept; `vtc-client` and `cnm` never called them.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`, fmt
- [x] changed targets: `signed_step_up` (enrolment, capped lifetime, oracle parity, digest binding, key-rule codes, cap, revoke authority, list, routes gone, console key cannot sign an approval), `unrestricted_admin_consent`, `trust_task_manifest`, `openapi_schema_names`; lib `spine_proof_tests` (89), `step_up_passkey_tasks`, `signing_key_tasks` (rate limits), `acl::`, `git_ns::tests`
- [x] openapi snapshot and `wire.ts` regenerated; admin-ui lint; vitest 495/495
- [ ] CI

feat(vtc-service)!: the community's REST-only admin surfaces are signed Trust Tasks (#1835)

* feat(vtc-service)!: the policy log and the community's DID log are signed Trust Tasks

policy/{list,get,active,upsert,activate}, vtc/policies/test and
did-management/did/register are served by the spine
(trust_tasks::policy_tasks) on every transport, with the signer's ACL row
as authority: Admin for the policy verbs, an unrestricted Admin for the
DID log, as the bearer routes' AdminAuth and SuperAdminAuth asked.
policy/activate refuses a purpose the revision does not decide. The
console signs every policy call.

Per-type document limits come from the specifications: size.rs reads the
codegen'd maxDocumentBytes (schema_index::max_document_bytes_for) and keeps
an interim entry only for policy/upsert and did/register, whose specs
declare none yet. A raised limit applies to a served type only, and only
when the claimed issuer holds a live ACL entry (or is a signing key
delegated by one), looked up before verification. The HTTPS cap is the
largest served limit; a refusal does not echo an oversized type.

Removed: GET /v1/policies/active, POST /v1/policies/{id}/test.
Kept while vtc-client calls them: GET/POST /v1/policies,
