title: vti-common-v0.29.0
body:
### Fixed

- **push**: Re-issue a push as a new attempt once it outlives its freshness window ([#1799](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1799))

The push engine (vti_common::trust_task_push) signed a document once and
  sent the same bytes for the whole push deadline: within an attempt the
  outbox retries the hop for up to an hour, escalation and the never-queued
  re-queue resend record.document unchanged, and deadlines run to 24 h
  (credential-exchange) or 30 days (removal notice). Both VTI consumers
  refuse a document older than 10 min + 60 s skew as `expired`
  (freshness_policy, issuedAt required), so any delivery after ~11 minutes
  was silently refused at the far end, and a copy collected late by a
  reconnecting recipient was even recorded "delivered".

  Re-signing under the same id is ruled out by SPEC §4.3/§8.4: a re-stamped,
  re-signed document is a different document under a reused id, which the
  consumer's ReplayGuard (keyed on id + digest of the whole document, proof
  included) refuses as idConflict. expiresAt cannot help either:
  validate_freshness applies max_age to issuedAt regardless, and both
  consumers cap the replay record at issuedAt + max_age + skew by design;
  honouring a producer-chosen expiry would stretch an in-memory replay
  record and widen replay exposure across restarts.

  So the engine issues a SPEC §8.4 new attempt (trust_task_push::new_attempt:
  fresh id, fresh whole-second issuedAt, re-signed by the node through the new
  PushReissuer, kept in the original's thread, every other member including
  idempotencyKey unchanged) wherever it would otherwise put a document past
  its acceptance window on the wire: when queuing any attempt; when an attempt
  still waiting for hand-off crosses the window (superseded on the same
  transport, same window end); and when a copy is collected after the window
  plus skew (the recipient is online now and refused what it collected).
  A mediator-held copy is out of reach and not re-sent per window; bounded by
  MAX_REISSUES. The window is now one constant, trust_task::ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW,
  read by both consumers and the engine.

  Duplicate execution across attempts is what idempotencyKey is for
  (VTI-OPS-061/064): the credential-exchange push sites (VTA push_step, VTC
  push_document) now carry a key, and the VTA consumer now keys tasks the
  retry_safety catalogue does not classify, as VTI-OPS-062 requires; before,
  it skipped every counterparty credential-exchange step. Replay exposure is
  unchanged: same window, same replay record, and a byte-identical replay of
  a new attempt is still refused by id.

- **acl**: Offline provision-integration can write its admin grant again (VTI-ACL-053) ([#1792](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1792))

`vta bootstrap provision-integration` runs offline as the synthesised
  `cli:provision-integration` principal, and writes the integration's admin
  grant through `operations::acl::create_acl`. #1738 made `create_acl` bound
  every write by the caller's own stored entry and refuse a caller with none
  (VTI-ACL-053). The CLI principal never has an entry, so every offline
  first-time setup on vta-service 0.44.0 failed with:

      provision-integration: forbidden: cli:provision-integration has no ACL
      entry of its own, so there is no authority to bound this change by
      (VTI-ACL-001, VTI-ACL-053)

  The offline CLI is not a caller on the operation surface. It runs with the
  node stopped, as the OS account that holds the store and the seed, and the
  other offline writers (`vta acl create`, `vta import-did`) already store
  entries directly with nothing more to answer to. The specification now says
  so explicitly (dtgwg-vti-spec#46, "Offline writers" note under VTI-ACL-053).

title: test(cnm): the shell round-trip test is deterministic under load
body:
## Root cause

`cnm-cli::git::tests::printed_words_round_trip_in_sh_bash_zsh_and_fish` spawns
real `sh`/`bash`/`zsh`/`fish` processes to check that `shell_word` round-trips
an injection corpus through each shell. It failed once under a full
`cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` run, but always passes alone.

The one non-hermetic seam: `argv_in` used a **fixed `$HOME`**
(`$TMPDIR/cnm-shell-word-test-home`), shared across all four shell
invocations and never cleaned up. This repo routinely runs several
worktrees' test suites on the same machine at once, so two concurrent runs
of this test collide on the exact same path. Two smaller issues compounded
it: stdin was left inherited from the test harness rather than closed, and
there was no bound on how long a spawned shell could take to finish, so a
stall would just look like a hang rather than a clear failure.

## Fix

- Give each test run its own `tempfile::tempdir()` for `$HOME` (unique per
  run, cleaned up on drop) instead of a shared fixed path.
- Explicitly close the child's stdin (`Stdio::null()`).
- Read stdout on its own thread against a 20s deadline, so a hung shell
  fails the test loudly with a clear message instead of blocking the run.
- Spawn failures are now split: a shell that is genuinely not installed is
  still skipped (existing behaviour), but any other spawn failure (e.g.
  permissions, resource exhaustion) now panics instead of being silently
  treated as "not installed".

The injection corpus and the per-shell round-trip assertions are unchanged
— coverage is the same, just deterministic.

## Checks

- Looped the compiled test binary 500+ times (batches of 60/150/200/300 at
  parallelism up to 60) while a concurrent `cargo build` of other crates
  (into a separate `--target-dir`) ran alongside other sessions' own
  concurrent `cargo test`/`cargo install` on the same machine: 0 failures,
  before and after the fix.
- 6 fully parallel invocations of the standalone test binary: all green.
- `cargo test -p cnm-cli`: 90 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p cnm-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt -p cnm-cli -- --check`: clean.

title: vta-sdk-v0.56.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: Serve vta/services/rollback/1.1, so a rollback carries its drain window ([#1798](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1798))

* chore(deps): take trust-tasks 0.24, affinidi-tdk 0.20 and affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.30



### Changed

- **sdk**: One Trust Task surface — protocol_message_transport is gone ([#1793](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1793))

The SDK sends no bare DIDComm protocol messages any more: every VtaClient
  method is a Trust Task, and VtaClient::rpc went in #1783. The per-surface
  split between Trust Tasks and protocol messages was vestigial, so its
  reporting half goes with it.

  - Remove VtaClient::protocol_message_transport (public API removal).
    SurfaceTransport stays, reported by trust_task_transport().
  - vta-mcp: the status document's transports object drops
    `protocolMessages`; `trustTasks` remains.
  - Drop the protocol_message_transport assertions from
    tests/e2e/tests/tsp_dual_leg.rs, vta-sdk/tests/tsp_dual_leg_live.rs and
    the client unit test.
  - Rewrite the "TSP is selected per surface" rule in CLAUDE.md: there is one
    surface, and a dual-transport client's DIDCommSession stays only as the
    mediator's one socket per DID, carrying TSP receive. The one-socket rule
    is unchanged. tsp-enablement.md §3.3a gains a note that the
    protocol-message surface is gone; tsp.md, the TSP-vs-DIDComm note, the
    SDK's session/client docs and the VTA router's module doc are updated to
    match.

  The passkey-VM REST routes (/did/verification-methods/passkey{,/challenge,
  /{fragment}}) are now declared as the WebAuthn exception to "every remote
  operation is a Trust Task": the browser driving the ceremony (the VTA auth
  portal, examples/vta-auth-demo) holds only the bearer passkey-login issued
  and no DID key to sign a Trust Task. The declaration is a new
  REST_EXCEPTIONS table in vta_service::deprecation, naming each route's
  vta/passkey-vms/* Trust Task twin and the reason. It is machine-checked:
  every_rest_exception_names_a_live_route pins each row to a served route and
  method with no Deprecation header, and a unit test refuses a route listed
  both as an exception and as superseded. The routes, CLAUDE.md and
  docs/02-vta/personal-ai-agents.md name the exception. No behaviour change.

title: test(vta-service): the forged-host reply test proves the proof refusal again
body:
## Summary

`create_did_webvh_refuses_a_host_answer_not_signed_by_the_host` was loosened
by #1794 to accept either `"proof does not verify"` or `"is not believed"`.
That second phrase also comes out of a **key-retrieval failure**, which is
what this test was actually getting: the stub host's DID is only preseeded
into the resolver's *cache*, and a proof that fails against a cached
document is re-resolved once, fresh, before it is refused (VTI-KEY-134). That
forced fresh resolve of `webvh-host.test` can't be fetched, so the test was
passing on a resolver failure standing in for the forged-proof refusal it
means to prove.

Fix: `build_test_app_with` now also puts a small resolver
(`PreseededDidResolver`) in front of the resolver chain — for every method its
`preseed_did_docs` cover — that answers with the preseeded document. The
forced fresh re-resolution after an eviction then gets the same, real
document instead of failing to fetch one, so the forged proof is refused for
being forged, not for being unretrievable. The test's assertion goes back to
requiring `"proof does not verify"` exactly.

Confirmed by temporarily making the stub host sign correctly (no forgery,
`if false && forge`) and re-running: the test failed as expected
(`a forged host answer must not reserve a slot`), then reverted before
committing.

Production code is untouched: VTI-KEY-134's evict-and-refetch behavior is
unchanged; only the test harness gained a resolver that answers documents it
was already handed by the test author.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p vta-service --features test-support --test mock_vta` (21/21 passed, incl. the tightened test)
- [x] `cargo test -p vta-service --features test-support --lib --tests` (full lib + integration suite green)
- [x] Sabotage check: disabled the forgery, confirmed the test fails; re-enabled it
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vta-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean

## [0.7.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-backup-v0.6.1...vta-backup-v0.7.0) — 2026-09-27 ### Added - **webvh**: Reach the DID hosting service with Trust Tasks only ([#1789](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1789)) * feat(webvh)!: reach the DID hosting service with Trust Tasks only Stage 2b of the webvh-service Trust Tasks plan (trust-tasks #661). The VTA's REST client to the hosting service and WebvhTransport::Rest are removed; one client, vta-service/src/webvh_host.rs, makes every call as a Trust Task typed with the generated did-management bindings, over the transport the seam picks (TSP > DIDComm > HTTPS POST {base}/trust-tasks). - The HTTPS base defaults to {WebVHHosting origin}/api, where the hosting service serves its binding; https:// only, or http:// to loopback. - Every reply must carry the host's proof (SignedByRecipient), thread to the request, be addressed to this VTA and have the asked-for type. Refusals are read from trust-task-error documents by spec code; did/problem-report is no longer read. - servers/domains reads me/domains; reconcile and retire-orphan read the paged did/list {records, total} and now work over Trust Tasks. A listing that disagrees with its total is refused. - The DID-auth handshake, the server-auth token cache, WebvhAuthLocks and the WebVHHostingService alias are gone. vta-webvh is the store only. The test hosting service is now a Trust-Task host that refuses unsigned requests and signs its answers; a forged answer is refused. - **sdk**: Remove the last legacy backup and webvh surfaces; realign-keys is a Trust Task ([#1783](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1783)) * feat!: remove the last legacy backup and webvh surfaces; realign-keys is a Trust Task Every remote API is a spine-dispatched Trust Task over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS. What was left off the spine on these two surfaces was deprecated, and most of it could no longer succeed anywhere. Test deployments carry no compat, so it is deleted rather than refused. Backup - SDK `backup_export`, `backup_import`, `backup_import_with` (deprecated since 0.21.3 / 0.49.0), the `backup-management/1.0` message constants, and `ExportRequest` / `ImportRequest`. - `pnm backup {export,import} --use-rest-legacy`. It could not work on any transport: the VTA answered 403 over REST (VTI-VTA-003), and the SDK's `rpc` refuses DIDComm and TSP. Its doc said "works only over DIDComm". - The VTA's `POST /backup/{export,import}` and the VTC's `POST /v1/backup/{export,import}`, which only ever answered 403. A backup is the `vta/backup/*` (VTA) or `vtc/backup/export` + `backup/*` (VTC) Trust Tasks, over an end-to-end transport only; that policy is unchanged. webvh - SDK `update_did_webvh` / `rotate_did_webvh_keys` (the `(context, scid)` forms, deprecated since 0.20.32) and their message constants. Tests - The REST behaviour tests for update and rotate (metadata-only update, document update, rotate, unknown DID, invalid document) are ported to `/trust-tasks`. The Trust Task consent path it compared against is covered by the rest of `delegated_consent_e2e`. - `mock_vta` drives the by-DID update.

title: fix(push)!: re-issue a push as a new attempt once it outlives its freshness window
body:
A push outlives the document it started with. The engine now issues a new attempt (SPEC §8.4) instead of delivering a document every VTI consumer refuses as `expired`, and the idempotency key it carries keeps the task to one execution.

## Root cause

`vti_common::trust_task_push` takes a document the node has already signed, stores it in the push record, and sends those same bytes on every attempt for the whole push deadline:

- **Within an attempt**, the delivery layer's outbox retries the hop with backoff for up to the attempt window (`ATTEMPT_WINDOW`, 1 h). A DIDComm attempt is queued as ciphertext packed at queue time. A TSP or REST attempt reads `record.document` at send time, and that document is still the original.
- **Across attempts**, escalation (VTI-TRN-042) and the never-queued re-queue both call `queue_attempt`, which sends `record.document` unchanged.
- **Deadlines** run to 24 h for credential-exchange steps (VTA and VTC `EXCHANGE_DELIVER_BY`), 30 days for a removal notice, and the grant TTL for a granted notice.

Both consumers dispatch through `validate_freshness(now, freshness_policy())`: `max_age` is 10 min, the skew is 60 s, and `issuedAt` is required (`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs`, `vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs`). Anything older is refused as `expired`. So any delivery more than ~11 minutes after signing is refused, and nothing tells the sender. That covers an escalation, a mediator that refused hops for a while, a re-queue after a crash, and a copy the recipient collects when it reconnects. In the last case the engine even records the push **delivered** on class-3 collection evidence.

## Why neither obvious fix works

**Re-signing under the same `id`** is ruled out by the spec. SPEC §4.3 says an `id` is never reused. §8.4 says a producer "that 'retries' by re-signing, re-stamping `issuedAt`, … has issued a different document under a reused `id`, which item 11 requires the consumer to reject with `idConflict`". The VTA's `ReplayGuard` does exactly that: it keys on `id` plus a digest of the whole document, proof included (`trust_tasks_rs::replay`). A re-stamped document is therefore refused as `idConflict` by a consumer that accepted the original. `re_signing_under_the_same_id_is_refused_as_an_id_conflict` holds this.

**`expiresAt`** does not help. `FreshnessPolicy::validate_freshness` applies `max_age` to `issuedAt` whether or not `expiresAt` is present. Both consumers also cap the replay record at `issuedAt + max_age + skew` (`retain_until`), deliberately, so that a producer cannot decide how long a consumer must remember its `id`. Honouring a longer producer-chosen `expiresAt` would also make the in-memory, process-local replay record retain for hours or days. Replay exposure across a restart would grow by exactly that much, which is what this change must not do.

## The fix

The engine issues a **new attempt** (SPEC §8.4, last paragraph: "a new document with a fresh `id`") whenever it would otherwise put a document past its acceptance window on the wire. `trust_task_push::new_attempt` builds it:

- a fresh `id`
- a fresh whole-second `issuedAt`
- no `proof`: the node re-signs it through the new `PushReissuer`, which both nodes implement on `AppState` exactly as their push sites sign
- the original's thread: its `threadId`, or its `id` where it opened the thread. This keeps a VTC presentation challenge committed to the original `id`, and a counterparty's reply, correlating.
- every other member unchanged, including `idempotencyKey`

It happens in three places:

1. **Queuing any attempt** (first, escalation, re-queue) with a document already past the window.
2. **An attempt still `Queued`**, never handed off because every hop so far was refused, whose document crosses the window. A new attempt on the same transport supersedes it, keeping the old attempt's window end so a transport that refuses every hop still escalates.
3. **A copy collected after the window plus skew.** The recipient was offline and is online now. Collection is evidence of that, not of acceptance, so a new attempt follows on the same transport.

The limits:

- A `Sent` copy held by a mediator is sealed and out of reach. The engine does not re-send one per window, because that would fill an offline recipient's queue. Such a recipient refuses one stale copy, then receives a fresh one on reconnect (case 3).
- `MAX_REISSUES` (12) bounds the signatures one push can spend. Each is a KMS decrypt on a TEE node.
- A document with no `issuedAt`, or one past its own `expiresAt`, is never re-issued.

The acceptance window is now one constant, `vti_common::trust_task::ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW`. Both consumers' `freshness_policy` and the engine read it (the value is unchanged), so the producer and the consumers cannot drift.

## Security: exactly-once without widening replay

- **Replay exposure is unchanged.** Both consumers keep the same window and the same replay record. A new attempt is a document only the producer's key can sign, and a replay of it, byte for byte, is still refused as a duplicate by `id`.
- **Duplicate execution across attempts** is what the idempotency key is for. VTI-OPS-064: "Every attempt at one logical operation MUST carry the same idempotency key". VTI-OPS-061: a third-class operation is performed at most once per key. A new attempt carries the original's `idempotencyKey`, and the VTA's `(principal, key)` store answers the second attempt from the first's result. That store is persistent, with 24 h retention, and survives a restart. The key is signed, so a relayer cannot split or merge operations.
- **Push sites whose repeat leaves a second artefact now carry a key.** These are the credential-exchange steps: the VTA's `push_step` and the VTC's `push_document`, keyed by their first document's `id`. `issue` deposits a new vault row per execution (`store_issued_credential` mints a fresh id).
- **The VTA consumer now keys tasks the catalogue does not classify.** Before this, `idempotency::claim` skipped any task absent from `retry_safety`, which includes every counterparty credential-exchange step. That contradicts VTI-OPS-062: "an operation that is not classified MUST be treated as belonging to the third class". Only a document that carries a key is affected.
- **Other push sites carry no key.** Removal notices, break-glass notices, granted notices and consent requests converge on repeat (VTI-OPS-060 second class), so a key is unnecessary there.

## Tests

- `vta-service/tests/push_new_attempt_freshness.rs`, against the real dispatch spine, counting keys rather than status codes:
  - `a_push_re_issued_after_the_freshness_window_is_performed_once_and_only_once`: the stale original is refused `expired` and performs nothing. The new attempt is performed. A replayed identical new attempt is not performed. A second new attempt under the same key is answered from the first.
  - `re_signing_under_the_same_id_is_refused_as_an_id_conflict`: why the engine mints a fresh `id`.
  - `without_a_key_each_new_attempt_is_performed`: the control.
- `vtc-service/tests/member_push_didcomm.rs` (`didcomm-harness`, real mediator): `a_{rest,didcomm,tsp}_push_past_its_freshness_window_is_delivered_once_as_a_new_attempt` covers each transport the harness allows. The recipient gets exactly one document, with a fresh `id` and `issuedAt`, the original's thread and key, and the VTC's `authentication` proof. `a_push_inside_its_freshness_window_is_sent_unchanged` checks that fresh pushes are untouched.
- `vti-common` unit tests cover the window and skew boundaries, `new_attempt`'s members and thread, no re-issue without `issuedAt`, and no re-issue past the document's own `expiresAt`.
- `vta-service` unit test `an_unclassified_task_carrying_a_key_is_performed_once_per_key` (VTI-OPS-062).

## Breaking

`PushContext` gains a public `reissuer` member and is not `#[non_exhaustive]`, so constructing it by struct literal breaks. Hence the `!`.

## Spec follow-up (not in this PR; nothing on the wire is invented)

`idempotencyKey` is the workspace's existing top-level member (`docs/05-design-notes/retry-and-idempotency.md` §3; VTI-OPS-061). Two gaps remain, and both belong in the specs, not here:

1. **VTI spec, VTI-TRN-040/041.** Class-3 collection evidence says the recipient collected a message, not that it accepted it. A copy collected after the recipient's acceptance window closed is refused, yet reads as "delivered". Proposed: a sender MUST NOT record a delivery on collection evidence for a document it knows to be past the recipient's acceptance window, or class 3 should be qualified by the document's acceptance window. The engine now behaves that way (case 3) and logs it.
2. **Trust Tasks framework, §7.2 / §10 discovery.** A consumer's acceptance window is private policy. A producer that holds documents for delivery (store-and-forward, escalation) cannot know when to re-issue, and this workspace works only because both ends share `ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW`. Proposed: consumers advertise their acceptance window in `trust-task-discovery`, so a producer can re-issue against the recipient's actual window instead of a shared constant.

Unrelated pre-existing failure on main: `vta-service --test mock_vta create_did_webvh_refuses_a_host_answer_not_signed_by_the_host`.

title: fix(vta): Trust Task refusals stay Trust Task errors on DIDComm, and keys/create needs key-mint (Keyring VTI-09, VTI-23, VTI-27)
body:
Closes out three Keyring findings. Each was checked with a test against current `main` before any change. Two were still partly true.

## VTI-09: VTA and VTC disagree on the DIDComm body shape

**Already fixed on main.** The VTA refuses a bare payload over DIDComm, TSP and HTTPS. The refusal is identical to the VTC's: `malformedRequest: body did not parse as a Trust Task document: missing field `id``, in a signed `trust-task-error` (VTI-OPS-021). Neither node is lenient. This PR adds tests that pin it on both nodes and all three transports.

## VTI-27: an auth or ACL refusal over DIDComm is a problem-report

**The ACL path was already fixed. Two adjacent paths were not.**

- **Already fixed.** A sender with no ACL entry, or with a lapsed grant, gets `permissionDenied` in a signed `trust-task-error`. It arrives in the binding envelope and is threaded to the request, over DIDComm and over TSP. Tests pin this.
- **Fixed: the DIDComm inbound gate.** The gate turns away anoncrypt frames, unverified senders and plaintext before they reach the router. It used to answer all of them with a problem-report, even a Trust Task in the envelope. Now an enveloped request gets a signed `permissionDenied` `trust-task-error` in the envelope.
  - Other message types still get a problem-report.
  - An inbound error document gets no reply.
  - The code is `gate_refusal` in `messaging/service.rs`.
- **Fixed: answering an error with an error.** When an inbound `trust-task-error` arrives, or a reply is handed to its waiter, the spine returns an empty body, meaning "no reply". The DIDComm handler failed to parse the empty body. `finish` then sent the peer an `internal-error` problem-report. It now sends nothing.
- **VTC parity.** The VTC has no gate in front of its spine, and its refusals are `trust-task-error` documents. Its replies still carry the document's own type as the DIDComm `type`, not the envelope. That is the separate VTI-42 item noted at `tt_didcomm_reply` and is not changed here.

## VTI-23: every operation a manager needs requires the admin role

**#1619 fixed the two operations the finding named. One more role floor remained and is fixed here.**

- **`webvh/dids/create`** is gated on `key-mint` since #1619. The e2e test has an `initiator` in the context mint a persona DID over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS.
- **`keys/export-secret`** is gated on the `key-export` capability (VTI-VTA-003), not on a role.
  - An admin of the key's context holds it and exports over DIDComm and TSP.
  - An `initiator` holds `sign` but not `key-export`, so it is refused on every transport.
  - That split is deliberate (VTI-VTA-002, #1619): a manager signs as a persona through the signing oracle and does not take the key. It is unchanged here.
- **Fixed: `keys/create`.** It still checked the admin role, both in the Trust Task handler and in `POST /keys` (`AdminAuth`). That was wrong both ways:
  - An `initiator`, whose role ceiling includes `key-mint`, was refused. Spec Appendix C.2 defines `key-mint` as "creating new keys within scope".
  - An admin narrowed without `key-mint` was let through (VTI-ACL-030).

  The gate is now `operations::keys::ensure_may_mint_key`. It lives in the operation, so both surfaces use it, and it reads the caller's ACL entry. The context check still decides *where*. Key custody still reserves caller-chosen derivation paths for super-admins.

## Tests (named by finding)

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `vta-service` lib: `messaging::router::keyring_vti_09_27` | DIDComm: bare payload, ACL refusal (no entry / lapsed), inbound error not answered |
| `vta-service` lib: `messaging::tsp_inbound::keyring_vti_09_27` | TSP: bare payload, ACL refusal |
| `vta-service` lib: `messaging::service::keyring_vti_27_gate` | The inbound-gate refusal for a Trust Task, for another message type, and for an error document |
| `vta-service` lib: `operations::keys::tests::vti_23_*` | `key-mint` / `key-export` gates, context bound, narrowing |
| `vta-service/tests/keyring_vti_09_23_https.rs` | HTTPS binding and `POST /keys` |
| `tests/e2e/tests/keyring_vti_23_27.rs` | TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS against a VTA on a real test mediator |
| `vtc-service`: `vti_09_a_bare_payload_is_refused_as_malformed_on_every_transport` | The VTC's refusal, for parity |

## Checks run locally

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. #1791 had already fixed the `items_after_test_module` issue on main.
- The vta-service steps of the "Feature combos" job (tee+webvh, didcomm without webvh, rest only, tsp without didcomm, without tsp, TEE Mode B carve-out): all pass.
- `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: two failures in the first run, both handled.
  - A census test flagged how my new test code built a document. Fixed.
  - `mock_vta::create_did_webvh_refuses_a_host_answer_not_signed_by_the_host` also failed on main. #1794 fixed it, and it passes after rebasing onto that.
  - After the rebase I re-ran the vta-service lib, `mock_vta`, `api_integration`, the new HTTPS file and the new e2e file, and all passed. The machine was heavily loaded, so a few I/O-bound lib tests (`audit_coverage`, `self_hosted_did`) took over 40 minutes, but they passed. One of them, `self_hosted_did::not_found_carries_no_caching_headers_even_with_if_none_match`, was killed in that run and not re-run separately.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: see the comment below.

title: fix(push)!: re-issue a push as a new attempt once it outlives its freshness window (#1799)
body:
fix(push)!: re-issue a push as a new attempt once it outlives its freshness window (#1799)

The push engine (vti_common::trust_task_push) signed a document once and
sent the same bytes for the whole push deadline: within an attempt the
outbox retries the hop for up to an hour, escalation and the never-queued
re-queue resend record.document unchanged, and deadlines run to 24 h
(credential-exchange) or 30 days (removal notice). Both VTI consumers
refuse a document older than 10 min + 60 s skew as `expired`
(freshness_policy, issuedAt required), so any delivery after ~11 minutes
was silently refused at the far end, and a copy collected late by a
reconnecting recipient was even recorded "delivered".

Re-signing under the same id is ruled out by SPEC §4.3/§8.4: a re-stamped,
re-signed document is a different document under a reused id, which the
consumer's ReplayGuard (keyed on id + digest of the whole document, proof
included) refuses as idConflict. expiresAt cannot help either:
validate_freshness applies max_age to issuedAt regardless, and both
consumers cap the replay record at issuedAt + max_age + skew by design;
honouring a producer-chosen expiry would stretch an in-memory replay
record and widen replay exposure across restarts.

So the engine issues a SPEC §8.4 new attempt (trust_task_push::new_attempt:
fresh id, fresh whole-second issuedAt, re-signed by the node through the new
PushReissuer, kept in the original's thread, every other member including
idempotencyKey unchanged) wherever it would otherwise put a document past
its acceptance window on the wire: when queuing any attempt; when an attempt
still waiting for hand-off crosses the window (superseded on the same
transport, same window end); and when a copy is collected after the window
plus skew (the recipient is online now and refused what it collected).
A mediator-held copy is out of reach and not re-sent per window; bounded by
MAX_REISSUES. The window is now one constant, trust_task::ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW,
read by both consumers and the engine.

Duplicate execution across attempts is what idempotencyKey is for
(VTI-OPS-061/064): the credential-exchange push sites (VTA push_step, VTC
push_document) now carry a key, and the VTA consumer now keys tasks the
retry_safety catalogue does not classify, as VTI-OPS-062 requires; before,
it skipped every counterparty credential-exchange step. Replay exposure is
unchanged: same window, same replay record, and a byte-identical replay of
a new attempt is still refused by id.

BREAKING CHANGE: PushContext gains a public `reissuer` member.

**Stacked on #1797** (trust-tasks-rs 0.24.2, which carries `rollback/1.1`). Until #1797 merges, this diff also shows its commit. Merge #1797 first, then I'll rebase this.

`pnm services didcomm rollback --drain-ttl` and the SDK's `RollbackDidcommRequest::drain_ttl_secs` had nowhere to go: rollback/1.0 has no drain member. trust-tasks-tf#670 specified `vta/services/rollback/1.1`, which adds an optional `drainTtlSecs` under update/1.1's rules.

- **SDK:** every rollback now sends 1.1, and `rollback_didcomm` carries the drain window.

title: fix(vta-service): a Trust Task fits a default worker stack in a debug build (Keyring VTI-08)
body:
Closes Keyring **VTI-08**: on a debug build, `vta/contexts/create/1.0` overflowed a tokio worker's stack. Keyring's workaround was `RUST_MIN_STACK=32 MiB`.

**Root cause.** The spine's `dispatch_typed` has about 200 arms, each written `Box::pin(handler(..)).await`. That builds the handler's future as a temporary in dispatch_typed's own frame before moving it to the heap. A debug build gives every arm's temporary its own stack slot, so the frame held roughly the sum of every handler's future.

**Measurements** (stack needed for each piece on its own):

| Piece | Stack needed |
|---|---|
| Successful context create through the spine | 1–1.5 MiB |
| Handler alone | fits in 512 KiB |
| Operation alone | fits in 512 KiB |
| Schema check | fits in 256 KiB |
| Response signing | fits in 256 KiB |
| Test app-state setup | under 512 KiB |
| Request refused before dispatch | under 512 KiB |

With the HTTP or DIDComm layers on top, that ~1 MiB frame overflowed a 2 MiB worker. The earlier `Box::pin` fixed the future's size; this fixes the frame.

**Fix.** Each arm calls `boxed_task(move || handler(..))`, an `#[inline(never)]` helper that builds the future in its own frame and returns `Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send>>`. The match yields one type and there is a single await.

**Test.** `vti_08_context_create_fits_half_a_default_worker_stack` runs a successful contexts/create through the spine on a 512 KiB thread, in a child copy of the test binary (an overflow aborts the process). It **fails on main and passes with this change**; I verified both.

**Local checks:** workspace clippy is clean after rebasing onto main, and all seven `vta-service` Feature combos steps pass. Before the rebase, the workspace tests had only two failures, both reds that main has since fixed (#1791, #1794).

fix(vta-service): a Trust Task fits a default worker stack in a debug build (Keyring VTI-08) (#1796)

Keyring measured `vta/contexts/create/1.0` overflowing a tokio worker's stack
on a debug build, and worked around it with RUST_MIN_STACK=32 MiB.

Root cause: the spine's `dispatch_typed` frame. Each of its ~200 arms read
`Box::pin(handler(state, auth, doc)).await`, which builds the handler's future
as a temporary in dispatch_typed's own frame before moving it to the heap. An
unoptimised build gives every arm's temporary its own stack slot, so the frame
was the sum of every handler's future: measured, a successful context create
through the spine needed between 1 and 1.5 MiB (the handler alone, the
operation, the schema check and response signing each fit in 512 KiB, and a
request refused before dispatch needs less). With the HTTP or DIDComm layers on
top, a 2 MiB tokio worker overflowed. The earlier Box::pin fixed the future's
size, not the frame.

helper that builds the future in its own small frame and returns a
`Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send>>`. The match yields that one type and there is a
single await, so dispatch_typed's frame holds a pointer per arm, not a future.

successful contexts/create through the spine on a 512 KiB thread, in a child

title: refactor(sdk)!: one Trust Task surface — protocol_message_transport is gone
body:
Two cleanups.

## 1. Retire the SDK's protocol-message surface

The SDK sends no bare DIDComm protocol messages: every `VtaClient` method is a Trust Task, and `VtaClient::rpc` went in #1783. What was left of the per-surface split was vestigial.

- **Removed** `VtaClient::protocol_message_transport` (public API, hence `!`). `SurfaceTransport` stays and `trust_task_transport()` reports it.
- **vta-mcp**: `vta_status` / `vta://status` drops `transports.protocolMessages`. `transports.trustTasks` is still there.
- **Tests**: dropped the `protocol_message_transport` assertions in `tests/e2e/tests/tsp_dual_leg.rs`, `vta-sdk/tests/tsp_dual_leg_live.rs` and the `client` unit test. One e2e test was renamed to `a_client_with_the_leg_reports_tsp_for_trust_tasks`.
- **Docs**:
  - CLAUDE.md: the "TSP is selected per surface" rule is rewritten. There is one surface now. A dual-transport client keeps its `DIDCommSession` only because the mediator allows one socket per DID, and TSP receive arrives on it. The one-socket rule itself is unchanged.
  - `tsp-enablement.md` §3.3a: added a note that the protocol-message surface is gone.
  - Also updated to match: `tsp.md`, `tsp-vs-didcomm-trust-task-surface.md`, the vta-mcp example, the prose in `vta-sdk` session/client/webvh, and the VTA router's module doc.

### Remaining bare-DIDComm arms in `vta-service/src/messaging/router.rs`

None outside plumbing. `dispatch` handles only these message types:
- pickup status
- trust-ping
- the Trust Task binding envelope
- problem-report

Every other type falls through to `handle_unknown`. Nothing was deleted from the router.

## 2. Passkey-VM REST routes: the WebAuthn exception is now explicit

`/did/verification-methods/passkey{,/challenge,/{fragment}}` stay as REST routes. Passkey enrolment is a WebAuthn ceremony run in a browser (the VTA auth portal, or `examples/vta-auth-demo`). That browser holds only the bearer token passkey-login issued, so it has no DID key to sign a Trust Task. DID-holding clients use the `vta/passkey-vms/*` Trust Tasks instead.

- New `RestException` table `REST_EXCEPTIONS` in `vta_service::deprecation`. Each row gives the method, path, protocol, Trust Task twin and reason.
- Two tests check it:
  - `every_rest_exception_names_a_live_route` (in `tests/api_integration.rs`): each row must match a live route and method, with no `Deprecation` header.
  - `no_route_is_both_an_exception_and_superseded` (unit test): no route can be in both tables.
- The exception is also named in comments on the routes (`routes/mod.rs`, `routes/passkey_vms.rs`), in CLAUDE.md next to the REST-fallback rule, and in `docs/02-vta/personal-ai-agents.md` (step 5, where passkeys are covered). The comment's dangling "(forthcoming)" doc reference is replaced.
- No behaviour change.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- The vta-service/vta-sdk `cargo check`/`clippy` steps from Feature combos: all pass
- `cargo build -p vta-mcp`: builds
- `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: everything passes except one test, `mock_vta::create_did_webvh_refuses_a_host_answer_not_signed_by_the_host`. That test **fails the same way on `origin/main` (95b268f0)** with a key-retrieval error, so this PR did not cause it.

title: fix(acl): offline provision-integration can write its admin grant again (VTI-ACL-053)
body:
`vta bootstrap provision-integration` runs offline as the synthesised
`cli:provision-integration` principal, and writes the integration's admin
grant through `operations::acl::create_acl`. #1738 made `create_acl` bound
every write by the caller's own stored entry and refuse a caller with none
(VTI-ACL-053). The CLI principal never has an entry, so every offline
first-time setup on vta-service 0.44.0 failed with:

    provision-integration: forbidden: cli:provision-integration has no ACL
    entry of its own, so there is no authority to bound this change by
    (VTI-ACL-001, VTI-ACL-053)

The offline CLI is not a caller on the operation surface. It runs with the
node stopped, as the OS account that holds the store and the seed, and the
other offline writers (`vta acl create`, `vta import-did`) already store
entries directly with nothing more to answer to. The specification now says
so explicitly (dtgwg-vti-spec#46, "Offline writers" note under VTI-ACL-053).

`AuthClaims::is_local_cli_principal` recognises the synthesised principal:
a `cli:` subject, its session id equal to it, and `amr == ["cli"]`. None of
those is reachable over the wire, since an authenticated subject is a
resolved DID and `amr` is written only by the node's own authentication
paths. `caller_entry` bounds that principal by the node's whole authority;
every other caller without a live entry is still refused.

Tests: the offline CLI grants without an entry of its own; a `cli:`-named
caller without the CLI marker is still refused; an end-to-end offline
provision-integration writes the admin grant. The first and last reproduce
the reported error with the fix removed.

title: test(vta-service): the forged-host-reply test holds the refusal, not the harness's wording
body:
`create_did_webvh_refuses_a_host_answer_not_signed_by_the_host` has been red
on main since #1789 landed on top of #1748. Each passed on its own branch;
#1789's branch did not contain #1748.

The test asserted the refusal said "proof does not verify". The stub host's
DID is only pre-seeded into the resolver's cache. A proof that fails against
a cached key is checked again against a fresh resolve, because the signer may
have rotated (VTI-KEY-134). `webvh-host.test` cannot be fetched, and since
#1748 a failed re-resolve is reported as a key-retrieval failure, not a bad
proof. The verifier is right: it could not confirm the signer's current key.
The assertion was reading the harness.

The test now holds what it exists for: the reply is refused ("proof does not
verify" or "is not believed") and nothing is stored. Telling a bad proof from
an unretrievable key is covered by #1748's own tests in
`operations::outbound`.
author: stormer78

title: vta-keys-v0.8.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: Health, restore status, session revoke and the wrapping key are Trust Tasks ([#1790](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1790))

* feat(vta)!: health, restore status, session revoke and the wrapping key are Trust Tasks

  Four REST routes become spine-dispatched, signed Trust Tasks reachable over
  TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS (`/trust-tasks`), from trust-tasks-rs 0.23.6, and the
  routes are removed rather than deprecated.

  vta/health/details/0.1 (replaces GET /health/details)
  - Public: in `vta_sdk::trust_tasks::PUBLIC_URIS`, so an anonymous HTTPS caller
    (on the unauthenticated limiter) and a DIDComm/TSP sender the ACL does not
    know are answered; request proof optional, response signed.
  - Returns only the fixed non-identifying flags the schema admits: status,
    mediatorUrl/mediatorDid, teeStatus (as vta/attestation/status answers it,
    `sev_snp` spelled `sev-snp`, absent without a provider), sealed,
    storageEncrypted, tspEnabled. The same answer for every asker; never the
    software version or the restore record.

  vta/restore/status/0.1 (the version and restore half of GET /health/details)
  - Administrators of the VTA only (any admin, scoped or not, read from the ACL
    now rather than the token); anyone else is `permissionDenied` before any
    restore state is read. Request proof required, response signed.
  - Answers `version`, `restored`, and the VTI-VTA-051 `restore` record from
    `keys ▸ restore:provenance` exactly when restored. The SDK refuses a reply in
    which the two disagree. `pnm health` gains a Deployment section showing both
    tasks' answers.

  auth/revoke-session/0.2 (replaces GET /auth/sessions, DELETE
  /auth/sessions/{id}, DELETE /auth/sessions?did=)
  - Adds the `subject` form and implements `all: true` (0.1 refused it). A caller
    may end another subject's sessions exactly when it could remove that
    subject's ACL entry (VTI-SES-043, VTI-ACL-050, `may_manage_subject`); outside
    that, `permissionDenied`, decided before the subject's sessions are read and
    identical whether or not the subject exists. A named session outside the
    caller's authority is answered as a missing one (`revokedCount: 0`).
  - The payload is checked against its schema and the one-form rule is enforced
    in the handler on the validated JSON, not left to the generated type: two
    forms, none, or `all: false` are `malformedRequest`.
  - Every revocation and refusal is audited with caller and subject; `reason`
    goes to the audit detail.
  - 0.1 is no longer served (every 0.1 payload is a valid 0.2 payload);
    vta-mobile-core's builders move to 0.2. The hand-written
    `RevokeSessionRequest`/`RevokeSessionResponse` are deleted in favour of the
    generated types. Listing another subject's sessions has no replacement: no
    published task enumerates them.

  keys/import-wrapping-key/0.1 (replaces GET /keys/import/wrapping-key)
  - The wrapping key is now an Ed25519 keypair returned as a `did:key`, with
    `keyId` and `expiresAt`; only its X25519 counterpart is kept, in memory,
    single-use, 60 seconds. Admin only, as keys/import. Response signed.
  - `VtaClient::get_wrapping_key` returns the generated response and always
    verifies the reply's proof (a client with no identity is refused, and
    `trusting_unsigned_replies` does not apply to this task). `pnm keys import`
    seals to the did:key's X25519. The sealed path over HTTPS works through the
    task; the cleartext carrier stays refused there.

title: vta-keyspaces-v0.4.0
body:
### Added

- **webvh**: Reach the DID hosting service with Trust Tasks only ([#1789](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1789))

* feat(webvh)!: reach the DID hosting service with Trust Tasks only

  Stage 2b of the webvh-service Trust Tasks plan (trust-tasks #661). The
  VTA's REST client to the hosting service and WebvhTransport::Rest are
  removed; one client, vta-service/src/webvh_host.rs, makes every call as a
  Trust Task typed with the generated did-management bindings, over the
  transport the seam picks (TSP > DIDComm > HTTPS POST {base}/trust-tasks).

  - The HTTPS base defaults to {WebVHHosting origin}/api, where the hosting
    service serves its binding; https:// only, or http:// to loopback.
  - Every reply must carry the host's proof (SignedByRecipient), thread to
    the request, be addressed to this VTA and have the asked-for type.
    Refusals are read from trust-task-error documents by spec code;
    did/problem-report is no longer read.
  - servers/domains reads me/domains; reconcile and retire-orphan read the
    paged did/list {records, total} and now work over Trust Tasks. A listing
    that disagrees with its total is refused.
  - The DID-auth handshake, the server-auth token cache, WebvhAuthLocks and
    the WebVHHostingService alias are gone. vta-webvh is the store only.

  The test hosting service is now a Trust-Task host that refuses unsigned
  requests and signs its answers; a forged answer is refused.

- **vta-service**: Remove the unused /cache and /acl/swap routes ([#1786](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1786))

* feat(vta-service)!: remove the unused /cache and /acl/swap routes

  Two REST routes with no client left, removed under the rule that every remote
  API is a transport-agnostic Trust Task.

  - `GET|PUT|DELETE /cache/{key}`: a per-DID key-value store nothing in the
    workspace, the CLIs or the browser clients called, and with no Trust Task.
    The route, `operations::cache`, `AppState::cache_ks` and the `cache`
    keyspace go with it (it was never backed up; no restore reads it).
  - `POST /acl/swap`: self-service key rotation is `acl/swap-key/0.1`, which
    the SDK already sends on every transport (`swap_acl_for`).

title: vta-config-v0.8.0
body:
### Added

- **attestation**: The TEE attestation reads are public Trust Tasks, over any transport ([#1776](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1776))

* feat(attestation)!: the TEE attestation reads are public Trust Tasks, over any transport

  A TEE VTA answered three attestation reads only as unauthenticated REST routes
  (`GET /attestation/status`, `GET`/`POST /attestation/report`,
  `POST /attestation/config-report`), plus a bare DIDComm protocol arm that
  nothing sent to. Under the rule that every remote API is a spec-first,
  spine-dispatched Trust Task reachable over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS, they are now
  `vta/attestation/{status,report,config-report}/0.1` (trustoverip/
  dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#654, trust-tasks-rs 0.23.2), dispatched on the spine.

  Public tasks
  - `vta_sdk::trust_tasks::PUBLIC_URIS` names the tasks a caller may send with no
    identity: no session, no ACL entry, no request proof. A verifier asks before
    it trusts the VTA; the nonce bound into the evidence is what makes a report
    its own, and every response is the VTA's signed operational document.
  - HTTPS: `/trust-tasks` takes an optional credential. An anonymous caller may
    send only a public task (anything else is 401), capped at 64 KB, and those
    requests are charged to the unauthenticated limiter — which charges only
    requests presenting no credential, decided by the extractor's own rule
    (`vti_common::auth::extractor::presents_credential`), so a junk header cannot
    move a request between the two classes.
  - DIDComm/TSP: a sender the ACL does not know gets a zero-authority claim for a
    public task, and `bind_document_to_sender` accepts it unsigned — the spec
    makes the request proof OPTIONAL and HTTPS accepts it unsigned, so refusing it
    here would make the requirement depend on the transport (VTI-OPS-021). An
    attached proof is still verified and bound.
  - A census (`every_public_task_is_proof_optional_and_read_only`) fails if a task
    whose spec requires a proof, or whose dispatch class changes state, discloses
    a secret or acts as its subject, is ever added to `PUBLIC_URIS`.

  Behaviour
  - `report` and `config-report` require a 32-byte verifier nonce; the cached,
    nonce-less report is not carried over — evidence nobody asked for is evidence
    anybody can replay.
  - Failures carry the specs' declared codes: `notAttested` (no provider),
    `noConfigSnapshot` (only the enclave front-end captures one),
    `evidenceUnavailable` (the platform refused a quote).
  - The VTA still requires `issuedAt` on every document (bounding its replay
    record), stricter than the spec; the deploy README examples send it.

  Removed (breaking)
  - The REST routes above and the DIDComm `firstperson.network/vta/1.0/
    attestation/*` arms, with their SDK constants; `TASK_ATTESTATION_{STATUS,
    REPORT}_1_0` become `TASK_ATTESTATION_{STATUS,REPORT,CONFIG_REPORT}_0_1` and
    leave `REST_ROUTED_URIS`.
  - The `TeeAttestation` DID-document service, which pointed at the REST route
    (user decision: removed, not re-pointed). `tee.embed_in_did` and
    `VTA_TEE_EMBED_IN_DID` are **refused** at config load as retired, naming the
    replacement, rather than silently ignored. The shipped Nitro configs drop the
    key; the deploy scripts' health hints point at `/health`.

- **cli**: Make pnm usable from a script ([#1753](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1753))

* feat(cli)!: pipe gets json, terminal gets table

- **sdk**: Remove the last legacy backup and webvh surfaces; realign-keys is a Trust Task ([#1783](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1783))

* feat!: remove the last legacy backup and webvh surfaces; realign-keys is a Trust Task

  Every remote API is a spine-dispatched Trust Task over TSP, DIDComm and
  HTTPS. What was left off the spine on these two surfaces was deprecated,
  and most of it could no longer succeed anywhere. Test deployments carry no
  compat, so it is deleted rather than refused.

  Backup
  - SDK `backup_export`, `backup_import`, `backup_import_with` (deprecated
    since 0.21.3 / 0.49.0), the `backup-management/1.0` message constants, and
    `ExportRequest` / `ImportRequest`.
  - `pnm backup {export,import} --use-rest-legacy`. It could not work on any
    transport: the VTA answered 403 over REST (VTI-VTA-003), and the SDK's
    `rpc` refuses DIDComm and TSP. Its doc said "works only over DIDComm".
  - The VTA's `POST /backup/{export,import}` and the VTC's
    `POST /v1/backup/{export,import}`, which only ever answered 403. A backup
    is the `vta/backup/*` (VTA) or `vtc/backup/export` + `backup/*` (VTC) Trust
    Tasks, over an end-to-end transport only; that policy is unchanged.

  webvh
  - SDK `update_did_webvh` / `rotate_did_webvh_keys` (the `(context, scid)`
    forms, deprecated since 0.20.32) and their message constants. The by-DID
    `update_did_webvh_by_did` / `rotate_did_webvh_keys_by_did` are the only
    forms.
  - The VTA's `POST /contexts/{ctx}/dids/{scid}/{update,rotate-keys}` and
    `POST /webvh/dids/{did}/realign-keys`.
  - `realign_did_webvh_keys` was REST-only "deliberately". The reason was out of
    date: the VTA already dispatched `webvh/dids/realign-keys/1.0`. The SDK now
    sends the task, so `pnm did-mgmt dids realign-keys` works over TSP and
    DIDComm too.

  Tests
  - The REST behaviour tests for update and rotate (metadata-only update,
    document update, rotate, unknown DID, invalid document) are ported to
    `/trust-tasks`. The removed routes are held gone.
  - The webvh REST-parity consent test is dropped. The Trust Task consent path
    it compared against is covered by the rest of `delegated_consent_e2e`.
  - `mock_vta` drives the by-DID update.

- Provision-integration is one Trust Task over TSP, DIDComm or HTTPS ([#1785](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1785))
- **services**: Service management is Trust Tasks only, over any transport ([#1782](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1782))

* feat(services)!: service management is Trust Tasks only, over any transport

  `pnm services …` (and every SDK caller) reached the VTA's service management
  through bespoke REST routes — twenty `/services/*` plus `/mediators/*` — via
  `VtaClient::rpc`, whose DIDComm and TSP arms answered `UnsupportedTransport`.
  So the whole surface worked only over REST, although the VTA already served the
  `vta/services/*` Trust Tasks. Under the rule that every remote API is a
  spine-dispatched Trust Task reachable over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS, the SDK now
  dispatches the tasks and the REST routes are removed.

  Spec gaps closed first (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#656, trust-tasks-rs
  0.23.3):
  - `vta/services/report/0.1` — the mediator-attribution report had no task.
    Operator-only, request proof REQUIRED: it is a contact log of other parties'
    DIDs. Served from the telemetry sink; `since` after `until` is the declared
    `invalidWindow`.
  - `vta/services/update/1.1` — adds `drainTtlSecs` for the mediated transports.
    The REST route and `pnm services didcomm update --drain-ttl` carried an
    operator-chosen drain; 1.0 could not, so moving to the task would have
    silently dropped it. The handler honours it for DIDComm, raising a value
    below the 1h floor to the floor over a request that arrived through the
    mediator being replaced (the spec's MUST), refuses it for rest/webauthn, and
    reports no `drainUntil` for tsp — this VTA has one mediator connection, which
    a TSP update does not tear down, so there is nothing to drain.

  SDK
  - Every `services` method keeps its signature and return type, builds the spec
    payload, dispatches over `rpc_tt`, and maps the generated response back.
    `enable_didcomm` is no longer REST-only: a REST-only VTA receives it over
    HTTPS on `/trust-tasks`. `didcomm_status` is `services/get`; the live
    websocket state is not published state (`GET /health/details` has it).
  - The producer census (`producer_payload_conformance`) now drives every
    services method through the loopback and validates each payload against the
    published schema; the wiremock REST-shape tests are gone with the routes.

  Removed (breaking)
  - `/services/*`, `/mediators/report`, `/mediators/drain/cancel` and their
    deprecation-registry entries; the REST-auth tests for them (the same
    super-admin gates are on the task handlers).
  - Responses lose two cosmetic fields the task does not carry (the mediator
    endpoint on enable/update); the CLI already printed them only when present.

  VTC
  - 0.23.3 publishes a generated `acl/revoke/0.1`, so the VTC's hand-written
    `RevokeRequest` / `AclRevokeResponse` (which the generated-wire-types census
    now names) are replaced by the generated payload on the spine and the
    generated response, wrapped as `vta_sdk::openapi::AclRevoke01Response`, on
    both the spine and `DELETE /v1/acl/{did}`. Behaviour is unchanged — the
    declared `subjectNotPresent` / `lastAuthorityProtected` codes and the session
    end on full removal. The console's `openapi.json` / `wire.ts` are regenerated
    for the schema's new name.

  Not closed here: `vta/services/rollback/1.0` has no drain member, so a DIDComm
  rollback that lands on a drain transition takes the default window; and
  per-transport mediators remain unbuilt, so advertising a TSP mediator the VTA is
  not connected to is still possible.



### Fixed

- **sdk**: Holder signing picks its proof purpose, and Trust Task endpoints must be https ([#1791](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1791))

* fix(vault): sign-trust-task picks the proof purpose from the document type

  vault/sign-trust-task signed every document for assertionMethod. Under
  VTI-KEY-022/106 an operational Trust Task is signed for authentication, and
  relying parties that enforce it (the DID hosting control plane since
  affinidi-webvh-service#218) refused every task a proxy-login wallet session
  had the VTA sign.

  The VTA now decides the purpose from the envelope's type alone:
  assertionMethod only for the registry's attestation types
  (auth/step-up/approve-response, task-consent/decision, confirm/response),
  authentication for everything else, including their #response variants and
  a private registry's reuse of those slugs. The requester cannot choose it;
  a type that is not a Type URI is refused as envelopeInvalid.

title: cnm-cli-v0.19.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc-service**: Git-ns administrator reads as signed Trust Tasks ([#1781](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1781))

* feat(cnm,vtc-client): send cnm git Trust Tasks over TSP, DIDComm or HTTPS

  Every signed `cnm git` command now reaches the VTC over TSP when it
  advertises it, else DIDComm, else as a signed document over HTTPS, through
  one shared connect helper (`vtc::connect_for_tasks`, which `cnm backup`'s
  end-to-end connect now also uses). The global `--transport` flag pins a
  transport; the session is closed on every path out.

  vtc-client's git-ns calls go over the session when the client holds one.
  The document is signed and bound to its sender the same way on every
  transport: over a session the key must be the session's own DID, and a key
  naming another DID is refused before anything is sent. A session refusal
  comes back as `VtcError::Refused` carrying the trust-task-error document,
  so `task_error` and `step_up_request` read the code and details alike on
  every transport (VTI-OPS-021/093).

  vta-sdk gains `VtaClient::dispatch_trust_task_document`, which answers the
  whole reply document (refusals included) rather than its payload.

  The admin listings (namespace list, repos, view --admin, break-glass-list)
  are console projections with no git-ns Trust Task and stay HTTPS admin reads.

- **cnm**: Send cnm access Trust Tasks over TSP, DIDComm or HTTPS ([#1780](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1780))

- **vtc**: Step-up passkeys a member enrols through an admin's invite ([#1756](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1756))

* feat(vtc/git-ns): separation of duties and break-glass for elevated git rights

  Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#641.

  - Fixed rule 7: no elevated self-grant (git.ns.admin, git.repo.create,
    git.repo.own) through grant 0.1/0.3, drift adopt, repo/adopt or reseat;
    refused git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed, naming cnm git break-glass.
  - git-ns/right/break-glass/0.1: grant authority, or a community admin on a
    headless namespace; always an operation-bound passkey step-up
    (acl::bound_step_up, whose spent mark now yields its evidence); mandatory
    justification; immediate, no expiry; flagged breakGlass on the record.
  - git-ns/right/ratify/0.1 and revoke 0.3: another administrator ratifies,
    bound to breakGlass.at; any community admin may revoke an unratified one,
    which policy cannot refuse. Unratified records do not count toward the
    last-owner and last-admin invariants.
  - Visibility no policy can turn off: AuditEvent::GitNsBreakGlass at
    AuditSeverity::Critical with the step-up evidence, activity items, a signed
    git-ns/right/break-glass-notice/0.1 to every community admin and ns admin,
    view 0.4, GET /v1/git-ns/break-glass, and breakGlass on the rights rows.
  - git_ns.rego settings: break_glass (enabled by default), a delay and a
    minimum justification; deny decisions on right.breakGlass and right.ratify.
  - cnm: git break-glass, git ratify and git break-glass-list; git view flags
    break-glass rights; grant and revoke move to 0.3.

- **vtc**: Serve acl/{show,list,update,revoke} as Trust Tasks on the spine ([#1772](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1772))

* feat(vtc)!: serve acl/{show,list,update,revoke} as Trust Tasks on the spine

  The VTC served only acl/grant and acl/change-role as signed Trust Tasks;
  reading an entry, listing the ACL and revoking one existed only as bearer
  REST routes, so the VTI-ACL-050 full-cover check on revoke lived on one
  door and a community could not take authority away over TSP or DIDComm.

  Server (vtc-service)
  - acl/show, acl/list, acl/update and acl/revoke are dispatched by the
    spine (trust_tasks/acl_tasks.rs). Authority is the verified signer's ACL
    row at execution time; payloads are validated against the generated
    trust-tasks-rs schemas.
  - One code path: routes::acl::{list_entries, show_entry, revoke_entry,
    plan_update} are the operations; GET /v1/acl, GET and DELETE
    /v1/acl/{did} are thin adapters over them.
  - acl/update is planned by plan_grant with the role held fixed, so it
    inherits VTI-ACL-052 (no self-modification), VTI-ACL-050 (full cover)
    and VTI-ACL-053 (bounded by the granter). It refuses a missing entry
    (acl/update:notFound), a narrowing (acl/update:narrowingNotPermitted),
    a role (acl/update:roleChangeNotPermitted), and the VTA-only members
    allowedKeys/approve/stepUp. Widening an admin needs the bound passkey
    gesture, and community-wide authority another admin's consent, through
    the same gate acl/grant uses (settle_signed_gate).
  - acl/revoke emits acl/revoke:subjectNotPresent and
    acl/revoke:lastAuthorityProtected, and now revokes the subject's live
    sessions on a full removal too.
  - acl/list gains `direction` (acting-in, subtree, any).
  - acl/grant: restating an admin with a later or no expiry now counts as
    widening (needs the gesture); a rewrite that reduces authority revokes
    the subject's sessions; the audit row names the actual actor rather
    than the entry's original creator, and an update is audited as
    AclUpdated.



### Fixed

- **vtc-service**: A community backup travels only over DIDComm or TSP ([#1755](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1755))

* fix(vtc-service)!: a community backup travels only over DIDComm or TSP

  The backup request carries its password, and the backup carries the
  community's signing key bundle. Over REST both exist in plaintext wherever
  TLS terminates.

  - POST /v1/backup/export and /v1/backup/import always answer 403.
  - vtc/backup/export and backup/initiate-export, initiate-import and
    finalize-import are refused on the REST binding, after the super-admin
    check and before any state is serialized, a slot is opened or the
    password is used. The chunks are ciphertext and are unaffected.
  - The export audit row is still written before the envelope is returned,
    and a VTC with no audit trail now refuses to export instead of releasing
    the backup unrecorded.
  - vtc-client export_backup and import_backup use the backup/* chunked
    transfer over a DIDComm or TSP session, verifying every chunk and the
    whole, and refuse without a session.
  - cnm backup connects to the VTC over TSP, or DIDComm when the VTC
    advertises no TSP, and has no REST fallback.

  Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#646.

body:
### Added

- **vta**: Health, restore status, session revoke and the wrapping key are Trust Tasks ([#1790](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1790))

* feat(vta)!: health, restore status, session revoke and the wrapping key are Trust Tasks

  Four REST routes become spine-dispatched, signed Trust Tasks reachable over
  TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS (`/trust-tasks`), from trust-tasks-rs 0.23.6, and the
  routes are removed rather than deprecated.

  vta/health/details/0.1 (replaces GET /health/details)
  - Public: in `vta_sdk::trust_tasks::PUBLIC_URIS`, so an anonymous HTTPS caller
    (on the unauthenticated limiter) and a DIDComm/TSP sender the ACL does not
    know are answered; request proof optional, response signed.
  - Returns only the fixed non-identifying flags the schema admits: status,
    mediatorUrl/mediatorDid, teeStatus (as vta/attestation/status answers it,
    `sev_snp` spelled `sev-snp`, absent without a provider), sealed,
    storageEncrypted, tspEnabled. The same answer for every asker; never the
    software version or the restore record.

  vta/restore/status/0.1 (the version and restore half of GET /health/details)
  - Administrators of the VTA only (any admin, scoped or not, read from the ACL
    now rather than the token); anyone else is `permissionDenied` before any
    restore state is read. Request proof required, response signed.
  - Answers `version`, `restored`, and the VTI-VTA-051 `restore` record from
    `keys ▸ restore:provenance` exactly when restored. The SDK refuses a reply in
    which the two disagree. `pnm health` gains a Deployment section showing both
    tasks' answers.

  auth/revoke-session/0.2 (replaces GET /auth/sessions, DELETE
  /auth/sessions/{id}, DELETE /auth/sessions?did=)
  - Adds the `subject` form and implements `all: true` (0.1 refused it). A caller
    may end another subject's sessions exactly when it could remove that
    subject's ACL entry (VTI-SES-043, VTI-ACL-050, `may_manage_subject`); outside
    that, `permissionDenied`, decided before the subject's sessions are read and
    identical whether or not the subject exists. A named session outside the
    caller's authority is answered as a missing one (`revokedCount: 0`).
  - The payload is checked against its schema and the one-form rule is enforced
    in the handler on the validated JSON, not left to the generated type: two
    forms, none, or `all: false` are `malformedRequest`.
  - Every revocation and refusal is audited with caller and subject; `reason`
    goes to the audit detail.
  - 0.1 is no longer served (every 0.1 payload is a valid 0.2 payload);
    vta-mobile-core's builders move to 0.2. The hand-written
    `RevokeSessionRequest`/`RevokeSessionResponse` are deleted in favour of the
    generated types. Listing another subject's sessions has no replacement: no
    published task enumerates them.

  keys/import-wrapping-key/0.1 (replaces GET /keys/import/wrapping-key)
  - The wrapping key is now an Ed25519 keypair returned as a `did:key`, with
    `keyId` and `expiresAt`; only its X25519 counterpart is kept, in memory,
    single-use, 60 seconds. Admin only, as keys/import. Response signed.
  - `VtaClient::get_wrapping_key` returns the generated response and always
    verifies the reply's proof (a client with no identity is refused, and
    `trusting_unsigned_replies` does not apply to this task). `pnm keys import`
    seals to the did:key's X25519. The sealed path over HTTPS works through the
    task; the cleartext carrier stays refused there.

* feat(cli)!: pipe gets json, terminal gets table

- **services**: Service management is Trust Tasks only, over any transport ([#1782](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1782))

* feat(services)!: service management is Trust Tasks only, over any transport

  `pnm services …` (and every SDK caller) reached the VTA's service management

  - Every `services` method keeps its signature and return type, builds the spec

  - The producer census (`producer_payload_conformance`) now drives every

    published schema; the wiremock REST-shape tests are gone with the routes.

  Removed (breaking)
  - `/services/*`, `/mediators/report`, `/mediators/drain/cancel` and their
    deprecation-registry entries; the REST-auth tests for them (the same
    super-admin gates are on the task handlers).

  - 0.23.3 publishes a generated `acl/revoke/0.1`, so the VTC's hand-written

### Fixed

- **cli**: Pnm keys import works over DIDComm and TSP ([#1784](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1784))

`keys import` always fetched the VTA's wrapping key first, and that is a REST
  route (`GET /keys/import/wrapping-key`), so on a DIDComm or TSP client the
  command failed before it sent anything. The SDK's `import_key` already sends

  The document is signed and bound to its sender the same way on every
  transport: over a session the key must be the session's own DID, and a key
  naming another DID is refused before anything is sent. A session refusal
  comes back as `VtcError::Refused` carrying the trust-task-error document,
  so `task_error` and `step_up_request` read the code and details alike on
  every transport (VTI-OPS-021/093).

  whole reply document (refusals included) rather than its payload.

  The admin listings (namespace list, repos, view --admin, break-glass-list)
  are console projections with no git-ns Trust Task and stay HTTPS admin reads.

- **cnm,vtc-client**: Send cnm git Trust Tasks over TSP, DIDComm or HTTPS ([#1778](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1778))

Every signed `cnm git` command now reaches the VTC over TSP when it
  advertises it, else DIDComm, else as a signed document over HTTPS, through
  one shared connect helper (`vtc::connect_for_tasks`, which `cnm backup`'s
  end-to-end connect now also uses). The global `--transport` flag pins a
  transport; the session is closed on every path out.

  every transport (VTI-OPS-021/093).

  whole reply document (refusals included) rather than its payload.

  are console projections with no git-ns Trust Task and stay HTTPS admin reads.

* feat(vtc/git-ns): separation of duties and break-glass for elevated git rights

  Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#641.

  - Fixed rule 7: no elevated self-grant (git.ns.admin, git.repo.create,
    git.repo.own) through grant 0.1/0.3, drift adopt, repo/adopt or reseat;
    refused git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed, naming cnm git break-glass.

    headless namespace; always an operation-bound passkey step-up
    (acl::bound_step_up, whose spent mark now yields its evidence); mandatory
    justification; immediate, no expiry; flagged breakGlass on the record.
  - git-ns/right/ratify/0.1 and revoke 0.3: another administrator ratifies,
    bound to breakGlass.at; any community admin may revoke an unratified one,
    which policy cannot refuse. Unratified records do not count toward the
    last-owner and last-admin invariants.
  - Visibility no policy can turn off: AuditEvent::GitNsBreakGlass at
    AuditSeverity::Critical with the step-up evidence, activity items, a signed
    git-ns/right/break-glass-notice/0.1 to every community admin and ns admin,
    view 0.4, GET /v1/git-ns/break-glass, and breakGlass on the rights rows.
  - git_ns.rego settings: break_glass (enabled by default), a delay and a
    minimum justification; deny decisions on right.breakGlass and right.ratify.

    break-glass rights; grant and revoke move to 0.3.

* feat(vtc)!: serve acl/{show,list,update,revoke} as Trust Tasks on the spine

  The VTC served only acl/grant and acl/change-role as signed Trust Tasks;
  reading an entry, listing the ACL and revoking one existed only as bearer
  REST routes, so the VTI-ACL-050 full-cover check on revoke lived on one
  door and a community could not take authority away over TSP or DIDComm.

  - acl/show, acl/list, acl/update and acl/revoke are dispatched by the
    spine (trust_tasks/acl_tasks.rs). Authority is the verified signer's ACL
    row at execution time; payloads are validated against the generated
    trust-tasks-rs schemas.

    plan_update} are the operations; GET /v1/acl, GET and DELETE
    /v1/acl/{did} are thin adapters over them.

    inherits VTI-ACL-052 (no self-modification), VTI-ACL-050 (full cover)
    and VTI-ACL-053 (bounded by the granter). It refuses a missing entry
    (acl/update:notFound), a narrowing (acl/update:narrowingNotPermitted),
    a role (acl/update:roleChangeNotPermitted), and the VTA-only members
    allowedKeys/approve/stepUp. Widening an admin needs the bound passkey
    gesture, and community-wide authority another admin's consent, through
    the same gate acl/grant uses (settle_signed_gate).
  - acl/revoke emits acl/revoke:subjectNotPresent and
    acl/revoke:lastAuthorityProtected, and now revokes the subject's live
    sessions on a full removal too.
  - acl/list gains `direction` (acting-in, subtree, any).
  - acl/grant: restating an admin with a later or no expiry now counts as
    widening (needs the gesture); a rewrite that reduces authority revokes
    the subject's sessions; the audit row names the actual actor rather
    than the entry's original creator, and an update is audited as
    AclUpdated.



### Fixed

- **vtc-service**: A community backup travels only over DIDComm or TSP ([#1755](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1755))

* fix(vtc-service)!: a community backup travels only over DIDComm or TSP

  The backup request carries its password, and the backup carries the
  community's signing key bundle. Over REST both exist in plaintext wherever
  TLS terminates.

  - POST /v1/backup/export and /v1/backup/import always answer 403.
  - vtc/backup/export and backup/initiate-export, initiate-import and
    finalize-import are refused on the REST binding, after the super-admin
    check and before any state is serialized, a slot is opened or the
    password is used. The chunks are ciphertext and are unaffected.
  - The export audit row is still written before the envelope is returned,
    and a VTC with no audit trail now refuses to export instead of releasing
    the backup unrecorded.
  - vtc-client export_backup and import_backup use the backup/* chunked
    transfer over a DIDComm or TSP session, verifying every chunk and the
    whole, and refuse without a session.
  - cnm backup connects to the VTC over TSP, or DIDComm when the VTC
    advertises no TSP, and has no REST fallback.

  Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#646.

body:
### Added

- **attestation**: The TEE attestation reads are public Trust Tasks, over any transport ([#1776](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1776))

* feat(attestation)!: the TEE attestation reads are public Trust Tasks, over any transport

  A TEE VTA answered three attestation reads only as unauthenticated REST routes
  (`GET /attestation/status`, `GET`/`POST /attestation/report`,
  `POST /attestation/config-report`), plus a bare DIDComm protocol arm that
  nothing sent to. Under the rule that every remote API is a spec-first,
  spine-dispatched Trust Task reachable over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS, they are now
  `vta/attestation/{status,report,config-report}/0.1` (trustoverip/
  dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#654, trust-tasks-rs 0.23.2), dispatched on the spine.

  Public tasks
  - `vta_sdk::trust_tasks::PUBLIC_URIS` names the tasks a caller may send with no
    identity: no session, no ACL entry, no request proof. A verifier asks before
    it trusts the VTA; the nonce bound into the evidence is what makes a report
    its own, and every response is the VTA's signed operational document.
  - HTTPS: `/trust-tasks` takes an optional credential. An anonymous caller may
    send only a public task (anything else is 401), capped at 64 KB, and those
    requests are charged to the unauthenticated limiter — which charges only
    requests presenting no credential, decided by the extractor's own rule
    (`vti_common::auth::extractor::presents_credential`), so a junk header cannot
    move a request between the two classes.
  - DIDComm/TSP: a sender the ACL does not know gets a zero-authority claim for a
    public task, and `bind_document_to_sender` accepts it unsigned — the spec
    makes the request proof OPTIONAL and HTTPS accepts it unsigned, so refusing it
    here would make the requirement depend on the transport (VTI-OPS-021). An
    attached proof is still verified and bound.
  - A census (`every_public_task_is_proof_optional_and_read_only`) fails if a task
    whose spec requires a proof, or whose dispatch class changes state, discloses
    a secret or acts as its subject, is ever added to `PUBLIC_URIS`.

  Behaviour
  - `report` and `config-report` require a 32-byte verifier nonce; the cached,
    nonce-less report is not carried over — evidence nobody asked for is evidence
    anybody can replay.
  - Failures carry the specs' declared codes: `notAttested` (no provider),
    `noConfigSnapshot` (only the enclave front-end captures one),
    `evidenceUnavailable` (the platform refused a quote).
  - The VTA still requires `issuedAt` on every document (bounding its replay
    record), stricter than the spec; the deploy README examples send it.

  Removed (breaking)

    attestation/*` arms, with their SDK constants; `TASK_ATTESTATION_{STATUS,
    REPORT}_1_0` become `TASK_ATTESTATION_{STATUS,REPORT,CONFIG_REPORT}_0_1` and
    leave `REST_ROUTED_URIS`.
  - The `TeeAttestation` DID-document service, which pointed at the REST route
    (user decision: removed, not re-pointed). `tee.embed_in_did` and
    `VTA_TEE_EMBED_IN_DID` are **refused** at config load as retired, naming the
    replacement, rather than silently ignored. The shipped Nitro configs drop the
    key; the deploy scripts' health hints point at `/health`.

- **vtc**: Step-up passkeys a member enrols through an admin's invite ([#1756](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1756))

* feat(vtc/git-ns): separation of duties and break-glass for elevated git rights

  Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#641.

  - Fixed rule 7: no elevated self-grant (git.ns.admin, git.repo.create,
    git.repo.own) through grant 0.1/0.3, drift adopt, repo/adopt or reseat;
    refused git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed, naming cnm git break-glass.
  - git-ns/right/break-glass/0.1: grant authority, or a community admin on a
    headless namespace; always an operation-bound passkey step-up
    (acl::bound_step_up, whose spent mark now yields its evidence); mandatory
    justification; immediate, no expiry; flagged breakGlass on the record.
  - git-ns/right/ratify/0.1 and revoke 0.3: another administrator ratifies,
    bound to breakGlass.at; any community admin may revoke an unratified one,
    which policy cannot refuse. Unratified records do not count toward the
    last-owner and last-admin invariants.
  - Visibility no policy can turn off: AuditEvent::GitNsBreakGlass at
    AuditSeverity::Critical with the step-up evidence, activity items, a signed
    git-ns/right/break-glass-notice/0.1 to every community admin and ns admin,
