title: feat(vta)!: health, restore status, session revoke and the wrapping key are Trust Tasks
body:
**Stacked on #1776.** This branch carries a rebased copy of #1776's attestation commit (`a80844f9`) underneath its own, because `vta/health/details/0.1` is a public task and needs #1776's `PUBLIC_URIS` / anonymous-dispatch machinery. Once #1776 merges and this is rebased onto main, that commit drops out. Review only the top commit: `feat(vta)!: health, restore status, session revoke and the wrapping key are Trust Tasks`.

Four REST routes become spine-dispatched, signed Trust Tasks, reachable over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS (`/trust-tasks`). The routes are removed, not deprecated. `trust-tasks-rs` floor: **0.23.6**.

## What each task replaces

| Task | Replaces | Who may call | Proof |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vta/health/details/0.1` | `GET /health/details` | anyone (public, in `PUBLIC_URIS`) | request optional; response signed |
| `vta/restore/status/0.1` | the version and `restored` parts of `GET /health/details` | administrators of the VTA | request required; response signed |
| `auth/revoke-session/0.2` | `GET /auth/sessions`, `DELETE /auth/sessions/{id}`, `DELETE /auth/sessions?did=` (the self-listing already exists as `auth/sessions/list/0.1`) | subject itself, or anyone who could remove the subject's ACL entry (VTI-SES-043, VTI-ACL-050) | required both ways |
| `keys/import-wrapping-key/0.1` | `GET /keys/import/wrapping-key` | admin (same authority as `keys/import`) | response required |

## Behaviour changes (breaking)

- **Health details are public now, but show less.** Anyone gets the same fixed flags: status, mediatorUrl/mediatorDid, teeStatus, sealed, storageEncrypted, tspEnabled.
  - teeStatus matches what `vta/attestation/status` reports. `sev_snp` is spelled `sev-snp`, and the field is absent when there is no attestation provider.
  - The software version and the restore record are never in this answer.
- **Version and restore record moved to an admin-only task.** `vta/restore/status/0.1` returns `version`, `restored` and the VTI-VTA-051 `restore` record (read from `keys ▸ restore:provenance`).
  - Any admin qualifies, scoped or not. The check reads the ACL at request time, not the token's role.
  - Anyone else gets `permissionDenied` before any restore state is read.
  - The SDK treats a reply where `restored` and `restore` disagree as malformed.
  - `pnm health` has a new **Deployment** section that shows both tasks' answers, so operators still see the restore record.
- **Session REST routes removed.** `auth/revoke-session/0.2`:
  - Adds the `subject` form and implements `all: true` (0.1 refused it).
  - Authority reuses `may_manage_subject`, the same check `acl/revoke` applies. A subject outside the caller's authority gets `permissionDenied`, decided before its sessions are read and identical whether or not the subject exists.
  - A named session outside the caller's authority returns `revokedCount: 0`, the answer the spec recommends.
  - The payload is schema-validated, then the one-form rule is enforced in the handler on the validated JSON. It does not rely on the generated type (from trust-tasks-rs 0.24 that type is a struct of optionals). Two forms, no form, or `all: false` → `malformedRequest`.
  - Every revocation and refusal is audited with both the caller and the subject.
  - **Not replaced:** listing *other* subjects' sessions. `auth/sessions/list/0.1` only lists the caller's own sessions, and no published task lists anyone else's.
- **Revoke-session 0.1 is no longer served.** The repo's standing rule is to delete rather than deprecate, and every 0.1 payload is a valid 0.2 payload.
  - `vta-mobile-core`'s builders now send 0.2.
  - The hand-written `RevokeSessionRequest` / `RevokeSessionResponse` are deleted in favour of the generated types.
- **The wrapping key is now an Ed25519 `did:key`** (with `keyId` and `expiresAt`), where it used to be an unsigned X25519 JWK.
  - The VTA keeps only the derived X25519 half: in memory, single-use, 60 s.
  - `VtaClient::get_wrapping_key` returns the generated response. It always verifies the reply's proof: a client with no identity is refused, and `trusting_unsigned_replies` does not apply to this task.
  - `pnm keys import` (the REST sealed arm from #1784) seals to the X25519 key derived from the did:key.
  - A sealed import over HTTPS now works end to end through the task. The cleartext carrier is still refused over HTTPS.
- **`check_auth` (REST) now asks `auth/whoami/0.1`.** Health details are public, so they can no longer tell a live token from none.
- **Also removed:** the unused legacy DIDComm constants `key-management/1.0/get-wrapping-key`.

## Other changes

- New SDK methods: `health_details`, `restore_status`, `list_my_sessions`, `revoke_sessions(RevokeSessions::{Session, AllMine, Subject}, reason)`.
- `vta_sdk::retry_safety` classifies the new tasks: health and restore are `ReadOnly`; revoke-session 0.2 and the wrapping key are `RetrySafe`.
- Conformance witnesses added for all four tasks.
- `vta-mcp` guard now classifies `details` and `keys/import-wrapping-key` as `ReadOnly`.
- The auth demo's session panel now sends `auth/sessions/list/0.1` and `auth/revoke-session/0.2` through its trust-task POST path.
- Docs updated: root `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/01-concepts/architecture.md`, `docs/02-vta/{backup-restore,tsp,didcomm-protocol}.md`, design notes, `vta-service/README.md`.
- Knock-ons from the bump, in `vtc-service` tests:
  - 0.23.6 publishes `auth/passkey/admin-list/0.1`, so its unpublished-canonical entry drops to zero and the spine proof census rises to 52. The hand-written `passkey_admin_list_v0_1` module is **not** migrated to the generated type here.
  - The `spec/vta/` unpublished count drops from 6 to 4, for the attestation 1.0 URIs #1776 retires. That test fails on #1776 alone.
- The VTA OpenAPI path floor drops to 50 (54 paths remain).

## Tests

Each new path has tests named by task across **TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS**: `tests/e2e/tests/health_restore_sessions_wrapping_tasks.rs`, using `MockVta::start_with_transports` with a real test mediator.
- `vta_health_details_0_1_over_tsp_didcomm_and_https`: anonymous callers, including DIDComm and TSP senders the ACL doesn't know.
- `vta_restore_status_0_1_over_tsp_didcomm_and_https`: an admin is answered, a reader is refused.
- `auth_revoke_session_0_2_over_tsp_didcomm_and_https`
- `keys_import_wrapping_key_0_1_over_tsp_didcomm_and_https`: seals to the did:key and imports over each transport.

Also:
- The ported REST test `context_admin_reaches_only_sessions_it_may_manage`, now on `auth/sessions/list/0.1` + `auth/revoke-session/0.2` with documents signed as several DIDs.
- Refusal-identity, two-forms/no-form, super-admin, self and 0.1-not-served tests.
- Handler unit tests.
- Anonymous-HTTPS and route-gone tests in `api_integration`.

## Local runs (at `f35f4c92`, on `origin/main` `43679076`)

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The three reduced-feature `vta-service` clippy runs (`rest`; `setup,keyring,rest,tsp,cli-synthesis`; `setup,keyring,rest,didcomm,cli-synthesis`): clean. `--features tee` also clean.
- `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: **5088 passed, 0 failed, 52 ignored** (132 test binaries).
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`:
  - Full run: 2362 passed, 1 failed, 3 ignored. The failure was `trust_task_manifest::every_bound_canonical_task_exists_in_the_registry`, the bump knock-on described above.
  - After that fix, `trust_task_manifest` passes 8/8. The full VTC suite was not re-run after that one-line change.

No pre-existing failures reproduced on this base: the `acl/revoke` census and the backup-wording failures are gone from main since #1782 and #1785.

title: fix(vault): sign-trust-task picks the proof purpose from the document type
body:
## What

`vault/sign-trust-task` signed every document a page or wallet asked for with `proofPurpose: assertionMethod`. It now takes the purpose from the envelope's `type` alone:

- **`assertionMethod`** only for request documents of the registry's attestation types. These are the specs that say their documents are the issuer's attestation or decision:
  - `auth/step-up/approve-response`
  - `task-consent/decision`
  - `confirm/response`
- **`authentication`** for every other document, which is operational. That includes:
  - the `#response` variant of those slugs (the executor's reply);
  - the same slug under a private registry authority.

The requester has no say. The spec gives it no field to choose, and a pre-filled `proof` is refused by the schema. A `type` that is not a Type URI is refused as `envelopeInvalid`, since nothing else could decide the purpose.

The rule is `vta_sdk::trust_task_proof::purpose_for_document_type`, with the slug list in `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`, so other signers can use the same rule. It is re-exported from `vti_common::auth`. The audit log line now records the purpose.

## Why

VTI-KEY-022/106: an operational document is signed for `authentication`, and `assertionMethod` is only for attestations and approver decisions. The DID hosting control plane has enforced this since affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#218, so every task a proxy-login wallet session had the VTA sign was refused. The plugin's holder path was fixed in OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#280; this is the VTA half it deferred.

## Spec

`vault/sign-trust-task` 0.1/0.2 said the proof MUST be `assertionMethod`, which contradicts the framework rule from trust-tasks #637. trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#667 amends both versions in place (draft; wire unchanged) to say the purpose follows the type, and is never chosen by the consumer.

## Tests

- `vta-service/tests/vault_sign_trust_task_purpose.rs` (new, over `/api/trust-tasks` with a real key in the entry's context):
  - operational types (`acl/grant`, `did/list`, `approve-request`, a `#response`, a private-registry reuse) are signed for `authentication`;
  - `approve-response`, `task-consent/decision` and `confirm/response` are signed for `assertionMethod`;
  - each proof verifies over the envelope under the principal's key, every other member is unchanged, and relabelling the purpose breaks verification;
  - refusals: a `type` that is not a Type URI (`envelopeInvalid`, or `malformedRequest` from the schema gate for a non-string) and a requester-supplied proof. Neither returns a signed envelope.
- `vta-sdk` `trust_task_proof::purpose` unit tests for the classifier.

## Local results

- `cargo test -p vta-service --test vault_sign_trust_task_purpose --test vault_trust_task`: pass (4, 16)
- `cargo test -p vta-service --features transport-harness --test vault_release_didcomm`: pass
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib`: 1351 pass, 1 fail. The failure is `routes::cors_tests::openapi_spec_covers_the_route_groups` (documented surface >= 60 paths), which fails on main since #1782 and does not touch this change.
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --all-features --lib trust_task_proof::purpose`: pass
- vta-sdk and vtc-service census tests: pass
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: pass

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — none added
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — n/a, signing only
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire type change
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — an unparseable type is refused, an unknown one gets authentication
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — no mutation
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```

body:
## Summary

### cnm-cli
- New shared connect helper `vtc::connect_for_tasks(keyring, target, TransportChoice)`. It and `connect_end_to_end` (used by `cnm backup`) now share one implementation (`connect_with`), so there is no per-command transport logic.
- The global `--transport auto|tsp|didcomm|rest` flag now applies to `cnm git`. `tsp` and `didcomm` pin a transport and fail instead of falling back. `auto` warns before each fallback.
- `git::run` opens one connection per command and passes it to every signed command. It calls `VtcClient::shutdown` on every exit path.
- Commands changed: `namespace bind|unbind`, `grant`, `revoke`, `create`, `transfer`, `archive`, `adopt`, `view`, `break-glass`, `ratify`, `link` (including `--list` and `--status`), `unlink`, `drift resolve`, `reproject`, `reseat`.
- Not changed: `namespace list`, `repos`, `view --admin` and `break-glass-list`. These are console projections that no `git-ns/*` specification defines, so there is no Trust Task to send. They stay admin-session reads over HTTPS. Moving them needs spec'd tasks first.

### vtc-client
- The `git-ns/*` calls (`git_ns_task` and every wrapper, plus `git_ns_send_signed`) go over the session when the client holds one.
- A document is signed and bound to its sender the same way on every transport. Over a session the VTC accepts a document only when its proof, its `issuer` and the envelope sender are the same DID (VTI-OPS-021/093). The client therefore refuses a `HolderKey` for any other DID before sending anything (`VtcError::Signing`).
- `git_ns_send_signed` over a session sends the signed document's payload in the document the session signs. The client first checks that the issuer is the session's DID and the recipient is the community. Step-up marks are bound to the payload digest, so the retry is the same operation.
- New `VtcError::Refused { document }` holds a session refusal's `trust-task-error` document. `task_error` and `step_up_request` read the code and `details.stepUpRequest` from it the same way they read `Http`'s body over HTTPS.

### vta-sdk
- New `VtaClient::dispatch_trust_task_document`: it returns the whole reply document, including refusals, instead of the extracted payload. `dispatch_trust_task` now wraps it, and its behaviour does not change. `#response` documents are verified as before.

## Tests
- `vtc-service/tests/git_ns_vtc_client.rs` (`--features didcomm-harness`) runs the vtc-client git-ns calls against the VTC test harness. Each test does bind → view → refused re-bind (checks the `alreadyBound` code comes back) → unbind sent as a pre-signed document:
  - `git_ns_tasks_answer_over_tsp`
  - `git_ns_tasks_answer_over_didcomm`
  - `git_ns_tasks_answer_over_https`
  - The two session tests also check that a key for a different DID is refused before anything is sent.
- vtc-client unit test: a refusal reads the same over a session and over HTTPS.
- Local runs:
  - cnm-cli tests: 86 passed.
  - vtc-client `--all-features`: 33 passed.
  - vta-sdk `client::`: 160 passed.
  - vtc-service harness (`git_ns_vtc_client`, `backup_didcomm`, `backup`, `acl_trust_tasks`, `vtc_client_live`, `join_tsp`, `join_didcomm`): all passed.
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

## Coordination
#1756 adds `cnm git enrol-step-up-passkey` and step-up answer commands. Once it merges, those commands take the same path with no extra work: they run through `run_task` on the client that `connect_for_tasks` opens.

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.3.8`) | `0.3.7` → `0.3.8` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.3.7` → `0.3.8` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: spec(vault/sign-trust-task): the proof purpose follows the document type
body:
## What

`vault/sign-trust-task` 0.1 and 0.2 said the maintainer's proof MUST be `proofPurpose: assertionMethod`, whatever it signed. Both now say:

- the maintainer decides the purpose from the envelope's `type` alone;
- `assertionMethod` only when `type` is a `https://trusttasks.org` request (bare or `#request`) of one of a closed list of attestation specifications, `auth/step-up/approve-response`, `task-consent/decision` and `confirm/response`, at any version, compared exactly;
- `#response` variants of those types and a private registry's reuse of their slugs are `authentication`;
- `authentication` for every other document, which is operational;
- the consumer does not choose it, and an operational document MUST NOT be signed for `assertionMethod`;
- `type` must parse as a Type URI (`envelopeInvalid` otherwise), because it decides the purpose.

The response example now shows `authentication`, since it signs an `acl/grant`. The schema's `signedEnvelope` description says the same. A Security & Privacy paragraph explains why the choice is not the consumer's.

## Why

The framework rule from #637 is that a Trust Task document's proof shows the issuer's controller produced it (`authentication`), and that `assertionMethod` is for documents a spec defines as attestations. This spec contradicted that rule. Relying parties that enforce it, such as the DID hosting control plane since affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#218, refused every operational task a wallet session had the VTA sign. The VTA side is OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1788.

## Compatibility

This is an in-place edit to a `draft` spec. The wire shape is unchanged. The generated bindings change only in the embedded schema description. All deployments are test instances.

## Checks

- `npm run validate`: pass
- all four bindings regenerated
- `npm run check-bindings`: pass (591 specs, all agree)

title: fix(signing): bind a page's origin to the relying party it can have documents signed for
body:
Stacked on #280 (`feat/step-up-trust-tasks`), which is not merged yet. This PR targets that branch. Retarget it to `main` once #280 merges.

## The gap

`signTrustTask` (restricted by #280's `pageSignRefusal`) required a `recipient` but accepted any one. `stepUpVta` took its `baseUrl` and `rpDid` from the page. So a page the user had approved could get a signature addressed to a **different** relying party, or steer a step-up approval at one.

## The fix

This reuses login's origin -> RP DID pin (`origin-pin.ts`, M5) rather than adding a second mechanism.

- **`signTrustTask`** refuses, before any prompt, a document whose `recipient` is not the RP DID pinned for the browser-attested origin (`pageSignBindingRefusal`).
- **`stepUpVta`** refuses, before anything is sent or prompted, an `rpDid` or `baseUrl` other than the pinned ones (`pageStepUpBindingRefusal`). The REST `login()` now pins its normalized `baseUrl` beside the RP DID. The mid-flow step-up prompt checks the pin again and denies if it changed underneath the flow.
- **No pin means refusal**, with a reason that says to sign in from the site first. Neither path ever pins. As with login, a pin is seeded only by a sign-in the human approved. `proxyLogin` with a target DID now follows the same rule (a changed target gets the loud prompt, and an approval pins), so `signTrustTask({ asDid })` after `proxyLogin` keeps working.
- **Exact-origin lookup.** A subdomain, a lookalike, or the same host on another scheme or port is a different origin and has no pin.
- **A changed base URL at login** gets the same loud, never-short-circuited prompt as a changed RP DID, because the pinned base URL is where step-up may go.
- **Prompts** for signing and step-up show a "Pinned relying party" card: `origin <-> rpDid` (and `via <baseUrl>` for step-up).

A `loginDidcomm()` names no base URL. It keeps a base URL already pinned for the same RP DID and drops it for a different one. A site that signed in only over DIDComm therefore can't use `stepUpVta` (which is HTTPS to `{baseUrl}/trust-tasks`) until it signs in with `login()`. The refusal says so.

Nothing is deployed, so pins stored before this change carry no base URL. Step-up from such an origin is refused until the site signs in again. There is no migration.

## Tests

`packages/extension/tests/page-rp-binding.test.mts` covers:
- a mismatched recipient, which is refused and the reason names both DIDs
- a mismatched RP DID for step-up
- a mismatched base URL for step-up: another host, another path, a pinned host used as a label prefix, http, credentials, a query, and unparsable input
- an unpinned origin, for both signing and step-up, and a check that asking doesn't pin it
- subdomain, lookalike, scheme and port origins
- a pin seeded without a base URL
- the happy path, including an equivalent base URL spelling
- login's base-URL change detection and how pins are kept or dropped across login kinds

## Local results

- `npm run lint` (all workspaces): pass
- `npm test` (all workspaces): 1692 tests pass, 0 fail

title: feat(step-up): step up at a did-hosting relying party as Trust Tasks
body:
Plan step 3 (plugin half) of the webvh-service Trust Tasks plan (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#661). The did-hosting control plane serves `auth/step-up/start/0.1`, `approve-response/0.5` and `auth/refresh/0.1` over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS since affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#218 (merged). The console half, which calls `vtaWallet.stepUpVta` with the parameters below, is affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#219.

## Step-up as Trust Tasks (`packages/core/src/rp-login/step-up.ts`)

- **`stepUpVtaStart`** sends a wallet-signed `auth/step-up/start/0.1` (`issuer` the holder, `recipient` the RP, `payload.sessionId`, `proofPurpose: authentication`) to `{base}/trust-tasks`.
  - The reply must be signed by the RP, of the start response type, threaded to the request and addressed back to the holder.
  - It then verifies the embedded `approve-request/0.3` and refuses one that is signed by anyone but the RP, addressed to someone else, names another subject, or is bound to another session.
- **`stepUpVtaFinish`** sends the signed `approve-response/0.5` as a Trust Task.
  - It requires a signed `elevated` acknowledgement.
  - It then sends `auth/refresh/0.1` and returns the new tokens, keeping the presented refresh token when the RP does not rotate it.
- `performStepUpVta` keeps its order: start → verify → consent → sign → finish. A refused start never reaches the human.
- **Gone:** the `/auth/step-up/vta/{start,finish}` paths, the legacy top-level start fields and their cross-check, and the snake_case finish parsing.
- The reply checks reuse `decodeTrustTaskHttpReply`: body-first error parsing (R3.7), the proof, and the signer binding. It gains an optional `inReplyTo` (thread plus recipient), which only this caller passes.

## Verification helpers (`packages/core/src/vta/step-up.ts`)

- `verifyStepUpApproveRequest(doc, { acceptTypes, … })` takes the document directly. `acceptTypes` is required and says which party's versions are acceptable:
  - `RP_APPROVE_REQUEST_TYPES` (0.3, the control plane);
  - `AGENT_APPROVE_REQUEST_TYPES` (0.2 and 0.1, the agent's disclosure and push flows, used by `persona/`).
- Expiry is read from the document's `expiresAt` as well as the payload's.
- `buildStepUpApproval` mints 0.3 (the agent) or 0.5 (the control plane). 0.2 had no remaining sender and is gone. It now sets `issuedAt`, which 0.5 requires.

## Two proof-purpose fixes found on the way

- **Approve-requests are verified as `proofPurpose: authentication`, not `assertionMethod`.** A request is its issuer's operational message; both the control plane (`signing.rs`) and the agent (`step_up.rs`) sign it that way. The old check could only pass against the test fixtures, which signed with `assertionMethod`. The persona fixture now signs as the agent does.
- **Documents a page asks the wallet to sign (`vtaWallet.signTrustTask`, holder path) are signed for `authentication`.** They are the holder's own requests to the RP. Since affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#213/#218, the control plane refuses an `assertionMethod` proof on operational tasks, so every wallet-signed console call was being refused. The proxy path (`vault/sign-trust-task`) is signed by the VTA and is not changed here; see Deferred.

## Page API (`packages/extension`)

- `stepUpVta({ baseUrl, rpDid, accessToken, refreshToken, sessionId })`. `vtaDid` and `vtaMediatorDid` are gone.
- The holder that signs is the active connection's. The background reads it and passes it to the offscreen document, so the page no longer names it.
- The demo page's step-up panel follows.

## Tests

- `tests/rp-login.step-up.mjs`, rewritten against a fake RP that signs like the control plane (22 tests):
  - Start: the document's shape and proof, then refusals for an unsigned reply, a reply signed by someone else, a reply threaded to another request, a reply addressed to someone else, an approve-request for another session, one naming another subject, and one signed by another enrolled executor. A refusal keeps the RP's code.
  - Finish: approve-response then a signed refresh; a refresh that does not rotate; a non-`elevated` acknowledgement is refused without refreshing; an unsigned acknowledgement is refused.
  - `verifyStepUpApproveRequest` refusals: unenrolled signer, unsigned, another party's version, lapsed, `assertionMethod`-signed, tampered reason.
  - `performStepUpVta` order, decline and refusal.
- `persona.step-up.mjs` follows the fixture and version changes. `task-surface.mjs` records `auth/step-up/start/` and `approve-response/0.5` as served by the RP, not the agent.
- `npm run lint`: pass. `npm test`: pass (all workspaces).
- `@openvtc/trust-tasks` ^0.20.1 → ^0.21.7, for the start, approve-request 0.3 and approve-response 0.5 bindings.

## Deferred

- The proxy-login path's `vault/sign-trust-task/0.1` is signed by the VTA with `assertionMethod`. Wallet sessions logged in by proxy will be refused by the control plane on operational tasks until the VTA signs those for `authentication`. That is a VTI change.
- Step-up signs as the holder. A session logged in as a per-site persona can't step up through this path yet.
- The same documents can go over TSP or DIDComm through a `TrustTaskSender` once the page API carries the RP's endpoint; for now they go over HTTPS only.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — withFetchTimeout
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — nothing is stored; the caller stores the tokens returned
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retries
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — generated types; the console (affinidi-webvh-service#219) is the page caller
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — the RP consumes the challenge; a lost finish means stepping up again
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```

title: feat(webvh)!: reach the DID hosting service with Trust Tasks only
body:
## What

Stage 2b of the webvh-service Trust Tasks plan (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#661). The VTA reaches a DID hosting service only through Trust Tasks. Its REST client is removed.

### One client: `vta-service/src/webvh_host.rs`

- **Replaces three pieces:** `webvh_didcomm.rs`, `vta-webvh`'s `webvh_client.rs` and `webvh_auth.rs`, and the `WebvhTransport { Rest, TrustTask }` enum.
- **Generated types:** every call uses the request and response types `trust-tasks-rs` generates for `did-management/*`: `did/check-name`, `did/register`, `did/delete`, `did/list`, `agent-name/{update,remove,list,check}` and `me/domains`.
  - Requests are built from the generated `Payload`, so an undeclared member cannot be sent. The old `didLog` alias on `agent-name/*` is gone in favour of the spec's `didData`.
  - Replies parse into the generated `Response`, which refuses unknown members.
- **Transport:** the seam (`operations::outbound`) chooses, in the order TSP > DIDComm > HTTPS `POST {base}/trust-tasks`.
  - The hosting service advertises TSP, DIDComm and `WebVHHosting`, not `TrustTaskHTTPS`. It serves its HTTPS binding at `{WebVHHosting origin}/api/trust-tasks` (affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#217, #218).
  - `Outbound::with_https_base` fills that slot only when the peer advertises no HTTPS Trust-Task endpoint of its own.
  - The origin must be `https://`. Plain `http://` is accepted only to a loopback host, which is the rule the REST client had.
- **Replies:** each one must pass four checks, on every transport:
  - it carries the host's proof (`ReplyTrust::SignedByRecipient`, where it was `TransportAuthenticated`);
  - it threads to this request;
  - it is addressed to this VTA;
  - it has the response type that was asked for.
- **Errors:** refusals are read from `trust-task-error` documents. The spec code's local part maps to a status (`notFound` 404, `notOwner`/`permissionDenied` 403, `pathTaken`/`nameTaken` 409, `invalid*`/`unknownDomain` 400, anything else 502). `did/problem-report` is no longer read.

### Operations that were REST-only

- **`vta/webvh/servers/domains`** reads `me/domains`. Over the seam it used to answer an empty list.
- **`vta/webvh/servers/reconcile`** and **`retire-orphan`** now work over Trust Tasks, where they used to refuse. They read the paged `did/list` `{records, total}`:
  - pages of up to 1000, bounded at 100 pages;
  - a listing whose pages stop short of, or overrun, `total` is refused rather than reported. A short read would name live DIDs as orphans.

### Removed, with no compatibility layer (test deployments)

- The REST client and its DID-auth handshake.
- The `server-auth:{id}` token cache (`WebvhServerAuthRecord`).
- `WebvhAuthLocks`, and its plumbing through `AppState`, `VtaState`, `WebvhDeps`, `CreateDidWebvhDeps`, `ServiceOpDeps`, `ProvisionIntegrationDeps`, the offline CLIs and the e2e fixture. There is no token left to serialise.
- The `WebVHHostingService` legacy alias.
- `vta-webvh` is now the store only. It drops `affinidi-tdk`, `reqwest`, `url`, `zeroize`, `chrono`, `tracing` and `wiremock`.

## Not needed

- **trust-tasks-rs 0.24.** Every `did-management` type used here is in 0.23.3, the current floor, so there is no bump. The `auth/revoke-session/0.2` / invite-update permissive-type note does not apply.

## Tests

- **`webvh_host` unit tests.**
  - Building requests: payloads come from the generated types, undeclared members are refused before signing, and auto-assign omits `path`.
  - Reading replies:
    - the error-code mapping table;
    - refusals for a reply to another request, one addressed elsewhere, one of another type, and an undeclared member;
    - a `did/problem-report` is not an answer;
    - `did/list` is read as `{records, total}`, with `{dids}` refused;
    - paging reaches `total`, and a short or overlong listing is refused.
  - The VTA's proof: the document is signed for `authentication`, and a bridge with no signer signs nothing.
- **`transport` unit tests.**
  - Reachability, and the `{origin}/api` base.
  - A plaintext origin off loopback is refused; loopback `http://` is allowed.
  - The retired alias no longer counts.
- **`StubWebvhHost` rewritten as a Trust-Task host.** It serves `POST /api/trust-tasks`. It refuses unsigned requests and requests not signed for `authentication`. It checks each payload against the generated type, and signs every answer with a key listed in its seeded DID document. So every `mock_vta` webvh test now covers both halves of the proof exchange over HTTPS.
- **New `mock_vta` refusal test:** `create_did_webvh_refuses_a_host_answer_not_signed_by_the_host`. The stub signs with a foreign key under its own method id, and the reservation is refused with nothing stored.
- **`mock_vta` assertions strengthened:**
  - `servers/domains` returns the host's domains;
  - `reconcile` reports the host-only slot and the agent-only DID;
  - `agent-name/list` relays RFC 3339 `createdAt` as Unix seconds.

## Local results

- `cargo test -p vta-service --no-fail-fast --tests --bins`: 1772 pass, 1 fail. The failure is `routes::cors_tests::openapi_spec_covers_the_route_groups` (documented surface >= 60 paths), which fails on main since #1782.
- `cargo test -p vta-service --features transport-harness transport_harness_tests`: pass (9)
- `cargo test -p vta-service --test mock_vta`: pass (21, including the new refusal test)
- `cargo test -p vta-webvh`: pass
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --all-features`: pass (1193, including the census tests)
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --test openapi_response_census`: pass
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: pass
- The CI feature combos for `vta-service` pass: `tee,rest,didcomm`; `rest,didcomm`; `rest` (clippy); `setup,keyring,rest,tsp,cli-synthesis` (clippy); `aws-secrets,keyring,rest`; `setup,keyring,rest,didcomm,cli-synthesis` (clippy). The `vta-enclave` `rest,didcomm,vsock-store[,tenant-overlay]` checks also pass.

## Deferred

- **webvh-service should advertise `TrustTaskHTTPS`** (base `{origin}/api`). The seam would then find the HTTPS binding from the DID document, and the `WebVHHosting` fallback could go.
- **`vta-keyspaces` still marks `server-auth:` as environment-bound.** No such row is written any more. It is left because `vta-backup`'s export test asserts on it, and #1783 is editing that file.
- **`pnm-cli/src/cli.rs` help text** still mentions `WebVHHostingService` and `/api/me/domains`. #1783 edits that file, so it is left for after that merges.
- **A signer DID change at runtime.** The bridge signer is installed at startup. A VTA whose own DID changes while it runs (only a test does this today) signs with the old key until it restarts, and the host client refuses to send rather than sign as the wrong identity. `TestAppContext::adopt_vta_did` does what the restart would.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — the seam's rest_client (timeouts, same-origin redirects); the REST client is removed
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — the per-server auth mutex held across daemon calls is removed with the token cache
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — unchanged publish/reconcile ordering
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — the REST 401-retry is gone; no new retry
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — retire-orphan deletes only after a complete listing
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — generated did-management types both ways
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no reachable transport, a plaintext origin or an unsigned reply is a refusal
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — domains no longer answers an empty list for "not asked"
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```

feat(webvh)!: reach the DID hosting service with Trust Tasks only (#1789)

* feat(webvh)!: reach the DID hosting service with Trust Tasks only

Stage 2b of the webvh-service Trust Tasks plan (trust-tasks #661). The
VTA's REST client to the hosting service and WebvhTransport::Rest are
removed; one client, vta-service/src/webvh_host.rs, makes every call as a
Trust Task typed with the generated did-management bindings, over the
transport the seam picks (TSP > DIDComm > HTTPS POST {base}/trust-tasks).

  service serves its binding; https:// only, or http:// to loopback.
- Every reply must carry the host's proof (SignedByRecipient), thread to
  the request, be addressed to this VTA and have the asked-for type.
  Refusals are read from trust-task-error documents by spec code;
  did/problem-report is no longer read.
- servers/domains reads me/domains; reconcile and retire-orphan read the
  paged did/list {records, total} and now work over Trust Tasks. A listing
  that disagrees with its total is refused.
- The DID-auth handshake, the server-auth token cache, WebvhAuthLocks and
  the WebVHHostingService alias are gone. vta-webvh is the store only.

The test hosting service is now a Trust-Task host that refuses unsigned
requests and signs its answers; a forged answer is refused.

- did/list advances its offset by the records received, so a host that

title: feat(cli)!: make pnm usable from a script
body:
## Why

A script cannot trust what `pnm` reports.

- `--json` accepted and ignored on seven commands. Exit 0, human text. The parse error lands in a later stage, nowhere near the cause.
- `pnm health` printed a cross and exited 0, so a pipeline stayed green over a dead mediator. A profile with no VTA configured also exited 0, having checked nothing.
- `PNM_HOME` accepted and ignored. An operation believed sandboxed ran against the real profile.
- Every error exited 1. A missing name, a bad argument and an expired credential were indistinguishable.
- Colour and a six-line logo went into pipes and logs.
- `acl create --help` pointed at a command that refuses the job.

## What

Terminal gets the table, colour and banner. Anything else gets json. `--json` still forces json on a terminal. `NO_COLOR` honoured.

Exit codes: 1 failed, 2 usage, 3 not found, 4 config, 5 auth. Picked from the SDK's typed error in the one place every command lands, so a call site does not have to know one. Being refused a permission stays 1: the operation ran and failed, which is not the same signal as a bad credential.

`health` derives its exit status from its checks and emits one document per check. A run that checked nothing is not a pass.

`PNM_HOME` moves config, sessions, pending setups and bootstrap secrets together.

## Breaking

Piped output is json. Scripts parsing the human table must read json instead.

Human output at a terminal is byte-identical to before: same banner, colours and tables.

## Not covered

Backup password on stdin, re-point after a VTA rebuild, `--outcome` matching, `--full-display` truncation, and guarding an unreissuable admin credential, which needs provenance nothing persists today.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Follow-up changes

- **`PNM_HOME` isolates the credential store too.** In the platform keyring a session is stored under `("pnm-cli", "vta:<slug>")` in every profile, so moving the files alone did not isolate it. A `PNM_HOME` profile with a slug that matched the real profile's could read, overwrite, or on `vta delete` erase the real credential. The keyring service is now `pnm-cli:<digest of the profile path>`. The profile directory is `$PNM_HOME` itself, created 0700. The rule lives in vta-sdk `agent_connect` (`pnm_profile_dir`, `pnm_service_name`), so `AgentConnect`'s defaults follow `PNM_HOME` as well. The rewrite of `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` inside the running runtime is gone.
- Error paths before dispatch map exit codes through `exit_code_for` as well. A profile with no usable VTA exits `4`.
- `NO_COLOR` and non-terminal output now strip colour from every hand-coloured line. The `render` ANSI constants are a `Display` type gated on the colour setting.

title: fix(auth)!: split a resolver failure from an invalid proof in reply verification (FTL-29595)
body:
## Ugh. Problem.

Reply come back from other VTA. Code check signature good or bad.

Sometimes code no reach key-lookup place (network bad, rate-limit, whatever).
Code say "signature bad" anyway. WRONG. Maybe signature good, code just no
reach lookup place. Caller then retry thing that already work. Bad.

## Fix small (four file, real code)

Code now have two box instead of one:

- Box A: "no reach lookup place, not bad signature, try again."
- Box B: "signature actually bad, for real."

Two box look **same word** at stranger door (auth login, step-up gate, join
request, room presenter, ~12 place total). Stranger no learn anything new.
Safe, no leak.

Two box look **different word** at two "check my own reply" door:
- `vta-sdk` client (pnm side)
- VTA calling out to peer/room, checking reply back

Only those two door say new helpful thing now.

One file (`step_up.rs`) already peek inside old box by hand — had to teach it
about new box too, else no compile, and it the one spot that could've leaked
if done wrong.

## Not-fix (three file, test only)

Other three file (`routes/auth.rs`, `vtc-service/helpers.rs`,
`room-host/lib.rs`) — zero real-code line touch. They already just print
`{e}` as string, so they automatic safe. Added test proving it, that all.

## Test

- Box A and Box B print identical word (the thing that must never break).
- Both new-message door: new word show up for lookup-fail, old word still
  show up for real-bad-signature.
- Four of the twelve stranger door: proof lookup-fail and real-bad-signature
  give byte-identical output.
- Also run whole thing live against real local VTA + PNM + mediator (docker
  harness), broke the lookup on purpose, saw new message, confirmed the
  underlying write still went through server-side. Real repro, not just
  unit test.

All four crate full test suite green (vta-sdk, vta-service, vtc-service,
room-host). Clippy clean. Fmt clean.

## Ug, one warning

`DiProofError` not marked `#[non_exhaustive]`. New box mean any outside code
matching every box by hand need add new arm. Everything inside this repo
already fixed.

No touch `affinidi-data-integrity` public API.


## Follow-up changes

- `ResolverFailed` now means only that the signer's key could not be retrieved: no resolver configured for its method, or its DID did not resolve. The resolver also reports a key not listed under the proof's purpose, a controller mismatch, and a malformed or unsupported method through the same upstream `Resolver` variant. Those are verdicts on the proof, so they stay `VerifyFailed` and no longer read as "the reply may be genuine".
- The VTA's outbound reply check still refuses with 403, not 502. The SDK retries a 5xx under the caller's idempotency key, so a 502 would re-send a request the peer may already have applied.
- Both self-reply messages now say "check its state before sending it again" instead of "retry".

title: fix(auth)!: split a resolver failure from an invalid proof in reply verification (FTL-29595) (#1748)
body:
fix(auth)!: split a resolver failure from an invalid proof in reply verification (FTL-29595) (#1748)

* fix(auth)!: split a resolver failure from an invalid proof in reply verification (FTL-29595)

The distinction already existed two layers down and was thrown away one layer
up. affinidi-data-integrity's DataIntegrityError::Resolver(String) is already
distinct from InvalidSignature, and TrustTaskVmResolver::resolve constructs it
specifically on a DID-cache resolution failure — but
verify_trust_task_proof_with collapsed every DataIntegrityError variant into
one opaque DiProofError::VerifyFailed. A caller verifying a peer's reply
therefore could not tell "I could not retrieve the verification key" (a
retrieval failure — the peer's response may be entirely genuine) from "the
signature does not verify" (an actual bad proof), and reported both as the
same "proof does not verify" — which invites blind retries against a mutation
that already committed.

Adds DiProofError::ResolverFailed(String), rendering byte-identical to
VerifyFailed on the wire ("proof verification failed"): DiProofError's
Display is deliberately opaque because most of its ~15 callers are
unauthenticated inbound routes, where telling a resolver failure apart from a
bad signature is an oracle (whether a DID resolves at all). Every one of
those routes still sees the same string; only the two caller-side sites where
the audience already knows what it asked for now branch on the variant:

- vta-sdk::client's reply-verification (a client checking its own outbound
  reply)
- vta-service::operations::outbound's reply-verification (the VTA acting as
  an outbound caller to a peer/room-host)

Both now report a resolver failure as a retrieval failure with a distinct
message, instead of folding it into "is unsigned or its proof does not
verify".

One exhaustive match over DiProofError existed at vta-service's
trust_tasks::step_up::verify_did_signed_gate — the one inbound call site with
any per-variant branching at all, and so the one actual risk in this change.
Folded the new variant into its existing VerifyFailed arm; no behavior
change, since that gate is did:key-only and the resolver path never runs
there.

Tests: Display/cause() parity and correct classification on DiProofError
directly (the chokepoint every inbound route's opacity rests on); the two new
message pairs (resolver failure vs. an actual bad signature) at both
caller-side sites; and the same pairwise check at four of the twelve inbound
sites chosen for being deterministically testable offline
(trust_tasks::step_up, routes::auth, vtc-service's
trust_tasks::helpers::verify_trust_task_proof, room-host's presenter).

Breaking: DiProofError is not #[non_exhaustive], so an external consumer
matching it exhaustively needs a new arm for ResolverFailed. Every match
inside this workspace already covers it.

No change to affinidi-data-integrity's public API.

Signed-off-by: Marat Shakirov <marat.s@affinidi.com>

* fix(auth): only a key that could not be retrieved is a resolver failure

The resolver reports "not listed under the proof's purpose", controller
mismatches and malformed or unsupported methods through the same upstream
`DataIntegrityError::Resolver` variant it uses for a failed lookup. Mapping
all of them to `ResolverFailed` told a caller that a reply signed with an
unauthorised key "may be genuine". Only "no resolver configured" and "the
DID did not resolve" are retrieval failures now; everything else stays
`VerifyFailed`.

The VTA's outbound reply check keeps refusing with 403 rather than 502. The
SDK retries a 5xx under the caller's idempotency key, which would re-send a
request the peer may already have applied. Both self-reply messages now say
to check the operation's state before sending it again, not to retry.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(attestation)!: the TEE attestation reads are public Trust Tasks, over any transport
body:
A TEE VTA answered three attestation reads only as unauthenticated REST routes
(`GET /attestation/status`, `GET`/`POST /attestation/report`,
`POST /attestation/config-report`), plus a bare DIDComm protocol arm that
nothing sent to. Under the rule that every remote API is a spec-first,
spine-dispatched Trust Task reachable over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS, they are now
`vta/attestation/{status,report,config-report}/0.1` (trustoverip/
dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#654, trust-tasks-rs 0.23.2), dispatched on the spine.

Public tasks
- `vta_sdk::trust_tasks::PUBLIC_URIS` names the tasks a caller may send with no
  identity: no session, no ACL entry, no request proof. A verifier asks before
  it trusts the VTA; the nonce bound into the evidence is what makes a report
  its own, and every response is the VTA's signed operational document.
- HTTPS: `/trust-tasks` takes an optional credential. An anonymous caller may
  send only a public task (anything else is 401), capped at 64 KB, and those
  requests are charged to the unauthenticated limiter — which charges only
  requests presenting no credential, decided by the extractor's own rule
  (`vti_common::auth::extractor::presents_credential`), so a junk header cannot
  move a request between the two classes.
- DIDComm/TSP: a sender the ACL does not know gets a zero-authority claim for a
  public task, and `bind_document_to_sender` accepts it unsigned — the spec
  makes the request proof OPTIONAL and HTTPS accepts it unsigned, so refusing it
  here would make the requirement depend on the transport (VTI-OPS-021). An
  attached proof is still verified and bound.
- A census (`every_public_task_is_proof_optional_and_read_only`) fails if a task
  whose spec requires a proof, or whose dispatch class changes state, discloses
  a secret or acts as its subject, is ever added to `PUBLIC_URIS`.

Behaviour
- `report` and `config-report` require a 32-byte verifier nonce; the cached,
  nonce-less report is not carried over — evidence nobody asked for is evidence
  anybody can replay.
- Failures carry the specs' declared codes: `notAttested` (no provider),
  `noConfigSnapshot` (only the enclave front-end captures one),
  `evidenceUnavailable` (the platform refused a quote).
- The VTA still requires `issuedAt` on every document (bounding its replay
  record), stricter than the spec; the deploy README examples send it.

Removed (breaking)
- The REST routes above and the DIDComm `firstperson.network/vta/1.0/
  attestation/*` arms, with their SDK constants; `TASK_ATTESTATION_{STATUS,
  REPORT}_1_0` become `TASK_ATTESTATION_{STATUS,REPORT,CONFIG_REPORT}_0_1` and
  leave `REST_ROUTED_URIS`.
- The `TeeAttestation` DID-document service, which pointed at the REST route
  (user decision: removed, not re-pointed). `tee.embed_in_did` and
  `VTA_TEE_EMBED_IN_DID` are **refused** at config load as retired, naming the
  replacement, rather than silently ignored. The shipped Nitro configs drop the
  key; the deploy scripts' health hints point at `/health`.

Tests: handler tests through the dispatch core with a simulated TEE (signed
answers to an anonymous caller, nonce binding, declared error codes), the
public-task census, the DIDComm unsigned-public exception, the envelope
carve-out, anonymous `/trust-tasks` rate limiting and the 401 for a non-public
task, conformance witnesses for the three tasks, and the retired config key.

## Release
For the **next** VTI release, not #1768 (user decision).

## Local runs (before the final rebase onto main)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. The three reduced-feature `vta-service` runs: clean. `-p vta-service -p vta-config -p vta-tee --all-features`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast` plus `cargo test -p vta-service --features tee`: 6907 passed, 1 failed. The one failure was `vta-mcp`'s verb census, which didn't know `config-report`; it's fixed and `vta-mcp` passes 37/37.
- After rebasing onto main: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` and `-p vta-service --features tee` are clean. CI checks the rebased tree.

  makes the request proof OPTIONAL and HTTPS accepts it unsigned, so refusing it
  here would make the requirement depend on the transport (VTI-OPS-021). An
  attached proof is still verified and bound.
- A census (`every_public_task_is_proof_optional_and_read_only`) fails if a task
  whose spec requires a proof, or whose dispatch class changes state, discloses
  a secret or acts as its subject, is ever added to `PUBLIC_URIS`.

Behaviour
- `report` and `config-report` require a 32-byte verifier nonce; the cached,
  nonce-less report is not carried over — evidence nobody asked for is evidence
  anybody can replay.
- Failures carry the specs' declared codes: `notAttested` (no provider),
  `noConfigSnapshot` (only the enclave front-end captures one),
  `evidenceUnavailable` (the platform refused a quote).
- The VTA still requires `issuedAt` on every document (bounding its replay
  record), stricter than the spec; the deploy README examples send it.

Removed (breaking)
- The REST routes above and the DIDComm `firstperson.network/vta/1.0/
  attestation/*` arms, with their SDK constants; `TASK_ATTESTATION_{STATUS,
  REPORT}_1_0` become `TASK_ATTESTATION_{STATUS,REPORT,CONFIG_REPORT}_0_1` and
  leave `REST_ROUTED_URIS`.
- The `TeeAttestation` DID-document service, which pointed at the REST route
  (user decision: removed, not re-pointed). `tee.embed_in_did` and
  `VTA_TEE_EMBED_IN_DID` are **refused** at config load as retired, naming the
  replacement, rather than silently ignored. The shipped Nitro configs drop the
  key; the deploy scripts' health hints point at `/health`.

Tests: handler tests through the dispatch core with a simulated TEE (signed
answers to an anonymous caller, nonce binding, declared error codes), the
public-task census, the DIDComm unsigned-public exception, the envelope
carve-out, anonymous `/trust-tasks` rate limiting and the 401 for a non-public
task, conformance witnesses for the three tasks, and the retired config key.

title: feat(sdk)!: remove the last legacy backup and webvh surfaces; realign-keys is a Trust Task
body:
Removes the last deprecated non-Trust-Task backup and webvh surfaces from the SDK, pnm, the VTA and the VTC. It also moves `realign_did_webvh_keys` onto `webvh/dids/realign-keys/1.0`, which the VTA already served, so `realign-keys` now works over TSP and DIDComm as well as HTTPS. VGI cleared this (groups 1 and 2 of the inventory; see the ledger).

## What's removed
- **SDK:**
  - `backup_export` / `backup_import{,_with}` and `update_did_webvh` / `rotate_did_webvh_keys`, all deprecated.
  - Their legacy message constants, plus `ExportRequest` / `ImportRequest`.
- **pnm:** `backup --use-rest-legacy`. It could not succeed on any transport: REST answered 403, and `rpc` refuses DIDComm and TSP.
- **VTA REST:**
  - `/backup/{export,import}`, which only ever answered 403.
  - `/contexts/{ctx}/dids/{scid}/{update,rotate-keys}`.
  - `/webvh/dids/{did}/realign-keys`.
- **VTC REST:** `/v1/backup/{export,import}`, also 403-only.

The backup tasks keep their end-to-end-transport-only policy. Full rationale is in the commit body.

## Tests
- The REST update/rotate behaviour tests are ported to `/trust-tasks`, and new tests hold the removed routes gone.
- The webvh REST-parity consent test is dropped. The Trust Task consent path is covered by the rest of `delegated_consent_e2e`.
- `mock_vta` uses the by-DID update.
- The SDK gains `/trust-tasks` wire tests for rotate-keys and realign-keys.

## Verification (local, CI-equivalent)
- fmt, workspace clippy, and the three reduced `vta-service` clippy feature sets: all clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 5065 passed.

  - Two failures come from outside this PR:
    - `generated_wire_types_census`: already failing on main because of the VTC `acl/revoke` types. Fixed by #1782.
    - `cnm-cli` `printed_words_round_trip_in_sh_bash_zsh_and_fish`: fails under full-workspace load and passes on its own. This PR doesn't touch cnm.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 2352 passed. The one failure (405 vs 404) is fixed; `tests/backup` 9/9.

`VtaClient::rpc` is now called only by the services methods, which #1782 moves to `rpc_tt`. Whichever of the two merges second deletes `rpc` and its refusal helpers.

* feat!: remove the last legacy backup and webvh surfaces; realign-keys is a Trust Task

Every remote API is a spine-dispatched Trust Task over TSP, DIDComm and
HTTPS. What was left off the spine on these two surfaces was deprecated,
and most of it could no longer succeed anywhere. Test deployments carry no
compat, so it is deleted rather than refused.

  `ExportRequest` / `ImportRequest`.

  transport: the VTA answered 403 over REST (VTI-VTA-003), and the SDK's
  `rpc` refuses DIDComm and TSP. Its doc said "works only over DIDComm".
- The VTA's `POST /backup/{export,import}` and the VTC's
  `POST /v1/backup/{export,import}`, which only ever answered 403. A backup
  is the `vta/backup/*` (VTA) or `vtc/backup/export` + `backup/*` (VTC) Trust
  Tasks, over an end-to-end transport only; that policy is unchanged.

webvh
- SDK `update_did_webvh` / `rotate_did_webvh_keys` (the `(context, scid)`
  forms, deprecated since 0.20.32) and their message constants. The by-DID
  `update_did_webvh_by_did` / `rotate_did_webvh_keys_by_did` are the only

  `POST /webvh/dids/{did}/realign-keys`.

  sends the task, so `pnm did-mgmt dids realign-keys` works over TSP and

  document update, rotate, unknown DID, invalid document) are ported to

title: fix(cli): pnm keys import works over DIDComm and TSP
body:
`pnm keys import` always fetched the VTA's wrapping key first. That fetch is a REST route, so on a DIDComm or TSP client the command failed before sending anything. The SDK's `import_key` already sends `keys/import/0.1` on every transport, and the VTA accepts the cleartext multibase carrier over a transport that is confidential end to end.

The CLI now chooses the carrier by the client's Trust Task transport:
- **DIDComm / TSP:** multibase, with no wrapping-key fetch.
- **REST:** sealed to the wrapping key, as before. The VTA still refuses a cleartext key over HTTPS.

Group 4 of the non-Trust-Task inventory, cleared by VGI. A wrapping-key Trust Task for HTTPS needs its own spec (group 6) and is not included here.

**Tests**

- Already on main: the server accepts multibase end to end (`trust_tasks::tests::keys_import_and_derive_and_sign`) and refuses it over REST (`api_integration::keys_import_trust_task_refuses_cleartext_over_rest`), and the SDK DIDComm import is tested in `tests/e2e/tests/client_didcomm.rs`.

title: fix(signing): bind a page's origin to the relying party it can have documents signed for
body:
fix(signing): bind a page's origin to the relying party it can have documents signed for

signTrustTask required a recipient but accepted any, and stepUpVta took
its base URL and RP DID from the page, so a page the user approved could
get a signature addressed to a different relying party, or steer a
step-up approval at one.

Both are now held to login's origin -> RP DID pin (M5). The REST login
pins its base URL beside the RP DID. Before any prompt:

- signTrustTask refuses a recipient other than the RP DID pinned for the
  requesting origin.
- stepUpVta refuses an RP DID or base URL other than the pinned ones, and
  re-checks the pin before its mid-flow prompt.
- An origin with no pin is refused on both. Neither path pins; a pin is
  seeded only by a login the human approved, now including proxyLogin
  with a target DID.

The pin is looked up by exact attested origin, so a subdomain, lookalike,
or other scheme or port has none. A login naming a different base URL is
prompted loudly, like a changed RP DID, even for a remembered site. The
signing and step-up prompts show the pinned origin <-> RP pairing.

title: fix(extension): bound what a page can have the wallet sign
body:
fix(extension): bound what a page can have the wallet sign

Page-requested documents are now signed for authentication, so a
signature a page obtains is the holder's own request at any relying
party that binds proofs to key roles. signTrustTask now refuses, before
any prompt: an envelope with no recipient (an unaddressed signature is
good at every party that accepts the holder key), one addressed to the
holder's own agent (a page drives the agent through requestTask, where
its policy applies), a step-up approve-request or approve-response
(built only by the wallet's own step-up flow), and the families a page
may not request. The prompt now shows the recipient as the relying
party.

Also tests the approve-request refusals the step-up flow checks but did
not test: addressed to someone else, and a lapsed payload expiry.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: feat(step-up): step up at a did-hosting relying party as Trust Tasks
body:
feat(step-up): step up at a did-hosting relying party as Trust Tasks

stepUpVtaStart sends a wallet-signed auth/step-up/start/0.1 to
{base}/trust-tasks and verifies the reply: signed by the RP, of the
start response type, threaded to the request and addressed back to the
holder. It then verifies the approve-request/0.3 inside it, and refuses
one signed by anyone but the RP, addressed to someone else, naming
another subject or bound to another session.

stepUpVtaFinish sends the signed approve-response/0.5 as a Trust Task,
requires an `elevated` acknowledgement, then sends auth/refresh/0.1 for
tokens at the new level. The bespoke /auth/step-up/vta/{start,finish}
paths and their snake_case parsing are gone.

The page API's stepUpVta now takes the session's refresh token and id,
and the holder that signs is the active connection's, not one the page
names.

Approve-requests are verified as their issuer's operational message
(proofPurpose authentication), which is how both the control plane and
the agent sign them. Documents a page asks the wallet to sign are signed
for authentication too: they are the holder's own requests, and the
control plane refuses an assertionMethod proof on them.

title: feat(services)!: service management is Trust Tasks only, over any transport
body:
Moves VTA service management off its bespoke REST routes and onto the `vta/services/*` Trust Tasks, so it works over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS alike, under the standing rule that every remote API is a spine-dispatched Trust Task.

## What changes
- **SDK:** every `services` method keeps its signature but dispatches the Trust Task over `rpc_tt` and decodes the generated response. `enable_didcomm` now reaches a REST-only VTA over HTTPS on `/trust-tasks`.
- **VTA:** serves two new tasks (spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#656, trust-tasks-rs 0.23.3):
  - `vta/services/update/1.1` adds `drainTtlSecs`, which keeps `--drain-ttl` working.
  - `vta/services/report/0.1` replaces `/mediators/report`.
- **Removed (breaking):** the twenty `/services/*` routes plus `/mediators/*`, their deprecation entries, and their REST tests. The same super-admin gates sit on the task handlers.
- **Producer census:** now drives every services method and schema-checks each payload.
- **VTC:** the hand-written `acl/revoke` request and response are replaced by the generated types, which the census flags now that 0.23.3 publishes them (requested by VGI). Behaviour is unchanged. `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are regenerated.

Full rationale is in the commit body.

## Verification (local, CI-equivalent)
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, plus the three reduced `vta-service` feature sets: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 5047 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 2334 passed, 1 failed.
  - The one failure is `openapi_response_census` on `routes/backup.rs` export/import. Main has been red on it since #1755, it is fixed by #1775, and this PR doesn't touch that file.

## Not closed here
- `vta/services/rollback/1.0` has no drain member.
- Per-transport mediators are still unbuilt.

title: feat(services)!: service management is Trust Tasks only, over any transport (#1782)
body:
feat(services)!: service management is Trust Tasks only, over any transport (#1782)

* feat(services)!: service management is Trust Tasks only, over any transport

`pnm services …` (and every SDK caller) reached the VTA's service management
through bespoke REST routes — twenty `/services/*` plus `/mediators/*` — via
`VtaClient::rpc`, whose DIDComm and TSP arms answered `UnsupportedTransport`.
So the whole surface worked only over REST, although the VTA already served the
`vta/services/*` Trust Tasks. Under the rule that every remote API is a
spine-dispatched Trust Task reachable over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS, the SDK now
dispatches the tasks and the REST routes are removed.

Spec gaps closed first (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#656, trust-tasks-rs
0.23.3):
- `vta/services/report/0.1` — the mediator-attribution report had no task.
  Operator-only, request proof REQUIRED: it is a contact log of other parties'
  DIDs. Served from the telemetry sink; `since` after `until` is the declared
  `invalidWindow`.
- `vta/services/update/1.1` — adds `drainTtlSecs` for the mediated transports.
  The REST route and `pnm services didcomm update --drain-ttl` carried an
  operator-chosen drain; 1.0 could not, so moving to the task would have
  silently dropped it. The handler honours it for DIDComm, raising a value
  below the 1h floor to the floor over a request that arrived through the
  mediator being replaced (the spec's MUST), refuses it for rest/webauthn, and
  reports no `drainUntil` for tsp — this VTA has one mediator connection, which
  a TSP update does not tear down, so there is nothing to drain.

SDK
- Every `services` method keeps its signature and return type, builds the spec
  payload, dispatches over `rpc_tt`, and maps the generated response back.
  `enable_didcomm` is no longer REST-only: a REST-only VTA receives it over
  HTTPS on `/trust-tasks`. `didcomm_status` is `services/get`; the live
  websocket state is not published state (`GET /health/details` has it).
- The producer census (`producer_payload_conformance`) now drives every
  services method through the loopback and validates each payload against the
  published schema; the wiremock REST-shape tests are gone with the routes.

Removed (breaking)
- `/services/*`, `/mediators/report`, `/mediators/drain/cancel` and their
  deprecation-registry entries; the REST-auth tests for them (the same
  super-admin gates are on the task handlers).
- Responses lose two cosmetic fields the task does not carry (the mediator
  endpoint on enable/update); the CLI already printed them only when present.

VTC
- 0.23.3 publishes a generated `acl/revoke/0.1`, so the VTC's hand-written
  `RevokeRequest` / `AclRevokeResponse` (which the generated-wire-types census
  now names) are replaced by the generated payload on the spine and the
  generated response, wrapped as `vta_sdk::openapi::AclRevoke01Response`, on
  both the spine and `DELETE /v1/acl/{did}`. Behaviour is unchanged — the
  declared `subjectNotPresent` / `lastAuthorityProtected` codes and the session
  end on full removal. The console's `openapi.json` / `wire.ts` are regenerated
  for the schema's new name.

Not closed here: `vta/services/rollback/1.0` has no drain member, so a DIDComm
rollback that lands on a drain transition takes the default window; and
per-transport mediators remain unbuilt, so advertising a TSP mediator the VTA is
not connected to is still possible.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(cli): pnm services is one path over every transport

The CLI kept a second, untyped code path for DIDComm and TSP clients
(`over_messaging`) that dispatched the `vta/services/*` tasks by hand. With
the SDK methods now dispatching the same tasks on every transport, the fork
was a duplicate, and a lossy one: over messaging, `services didcomm update`
dropped `--drain-ttl`, and `services report` refused as REST-only although
`vta/services/report/0.1` serves it. Every command now calls the typed SDK
method.

The SDK's `RollbackResponse::kind` also passed the wire's `noOp` through
while documenting `no_op`, so the CLI never printed its no-op message; it is
now mapped explicitly.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc): the REST backup refusal is checked for what it asks for

`backup_export_and_import_are_refused_over_rest` asserted the refusal said
"DIDComm or TSP". #1775 reworded it to "an end-to-end transport, TSP or
DIDComm", and the test has failed on main since. It now checks for the
requirement the message states — an end-to-end transport — rather than an
ordering of the transports that meet it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): rate_limit is not gated on webvh

Removing `mod protocol;` left its `#[cfg(feature = "webvh")]` attribute
behind, where it attached to the next item, `pub mod rate_limit;`. Every
build without `webvh` (the Feature combos `rest,didcomm` step) then lost the
rate limiter the unauthenticated routes need.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

body:
### Fixed

- **codegen**: Generate usable types for oneOf branches that use not ([#665](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/665))

typify (0.6) merges a `oneOf` branch's own keywords into the untagged
  enum variant it synthesizes for that branch. A bare `not: {"required":
  ["x"]}` is a shape it handles directly — property `x` is simply absent
  from that variant. Wrap the same exclusion in `anyOf` (the shape a
  3-way mutual-exclusion group needs, e.g.
  auth/passkey/enroll/invite/update/0.1's role/expiresAt/extendBy) and
  typify's merge instead produces an uninhabited `pub enum
  PayloadVariant0 {}` for that branch, so a payload carrying only `role`
  (plus `inviteId`) could never deserialize — and silently drops a
  property required only by that branch from every *other* branch's
  variant too, so `role` + `expiresAt` together also failed to
  round-trip. auth/revoke-session/0.2 has the same three-way `not:
  {anyOf: [...]}` shape and produced the same uninhabited nested type,
  though there it never broke a valid document (no shared field to
  drop).

  Only conformance example exercised extendBy alone, which is why this
  was never caught. Added role-only, expiresAt-only and role+expiresAt
  examples to auth/passkey/enroll/invite/update/0.1's spec.md, one per
  oneOf branch plus their combination.

  Fixed with a new preprocessing pass in trust-tasks-codegen,
  desugar_oneof_with_compound_not, which drops a oneOf combinator from
  the copy of the schema handed to typify whenever any branch's not is
  more than a single {"required": ["x"]} guard. Re-expressing the oneOf
  as anyOf (at least one) plus a pairwise not (no two at once) -
  oneOf's own JSON Schema definition - was tried first and does not
  help: typify applies the identical broken merge to a not wrapping
  anyOf/allOf regardless of which combinator carries it. The wire
  schema (SCHEMA_JSON / ValidatedPayload::validate_value, and the
  TypeScript/Go/Dart bindings, generated independently of typify) is
  captured before this pass runs and is unaffected, so the actual
  mutual-exclusion constraint is still enforced at runtime; only the
  Rust type for the two affected specs becomes fully permissive, matching
  what the other three languages already generate for this schema. A
  plain discriminated oneOf (every branch's not, if any, a single
  {"required": ["x"]}) is untouched and still renders as a clean Rust
  enum.

  Scanned every schema under specs/ for a oneOf/anyOf branch using not.
  Only these two combine it with oneOf; the rest (auth/revoke-session/0.1,
  vta/app-state/put/1.0, vta/app-state/put-many/1.0,
  vtc/registry/sync-jobs/retry/0.1, credential-exchange/issue/0.1, and a
  few uses of not outside any oneOf) were unaffected and are unchanged
  after regenerating.

  changed.

title: fix(codegen): generate usable types for oneOf branches that use not
body:
## Summary

- `auth/passkey/enroll/invite/update/0.1`'s `oneOf` gives its role-only
  branch a `not` wrapped in `anyOf` (`{required:[role], not:{anyOf:[
  {required:[expiresAt]},{required:[extendBy]}]}}`). typify (0.6) merges a
  branch's own keywords into the untagged enum variant it synthesizes for
  that branch; it handles a bare `not: {required: ["x"]}` directly, but the
  same exclusion wrapped in `anyOf` produced an uninhabited
  `pub enum PayloadVariant0 {}` for that branch — a payload carrying only
  `role` (plus `inviteId`) could never deserialize — and silently dropped
  `role` from the *other* branches' variants too, so `role` + `expiresAt`
  together also failed to round-trip. The only existing conformance example
  exercised `extendBy` alone, which is why this was never caught.
- `auth/revoke-session/0.2` has the same three-way `not: {anyOf: [...]}}`
  shape and produced the same class of uninhabited nested type
  (`PayloadVariant0Variant1 {}` etc.) for each branch, though there it never
  broke a valid document since every branch is a full three-way mutual
  exclusion with no shared field to drop.
- **Fixed in the codegen** (`trust-tasks-codegen`): a new preprocessing
  pass, `desugar_oneof_with_compound_not`, drops a `oneOf` combinator from
  the copy of the schema handed to typify whenever any branch's `not` is
  more than a single `{"required": ["x"]}` guard. The wire schema
  (`SCHEMA_JSON`/`ValidatedPayload::validate_value`, and the TypeScript/Go/
  Dart bindings, generated independently of typify) is unaffected — the
  actual mutual-exclusion constraint is still enforced at runtime. Only the
  Rust type for the two affected specs becomes fully permissive (every
  member optional, no combinator modelled in the type system), matching
  what the other three languages already generate for this schema.
  Re-expressing the `oneOf` as `anyOf` + a pairwise `not` (`oneOf`'s own
  JSON Schema definition) was tried first and does not help: typify applies
  the identical broken merge to a `not` wrapping `anyOf`/`allOf` regardless
  of which combinator carries it, producing the same class of
  dropped-property defect one level up. A plain discriminated `oneOf`
  (every branch's `not`, if any, a single `{"required": ["x"]}`) is
  untouched and still renders as a clean Rust enum — confirmed for
  `auth/revoke-session/0.1`, `vta/app-state/put/1.0`,
  `vta/app-state/put-many/1.0`, `vtc/registry/sync-jobs/retry/0.1` and
  `credential-exchange/issue/0.1`, none of which changed.
- Scanned every schema under `specs/` for a `oneOf`/`anyOf` branch using
  `not` (13 files carry the keyword at all). Only the two above combine it
  with `oneOf`; the rest use it inside `dependentSchemas`, an `items` `$ref`
  + `not: {const: ...}` restriction, or a bare object-level `not` outside
  any `oneOf` — none of those trigger typify's empty-enum defect
  (`grep -n "pub enum .* {\s*}" trust-tasks-rs/src/specs` is clean after
  regenerating).
- Added three conformance examples to `auth/passkey/enroll/invite/update/0.1`'s
  `spec.md` — role only, expiresAt only, and role+expiresAt — alongside the
  existing extendBy-only example, one per `oneOf` branch and their
  combination. Confirmed role-only and role+expiresAt fail to deserialize on
  `main` (`data did not match any variant of untagged enum Payload`) and
  pass after the fix.
- Regenerated all four bindings; only the two affected Rust modules
  changed — TS/Go/Dart are byte-identical, since they don't route through
  typify.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run validate`
- [x] `npm run check-bindings`
- [x] `cargo test -p trust-tasks-codegen` (new `desugar_oneof_tests`)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`
- [x] `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `go test -race ./...` (trust-tasks-go)
- [x] `npm test` (trust-tasks-ts)
- [x] `dart test` (trust-tasks-dart)
- [x] Confirmed the two previously-failing conformance tests (role-only,
      role+expiresAt) fail on `main` and pass on this branch

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.23.6
body:
### Added

- **vta**: Trust Tasks for the VTA's REST-only health, restore-status, session-revocation and wrapping-key routes ([#663](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/663))

* feat(vta): Trust Tasks for the VTA's REST-only health, session-revocation and wrapping-key routes

  Three Verifiable Trust Agent routes were reachable only over REST. Each
  gets a Trust Task, so an agent serves it identically over TSP, DIDComm
  and HTTPS.

  - vta/health/details/0.1 replaces GET /health/details: version,
    mediator, seal and at-rest encryption state, TEE status, TSP
    advertisement, and the restore the agent's state derives from.
    Public, anonymous, request proof OPTIONAL and response proof
    REQUIRED, like vta/attestation/status/0.1.
  - auth/revoke-session/0.2 replaces DELETE /auth/sessions?did=: adds a
    `subject` form ending every session of a subject the producer could
    withdraw the access of (a scoped administrator cannot reach an
    unrestricted one), answers a refusal with permissionDenied, and drops
    0.1's `notOwner`, which contradicted 0.1's own non-disclosure rule.
    Backwards-compatible: every 0.1 payload is a valid 0.2 payload.
  - keys/import-wrapping-key/0.1 replaces GET /keys/import/wrapping-key:
    a fresh, single-use, minutes-long key a producer seals a private key
    to for keys/import's privateKeySealed carrier over a transport that
    is not end to end. Returned as an Ed25519 did:key; the response proof
    is REQUIRED because the TLS terminator the task routes around could
    otherwise substitute its own key.

  Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.
