title: feat(vta): Trust Tasks for the VTA's REST-only health, restore-status, session-revocation and wrapping-key routes
body:
Three Verifiable Trust Agent routes in [verifiable-trust-infrastructure](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure) are still reachable only over REST. The rule there is now that every remote API is a transport-agnostic Trust Task, served over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS alike. This PR specifies the four tasks that replace them: `GET /health/details` is split into a public task and an administrator-only one. Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings are regenerated in the same PR.

| New Trust Task | Replaces | VTI code today |
|---|---|---|
| `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vta/health/details/0.1` | `GET /health/details`, public part | `vta-service/src/routes/health.rs` (`health_details`, `HealthDetailsResponse`) |
| `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vta/restore/status/0.1` | `GET /health/details`, `version` and `restored` | `vta-service/src/routes/health.rs` (`RestoredFrom`), `vta-backup/src/restore.rs` (`RestoreProvenance`, `read_provenance`) |
| `https://trusttasks.org/spec/auth/revoke-session/0.2` | `DELETE /auth/sessions?did=<did>` | `vta-service/src/routes/auth.rs` (`revoke_sessions_by_did`), authorised by `vta-service/src/operations/acl.rs` (`may_manage_subject`) |
| `https://trusttasks.org/spec/keys/import-wrapping-key/0.1` | `GET /keys/import/wrapping-key` | `vta-service/src/routes/keys.rs` (`get_wrapping_key`), `vta-keys/src/wrapping.rs` (`WrappingKeyCache`) |

## Health details split into a public task and an administrator task

`GET /health/details` answers some members that are safe for anyone and some that are not. It becomes two tasks rather than one task whose answer grows when the caller is authenticated. A response whose content varies with authentication invites leaks: a cache keyed without the caller, a log line, or one code path that forgets the check can hand the richer answer to the wrong party. It also leaves the schema unable to say what the task discloses. Two tasks give each one a fixed schema and a fixed disclosure policy.

### `vta/health/details/0.1` (public)

- Modelled on `vta/attestation/status/0.1`: public and read-only, anonymous callers allowed, request proof **OPTIONAL**, response proof **REQUIRED**. No authorization, and every asker gets the same answer.
- Carries only non-identifying flags: `status` (`ok`), `mediatorUrl`, `mediatorDid`, `teeStatus` (`teeType`/`detected`/`platformVersion`), `sealed`, `storageEncrypted` and `tspEnabled`. The mediator is kept because the DID document already advertises it.
- It **never** carries `version` or the restore record, whoever asks, and `additionalProperties: false` means the schema cannot carry them. `spec.md` says why: `version` is a fingerprint for targeting known-vulnerable builds, and the restore record identifies a super-administrator, a former DID, hosted DIDs and key identifiers.
- The response proof is **REQUIRED** because the answer is the agent's claim about itself: unsigned, an intermediary could report it sealed and encrypted when it is neither.

### `vta/restore/status/0.1` (administrators only)

- Request proof **REQUIRED** and response proof **REQUIRED**. The signer must hold an administrator role at the agent, and anyone else is refused with the standard `permissionDenied` before the record is read, so a refusal does not reveal whether the agent was restored.
- Returns `version`, a required `restored` boolean, and the VTI-VTA-051 `restore` record (`appliedAt`, `stagedAt`, `stagedBy`, `sourceDid`, `sourceEnvironment`, `targetEnvironment`, `internalKeysLost`, `hostedDidsDetached`), present exactly when `restored` is true. "Not restored" is stated, not inferred from an absent member.
- `version` lives here because the registry has no administrator-only VTA server-information task that would be a better home. The one nearby, `did-management/server/config`, belongs to the DID hosting service.
- Both tasks are in the `provenance` category, with the `vta/attestation/*` siblings.

## `auth/revoke-session/0.2` (chosen over a new `auth/sessions/revoke/0.1`)

**Why a MINOR of `revoke-session` rather than a new collective task:**
- `revoke-session/0.1` already has a collective form (`all: true`) and already returns a `revokedCount`.
- Its prose already allows an administrative producer. What it lacks is any way to *name* the subject, because `all` always means the producer's own sessions.
- A separate `auth/sessions/revoke` would duplicate `all: true` for the self case and split one decision ("may X end Y's sessions?") across two tasks, each with its own authorization text, audit key and retry classification.
- Adding an optional `subject` as a third `oneOf` arm is backwards-compatible under SPEC §5.2: every `0.1` payload is a valid `0.2` payload.

**What 0.2 specifies:**
- **Authorization.** A producer may end a subject's sessions exactly when it could withdraw that subject's access under the consumer's access-control policy. An administrative role is not enough on its own, so a context-scoped administrator cannot reach an unrestricted administrator or a subject in another context. The rule is written generically, with VTI-SES-043 / VTI-ACL-050 cited as a non-normative example.
- **Refusal.** A refused `subject` gets the standard `permissionDenied`, not a namespaced code (SPEC §8.5 forbids shadowing, and §7.2 names `permissionDenied`). The refusal is the same whether or not the subject is known.
- **Response.** `revokedCount` is the number of sessions this request invalidated. Zero is a success.
- **0.1's disclosure conflict.** 0.1 declared `notOwner` for someone else's session, yet also required that such a session's existence not be revealed. Those two cannot both hold. 0.2 drops `notOwner` and requires "absent" and "outside your authority" to be answered the same way: `revokedCount: 0` (RECOMMENDED, and what VTI does) or `sessionNotFound`.
- **Front matter.** 0.2 adds the Authorization section and the four Security & Privacy sub-headings that 0.1 lacked, plus `issuedAtRequirement: REQUIRED`, `retention` and `consequences`.

## `keys/import-wrapping-key/0.1`

- **What it returns.** A fresh key pair per request. The private half stays only in memory, is used at most once, and expires within minutes. The response carries `wrappingKey`, `keyId` and `expiresAt`.
- **Lifetime, as VTI implements it.** A 60-second TTL. The key is consumed when a sealed bundle opens with it, is kept in memory only, and is lost on restart. The spec makes single use and memory-only custody MUSTs, and leaves the exact lifetime to `expiresAt` (SHOULD be a few minutes at most).
- **Response proof is REQUIRED.** This is the core design point. The task exists for transports whose confidentiality ends at an intermediary, and that intermediary can swap the returned key for its own, then read, re-seal and forward every private key sealed to it. Only a response signed by the custodian's DID, and verified by the producer before it seals anything, detects that swap. The request proof is RECOMMENDED, the family's default for reads.
- **Authorization.** The same authority `keys/import` requires. This gates resource use (every key costs memory until it expires), not access to the key, which is public. `unavailable` with `retryAfter` covers a bound on outstanding keys.
- **Side effects.** `sideEffects: none`, with transient retention. Nothing is persisted, and a replayed request only yields another independent key.
- **Slug.** A flat `keys/import-wrapping-key` rather than `keys/import/wrapping-key`, to avoid the nested-slug-beside-version-folder layout the build warns about. This also matches the name VTI used internally (`vta/keys/import-wrapping-key`).

## Review points

1. **The `restored`/`restore` agreement in `vta/restore/status` is enforced in prose, not in the schema.** The rule is that `restore` is present exactly when `restored` is true. The schema can't state it: typify, the Rust generator, panics on `if`/`then`. A single nullable `restored: null | {…}` member would have been schema-enforced, but it degrades to untyped JSON in the Go (`json.RawMessage`) and Dart (`Object?`) bindings. The spec therefore makes agreement a consumer MUST, and requires a producer to treat a mismatch as malformed.
2. **VTI's handler must change for the split.** `version` and `restored` leave the public answer, and the admin gate moves to `vta/restore/status`. The REST route's authenticated-only access becomes public access for the remaining flags.
3. **`teeType` spelling.** The registry uses `sev-snp`, matching `vta/attestation/status/0.1`. VTI's `TeeType` currently serialises `sev_snp`, so its Trust Task handler must map it.
4. **`TeeStatus` is a local `$def` that mirrors the `attestation/status` response.** It is not a shared component: only this task references it as a named definition, and moving `attestation/status` onto a shared component would touch another spec's generated types. A follow-up could hoist both into `vta/_shared`.
5. **The wrapping key is an Ed25519 `did:key`, not the JWK the REST route returns.** The REST route returns `{kid, kty: "OKP", crv: "X25519", x}`. The registry and workspace convention is public keys as Ed25519 `did:key`, with the X25519 key derived by the RFC 7748 birational map. That is exactly how `vta/attestation/mnemonic-export`'s `clientDid` addresses a sealed-transfer recipient. VTI will need to mint an Ed25519 pair (deriving the X25519 secret) instead of a bare X25519 pair.
6. **`keyId` exists only for the `privateKeyJwe` carrier.** A sealed-transfer bundle does not need it, because VTI tries each unexpired key. VTI's current "JWE" is a bespoke `kid.epk.nonce.ciphertext` string, not an RFC 7516 compact serialization, although `keys/import/0.1` describes `privateKeyJwe` as JWE compact. That mismatch sits in `keys/import` and VTI, not here, but reviewers should know `keyId` is kept for it. Dropping `keyId` would be reasonable if the JWE carrier is on its way out.
7. **New `expiresAt` member.** The REST route returns no expiry; the Trust Task requires one, so VTI must compute it (issue time + TTL).
8. **The wrapping key is not bound to the producer.** VTI's sealed path tries every unexpired key. The spec permits binding (MAY) but does not require it. Tightening that to a SHOULD is a possible follow-up.
9. **`auth/revoke-session/0.2` behaviour change for VTI.** VTI's `0.1` handler refuses `all: true` (`revoke_all_unsupported`). Under 0.2 the `subject` form, with the producer as subject, is the same operation, so VTI will need to implement it. The REST route also required the admin role even to revoke one's own sessions by DID; 0.2 lets any subject end its own.
10. **Dropping `notOwner`** removes a declared code in a MINOR. This is allowed for a draft under SPEC §5.2, and VTI never emitted the code (doing so would breach 0.1's own non-disclosure rule). It is flagged in case another implementer relies on it.

title: feat(vta): Trust Tasks for the VTA's REST-only health, restore-status, session-revocation and wrapping-key routes (#663)
body:
feat(vta): Trust Tasks for the VTA's REST-only health, restore-status, session-revocation and wrapping-key routes (#663)

* feat(vta): Trust Tasks for the VTA's REST-only health, session-revocation and wrapping-key routes

Three Verifiable Trust Agent routes were reachable only over REST. Each
gets a Trust Task, so an agent serves it identically over TSP, DIDComm
and HTTPS.

- vta/health/details/0.1 replaces GET /health/details: version,
  mediator, seal and at-rest encryption state, TEE status, TSP
  advertisement, and the restore the agent's state derives from.
  Public, anonymous, request proof OPTIONAL and response proof
  REQUIRED, like vta/attestation/status/0.1.
- auth/revoke-session/0.2 replaces DELETE /auth/sessions?did=: adds a
  `subject` form ending every session of a subject the producer could
  withdraw the access of (a scoped administrator cannot reach an
  unrestricted one), answers a refusal with permissionDenied, and drops
  0.1's `notOwner`, which contradicted 0.1's own non-disclosure rule.
  Backwards-compatible: every 0.1 payload is a valid 0.2 payload.
- keys/import-wrapping-key/0.1 replaces GET /keys/import/wrapping-key:
  a fresh, single-use, minutes-long key a producer seals a private key
  to for keys/import's privateKeySealed carrier over a transport that
  is not end to end. Returned as an Ed25519 did:key; the response proof
  is REQUIRED because the TLS terminator the task routes around could
  otherwise substitute its own key.

Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta): split restore provenance and version out of health details

vta/health/details/0.1 stays public (anonymous, request proof OPTIONAL,
response proof REQUIRED) and now carries only non-identifying flags:
status, mediator URL/DID, TEE status, sealed, storageEncrypted and
tspEnabled. Its schema cannot carry `version` or `restored`
(additionalProperties: false): the version is a fingerprint for
targeting known-vulnerable builds, and the restore record identifies a
super-administrator, a former DID, hosted DIDs and key identifiers.

vta/restore/status/0.1 serves both to administrators only: request
and response proof REQUIRED, a non-administrator refused with
permissionDenied. It returns `version`, a required `restored` boolean,
and the VTI-VTA-051 `restore` record present exactly when `restored`
is true.

Two tasks rather than one whose content varies with authentication: a
conditional response invites leaks through caching, logging or a missed
branch, and leaves the schema unable to say what the task discloses.
Each task now has a fixed schema and a fixed disclosure policy.

The DeploymentEnvironment references are bare $refs, with the
description on the $def, so the generated TypeScript declares the type
once. Bindings regenerated.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.23.4` → `0.23.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.23.4` → `0.23.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.23.4` → `0.23.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.23.4` → `0.23.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.23.4` → `0.23.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.23.4` → `0.23.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.23.4` → `0.23.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.23.4` → `0.23.5` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.21.4` → `0.21.5` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.3.5`) | `0.3.4` → `0.3.5` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.3.4` → `0.3.5` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(did-management): Trust Tasks for the DID hosting service's REST-only surface
body:
Specs for every remote surface of [affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service](https://github.com/affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service) that has none, so that each can move onto the service's central Trust Task dispatch and work the same over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS (`POST /trust-tasks`). The implementation plan is at the end. Nothing in webvh-service changes in this PR.

## New specifications (29)

Every task declares `proof: REQUIRED`, except `did-management/server/info`, which is the one public read (request OPTIONAL, response REQUIRED). Each spec states the authority it needs, its side effects, its error codes and privacy notes. No optional member has a schema `default`. Where a member is optional, its description says what absence means.

**did-management — control plane, called by admins and DID owners**

| Task | Replaces (REST today) |
|---|---|
| `did-management/did/log/0.1` | `GET /api/log/{m}`, `GET /api/raw/{m}` (use `raw: true`) |
| `did-management/agent-name/resolve/0.1` | `POST /api/agent-names/resolve`. Answers only for DIDs the caller may read, so it can't be used to test whether a DID is hosted. |
| `did-management/domain/list/0.1` | `GET /api/domains` |
| `did-management/registry/list/0.1` | `GET /api/control/registry` (plus the fleet half of `GET /api/services/overview`) |
| `did-management/registry/get/0.1` | `GET /api/control/registry/{id}` |
| `did-management/registry/check/0.1` | `POST /api/control/registry/{id}/health` |
| `did-management/registry/purge-domain/0.1` | `POST /api/control/registry/{id}/domains/{d}/purge`. New `stillAssigned` interlock. |
| `did-management/stats/get/0.1` | `GET /api/stats`, `GET /api/stats/{m}` |
| `did-management/stats/timeseries/0.1` | `GET /api/timeseries`, `GET /api/timeseries/{m}` (`?domain=` included) |
| `did-management/server/config/0.1` | `GET /api/config` (plus the control-plane half of `/api/services/overview`). No secrets, by rule. |
| `did-management/server/info/0.1` | `GET /api/server-info`. Public bearer read; the response must be signed by the `serviceDid` it names. |
| `did-management/server/metrics/0.1` | `GET /metrics` (Prometheus). Admin-only, proof REQUIRED; the Prometheus endpoint is deleted, not kept alongside it. |
| `did-management/identity/list/0.1` | `GET /api/identity/generations` |
| `did-management/identity/retire/0.1` | `POST /api/identity/generations/{id}/retire` (the kill switch). The service can never be its own administrator. |

Shared: `did-management/_shared/0.2/service-instance.schema.json`, a superset of 0.1 with type, verdict, methods, advertised services and last inbound/outbound transport. `did-management/_shared/0.2/metrics-snapshot.schema.json`, a generic counters/gauges/histograms snapshot shape any service in this ecosystem can reuse for its own `server/metrics` task, not only this one.

**did-management/replica — control plane → hosting server (edge)**

Today the control plane sends these by reusing the *admin* URIs `domain/assign|unassign|purge/0.1` with a `{domain}` payload that doesn't match those specs, plus `domain/upsert/0.1`, which has no spec at all.

| Task | Note |
|---|---|
| `did-management/replica/domain/upsert/0.1` | Replicates a `DomainEntry`. The name must already be canonical. |
| `did-management/replica/domain/assign/0.1` | The edge records the assignment time on its own clock. |
| `did-management/replica/domain/unassign/0.1` | Schedules the purge after the edge's grace period and returns `purgeAt`. |
| `did-management/replica/domain/purge/0.1` | `stalePurge` freshness rule: a purge issued before the domain was re-assigned never wipes it. |

**webvh — sync, used by edges and watchers**

| Task | Replaces |
|---|---|
| `webvh/sync/update/0.2` | 0.1, and the watcher's `POST /api/sync/did`. Proof REQUIRED, camelCase, a REQUIRED `disabled` member, and a Source → Replica model that covers watchers. Adds `historyRewrite` and `deactivated`. |
| `webvh/sync/delete/0.2` | 0.1, and the watcher's `POST /api/sync/delete` |
| `webvh/sync/batch/0.1` | Already on the wire with no spec. Results per entry; a transient failure makes the whole batch retryable. |

Shared: `webvh/_shared/0.1/sync-update.schema.json`, used by `batch`. `update/0.2` inlines the same shape, because not every binding generator accepts a top-level `$ref` payload.

**webvh — witness service**

| Task | Replaces |
|---|---|
| `webvh/witness/sign/0.1` | `POST /api/proof/{id}`. The witness now receives the log and verifies it before signing: `versionId` must be the last entry and the witness must be listed. |
| `webvh/witness/key/create/0.1` | `POST /api/witnesses` |
| `webvh/witness/key/list/0.1` | `GET /api/witnesses`, `GET /api/witnesses/{id}` |
| `webvh/witness/key/delete/0.1` | `DELETE /api/witnesses/{id}` |

Shared: `webvh/_shared/0.1/witness-key.schema.json`.

**auth**

| Task | Replaces |
|---|---|
| `auth/step-up/start/0.1` | `POST /api/auth/step-up/vta/start`, the bespoke REST path the OpenVTC plugin (`rp-login/step-up.ts`) and the UI call. The response carries the signed `approve-request/0.3`. "Finish" becomes a plain `approve-response/0.5` Trust Task, followed by `auth/refresh` for tokens. |
| `auth/passkey/enroll/invite/list/0.1` | `GET /api/auth/passkey/invites`. Addressed by `inviteId`, and **never re-discloses tokens**. |
| `auth/passkey/enroll/invite/update/0.1` | `PUT /api/auth/passkey/invite/{token}` |
| `auth/passkey/enroll/invite/revoke/0.1` | `DELETE /api/auth/passkey/invite/{token}` |

Shared: `auth/_shared/0.1/passkey-invite.schema.json` (`InviteSummary`).

## Inventory: what already has a spec

Every other remote route already has a spec. Some of those specs are served as Trust Tasks today, others only over REST.

- **Served as Trust Tasks today, with a REST duplicate:**
  - `did/register` (`PUT /api/dids/{m}`, `POST /api/dids/register`)
  - `webvh/witness/publish` (`PUT /api/witness/{m}`)
  - `did/check-name` (`POST /api/dids/check`, `POST /api/dids`)
  - `did/list`, `did/info`, `did/delete`, `did/change-owner`
  - `agent-name/update|remove|check|list`
  - `me/domains`
  - `auth/challenge|authenticate|refresh`
  - `acl/*`
  - `server/register` (`/api/control/register-service`), `server/stats-sync` (`/api/control/stats`)
- **Spec exists, but only REST serves it:**
  - `did/set-state` (`/disable`, `/enable`), `did/rollback`
  - `domain/create|update|set-state|set-default|purge`
  - `domain/assign|unassign` (admin)
  - `registry/admin-register|deregister`
  - `auth/passkey/enroll/*`, `auth/passkey/login/*` (also used for passkey step-up), `auth/passkey/enroll/invite`
  - `auth/step-up/approve-response` (via `/auth/step-up/vta/finish`)

**Dead (no caller). Delete, don't spec:**
- `/api/proxy/{server,witness}/{id}/*`
- `POST /api/task-consent/request`
- `GET /api/auth/step-up/check` (demo)
- The witness `POST /api/didcomm` (a 501 stub)
- `ControlClient` (REST `register-service`)
- The typed `spec/did-hosting/did/*/1.0` and `spec/did-hosting/webvh/witness/publish/1.0` arms in `trust_tasks_did.rs`: undocumented, and nothing sends them
- The house `trusttasks.org/did-hosting/*/1.0` URIs, which only label permissive REST routes

**Excluded:**
- Resolution: `/.well-known/did.jsonl`, `/.well-known/did-witness.json`, `/.well-known/did.json`, the DID-serving fallback, and the `/@name` redirects
- Static UI assets

**Decided:** `/api/health` and the daemon's `/health` stay exactly as they are — plain, unauthenticated HTTP liveness probes with no detail, just liveness, for a load balancer or orchestrator that needs "is it up" and has no other use for a key. `/metrics` does not stay a Prometheus endpoint: it becomes `did-management/server/metrics/0.1`, a Trust Task, so an operational-metrics read is admin-authenticated and available over any transport like every other administrative read in this category; the Prometheus endpoint is deleted, not kept alongside it.

## Wire drift found (existing specs served off-spec)

1. The control plane sends `webvh/sync/update/0.1` with **snake_case** keys (`did_id`, `log_content`, …). The schema is camelCase with `additionalProperties: false`.
2. The `did/list/0.1` response is `{dids:[{did_id,…}]}`, but the spec says `{records,total}`. The VTA treats the listing as REST-only and refuses reconcile over Trust Tasks. A `did/list` that matches its spec removes the reason.
3. Control→edge domain directives reuse the admin URIs with a different payload. `domain/upsert/0.1` and `webvh/sync/batch/0.1` have no specs. (Fixed by `replica/*` and `sync/batch` above.)
4. A disabled DID's state never reaches edges: sync 0.1 has no member for it.
5. Watchers only get pushes from the edge's *own* REST writes (`watcher_push`), so in any control-fed deployment they receive nothing.
6. Several existing specs still declare proof RECOMMENDED or OPTIONAL for privileged operations that the service already refuses without a proof:
   - `did/list`, `did/info`, `me/domains`
   - `agent-name/list`, `acl/list`
   - `server/health`, `server/stats-sync`
   - `sync/*` 0.1

   Follow-up: a new minor version of each, making the proof REQUIRED.

## Implementation plan (webvh-service and callers)

Order: **1 → 2 → 3 → (4, 5, 6 in parallel) → 7 → 8.** Every deployment is a test instance, so each step is a clean cut with no compatibility window.

**Acceptance criteria.** This plan is not done until **both** deployment shapes pass an end-to-end smoke test on each transport (TSP, DIDComm, HTTPS): the single-process daemon (step 8), and the distributed topology — control plane + edge(s) (step 4) + witness (step 5) + watcher (step 6) wired together. Dropping the standalone-edge mode (step 4) is conditional on this: a hosting server with no `control_did` is no longer a supported shape, but the control plane driving remote edges is, and the smoke test is what proves it still works after the REST surface is gone.

1. **did-hosting-common.**
   - Take the trust-tasks release that carries these specs.
   - Build one dispatch table keyed on the generated `Payload::TYPE_URI`s.
   - Replace `bridge_did_management`'s hand-built `MSG_*` JSON with the generated request and response types, so every reply conforms to its `$defs.Response`.
   - Add a test that validates every reply against its schema.
2. **did-hosting-control: serve everything centrally** in `route_trust_task_doc`, on all three transports, next to the REST routes for now.
   - The new tasks above.
   - The spec-but-REST-only set: `did/set-state`, `did/rollback`, `domain/*`, `registry/*`, the `auth/passkey/*` family, invite list/update/revoke, `auth/step-up/start`, and `approve-response/0.5`.
   - Move step-up to `approve-request/0.3` / `approve-response/0.5`. `auth/refresh` must re-read the session's current `acr`.
   - `is_proofless` gains `did-management/server/info` and `auth/passkey/login/start`.
   - Invites get an `inviteId` separate from the token.
3. **Callers move to Trust Tasks.**
   - **did-hosting-ui** (`lib/api.ts`): every call through `trustTask()`, and `server-info` through `server/info`.
   - **pnm-browser-plugin** `packages/core/src/rp-login/step-up.ts`:
     - `stepUpVtaStart` sends a wallet-signed `auth/step-up/start/0.1` (recipient = `rpDid`) to `{base}/trust-tasks`, verifies the reply's proof, then verifies the embedded `approve-request/0.3`. The verification helpers in `vta/step-up.ts` move from 0.2 to 0.3.
     - `stepUpVtaFinish` sends the `approve-response/0.5` document as a Trust Task, then calls `auth/refresh` for tokens.
     - The bespoke `/auth/step-up/vta/{start,finish}` paths and their snake_case parsing go.
     - Because each task is transport-agnostic, the plugin can later send the same documents over DIDComm or TSP.
   - **VTA**:
     - Delete `vta-webvh`'s `WebvhClient` REST arm and `WebvhTransport::Rest`.
     - `list_dids_for_owner` becomes `did/list` and `list_my_domains` becomes `me/domains`, both over the Trust Task seam.
     - Reconcile and retire-orphan stop refusing over Trust Tasks.
4. **did-hosting-server (edge).**
   - Consume `replica/domain/*`, `webvh/sync/update/0.2`, `delete/0.2` and `batch/0.1`. The control plane's `server_push` emits them in camelCase, including `disabled`.
   - Delete the edge's entire `/api/*` management router: auth, dids, log, raw, disable/enable, services, stats, config and acl. What remains is resolution plus the Trust Task listener.
   - Also delete the edge ACL (the only authority is the configured `control_did`), the edge sessions, `watcher_push` and `WatcherClient`.
   - Stats sync leaves the HTTPS `POST /api/control/stats` and goes over the resolved binding.
   - A standalone edge with no `control_did` is no longer a supported mode; single-host deployments use the daemon (see Acceptance criteria above for what proves this doesn't regress).
5. **webvh-witness.**
   - Add a Trust Task listener: TSP and DIDComm on the mediator, plus `POST /api/trust-tasks`.
   - Serve `webvh/witness/key/*`, `webvh/witness/sign/0.1` (with log verification) and `acl/*` through the shared framework dispatcher.
   - Delete `/api/auth/*`, `/api/witnesses*`, `/api/proof/*`, `/api/acl*` and `/api/didcomm`.
   - `did_hosting_common::witness_client` becomes a Trust Task client. The `--witness` bootstrap in the server and daemon CLIs uses `sign/0.1` and sends the log.
6. **webvh-watcher.**
   - The watcher gets its own DID, with keys in a VTA context, and a Trust Task listener.
   - It accepts `webvh/sync/update/0.2` / `delete/0.2` from configured source DIDs, which replaces `push_tokens`, and verifies logs exactly as an edge does.
   - The control plane fans out to the watchers named in a log's `watchers` parameter, through its outbox, using a configured URL → DID map.
   - Delete `/api/sync/*`.
7. **Delete the REST surface in control.**
   - `router_without_fallback` shrinks to `/api/trust-tasks`, `/api/health` and the UI fallback. `/metrics` (Prometheus) is **deleted**, not kept alongside the new Trust Task — `did-management/server/metrics/0.1` is the only way to read operational metrics from here on. `/api/health` is **kept**, unchanged: a plain, unauthenticated liveness probe, not a Trust Task.
   - Delete:
     - the `TrustTaskRouter` permissive header machinery and the `did-hosting/*/1.0` house constants
     - the proxy, `task-consent/request`, `step-up/check`, and the REST identity, `control/stats` and `register-service` routes
     - the dead `trust_tasks_did.rs` `did-hosting/*` arms
     - `docs/openapi.json`
     - the Prometheus metrics exporter and its dependency, once `server/metrics/0.1` serves the same data
   - Update `CLAUDE.md`: "there is no trust-task REST sender between these services" becomes "`POST /trust-tasks` is the HTTPS binding, the same dispatch".
8. **did-hosting-daemon.** It inherits steps 2 and 7 through `build_control_router`. Check that the nested `/watcher` router now serves only resolution and the Trust Task listener, its own `/health` unchanged, and run a daemon-mode smoke over each transport (see Acceptance criteria above).

title: feat(did-management): Trust Tasks for the DID hosting service's REST-only surface (#661)
body:
feat(did-management): Trust Tasks for the DID hosting service's REST-only surface (#661)

* feat(did-management): Trust Tasks for the DID hosting service's REST-only surface

Specs for every remote surface of affinidi-webvh-service that had none, so each can move onto the service's central Trust Task dispatch over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS:

- did-management: did/log, agent-name/resolve, domain/list, registry/list|get|check|purge-domain, stats/get|timeseries, server/config|info, identity/list|retire, and _shared/0.2 service-instance.
- did-management/replica/domain: upsert, assign, unassign, purge (the control plane to edge hop, today sent on the admin URIs or unspecified).
- webvh: sync/update 0.2 and sync/delete 0.2 (proof required, a disabled member, watchers as replicas), sync/batch 0.1, witness/sign and witness/key/create|list|delete.
- auth: step-up/start (replaces the bespoke REST start/finish paths), and passkey/enroll/invite/list|update|revoke addressed by inviteId, never by token.

Every task requires a proof except the public did-management/server/info read. Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(specs): repair generator-hostile schemas; add server/metrics

Three generated conformance tests failed under cargo test:

- auth/passkey/enroll/invite/update/0.1 combined a top-level anyOf
  with a sibling not, and the generator silently dropped both
  expiresAt and extendBy from the struct. Restructured as a oneOf of
  three disjoint required+not branches (the pattern
  auth/revoke-session/0.1 already uses), which preserves the same
  constraint (at least one of role/expiresAt/extendBy; expiresAt and
  extendBy mutually exclusive) and generates all four fields.

- auth/step-up/start/0.1's embedded approveRequest only modelled
  `type` in its properties, so issuedAt, expiresAt and anything else
  not in that shortlist were dropped on round-trip. Modelled the full
  envelope (id/type/issuer/recipient/issuedAt/expiresAt/payload/proof),
  leaving payload and proof opaque so their own specs still own their
  shape.

- did-management/_shared/0.2/service-instance's servedDomains was
  optional, so the generator emitted a bare Vec with
  skip_serializing_if = Vec::is_empty; an example that carried an
  explicit empty array for a server instance lost it on re-serialize.
  Made servedDomains required (always present, empty when unused),
  matching its own description.

Also adds did-management/server/metrics/0.1: an admin-only, proof
REQUIRED Trust Task replacing the Prometheus /metrics endpoint, with
a generic did-management/_shared/0.2/metrics-snapshot shape other
services can reuse. The unauthenticated /api/health and daemon
/health liveness probes are unaffected and stay plain HTTP.

Regenerated the Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings for all of the above.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(pnm): up to ~20× faster commands on a distant VTA (ssh-style ControlMaster)
body:
> **Draft / WIP** — the feature works and is measured, but see *Not done yet* at the bottom.

## Why

Every `pnm` invocation is a fresh process. Each one re-resolves the VTA and mediator DIDs,
opens a TLS connection per host, authenticates to the mediator and upgrades a WebSocket —
and only then sends the command. None of that survives the process, so the next command
pays for all of it again.

On a local stack that is invisible: a round trip costs microseconds, so the setup is free
and every command looks instant. Against a VTA in another region it is the whole story.

Counted off the reverse proxy's access log, one `pnm acl list` over DIDComm is **12–17 HTTPS
requests**: 6 `did.jsonl` fetches, a mediator challenge and authenticate, a WebSocket
upgrade, an inbox drain, the actual outbound/inbound pair, and several cleanup `DELETE`s.
Because each fresh connection also pays TCP and TLS on top of its request, that is **~23
serialised round trips** — for a command whose useful work is one.

## What it costs today, and with this change

`pnm acl list`, three runs per cell, median. Both arms are the same binary and the same
`docker exec` into one long-lived container, so process startup is in neither number; the
~103 ms exec floor is subtracted. Latency injected with a delaying relay in front of the
stack, so these are propagation delay only — no jitter or loss, which makes them floors.

| RTT | one-shot (`--control-master no`) | multiplexed | removed | **ratio** |
|-----:|-----:|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 0 ms | 64 ms | 41 ms | 23 ms | **1.6×** |
| 50 ms | 1 378 ms | 107 ms | 1 271 ms | **12.9×** |
| 150 ms | 3 646 ms | 215 ms | 3 431 ms | **17.0×** |
| 300 ms | 6 892 ms | 360 ms | 6 532 ms | **19.1×** |

Both sides are linear in RTT, which is the useful form:

```
one-shot     ≈ 22.8 × RTT
multiplexed  ≈  1.06 × RTT
```

The ratio therefore climbs with distance and approaches **~21×** (22.8 / 1.06) as the
fixed local cost stops mattering: 19.1× is what was measured at 300 ms, not a ceiling.

A multiplexed command costs **one application round trip** — the same thing a trust ping
measures. So the rule needs no RTT estimate at all: **the multiplexed number is your trust
ping**, and everything above it is setup the one-shot CLI redoes every time.

| your trust ping | multiplexed | one-shot today |
|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 50 ms | 50 ms | ~1.2 s |
| 150 ms | 150 ms | ~3.5 s |
| 300 ms | 300 ms | ~7.0 s |

At 300 ms RTT a twenty-command script goes from over two minutes to about seven seconds.

### Starting the master is ~free

The first command has no master to talk to, so it starts one and then delegates. That costs
about what running the command directly would have, because the master does the setup the
command needed anyway:

| RTT | first command (starts master) | one-shot |
|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 0 ms | 168 ms | 64 ms |
| 50 ms | 1 432 ms | 1 378 ms |
| 150 ms | 3 638 ms | 3 646 ms |
| 300 ms | 7 044 ms | 6 892 ms |

Which is why the default can be `auto`: nobody has to think about it, and nobody pays to
find out.

## What this adds

```
--control-master no|auto|yes|ask    (default: auto)
--control-persist no|yes|10m|600    (default: 10m)
--control-path <PATH>               (default: per-VTA socket in a private dir)

pnm sidecar serve | status | stop   (ssh -M / -O check / -O exit)
```

Names and semantics follow `ssh_config(5)` so the behaviour transfers. Rarely typed:
`auto` starts a master on demand, the way nobody types `ssh -M`.

The client hands the master its own stdin/stdout/stderr over `SCM_RIGHTS`, so a delegated
command's output is indistinguishable from a direct one — same terminal, same `isatty`,
same colours, same redirection.

## Why it is safe to default on

A master that is missing, stale, wrong-version or unusable is **never an error**. Every
such path falls back to the ordinary one-shot command, so the worst case is exactly
today's behaviour. Verified by killing a master with `SIGKILL` and running the next
command: the stale socket is detected, unlinked, replaced, and the command succeeds.

## Security

The master holds the only copy of the operator's admin private key in memory and will run
any command handed to it, so the socket is the privilege boundary:

- control directory forced to `0700` and ownership-checked; socket `0600`
- a symlinked or foreign-owned control path is refused, which closes the path-swap race
- **peer uid verified on every connection** (`SO_PEERCRED` / `getpeereid`) rather than
  trusting file permissions alone, with no exemption for root
- protocol version checked, so a master left running across an upgrade is refused rather
  than guessed at
- `--control-persist 10m` bounds how long the key stays resident — a security control, not
  just resource hygiene
- `ask` confirms before a master is used or created

## Two details taken from the OpenSSH implementation, not its documentation

1. **The socket is claimed atomically.** Binding a temp path and `link()`ing it into place
   means a second master loses with `EEXIST`. The obvious `unlink()`-then-`bind()` would
   remove a live master's socket, leaving that master running but unreachable while every
   later client silently started another. There is a regression test for this.
2. **Stale sockets are removed by the client, on `ECONNREFUSED` only**, and not at all when
   multiplexing is disabled.

Deliberate divergences from ssh are documented in `control/client.rs`: we spawn a child
rather than forking a thread-bearing tokio process; we confirm on the client's terminal so
`ask` works headless (ssh's askpass silently denies with no `DISPLAY`); we vet the control
path, which ssh does not; we do not exempt root from the peer check; and `yes` means "never
silently fall back" rather than ssh's "be the master".

No OpenSSH code is used — the design is reimplemented in Rust.

## Testing

`cargo test -p pnm-cli` — 104 pass, including the socket race, socket mode, path
sanitisation, symlink refusal and the `ControlPersist` time vocabulary. `clippy` and `fmt`
clean.

Against a live stack: idle timeout evicts the master, `sidecar stop` exits it, a
`SIGKILL`ed master is recovered from, `--control-master no` still runs direct, and the
control socket is `0600` inside a `0700` directory on both macOS and Linux.

## Not done yet

- [ ] `-O stop` (stop-listening) as distinct from `-O exit` — matters less here, where a
      session is one short command rather than a shell
- [ ] config-file keys to match the flags, so a default can be set per VTA
- [ ] review of whether `auto` should be the shipped default or opt-in for a release or two
- [ ] the `ask` prompt is per master, not per command — worth deciding which is wanted

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.23.4
body:
### Added

- **git-ns**: Administrator reads — view 0.5, namespace/list and repo/list ([#659](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/659))

* feat(git-ns): administrator reads — view 0.5, namespace/list and repo/list

  Three signed read tasks replace the bearer-authenticated administrator
  views VTCs served beside git-ns/view:

  - git-ns/view/0.5 adds scope: administrator (everything in the
    namespaces the caller administers, reasons included) and
    breakGlass: true (narrow to break-glass records). The response is
    0.4's.
  - git-ns/namespace/list/0.1 lists administered namespaces with admins,
    repository count, bridge, role map and forge status.
  - git-ns/repo/list/0.1 lists repositories in administered namespaces
    with owners, right counts, bootstrap, sync and the bridge's report.

  Proof REQUIRED on all three; no side effects. Authority is the
  community-administrator capability (every namespace) or a live explicit
  git.ns.admin (that namespace); each declares notAdministrator, answered
  alike for an unknown namespace and one the caller does not administer.

- **auth/passkey**: An administrator lists one member's passkeys (admin-list 0.1) ([#658](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/658))

auth/passkey/list lists only the signer's own credentials and refuses a
  subject in the payload, so no task let an administrator see which step-up
  passkeys a member holds — and so which credentialId to hand to
  auth/passkey/revoke/start 0.2.

  auth/passkey/admin-list 0.1:

  - Proof REQUIRED: the administrator is the issuer. The subject and a purpose
    (session | stepUp, no default) are named in the payload, and are a request,
    never a grant: the consumer authorises the administrator over that subject
    from its own state.
  - Refusals, in order: notAdministrator (before the subject is looked at);
    subjectUnknown, also for a subject outside the administrator's authority,
    so the code is no oracle; purposeNotSupported; subjectNotMember.
  - The response is { subject, purpose, credentials }, each a ListedCredential
    of credentialId, deviceLabel, registeredAt, lastUsedAt and signCount — no
    key material, no public key, no attestation, additionalProperties false.
    The counter is disclosed to the administrator, as the operator who acts on
    a cloning signal.
  - sideEffects none: listing touches no counter and no last-used time.
  - Privacy: only administrators with authority over the subject; the family
    audits writes, not reads, and a consumer that audits administrative reads
    SHOULD include this one.

  Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.23.3` → `0.23.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.23.3` → `0.23.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.23.3` → `0.23.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.23.3` → `0.23.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.23.3` → `0.23.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.23.3` → `0.23.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.23.3` → `0.23.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.23.3` → `0.23.4` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.21.3` → `0.21.4` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.3.4`) | `0.3.3` → `0.3.4` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.3.3` → `0.3.4` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(git-ns): administrator reads — view 0.5, namespace/list and repo/list
body:
Four `cnm git` listings, and the admin console's Repos views, still read the VTC over HTTPS as bearer-authenticated console views with no Trust Task behind them:

- `namespace list`
- `repos`
- `view --admin`
- `break-glass-list`

This PR specifies them as signed `git-ns/*` reads.

## Tasks

| Task | Covers | Response |
|---|---|---|
| `git-ns/view/0.5` | `view --admin`, `break-glass-list`, the console's break-glass banner | 0.4's, unchanged |
| `git-ns/namespace/list/0.1` | `namespace list`, the console's Namespaces card | `{ namespaces: [NamespaceStatus] }` |
| `git-ns/repo/list/0.1` | `repos`, the console's Repos table | `{ repos: [RepoStatus] }` |

### Why an admin mode on `view` rather than a new task
The administrator's view and the break-glass list are both views of the records `git-ns/view` already returns. Only the audience differs. So `view` 0.5 adds two request members and leaves the response alone:

- **`scope: administrator`** returns everything in the namespaces the caller administers, with every `reason` and `breakGlass`. A community administrator administers every namespace. Anyone else administers the namespaces where they hold a live, explicitly recorded `git.ns.admin`.
- **`breakGlass: true`** narrows the answer to break-glass records, ratified ones included. With the default scope, it returns the unratified records 0.4 already shows to each administrator and owner they concern. With `scope: administrator`, it returns the full review list.

### Why two list tasks
Namespace and repository status is operational detail for the people who fix things: admins, forge status, missing app permissions, bootstrap errors, the guard in force, and role-map staleness. None of it belongs in a member's `view`. The row shapes match what the console and `cnm` show today.

## Common to all three
- **Proof** is REQUIRED.
- **Side effects:** none.
- **Authority:** the community-administrator capability (every namespace), or a live explicit `git.ns.admin` (that namespace), held by a current member. A context-scoped admin role does not count, and neither does a bearer session.
- **Refusal:** each task declares `notAdministrator`. An unknown namespace gets the same answer as one the caller does not administer, so the code cannot be used to find out which namespaces exist.
- **Security & Privacy** says what each task discloses and to whom. It also records that these views used to go to any admin session.

## Checks
- All four bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).
- `npm run validate` passes.
- `npm run check-bindings`: 557 specs, all agree.
- The example payloads in each `spec.md` validate against their schemas, and every `payload.invalid-examples.json` entry is refused. This was checked with a local ajv run.

title: feat(vtc): list a member's step-up passkeys as auth/passkey/admin-list/0.1
body:
**This merges after #1756.** It is built on that branch so the diff stays small. Until #1756 lands, GitHub shows #1756's commits here as well. Review only the top commit.

An administrator reads a member's step-up passkeys through `GET /v1/admin/step-up-passkeys` today. That is a bearer route with no Trust-Task binding, because no published task let one subject read another's credentials: `auth/passkey/list` lists only the signer's own. trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#658 specifies `auth/passkey/admin-list/0.1`. This PR serves it on the spine, the same way over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS.

## Behaviour
- **Who can list.** The request must be signed by an administrator with authority over the member:
  - a community-wide admin can list any member;
  - a context-scoped admin can list a member whose entry names one of their contexts. This is the same visibility `acl/show` uses.
- **Refusals:**

  | Case | Code |
  |---|---|
  | unsigned document | `proofRequired` |
  | signer is not an admin (decided before the subject is read) | `notAdministrator` |
  | subject outside the admin's authority, or unknown (answered the same way) | `subjectUnknown` |
  | former member | `subjectNotMember` |
  | `purpose: session` | `purposeNotSupported` |

- **The response is metadata only.** Each credential carries `credentialId`, `deviceLabel`, `registeredAt`, `lastUsedAt` and `signCount`, newest first. There is no key material.
- **No side effects.** A read writes no audit row, counter or last-used time.

## Stand-in until trust-tasks-rs publishes #658
- `trust_tasks::passkey_admin_list_v0_1` is a hand-written copy of the schema, marked `TODO(trust-tasks release carrying trust-tasks #658)`.
- The URI is listed in `UNPUBLISHED_CANONICAL_OK` with a count of 1.
- Until the release, the registry cannot tell the spine that the task requires a proof. The handler therefore refuses unsigned documents itself, and the spine's proof census stays at 51. It should move to 52 when the stand-in is swapped for the generated type.

## Removed
- `GET /v1/admin/step-up-passkeys`, along with its OpenAPI schemas (`StepUpPasskeyList`, `StepUpPasskeyCredential`) and wire types.
- The console's step-up passkey card now signs `admin-list` with the browser's console key through `postSignedTrustTask`, and shows the counter.

## Tests
The spine tests run over REST, DIDComm and TSP contexts:
- `admin_list_by_an_administrator_with_authority_lists_metadata_and_changes_nothing`
- `admin_list_by_a_scoped_administrator_over_a_member_in_their_context`
- `admin_list_refuses_a_signer_who_is_not_an_administrator`
- `admin_list_refuses_a_member_outside_the_administrators_authority`
- `admin_list_refuses_an_unknown_or_former_member_and_session_credentials`
- `admin_list_refuses_an_unsigned_document`
- `admin_list_refuses_a_payload_the_schema_refuses`

Also:
- `tests/step_up_passkeys.rs` checks that the GET route is gone.
- A vitest case covers the card.
- The base branch added the `step_up_passkeys` keyspace without updating the keyspace count test, which was failing. Its expected count is now 41.

Local results:
- vtc-service lib: 1527 passed. The first full run failed only that keyspace count test; after the fix it passes on its own.
- `trust_task_manifest`: 8 passed.
- `openapi_snapshot`: 4 passed.
- `step_up_passkeys` (tsp, didcomm-harness): 3 passed.
- admin-ui lint passes, and vitest passes 43 files / 489 tests. That run includes the new card test.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`: clean. After the last test edit it was re-run for `vtc-service` only.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

* feat(vtc/git-ns): separation of duties and break-glass for elevated git rights

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#641.

- Fixed rule 7: no elevated self-grant (git.ns.admin, git.repo.create,
  git.repo.own) through grant 0.1/0.3, drift adopt, repo/adopt or reseat;
  refused git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed, naming cnm git break-glass.
- git-ns/right/break-glass/0.1: grant authority, or a community admin on a
  headless namespace; always an operation-bound passkey step-up
  (acl::bound_step_up, whose spent mark now yields its evidence); mandatory
  justification; immediate, no expiry; flagged breakGlass on the record.
- git-ns/right/ratify/0.1 and revoke 0.3: another administrator ratifies,
  bound to breakGlass.at; any community admin may revoke an unratified one,
  which policy cannot refuse. Unratified records do not count toward the
  last-owner and last-admin invariants.
- Visibility no policy can turn off: AuditEvent::GitNsBreakGlass at
  AuditSeverity::Critical with the step-up evidence, activity items, a signed
  git-ns/right/break-glass-notice/0.1 to every community admin and ns admin,
  view 0.4, GET /v1/git-ns/break-glass, and breakGlass on the rights rows.
- git_ns.rego settings: break_glass (enabled by default), a delay and a
  minimum justification; deny decisions on right.breakGlass and right.ratify.
- cnm: git break-glass, git ratify and git break-glass-list; git view flags
  break-glass rights; grant and revoke move to 0.3.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-admin-ui): break-glass banner, list, flags and passkey step-up

- A banner on every page for every administrator while any break-glass grant
  is unratified or pending; it clears only when one is ratified or revoked.
- Repos > Break-glass grants: ratify or revoke through the signed-task flow;
  the grantee is never offered Ratify. Hand-over commands are fish-safe.
- The break-glass flag next to every flagged right.
- An elevated self-grant is not offered; Break glass... is, with its
  justification and consequences stated.
- SignTaskDialog answers a stepUpRequest refusal with the passkey and
  re-sends the identical document; /admin/step-up completes a step-up
  handed over from cnm.
- Grant and revoke are sent as 0.3.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc/git-ns): serve grant and revoke at 0.3 only; refuse a self-adopt in the console

- git-ns/right/grant and git-ns/right/revoke are served at 0.3 only: 0.1 is
  dropped with no compatibility window, so no client reaches a grant that
  skips fixed rule 7 or a record answered without its breakGlass flag. The
  VTC's internals and the drift adoption use the 0.3 payload; vtc-client's
  git_ns_grant and git_ns_revoke are the 0.3 calls (the _v3 names and the
  0.1 methods are gone). Revoke's pre-DID-core subject accommodation goes
  with 0.1: 0.3's schema holds every subject to DID-core.
- Test: adopting drift on one's own linked forge account into git.repo.own
  is refused git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed, naming break-glass; nothing is
  written and the item stays outstanding.
- Test: grant and revoke 0.1 and 0.2 are not served.
- Console: adoptStanding never offers a viewer their own account as an
  elevated right; it hands the command to another administrator and names
  break-glass. The member page flags a break-glass right with
  BreakGlassChip.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): step-up passkeys a member enrols through an admin's invite

A git break-glass always needs a passkey gesture bound to the one request
(acl::bound_step_up), and a namespace admin who is no console user had no
passkey this community knew, so could never break the glass. Implements the
step-up credential of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#645.

- step_up_passkey: auth/passkey/enroll/invite/0.2 (purpose stepUp),
  enroll/redeem/{start,finish}/0.1 and revoke/{start,finish}/0.2 for an
  administrator acting for the member. The invite is a community admin's, at a
  stepped-up session, never to themselves, for a current member, with an
  Argon2id-hashed claim code shown once and never in the URL (the token rides
  in the fragment). Single use; five wrong codes void it; a wrong token and a
  wrong code are one refusal; a second passkey needs a gesture from the first.
- The credentials live in their own keyspace (step_up_passkeys) that login and
  session step-up never read. acl::bound_step_up offers them beside the
  actor's session passkeys and accepts them only for the actor's own step-up;
  a revoked one loses its mapping and cannot answer a step-up already pending.
- AuditEvent::StepUpPasskeyChanged (invited, registered, inviteInvalidated,
  revoked); the token and code are never recorded. Excluded from backup like
  passkey.
- Console: a Step-up passkeys card on the member page (invite showing the link
  and the claim code apart; revoke with the admin's own passkey), a
  /admin/enrol-step-up page reachable without signing in, and /admin/step-up
  answering unsigned when the browser holds no console key.
- cnm's step-up prompt names the step-up passkey. Docs in
  docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): serve members' step-up passkeys as Trust Tasks, redeemed by the member's own signature

Step-up passkey enrolment and management move onto the signed-document spine
(trust_tasks::step_up_passkey_tasks), so the same code serves them over TSP,
DIDComm and HTTPS. The REST invite, redeem and revoke routes are gone; only the
administrator's read of a member's credentials stays on REST, since no
published task covers it.

- auth/passkey/enroll/invite/0.2: signed by a community administrator, with a
  passkey gesture of theirs bound to the document; checks run before the
  gesture is asked for. The response (token, claim code) is not kept in the
  duplicate-delivery record.
- auth/passkey/enroll/redeem/start/0.1 must be signed by the member the invite
  names. A wrong code, or a signer the invite was not issued to, counts toward
  the five attempts. redeem/finish may come unsigned from the browser; signed,
  it must be the member's. A credential id already registered is refused.
- auth/passkey/revoke/{start,finish}/0.2 with subject: signed by a community
  administrator, verified with their own passkey (counter persisted).
- Generated trust-tasks 0.23 payload, response and error-code types replace the
  hand-written ones.
- auth/step-up/approve-response: the approver is the verified signer (or the
  admin its console key acts for), with no admin role required, so a member can
  answer a step-up asked of them. The proof is always required; the passkey is
  beside it, never instead (approve-response 0.5). The console no longer sends
  an unsigned answer: without a console key it shows an answer code, which
  cnm signs with the member's key.
- A former member's step-up passkeys are offered for nothing; expired invites
  and ceremonies are swept; long DIDs are abbreviated in WebAuthn user.name.
- cnm: `cnm git enrol-step-up-passkey <invite link>`, and answer-code handling
  in the step-up prompt. vtc-client exports the two type URIs.
- Console: the member card signs the invite and confirms the bound gesture;
  /admin/enrol-step-up points an invite link at cnm and finishes the
  redemption cnm starts; /admin/step-up hands a no-key member an answer code.
- Tests: spine tests per task over REST, DIDComm and TSP contexts; a
  live-mediator test over DIDComm, TSP and HTTPS; manifest census checks the
  console's document types against the dispatcher.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc): count the step-up passkey tasks in the spine's dispatch and proof censuses

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): list a member's step-up passkeys as auth/passkey/admin-list/0.1

An administrator's read of a member's step-up passkeys was
GET /v1/admin/step-up-passkeys, a bearer route with no Trust-Task binding,
because no published task let one subject read another's credentials.
trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#658 specifies auth/passkey/admin-list 0.1,
and this serves it on the spine, over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS alike.

title: feat(auth/passkey): an administrator lists one member's passkeys (admin-list 0.1)
body:
`auth/passkey/list` lists only the signer's own credentials and refuses a subject in the payload, by design. So nothing let an administrator see which step-up passkeys (#645) a member holds, or which `credentialId` to pass to `auth/passkey/revoke/start` 0.2 when revoking for them.

## `auth/passkey/admin-list` 0.1

- **Proof REQUIRED**, so the issuer is the administrator. The payload names `subject` and `purpose` (`session` | `stepUp`, with no default). The consumer checks, from its own state, that the administrator has authority over that subject. The payload grants nothing.
- **Refusals, in order:**
  1. `notAdministrator`, before the subject is looked at.
  2. `subjectUnknown`, also returned for a subject outside the administrator's authority, so the code cannot be used to probe.
  3. `purposeNotSupported`.
  4. `subjectNotMember`.
- **The response** is `{ subject, purpose, credentials }`. Each credential is a `ListedCredential`: `credentialId`, `deviceLabel`, `registeredAt`, `lastUsedAt`, `signCount`. It never carries key material, the public key or attestation, and `additionalProperties` is `false`. `auth/passkey/list` withholds the counter from the subject. This task shows it to the administrator, because the administrator is the operator who acts on a cloning signal.
- **`sideEffects: none`.** Listing does not change any counter or last-used time.
- **Privacy.** Only administrators with authority over the subject can list. The `auth/passkey` family audits issuance, redemption and revocation, but not reads. A consumer that does audit administrative reads SHOULD include this task.

Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings are regenerated. `npm run validate` and `npm run check-bindings` pass.

First consumer: the VTC admin console's member step-up passkey card (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure). It currently uses a bearer REST read, which this task replaces.

title: feat(vtc): step-up passkeys a member enrols through an admin's invite
body:
Implements the step-up credential specified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#645 (`auth/passkey`, trust-tasks 0.23), now on current `main`.

## Why

A git break-glass always needs a passkey gesture bound to that one request (`acl::bound_step_up`). A namespace admin who is not a console user acts only through signed documents, so the community knows no passkey of theirs and they could never break the glass. Their signing key alone must not be able to enrol one, or a stolen key would enrol the thief's passkey. So a step-up passkey takes two factors held by two parties: a community administrator's single-use invite with its claim code, and the member's own signature on the redemption.

## What

Every remote step is a Trust Task on the signed-document spine (`trust_tasks::step_up_passkey_tasks`). The same code serves them over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS. No REST route issues, redeems or revokes one.

| Task | Signed by | Authority |
|---|---|---|
| `auth/passkey/enroll/invite/0.2` (`purpose: stepUp`) | a community administrator | their ACL row, plus a passkey gesture of theirs bound to this document |
| `auth/passkey/enroll/redeem/start/0.1` | the member the invite names (required here, although the spec allows no proof) | the token, the claim code and the signer, together |
| `auth/passkey/enroll/redeem/finish/0.1` | the member, or nobody (the browser that made the passkey) | the ceremony the signed start opened |
| `auth/passkey/revoke/{start,finish}/0.2` with `subject` | a community administrator | their ACL row, plus a user-verified assertion from their own passkey |

The payloads, responses and error codes are the generated trust-tasks 0.23 types. No hand-written wire types or patched dependency remain.

**Invite rules**
- Only a community administrator can issue one, never to themselves, and only to a current member.
- An invite is single use and time-bounded: one hour by default, 24 h at most.
- It carries no role and no scopes.
- The token and the claim code are stored only as hashes. The code is Argon2id-hashed, shown once, and never in the URL.
- The invite response is not kept in the duplicate-delivery record, so the secret exists only in the one reply.

**Redemption rules**
- `redeem/start` must be signed by the invited member.
- A wrong code, or a signer the invite was not issued to, counts as a wrong attempt, and five void the invite. Both get the same refusal as a wrong token.
- A second step-up passkey needs a user-verified gesture from the first.
- A credential id already registered, as a session passkey or a step-up passkey, is refused.

**Step-up only**
- The credentials live in their own keyspace, `step_up_passkeys`, which login and session step-up never read.
- `acl::bound_step_up` offers them only to their own member, while that member is still a current member.

**Never instead of a proof**
- Every `auth/step-up/approve-response` must carry the approver's `assertionMethod` proof, as approve-response 0.5 requires; the passkey assertion is a second gate beside it.
- An unsigned answer, or one signed by anyone but the step-up's subject, is refused before the pending step-up is touched.
- The approve-response handler now takes the approver from the verified signer (or the admin a console key acts for) without requiring an admin role, so a member can answer a step-up asked of them.

**Audit**
- `AuditEvent::StepUpPasskeyChanged` records each stage: `invited`, `registered`, `inviteInvalidated` and `revoked`.
- Each use is the `OperationStepUpRecorded` row of the step-up it answered.
- The token and the code are never recorded.

**Retention and backup**: expired invites and ceremonies are swept. The `step_up_passkeys` keyspace is excluded from backup, like `passkey`.

**Clients**
- **cnm**
  - `cnm git enrol-step-up-passkey <invite link>` prompts for the claim code, signs `redeem/start`, and prints the link where the browser creates the passkey.
  - On a step-up refusal, cnm takes the page's **answer code** (the passkey assertion) and signs the approve-response with the member's key.
- **Console**
  - The *Step-up passkeys* card on the member page signs the invite, asks for the bound gesture as its own click, and revokes through the revoke tasks.
  - `/admin/enrol-step-up` shows the cnm command for an invite link, and finishes a redemption from the link cnm prints.
  - `/admin/step-up` signs with the console key when the browser has one. Otherwise it shows the answer code and never sends an answer unsigned.
- **vtc-client** exports the approve-response and redeem-start type URIs.

The console lists a member's credentials through `GET /v1/admin/step-up-passkeys?subject=`, for community administrators only. No published task covers this read: `auth/passkey/list` lists only the signer's own credentials.

**Docs**: `docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md` (*Step-up passkeys for members*), `backup-restore.md`, and `CLAUDE.md`.

## Tests

- **Spine unit tests** (`trust_tasks::step_up_passkey_tasks`, named by task) run every task as each transport hands it over:
  - the invite's bound gesture, and its refusals before any gesture is asked for;
  - redemption only by the invited member;
  - five wrong attempts void an invite;
  - the unsigned browser finish;
  - the second-passkey gesture;
  - approve-response needs the member's own proof;
  - an administrator cannot answer with a member's passkey;
  - a former member's passkey counts for nothing;
  - revocation stops a step-up already pending;
  - the audit rows.
- **`tests/step_up_passkeys.rs`** covers the same flow end to end over a live mediator (DIDComm and TSP) and over HTTPS. It also checks an unsigned answer is refused, and that no REST route serves these tasks.
- **Also passing**: `signed_step_up`, `admin_invites`, `trust_task_manifest` (console document types checked against the dispatcher), `openapi_snapshot`, `passkey_state`, `emergency_bootstrap`, cnm-cli, and `vtc-service` lib tests for passkey, step-up and `trust_tasks`.
- **Console**: `tsc`, `wire:check`, and vitest (new `EnrolStepUp.test.tsx`, plus answer-code and no-unsigned-answer cases).
- **Clippy** (`--workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`) and fmt are clean.

## Not in this PR

- **A member revoking their own step-up passkey.** `revoke/start` 0.2 allows it, but the gesture needs the same answer-code hand-over. An administrator revokes on the member's behalf.
- **Telling the member when a credential is bound or revoked.** The specs make this a SHOULD.
- **Moving the VTC's approve-response from 0.4 to 0.5.** The 0.5 rule (proof always required) is already enforced here.
- **Letting cnm's `git` commands choose TSP or DIDComm.** They still post to the VTC's HTTPS Trust Task endpoint, as all of them do today.

body:
feat(vtc): step-up passkeys a member enrols through an admin's invite (#1756)

* feat(vtc/git-ns): separation of duties and break-glass for elevated git rights

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#641.

- Fixed rule 7: no elevated self-grant (git.ns.admin, git.repo.create,
  git.repo.own) through grant 0.1/0.3, drift adopt, repo/adopt or reseat;
  refused git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed, naming cnm git break-glass.
- git-ns/right/break-glass/0.1: grant authority, or a community admin on a
  headless namespace; always an operation-bound passkey step-up
  (acl::bound_step_up, whose spent mark now yields its evidence); mandatory
  justification; immediate, no expiry; flagged breakGlass on the record.
- git-ns/right/ratify/0.1 and revoke 0.3: another administrator ratifies,
  bound to breakGlass.at; any community admin may revoke an unratified one,
  which policy cannot refuse. Unratified records do not count toward the
  last-owner and last-admin invariants.
- Visibility no policy can turn off: AuditEvent::GitNsBreakGlass at
  AuditSeverity::Critical with the step-up evidence, activity items, a signed
  git-ns/right/break-glass-notice/0.1 to every community admin and ns admin,
  view 0.4, GET /v1/git-ns/break-glass, and breakGlass on the rights rows.
- git_ns.rego settings: break_glass (enabled by default), a delay and a
  minimum justification; deny decisions on right.breakGlass and right.ratify.
- cnm: git break-glass, git ratify and git break-glass-list; git view flags
  break-glass rights; grant and revoke move to 0.3.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-admin-ui): break-glass banner, list, flags and passkey step-up

- A banner on every page for every administrator while any break-glass grant
  is unratified or pending; it clears only when one is ratified or revoked.
- Repos > Break-glass grants: ratify or revoke through the signed-task flow;
  the grantee is never offered Ratify. Hand-over commands are fish-safe.
- The break-glass flag next to every flagged right.
- An elevated self-grant is not offered; Break glass... is, with its
  justification and consequences stated.
- SignTaskDialog answers a stepUpRequest refusal with the passkey and
  re-sends the identical document; /admin/step-up completes a step-up
  handed over from cnm.
- Grant and revoke are sent as 0.3.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc/git-ns): serve grant and revoke at 0.3 only; refuse a self-adopt in the console

- git-ns/right/grant and git-ns/right/revoke are served at 0.3 only: 0.1 is
  dropped with no compatibility window, so no client reaches a grant that
  skips fixed rule 7 or a record answered without its breakGlass flag. The
  VTC's internals and the drift adoption use the 0.3 payload; vtc-client's
  git_ns_grant and git_ns_revoke are the 0.3 calls (the _v3 names and the
  0.1 methods are gone). Revoke's pre-DID-core subject accommodation goes
  with 0.1: 0.3's schema holds every subject to DID-core.
- Test: adopting drift on one's own linked forge account into git.repo.own
  is refused git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed, naming break-glass; nothing is
  written and the item stays outstanding.
- Test: grant and revoke 0.1 and 0.2 are not served.
- Console: adoptStanding never offers a viewer their own account as an
  elevated right; it hands the command to another administrator and names
  break-glass. The member page flags a break-glass right with
  BreakGlassChip.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): step-up passkeys a member enrols through an admin's invite

A git break-glass always needs a passkey gesture bound to the one request
(acl::bound_step_up), and a namespace admin who is no console user had no
passkey this community knew, so could never break the glass. Implements the
step-up credential of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#645.

- step_up_passkey: auth/passkey/enroll/invite/0.2 (purpose stepUp),
  enroll/redeem/{start,finish}/0.1 and revoke/{start,finish}/0.2 for an
  administrator acting for the member. The invite is a community admin's, at a
  stepped-up session, never to themselves, for a current member, with an
  Argon2id-hashed claim code shown once and never in the URL (the token rides
  in the fragment). Single use; five wrong codes void it; a wrong token and a
  wrong code are one refusal; a second passkey needs a gesture from the first.
- The credentials live in their own keyspace (step_up_passkeys) that login and
  session step-up never read. acl::bound_step_up offers them beside the
  actor's session passkeys and accepts them only for the actor's own step-up;
  a revoked one loses its mapping and cannot answer a step-up already pending.
- AuditEvent::StepUpPasskeyChanged (invited, registered, inviteInvalidated,
  revoked); the token and code are never recorded. Excluded from backup like
  passkey.
- Console: a Step-up passkeys card on the member page (invite showing the link
  and the claim code apart; revoke with the admin's own passkey), a
  /admin/enrol-step-up page reachable without signing in, and /admin/step-up
  answering unsigned when the browser holds no console key.
- cnm's step-up prompt names the step-up passkey. Docs in
  docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): serve members' step-up passkeys as Trust Tasks, redeemed by the member's own signature

Step-up passkey enrolment and management move onto the signed-document spine
(trust_tasks::step_up_passkey_tasks), so the same code serves them over TSP,
DIDComm and HTTPS. The REST invite, redeem and revoke routes are gone; only the
administrator's read of a member's credentials stays on REST, since no
published task covers it.

- auth/passkey/enroll/invite/0.2: signed by a community administrator, with a
  passkey gesture of theirs bound to the document; checks run before the
  gesture is asked for. The response (token, claim code) is not kept in the
  duplicate-delivery record.
- auth/passkey/enroll/redeem/start/0.1 must be signed by the member the invite
  names. A wrong code, or a signer the invite was not issued to, counts toward
  the five attempts. redeem/finish may come unsigned from the browser; signed,
  it must be the member's. A credential id already registered is refused.
- auth/passkey/revoke/{start,finish}/0.2 with subject: signed by a community
  administrator, verified with their own passkey (counter persisted).
- Generated trust-tasks 0.23 payload, response and error-code types replace the
  hand-written ones.
- auth/step-up/approve-response: the approver is the verified signer (or the
  admin its console key acts for), with no admin role required, so a member can
  answer a step-up asked of them. The proof is always required; the passkey is
  beside it, never instead (approve-response 0.5). The console no longer sends
  an unsigned answer: without a console key it shows an answer code, which
  cnm signs with the member's key.
- A former member's step-up passkeys are offered for nothing; expired invites
  and ceremonies are swept; long DIDs are abbreviated in WebAuthn user.name.
- cnm: `cnm git enrol-step-up-passkey <invite link>`, and answer-code handling
  in the step-up prompt. vtc-client exports the two type URIs.
- Console: the member card signs the invite and confirms the bound gesture;
  /admin/enrol-step-up points an invite link at cnm and finishes the
  redemption cnm starts; /admin/step-up hands a no-key member an answer code.
- Tests: spine tests per task over REST, DIDComm and TSP contexts; a
  live-mediator test over DIDComm, TSP and HTTPS; manifest census checks the
  console's document types against the dispatcher.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc): count the step-up passkey tasks in the spine's dispatch and proof censuses

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc-service): count the step-up passkey keyspace

This PR adds a keyspace, so ALL now lists 41 AppState keyspaces.

title: feat(vta-sdk): advertise TSPTransport in the push-gateway template

## Summary

- The push gateway (vti-push-gateway #34) now serves Trust Tasks over TSP, DIDComm, and HTTPS, but `vta-sdk/templates/push-gateway.json` only ever advertised a `DIDCommMessaging` service — TSP was undiscoverable for any client resolving the gateway's DID document alone.
- Adds an optional `SERVICE_TSP` null-pruning slot to the template, copying the exact mechanism and shape `vtc-host` already uses for its messaging transports (`SERVICE_TSP` / `vta_sdk::did_templates::tsp_service(mediator_did)`): both TSP and DIDComm name the same mediator DID, TSP first (canonical transport-preference order), and the slot prunes entirely when no mediator is supplied — a gateway minted without TSP renders unchanged.
- Updates `docs/02-vta/did-templates.md` and `docs/02-vta/personal-ai-agents.md`'s provisioning example to show supplying `SERVICE_TSP` via `pnm bootstrap provision-request --var`, and a one-line note in `docs/05-design-notes/mobile-agent-architecture.md` on the gateway's transport preference order.
- Adds test coverage in `vta-sdk/src/did_templates/tests.rs` mirroring the `vtc-host` messaging-transport tests: loads/validates, DIDComm-alone when no mediator is supplied (regression guard), and both transports in canonical order when one is.

Pairs with vti-push-gateway #34.
