## [0.54.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.53.0...vta-sdk-v0.54.0) — 2026-09-26 ### Security - **acl**: No principal widens its own entry, and no grant exceeds its granter (VTI-ACL-052, VTI-ACL-053) ([#1738](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1738)) * security(acl)!: no principal widens its own entry, and no grant exceeds its granter (VTI-ACL-052, VTI-ACL-053) A context-scoped admin, such as a companion service's credential (`--role admin --contexts vgi-bridge`), could raise its own authority. `update_acl` had no self check and no test either way. Tests written against main confirm every case below. Adding a foreign context or raising the role was already refused. What went through was clearing any narrowing on the caller's own entry, and minting a sibling entry that carried none of it: - Self-update to clear its capability narrowing, drop its key filter, or extend its expiry. All three succeeded. - A create for another DID it controls, in the same context, with none of its own narrowing: full capabilities, no key filter, no expiry. - An update that cleared another entry's narrowing past what the caller itself held. - Self role change (`acl/change-role`). - Rotation (`acl/swap-key`) rebuilt the entry field by field. It dropped `expires_at`, `allowed_keys`, `approve_scope` and the step-up fields, so a one-hour bootstrap grant became permanent. It also dropped `created_by`. This violated VTI-CLT-029. - An initiator could grant approve authority it did not hold (VTI-ACL-042). - A context admin could update or delete an entry that also acts in a context it does not administer, because overlap was enough. VTA (`operations/acl.rs`, the choke point for REST, DIDComm, TSP and the Trust Task spine): - update and change-role refuse the caller's own entry (VTI-ACL-052). Delete already did. - create, update and change-role measure the resulting entry against the caller's stored entry (`validate_within_caller`, VTI-ACL-053). The entry must not exceed the caller's effective capabilities (additive ones stay under VTI-ACL-033), key filter, expiry, or confer authority (VTI-ACL-042). A caller with no live entry writes nothing. - update, change-role and delete require the caller to cover every context the entry acts or approves in, not just overlap (VTI-ACL-050 as tightened). - update re-runs the role and act-scope checks on the patched entry, so a role change alone cannot turn "nowhere" into "everywhere". - swap-key copies the entry exactly and only moves the subject. It refuses an expired entry (VTI-CLT-029). VTC (`routes/acl.rs`, `routes/admin/invites.rs`, `routes/members/update.rs`): - An `acl/grant` rewrite of your own entry is refused. Before, a re-grant with no `expiresAt` made a time-boxed admin permanent. - `acl/change-role` refuses your own entry in either direction; the ceremony already refused self-promotion. - `vtc/members/update` refuses a role or label change on your own entry. - Rewrite, change-role and revoke (including scoped revoke) require full coverage for every role, not only admin targets. - A grant cannot outlive the granter's expiry, and a granter with no live entry is refused. - `vtc/admin/invites/create` requires an unrestricted admin. It writes a community-wide admin entry, and a context admin could previously invite a DID it controls into one. - **vta-sdk**: A consent request must be signed under authentication ([#1766](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1766))

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.23.2
body:
### Added

- **vta/attestation**: Status, report and config-report as Trust Tasks ([#654](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/654))

A VTA running in a TEE answers three attestation reads today only as
  unauthenticated REST routes (`GET /attestation/status`, `POST`/`GET
  /attestation/report`, `POST /attestation/config-report`), and a DIDComm
  protocol arm nothing sends to. Specifying them lets the agent serve them on its
  Trust Task spine over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS alike, and retire both.

  - `vta/attestation/status/0.1` — which TEE the agent detected at boot. A claim,
    not evidence; it tells the verifier what to ask for.
  - `vta/attestation/report/0.1` — fresh evidence binding a verifier-chosen
    32-byte nonce and the agent's DID. The nonce is REQUIRED: there is no
    nonce-less (cached) form, because a report nobody asked for is one anybody can
    replay.
  - `vta/attestation/config-report/0.1` — fresh evidence binding the nonce and
    the SHA-384 of the canonical, secret-free view of the configuration the
    enclave booted, so a tenant can check operator-supplied settings (its KMS key)
    before onboarding.

  All three: request proof OPTIONAL (a verifier asks before it trusts the agent,
  often with no key the agent knows, and the nonce is what makes an answer its
  own), response proof REQUIRED (the agent's `authentication` signature ties its
  DID to the evidence it returns), no side effects, transient retention. Each
  spec states the verifier's checks — vendor root, measured image, the nonce
  inside the evidence, and the DID the evidence binds against the document's
  issuer.

  Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated; `npm run build`,
  `check-bindings` and the Rust tests pass.

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.3.1` → `0.3.2` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vta): attestation status/report/config-report and services/report as Trust Tasks
body:
Four VTA reads existed only as REST routes (the attestation reads are unauthenticated; the mediator report sits behind a bearer token), plus a DIDComm arm that nothing sends to. With specs, the agent can serve them on its Trust Task spine over TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS alike, and retire the routes.

| Spec | Request proof | Response proof | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vta/attestation/status/0.1` | OPTIONAL | REQUIRED | Which TEE the agent detected. A claim, not evidence. |
| `vta/attestation/report/0.1` | OPTIONAL | REQUIRED | Fresh evidence binding a **required** verifier nonce and the agent's DID. There's no nonce-less (cached) form, because it would be replayable. |
| `vta/attestation/config-report/0.1` | OPTIONAL | REQUIRED | Fresh evidence binding the nonce and the SHA-384 of the secret-free view of the booted config. |
| `vta/services/report/0.1` | **REQUIRED** | RECOMMENDED | Per-mediator inbound counts and each sender's last-seen mediator. Operator-only, because it's a contact log of third parties. |

Why the attestation requests don't need a proof: a verifier asks before it trusts the agent, often with no key the agent knows. What makes each answer the verifier's own is its nonce. Each response is signed with the agent's `authentication` key, which ties its DID to the evidence. Each spec lists the verifier's checks: vendor root, measured image, the nonce inside the evidence, and the DID the evidence binds against the document's issuer.

`did-log` is deliberately not specified. It's the did:webvh `did.jsonl`, which the method requires to be served over HTTPS for resolution. It's a DID-method artifact, not a remote API.

Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings are regenerated. `npm run build` (strict Security & Privacy lint) and `check-bindings` pass, and so do the Rust tests (900). The implementation in verifiable-trust-infrastructure follows once a trust-tasks-rs release carries these.

title: security(acl)!: no principal widens its own entry, and no grant exceeds its granter (VTI-ACL-052, VTI-ACL-053)
body:
## Confirmed: self-widening was real, though not on the axes first suspected

Tests written against `main` all fail there, which confirms each case. The test is named in brackets.

Take a context-scoped admin, for example the git bridge's credential (`--role admin --contexts vgi-bridge`). Two widenings were **already refused**: adding a foreign context to its own entry (`require_context`), and raising its role (it is already admin, and `acl/update` requires admin). The following **went through**:

| Path | What went through on `main` | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `acl/update` on own entry | Clearing its own capability narrowing, dropping its own key filter (`allowedKeys: null`), extending its own expiry, relabelling [`vti_acl_052_a_context_admin_cannot_update_its_own_entry`] | VTI-ACL-052 |
| `acl/change-role` on own entry | Accepted [`vti_acl_052_a_subject_cannot_change_its_own_role`] | VTI-ACL-052 |
| `acl/grant` for a second DID it controls | A narrowed admin mints a sibling in the same context with full capabilities, no key filter and no expiry [`vti_acl_053_a_narrowed_admin_cannot_mint_a_wider_sibling`] | VTI-ACL-053 (new, spec PR below) |
| `acl/update` on a peer | Clearing a peer's narrowing past what the caller holds [`vti_acl_053_an_update_cannot_widen_another_entry_past_the_caller`] | VTI-ACL-053 |
| `acl/swap-key` | Dropped `expiresAt`, `allowedKeys`, `approve` and step-up, so a one-hour bootstrap grant became permanent; also reset `createdBy`. This is self-service widening by the subject alone [`vti_clt_029_a_rotation_preserves_the_entry_exactly`] | VTI-CLT-029 |
| `acl/grant` by an initiator | Conferring approve authority it does not hold [`vti_acl_042_an_initiator_cannot_confer_approve_authority_it_lacks`] | VTI-ACL-042 |
| update / change-role / delete | A context-`a` admin changing or removing an entry acting in `[a, b]` [`a_context_admin_cannot_manage_an_entry_reaching_outside_its_contexts`] | VTI-ACL-050 (tightened) |
| any ACL write | By a caller with no ACL entry [`a_caller_without_an_entry_cannot_grant`] | VTI-ACL-001 |

On the VTC:

- `acl/grant` could rewrite the caller's own entry, so re-granting with no `expiresAt` made a time-boxed admin permanent.
- Rewrite, scoped revoke and non-admin role changes needed only overlap.
- **`vtc/admin/invites/create` let any context-scoped admin mint a community-wide (unrestricted) admin entry for any DID, including one it controls.**

## Change

**VTA** (`vta-service/src/operations/acl.rs`, the single choke point every transport reaches):

- REST `routes/acl.rs`, DIDComm `messaging/handlers.rs`, the Trust Task spine `trust_tasks/acl.rs`, and TSP (via the spine) all go through it.
- `refuse_self_modification` on update and change-role. Delete already refused the caller's own entry.
- `validate_within_caller` on create, update and change-role. The resulting entry is measured against the **caller's stored entry**, not its token:
  - Effective capabilities must be a subset of the caller's. Additive `persona-holder` stays under VTI-ACL-033 (super-admin only).
  - The key filter must be a subset of the caller's.
  - The expiry must be no later than the caller's.
  - Approve contexts must be ones the caller can confer in (`acl_entry_can_confer`).
  - A caller with no live entry is refused.
- `caller_covers_entry`: update, change-role and delete require the caller to administer every context the entry acts or approves in.
- update re-runs `validate_role_assignment` and `validate_acl_modification` on the patched entry.
- swap-key clones the entry and changes only the subject. It refuses an expired entry.

**VTC:**

- `routes/acl.rs`: no self-rewrite and no self role change. Coverage is required for every role on rewrite, change-role and revoke. A grant's expiry is bounded by the granter's entry. A granter with no live entry is refused.
- `routes/admin/invites.rs`: an unrestricted admin is required.
- `routes/members/update.rs`: no self role or label change.

**Spec first:** trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#44 adds VTI-ACL-053 (grants are bounded by the granter on every axis) and tightens VTI-ACL-050 from overlap to coverage. VTI-ACL-052, VTI-ACL-042 and VTI-CLT-029 were already normative.

## Breaks (all intended; test instances only, no migration)

- **Onboarding expiry now survives rotation** (VTI-CLT-029). A bootstrap entry granted with `--expires 1h` is still an expiring entry after `acl/swap-key`, and the sweeper removes it when it expires. Grant the bootstrap entry without an expiry, or have an administrator lift it after the swap; the subject cannot lift it.
  - This affects `pnm contexts create --admin-expires`, `vti-secrets` `IntegrationOnboarding`, and any script that relied on the swap discarding the TTL.
  - **Provision-integration rollover by an expiring ephemeral needs the hand-off marker.** Without it the rollover is refused. In the documented flow (`pnm contexts create --admin-did <ephemeral> --admin-expires 1h`), the ephemeral itself is the authenticated caller. Its long-term successor has no expiry, so VTI-ACL-053 refuses it before the ephemeral is retired. The row is kept, but the admin DID minted just before the refusal is left unused. It still works when the ephemeral is granted without an expiry (the rollover retires it), or when an operator whose own entry does not expire runs the provisioning. See **One-time hand-off**.
- A super-admin can no longer relabel its own entry (VTC console, `pnm acl update` on self).
- A narrowed or expiring caller can grant only inside its own bounds. This includes provision-integration run by an operator whose own entry expires.
- An initiator needs approve authority to confer it.
- Entries acting in several contexts are manageable only by an admin covering all of them.
- Context admins cannot send admin invites.
- ACL writes by a DID with no entry are refused. Test fixtures now seed the caller's entry: `TestVtc::token`, `bootstrap_test_vta`, and the VTA ACL unit tests.

## One-time hand-off (VTI-ACL-054 – 058, option (a))

Spec first: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#44 now also adds VTI-ACL-054 – 058 and VTI-CLT-017.

- **Setting it.** Only the granter can set the marker, and only at creation: `acl/grant` with `ext."org.openvtc.handoff": true`, on every transport.
  - It requires an expiry and a subject other than the caller, and the caller's own entry must carry no marker.
  - It records the granter's role, contexts, capabilities, approve scope, key filter and expiry at that moment.
  - An update naming it is refused. `acl/swap-key` drops it.
- **Using it.** `operations::acl::exercise_handoff`:
  - Only the subject may use it, only while its entry is unexpired, and only once.
  - The successor must fit both the marked entry (its expiry aside) and the recorded granter authority. It takes the granter's expiry.
- **Atomicity and audit.**
  - An `acl.handoff` audit row is written before the commit. If that write fails, nothing is committed.
  - The commit is `KeyspaceHandle::move_if_unchanged`, a new compare-and-move under the keyspace write lock: it writes the successor and removes the marked row only if the row is unchanged since it was validated.
  - A process-wide lock also covers the vsock backend, whose move is not atomic across round-trips.
- **Other admins.** A time-boxed admin without the marker still gets the VTI-ACL-053 refusal (VTI-ACL-058).
- **Provision-integration.** It uses the hand-off when the ephemeral itself rolls over and holds a marker. A lost race is not treated as a harmless retry.
- **Clients.**
  - `pnm contexts create --admin-handoff`, `pnm acl create --handoff`, `cnm contexts create --admin-handoff`, and the offline `vta contexts create --admin-handoff`.
  - SDK: `CreateAclRequest::handoff()` and `AclEntryResponse::handoff()`.
  - The mediator, WebVH and VTC setup hints, and the docs, now include `--admin-handoff`.
  - No migration: rows without the field have no marker.
- **Break.** Onboarding flows that roll over must add `--admin-handoff` to the grant.

## Not changed (reported)

- The token's role and contexts are still snapshots, so a demoted admin keeps its old role in the token until `/auth/refresh`. That is VTI-ACL-080 and a separate issue. The capability, key and expiry bounds here are read live.
- `device/register` still writes `kind` and the device binding onto the caller's own entry. That is metadata, not authority, and it is a spec'd self-service step.
- A context-scoped admin can still create *other* entries up to its own authority in its context. Narrowing a companion service below "context admin" needs the capability discussed on the parent task, not this PR.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib -- operations::acl`: 45 pass, including 8 new ones that fail on `main`.
- Provision-integration and trust-task tests use the seeded operator.
- `cargo test -p vta-service --test api_integration`: 132 pass. The token helpers now seed the caller's entry.
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib -- provision_integration`: 65 pass, including the new rollover test.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --test acl_canonical --test admin_invites`: 27 and 3 pass.
- `unrestricted_admin_consent` (from #1718): a last unrestricted admin's self-demotion is now refused with 403 VTI-ACL-052 instead of reaching the 409 attrition check. The entry is unchanged either way.
- `admin-ui/openapi.json` and `wire.ts` regenerated (invite 403 description).
- New VTC tests:
  - `acl_canonical`: `vti_acl_052_an_admin_cannot_rewrite_its_own_entry`, `vti_acl_052_an_admin_cannot_change_its_own_role`, `vti_acl_053_an_expiring_admin_cannot_grant_past_its_own_expiry`, `a_context_admin_cannot_manage_an_entry_straddling_its_scope`.
  - `admin_invites`: `a_context_scoped_admin_cannot_invite_a_community_wide_admin`.
- Hand-off:
  - `operations::acl`: 51 pass, 6 new. The one rollover succeeds; a second is refused; one after expiry is refused; one widening past the granter is refused; the holder cannot set the marker; a concurrent double rollover yields one success; there is no hand-off without a marker.
  - Swap-key drops the marker.
  - `provision_integration`: 66 pass, including `a_marked_ephemeral_rolls_over_once`.
  - `vti-common` `move_if_unchanged`: 2 pass (16-way race, changed or occupied row).
  - `vta-sdk` `acl_management` and `provision_client`: pass, including the update refusal.


## Merge order and sync with `main`

**trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#44 merges first.** This PR follows it. The spec's IDs were rechecked against the spec's `main` (#42, #43, #45): nothing collides, and nothing was renumbered.

Merged `main` (trust-tasks 0.23 / 0.23.1, #1733, #1734, #1739, #1740, #1743, #1752, #1757, #1765 – #1770, git-ns). The merge was clean and touched none of `admin_consent.rs`, `task_consent.rs` or `trust_task_push.rs`.

- **Transports.** Every ACL operation this PR changes runs through the shared `operations::acl` functions. That covers `grant_from_entry` (the hand-off marker travels in the entry's `ext`), `update_from_params`, `revoke_by_subject` and `swap_acl`. The Trust Task handlers in `trust_tasks/acl.rs` call them over every transport, behind the sender-bound proof spine. The REST routes are thin adapters over the same calls.
- **Hand-off.** The exercise is part of the shared `provision_integration` operation, which the `provision/integration/0.2` Trust Task reaches, as do the REST adapter and the offline CLI. `move_if_unchanged` and the vsock lock compile and pass against `main`'s store.
- **Known gap on the VTC, not introduced here.** The VTC exposes `acl/grant` and `acl/change-role` as Trust Tasks. On `main`, its ACL list, show and **revoke** exist only as REST routes (`routes/acl.rs::delete_acl`). The VTI-ACL-050 coverage check this PR adds to revoke therefore lives on that REST route. Moving VTC ACL revoke, list and show onto Trust Tasks is follow-up work.

Re-run after the merge (`--all-features`):

- vta-service:
  - `operations::acl`: 51 pass
  - `provision_integration`: 66 pass
  - `--test api_integration`: 132 pass
- vti-common `store`: 117 pass
- vtc-service:
  - `acl_canonical`: 27 pass
  - `admin_invites`: 3 pass
  - `unrestricted_admin_consent`: 19 pass
  - lib `routes::acl`: 17 pass
- pnm-cli: 98 pass
- cnm-cli: 85 pass
- vta-sdk `acl`: pass
- clippy `--workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` is clean, and fmt is clean.

title: security(acl)!: no principal widens its own entry, and no grant exceeds its granter (VTI-ACL-052, VTI-ACL-053) (#1738)
body:
security(acl)!: no principal widens its own entry, and no grant exceeds its granter (VTI-ACL-052, VTI-ACL-053) (#1738)

* security(acl)!: no principal widens its own entry, and no grant exceeds its granter (VTI-ACL-052, VTI-ACL-053)

A context-scoped admin, such as a companion service's credential
(`--role admin --contexts vgi-bridge`), could raise its own authority.
`update_acl` had no self check and no test either way. Tests written
against main confirm every case below. Adding a foreign context or
raising the role was already refused. What went through was clearing
any narrowing on the caller's own entry, and minting a sibling entry
that carried none of it:

- Self-update to clear its capability narrowing, drop its key filter,
  or extend its expiry. All three succeeded.
- A create for another DID it controls, in the same context, with none
  of its own narrowing: full capabilities, no key filter, no expiry.
- An update that cleared another entry's narrowing past what the caller
  itself held.
- Self role change (`acl/change-role`).
- Rotation (`acl/swap-key`) rebuilt the entry field by field. It dropped
  `expires_at`, `allowed_keys`, `approve_scope` and the step-up fields,
  so a one-hour bootstrap grant became permanent. It also dropped
  `created_by`. This violated VTI-CLT-029.
- An initiator could grant approve authority it did not hold
  (VTI-ACL-042).
- A context admin could update or delete an entry that also acts in a
  context it does not administer, because overlap was enough.

VTA (`operations/acl.rs`, the choke point for REST, DIDComm, TSP and the
Trust Task spine):

- update and change-role refuse the caller's own entry (VTI-ACL-052).
  Delete already did.
- create, update and change-role measure the resulting entry against
  the caller's stored entry (`validate_within_caller`, VTI-ACL-053). The
  entry must not exceed the caller's effective capabilities (additive
  ones stay under VTI-ACL-033), key filter, expiry, or confer authority
  (VTI-ACL-042). A caller with no live entry writes nothing.
- update, change-role and delete require the caller to cover every
  context the entry acts or approves in, not just overlap
  (VTI-ACL-050 as tightened).
- update re-runs the role and act-scope checks on the patched entry, so
  a role change alone cannot turn "nowhere" into "everywhere".
- swap-key copies the entry exactly and only moves the subject. It
  refuses an expired entry (VTI-CLT-029).

VTC (`routes/acl.rs`, `routes/admin/invites.rs`,
`routes/members/update.rs`):

- An `acl/grant` rewrite of your own entry is refused. Before, a re-grant
  with no `expiresAt` made a time-boxed admin permanent.
- `acl/change-role` refuses your own entry in either direction; the
  ceremony already refused self-promotion.
- `vtc/members/update` refuses a role or label change on your own entry.
- Rewrite, change-role and revoke (including scoped revoke) require
  full coverage for every role, not only admin targets.
- A grant cannot outlive the granter's expiry, and a granter with no
  live entry is refused.
- `vtc/admin/invites/create` requires an unrestricted admin. It writes
  a community-wide admin entry, and a context admin could previously
  invite a DID it controls into one.

Spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#44 adds VTI-ACL-053 and tightens
VTI-ACL-050 to coverage.

BREAKING CHANGE:
- Onboarding entries created with an expiry keep it after rotation. An
  administrator must lift it; the subject cannot.
- A super-admin can no longer relabel its own entry.
- A caller whose entry is narrowed or expiring can grant only within
  those bounds.
- An initiator needs approve authority to confer it.
- Entries straddling contexts are manageable only by an admin covering
  all of them.
- Context admins cannot send admin invites.
- An ACL write by a DID with no entry is refused.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(acl): seed the caller's own entry, and pin the expiring-ephemeral rollover (VTI-ACL-053)

An ACL write is bounded by the writer's stored entry, so a bearer with
no row behind it describes a caller that cannot exist. The VTA
api_integration and test_support token helpers now write that row when
the test has not seeded one.

The VTC self-promotion and self-grant tests now expect the VTI-ACL-052
refusal, which runs before the ceremony's own check.

New: an ephemeral with a time-boxed row that is itself the caller of
provision-integration cannot roll over to a permanent successor. The
row is kept.

Error strings no longer carry runs of spaces from a lost line
continuation.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(vtc-admin-ui): regenerate the API document for the unrestricted-admin invite refusal

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc): a self-demotion is refused as a self-modification before attrition (VTI-ACL-052)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(acl)!: a one-time hand-off the granter marks at creation (VTI-ACL-054 – 058)

VTI-ACL-053 refuses an entry that outlives its writer. That includes the
long-term admin an expiring ephemeral writes for itself through
provision-integration, which is the documented onboarding flow. Nothing
about a time-boxed entry tells a bootstrap apart from any other
short-lived admin, so the exemption is now the granter's explicit,
recorded decision.

Setting it (VTI-ACL-054):
- `acl/grant` with `ext."org.openvtc.handoff": true`, on every
  transport.
- The marker needs an expiry and a subject other than the caller, and
  the caller's own entry must carry no marker.
- It records the granter's role, contexts, capabilities, approve scope,
  key filter and expiry at that moment.
- An update naming it is refused (`UpdateAclBody::capabilities`).
- `acl/swap-key` drops it.

Using it (VTI-ACL-055 – 057), in `operations::acl::exercise_handoff`:
- Only the subject may exercise it, only while its entry is unexpired,
  and only once.
- The successor must fit both the marked entry (its expiry aside) and
  the recorded granter authority. It takes the granter's expiry.
- An `acl.handoff` audit row is written before the commit. The rollover
  is abandoned if that write fails.
- The commit is `KeyspaceHandle::move_if_unchanged`, a new
  compare-and-move under the keyspace write lock. It writes the
  successor and removes the marked row only if the row still holds the
  bytes that were validated. A process-wide lock also covers the vsock
  backend.

Provision-integration takes this path when the ephemeral itself rolls
over and holds a marker. Otherwise the ordinary bounded grant applies,
and without a marker an expiring ephemeral is still refused
(VTI-ACL-058). A lost race is not treated as a retry, since its
successor was never written.

Clients:
- `pnm contexts create --admin-handoff`, `pnm acl create --handoff`,
  `cnm contexts create --admin-handoff`, and the offline
  `vta contexts create --admin-handoff`.
- `CreateAclRequest::handoff()` and `AclEntryResponse::handoff()`.
- The setup hints printed by the mediator, WebVH and VTC wizards and the
  docs now include `--admin-handoff`.

Rows without the field have no marker. No migration.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: Bound every access control entry by its writer's own, and require full cover to modify one
body:
VTI-ACL-052 forbids a subject to modify its own entry. Nothing stopped the same subject from writing a wider entry for a second identifier it controls. VTI-ACL-042 bounds approve authority and VTI-ACL-071 bounds delegation, but an ordinary grant was bounded on role and context list only. Capabilities, key narrowing and expiry had no bound, so a narrowed context administrator could mint a sibling entry for a DID it holds with none of its own narrowing.

- **VTI-ACL-053 (new).** A caller MUST NOT create or modify an entry, for any subject, that holds authority the caller's own entry does not. This applies on every axis: role, effective capabilities, key narrowing, expiry and approve scope. Additive capabilities stay under VTI-ACL-033. The check is evaluated against the stored entry, not the token, and a caller with no live entry is refused.
- **VTI-ACL-050 (tightened).** Modifying or removing an entry requires the caller's act scope to *cover* the entry's act and approve scopes, not just overlap them. One entry has one capability set, one key filter and one expiry across all its contexts, so an overlapping administrator could change authority in contexts it does not hold. Overlap stays the rule for reading (VTI-ACL-051).
- **VTI-ACL-054 – 058 (new): one-time hand-off.** VTI-ACL-053 also refuses the long-term entry a bootstrap identifier writes for its successor, because that entry outlives its writer.
  - The granter may mark the bootstrap entry at creation. The marker records the granter's authority at that moment.
  - The subject may exercise it exactly once, while the entry is live. The successor is bounded by both the marked entry and the recorded granter authority, and the granter's expiry takes the place of the entry's own.
  - The rollover is atomic, and at most one of concurrent attempts succeeds.
  - It is audited before the commit, and a node that cannot record it does not commit it.
  - No update or rotation can set, extend or carry the marker, and a node MUST NOT infer a hand-off without it.
  - VTI-CLT-017 requires the marker in onboarding flows where the bootstrap identifier writes its own successor.
- **Rationale.** It explains why VTI-ACL-052 and VTI-ACL-053 are each empty without the other. It also explains why the rotation carve-out cannot be abused, since VTI-CLT-029 preserves every axis.

The implementation follows in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure (linked from there).

`npm run render` completes.


## Merge order

**This PR merges first**, then OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1738, which implements it and cites these requirement IDs.

Synced with `main` (#42, #43 and #45). The merge was clean, and the new IDs (VTI-ACL-053 – 058, VTI-CLT-017, and the tightened VTI-ACL-050) collide with nothing `main` added, so nothing was renumbered. `npm run render` passes with no errors.

body:
Bound every access control entry by its writer's own, and require full cover to modify one (#44)

* Bound every access control entry by its writer's own, and require full cover to modify one

VTI-ACL-052 forbids a subject to modify its own entry, but nothing stopped

key and a one-hour expiry could mint a sibling entry for a DID it holds,
with the same scope and none of the narrowing.

capabilities (additive ones stay under VTI-ACL-033), key narrowing,

act and approve scopes, not merely overlap them. One entry carries one
capability set, one key filter and one expiry across all its contexts,

subject's authority in contexts it does not administer. Overlap remains
the rule for reading (VTI-ACL-051).

empty without the other, and why the rotation exception cannot be used

* Let a granter mark a bootstrap entry as a one-time hand-off (VTI-ACL-054 – 058)

title: feat(credential-exchange)!: every step is a signed Trust Task on the spine, over any transport
body:
Every credential-exchange step — offer, request, issue, query, present — and
the VTC's `vtc/members/request-vmc` and `join-requests/submit-receipt` pushes
were bare DIDComm messages typed as their task URI, served beside the binding
envelope. `bindings/didcomm/0.2` §2 requires a consumer to refuse that
carriage; it skipped the spine's proof, freshness, recipient and replay checks;
and no transport but DIDComm could carry it. They were never missing a TSP
binding. Each is a signed Trust Task now.

VTC
- Pushes `offer`, `issue`, `query`, `request-vmc` and `submit-receipt` through
  the durable push engine (TSP > DIDComm > REST, escalating on no delivery
  evidence) as documents signed with its operational key under
  `authentication` — `credentials::delivery::push_document`, the one outbound
  funnel. `AppState::send_to_member` and `push_to_holder` are gone.
- Serves `credential-exchange/request` and `present` on the dispatcher, from
  every transport. None of the five steps defines a response, so what goes
  back on the carrying transport is the SPEC §4.4.2 empty `#response`
  acknowledgement; the answer is the next step, pushed on the thread (`issue`
  after `request`, threaded on the offer; `submit-receipt` after `present`,
  threaded on the query, to whoever sent it).
- The bare `request`/`present` arms are deleted; typed as themselves they are
  refused naming the envelope.
- The git-ns break-glass notice (#1745) was the last caller of the removed
  DIDComm-only send; it now goes through the push engine too, signed with the
  operational key under `authentication` like the removal notice it copies.

VTA (holder)
- Serves `offer`, `issue` and `query` on the spine and pushes `request` and
  `present` back. They are counterparty tasks: an issuer or verifier holds no
  ACL entry here, so they dispatch on a zero-authority claim beside the
  ceremony carve-out (`is_counterparty_task`), and each handler acts with the
  VTA's own authority under the gate it always had — an offer only with a
  configured `credential_holder_did`, a presentation only to a trusted verifier
  or after operator approval.
- This restores `query`, whose bare arm #1739 deleted, leaving a holder that
  could not answer a verifier. A deferred query is answered with silence (an
  acknowledgement would claim a task not yet performed); `pending-approve` now
  also pushes the `present` to the verifier on the query's thread.
- The bare `offer`/`issue` arms are deleted. The helpers only the TEE
  attestation arms still use are gated on `tee` until those arms go.

Breaking (wire): a holder or wallet must read the pushed documents and send
`request`/`present` as signed documents with `threadId`. openvtc #392 is the
companion and is merged.

Not fixed here, found on the way: the push engine carries one signed document
for the whole delivery window, while a receiving VTA refuses an `issuedAt`
older than ten minutes, so a holder offline when its credential is pushed gets
it `expired` (removal notices share this). And a counterparty's `issue` or
deferred `query` still costs this VTA a durable write from any sender, as the
bare handlers did; a floor like the ceremony one is a follow-up.

Tests: VTC harness `offer → request → issue` and `query → present` round trips
over DIDComm with document, proof and thread assertions, and a bare-step
refusal; VTA counterparty carve-out, `issue` stored and acknowledged, `offer`
declined without a holder DID; conformance witnesses for the three steps the
VTA now dispatches.

## Merge order
openvtc #392 (the holder side) is merged, so this can go now.

## Local runs (before the last rebase onto main)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. The three reduced-feature `vta-service` clippy runs: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: one failure, the missing conformance witnesses for the three new VTA steps. Added; they pass.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: two census failures (the dispatched and proof-required counts). Fixed; the trust_tasks tests pass.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --features didcomm-harness,tsp --tests`: 2240 passed, 0 failed.

After rebasing onto main (#1745, #1746, #1770), the only conflict was compile-level: the break-glass notice's call to the removed send. That's fixed above. CI is the check on the rebased tree; I'm rerunning the VTC suites locally too.

## Summary

- Bump `trust-tasks-rs` to 0.23.1 and `trust-tasks-capability-client` to 0.23.1 (the only `trust-tasks-*` crates that published a 0.23.1); `Cargo.lock` still resolves exactly one `trust-tasks-rs` node.

title: fix(openvtc): read pushed credential-exchange documents, answer request-vmc only when signed
body:
A VTC now pushes every credential-exchange step and `vtc/members/request-vmc` as a signed Trust Task document, over TSP or DIDComm (in the binding envelope), instead of a bare DIDComm message typed as its task URI. That's the companion VTI change, "credential exchange onto the Trust Task spine". This PR makes openvtc take them only in that form.

## What changes
- **`issue`:** `issued_credential::verify_issued_delivery` checks two things. First, the delivery document's proof: issuer and signer must both be the sender, under `authentication`. Then the credential's own proof. The dispatcher's credential job carries the whole document. `credential_in_issue` reads only a document whose `issuer` is the sender. A bare body is refused.
- **Vetter grant:** additionally requires `wire::open` before the grant is considered. It's read from the payload, where a current VTC puts it; before this it was read from the body root and missed.
- **`request-vmc`:** answered only after the operational-document check (signed, addressed to the persona, fresh, not seen before), because answering it signs and sends this member's VMC.
- `join-requests/submit-receipt` already read the payload and was verified, so it needed nothing.

**Breaking (wire)** and **(library)**, recorded in the CHANGELOG. Deployments are recreated, so no compatibility shim.

## Merge order
The stack it was built on (#381, #383, #384, #386, #387) is on `main`; this is rebased onto it. Merge this **before** the VTI change (verifiable-trust-infrastructure credential exchange onto the Trust Task spine), which makes the VTC send the signed documents this requires.

## Testing
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test --workspace -- --include-ignored`: 1690 passed, 0 failed (includes the ignored vetting e2e)
- New tests:
  - a pushed issue document is read;
  - one from someone other than its issuer is not read;
  - a bare body is not read;
  - `request-vmc` waits for the signature;
  - a bare vetter grant is refused;
  - a relayed vetter grant is refused.

title: fix(openvtc): read pushed credential-exchange documents, answer request-vmc only when signed (#392)
body:
fix(openvtc): read pushed credential-exchange documents, answer request-vmc only when signed (#392)

* fix(openvtc): read pushed credential-exchange documents, answer request-vmc only when signed

A VTC now pushes every credential-exchange step and `vtc/members/request-vmc`
as a signed Trust Task document, over TSP or DIDComm (in the binding envelope),
instead of a bare DIDComm message typed as its task URI (the companion VTI
change, verifiable-trust-infrastructure "credential exchange onto the Trust
Task spine"). Two handlers read the bare shape:

- `credential_in_issue` read `credential_response` from the message body. An
  opened envelope's body is the document, so the credential sits under
  `payload` and was never found: the membership credential a community delivers
  on admission would not be stored and the join would never complete. It now
  reads the document's payload, and refuses a document whose `issuer` is not
  the party that delivered it. A bare body from a VTC on the older release is
  still read; the credential's own proof, not the delivery, decides what is
  stored.
- `members/request-vmc` was answered on the transport sender alone, and makes
  this client sign and send its membership credential. It is now checked as the
  community's operational document before dispatch, like the removal notice —
  `authentication` key, addressed to the persona, fresh, not seen before — and
  an unverified one issues nothing. A VTC on the older release sends it bare, so
  its request is ignored (logged) until it updates; the member can still issue
  manually.

`join-requests/submit-receipt` already read the payload and was verified as an
operational document, so it needed nothing.

The ordering test that used `request-vmc` as its example of a message with no
check of its own now uses a trust-ping; `request-vmc` has its own test.

Merges after #381 → #383 → #386 → #387 (this branch is built on #387), and
before the VTI change deploys.

Not changed here: the peer vetting legs, including the vetter's statement
`issue`, are still sent typed as their task and unsigned; `vetting/wire.rs`
documents moving those sends as a later release, after every client reads the
envelope.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): claim a signed vetter grant as a vetter grant

A community pushes `credential-exchange/issue` as a signed Trust Task
document, so a vetter role credential sits under `payload`. The vetter-grant
path in `inbound::statement` read `/credential_response/credential` at the
body root and missed it, so a current VTC's grant would not make the persona a
vetter. It now reads the credential through `credential_in_issue`, the same
extraction the dispatcher used for the credential's proof check, which reads
the payload (refusing a document whose issuer is not the sender) or an older
VTC's bare body.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): take a credential delivery only as the community's signed document

A VTC signs every credential-exchange/issue it pushes, so there is nothing to
keep a bare delivery for, and a delivery nobody can attribute is not one this
client should act on. Deployments are recreated, so no older VTC needs the
bare shape.

- issued_credential::verify_issued_delivery: the delivery document's issuer
  must be the sender and its proof must be the sender's under
  authentication; then the credential inside is verified on its own proof.
  The dispatcher's credential job now carries the whole document and runs it.
- messaging::credential_in_issue reads only a document whose issuer is the
  sender; the bare-body branch is gone.
- A vetter grant additionally requires wire::open (issuer == sender, proof by
  the sender) before the grant is considered.
- Tests build signed deliveries; new tests refuse a bare grant and a grant
  relayed by another party.

Breaking (wire) and (library), recorded in the CHANGELOG.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(openvtc): run inbound network-bound checks off the UI loop (#387)
body:
fix(openvtc): run inbound network-bound checks off the UI loop (#387)

* fix(openvtc-core): verify the proof on issued credentials

A credential a community delivers over credential-exchange/issue was
stored after checking only that its issuer matched the DIDComm sender.
Verify it before storing: resolve the issuer's DID document, require
every Data Integrity proof (eddsa-jcs-2022, mldsa44-jcs-2024) to verify
with a key of the issuer's own DID listed under assertionMethod, check
the validity window, and refuse a revoked credential via the existing
status-list check.

handle_credential_issue now takes a VerifiedIssuedCredential, which only
the verifier produces. Account recovery (rebuild::plan) applies the same
check to each membership it would restore, and the vault sync skips a
locally held credential that does not verify.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): admit a join only on a verified membership credential

An approved join status or an allow verdict is an unsigned reply; it no
longer activates the membership. It acknowledges the join, and the
membership becomes Active - and the reciprocal membership credential is
sent - only when the community's credential arrives and verifies.

Factor the proof check into proof_check (signer DID binding, relationship
per proof purpose, proof sets) so other signed messages can use it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): fail closed on credential status, and read proof-set status lists

A credential's revocation status must now be established: an unreachable
or unverifiable status list refuses the credential, with a message that
says to retry. The list is read by a new status_list module that
verifies it with proof_check, so a list signed with a proof set
(Ed25519 + ML-DSA-44) verifies. The vetter grant check uses the same
reader. StatusPolicy is removed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): activate only a pending join; bind verification methods to their controller

- a credential lands only on a Pending or Active membership, and only a
  Pending join is activated; an ended membership is not revived
- a proof's verification method must be controlled by the signer
- allow five minutes of skew on a proof's created, matching issuedAt
- cache fetched status lists for at most five minutes (or the list's
  validUntil/ttl), re-verifying on every use

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): check a delivered credential locally before fetching; keep status fetches on public hosts

- a credential-issue is checked against local state (issuer is the sender,
  subject is our persona, known kind, a live membership with the sender)
  before its proof is verified or its status list fetched, so a party we
  hold no membership with cannot make this client resolve or fetch
- status-list fetches refuse loopback, private, link-local and other
  non-public hosts: IP literals and special-use names in the URL, names by
  what they resolve to, and every redirect hop (affinidi-net-guard); no proxy
- a VRC's proof goes through proof_check: assertionMethod purpose, a method
  the issuer lists and controls

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): require proofs for relationship DIDs, removal notices and community answers

The transport sender is a routing hint, not an identity. Decisions that
turn on who said something now rest on a Data Integrity proof checked
against the party's DID document (proof_check):

- relationship request/accept carry didProof (and personaProof for an
  R-DID) binding the DID to the handshake thread and both personas, by
  authentication keys; accept, finalize and reject are matched by the
  thread id of a request in the right state from the right party, with
  no fallback to the sender
- a removal notice is acted on only as the community's signed Trust
  Task document
- a community's vetting answers are acted on only when signed by it, and
  a vetter role credential is kept only when its proof verifies
- document the sender sources in didcomm.rs as routing hints

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): operational documents need the authentication key, a recipient, freshness and no replay

Removal notices and a community's vetting answers are operational
documents (VTI-KEY-106/107). They are acted on only with a proof under
proofPurpose authentication by a key listed under authentication, a
recipient that is one of our personas, an issuedAt inside the kind's
window (and any expiresAt), and a document id not seen before. Seen ids
are persisted in the protected config until their window passes, and
recorded only after the proof verifies.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): bind operational documents before recording them; bound the replay set without eviction

verify_operational no longer records: the caller commits the verified
document only once it is bound (a removal notice from a community the
named persona belongs to; a community answer that matched something of
ours). A manifest from a community we have no business with is ignored.
The replay set is keyed by (issuer, id), ids are capped at 256
characters, and per-issuer and issuer quotas refuse rather than evict.
The dispatcher reports a change whenever the set changes, so it is
persisted.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): bind operational documents to their signed type, and relationship proofs to their side

- an operational document is acted on only as its own signed `type`: the
  handler's type must equal it, and the freshness window follows from it
  (OperationalKind::of), so a community's signed answer cannot be replayed
  as a removal notice or as the answer to another question
- the relationship DID binding statement names its role (request or
  accept), so a request's proof cannot stand as an accept's in the same
  handshake

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): authenticate capability and git-ns replies, invitations and join failures

- capability and git-ns success replies must be the community's signed
  operational document; a capability reply is taken only from the
  community the view asked
- an invitation credential is verified (proof, window, revocation) before
  it is stored, listed as usable, presented or used to prefill the
  community DID, at every ingest point
- a problem-report from a party we hold no membership with records
  nothing
- the credential status fetch is Send, so verification can run in a
  spawned job

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): require the community's proof on capability and git-ns refusals too

A trust-task-error refusal offered to the capability or git-ns view must
now be the community's signed operational document like a success reply;
an unsigned refusal is ignored with a log line. The check runs once per
message, so a refusal offered to both views is not read as a replay.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): sign-gate the join replies, profile answers and VRC rejections; record capability replies only from members

- join submit-receipt, verdict, status response and trust-task-error are
  acted on only as the community's signed operational document, and
  recorded only once they matched a pending join
- a DIDComm problem-report (unsignable) is surfaced for a community we
  hold a record with and never changes a record
- a community profile answer must be signed and answer a question we
  asked; a declared attributed default never replaces pairwise
- a VRC rejection closes only our VRC request to that party
- capability and git-ns replies are recorded only from communities we
  belong to

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(openvtc-core): keep send_community_profile_show's doc comment on it

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): refuse a community reply from a non-member before checking its proof

- capability, git-ns and join/profile replies from a party we hold no
  membership with (Pending included) are refused before anything is
  resolved (OperationalError::NoStanding), and never recorded
- each reply is verified as its own signed type

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): sign every Trust Task request as the persona, for authentication

A community requires a document proof bound to the sender on every Trust
Task request. Every request this client sends is now signed with the
persona's authentication key under proofPurpose authentication (issuer
the persona, recipient the community, issuedAt, a fresh id):

- the capability list, community-profile question and personhood
  challenge, which were unsigned, are signed
- the requests already signed (join submit/status, self-remove, member
  VMC, personhood assertion, capability toggles, git-ns, vetting
  documents) use the authentication key and purpose
- credentials (member VMC, vetting cards and statements) stay signed
  with the assertion key
- the unsigned document builders are removed

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): run inbound network-bound checks off the UI loop

Verifying a delivered credential, a community's operational document
(removal notice, join replies, profile, capability/git-ns replies and
refusals), a relationship DID's binding proofs and a VRC's proof each
resolve a DID or fetch a status list. They ran inline in dispatch, so a
slow community froze the TUI.

- process_inbound sets such a message aside (InboundEffects::deferred)
  before anything about it is applied; a single worker runs the check
  in arrival order and hands the message back with its result, and it
  is dispatched again from the top with that result
- every handler takes its proof from the result and fails closed when
  none is present, is of the wrong kind, or is for another credential
- replay sets are checked and recorded on the loop, at apply time; the
  operational kind comes from the message type, never the document
- a join whose credential is being checked shows "Pending - verifying
  credential..." until it activates or is refused

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): local checks before queueing an inbound check; bound, supervise and keep the queue

- verification_job runs the cheap local checks first (membership with the
  sender for credentials and operational documents, an outstanding request
  for an accept, vet_vrc_issued, the relationship-request checks, business
  with the community for a vetting answer); only what passes is queued
- the queue (verify_queue) replaces the unbounded channels and single
  worker: a priority lane for communities we belong to, caps per lane and
  per sender, a 30 s timeout around every check (the VRC path included),
  and each check its own task, so a timeout or panic refuses that message
  and the queue goes on
- a community's message waiting on its check is kept in the protected
  config (deferred_inbound) and queued again on the next start: the
  mediator has already deleted it
- a message whose sender has checks queued waits behind them
  (VerifyJob::Barrier), so members/request-vmc behind the credential that
  activates the membership is answered rather than dropped
- a vetting community answer's proof is checked off the loop too
  (vetting::inbound::Context::community_answer)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): key the verification queue on the authenticated sender

- the transport-authenticated sender travels with each inbound event
  (DIDCommEvent::InboundMessage::authenticated; never the plaintext from)
- only a message whose authenticated sender equals its from and is a
  community we hold a record with gets the priority lane, is waited on,
  and is kept across a restart; everything else waits in the other lane
  under its authenticated sender's cap; no authenticated sender, not queued
- relationship-request checks limited to 20 a minute across all senders
- a barrier is triaged again on its turn and set aside for a check if it
  now needs one; barriers from member communities are kept too
- kept messages are restored as the queue has room and stay kept until
  they fit; kept copies are keyed by (authenticated sender, id), at most
  128 of 32 KiB

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vetting): sign the e2e manifest under its response type

The over-the-wire vetting test signed the community's manifest answer
with the request type (manifest/0.2) in the document while the message
carried manifest/0.2#response. #381's operational check correctly
refuses a document whose signed type differs from the type it is
handled as, so the applicant never learned the requirements. Sign it as
a VTC does, under the response type. The test is #[ignore]d and only
CI's coverage job (--include-ignored) runs it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): sign the statement delivery as the vetter persona

wire::credential_delivery sent the vetter's credential-exchange/issue
bare and unsigned, the one Trust Task document openvtc still sent
without a persona proof. It is now a Trust Task document from the
vetter persona to the applicant (fresh id and issuedAt, threaded on the
session) signed through wire::sign with the persona's authentication
key; the statement is its payload and keeps its own assertionMethod
proof.

On receipt the applicant claims an identity-vetting issue as before,
then opens it with wire::open (issuer bound to the sender, proof by the
sender) before reading the statement from the payload. A bare delivery
is still claimed, so it is refused rather than passed to the join
handler.

title: fix(openvtc): sign every Trust Task request as the persona, for authentication
body:
**Merge order:** #381 → #383 → #386 → #387. Each PR is based on the one before it; #381 is based on `main`.

**Up to date with `main`** (merge commits, no rebase): #380 (issued-credential proofs, the first part of this stack), #390 (personhood, capability and vetter profile/resend requests signed with the authentication key) and #391 (git-ns repo/create 0.3; trust-tasks 0.23, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.28.1, affinidi-tdk 0.18, vta-sdk 0.53, did-git-sign 0.5). The workspace resolves exactly one `trust-tasks-rs` (0.23.0).

## Summary

VTI #1739 makes the VTC require, on every DIDComm/TSP Trust Task request, a proof on the document that is bound to the sender. VTI #642 makes several of those proofs REQUIRED. So every Trust Task request openvtc sends to a VTC is now signed by the persona.

Each request's document carries:
- `issuer`: the persona DID
- `recipient`: the VTC DID
- `issuedAt`
- a fresh `id`
- an `eddsa-jcs-2022` proof with `proofPurpose: authentication`, made with the persona's **authentication** key

This is done by `capabilities::sign_document`, which every request signer goes through, directly or via `trust_task_doc::build_signed_value` / `vetting::wire::sign`.

### Requests that were unsigned and are now signed
- `governance/capability/list`
- `vtc/community/profile/show` (the background profile question)
- `members/personhood/challenge`

### Requests that were signed with the assertion key and now use the authentication key and purpose
- join `submit` / `status`
- `members/self-remove`
- `members/vmc`
- `members/personhood/assert` (the presentation it carries was already `authentication`-purpose; it is now made with the authentication key too)
- capability enable/disable
- git-ns documents
- every vetting document, whether sent to the community or to a peer

### Credentials still use the assertion key
The member VMC, vetting cards and statements, and VRCs are still signed with the assertion key. Where one request carries a credential (the member VMC and the vetting card), the credential and the document are now signed with separate keys.

### Unsigned document builders removed
`join::build_trust_task_document` and `personhood::build_document` are gone, so a request can't be sent unsigned by accident.

### Deliberately left unsigned
The anonymous HTTP manifest question (`vetting::discover`) sent before joining names no one by design, so it has no persona to sign as. Tasks sent to the VTA go through `vta-sdk`'s client, which openvtc does not build.

## Rollout

Deploy together with VTI #1739. These are test deployments upgraded together, so there is no compatibility window. A community that checks a request proof's purpose against `assertionMethod` will refuse these requests.

## Breaking changes
- **Wire:** request proofs are `authentication`-purpose, made with the persona's authentication key.
- **Library:**
  - `send_community_profile_show` and `request_challenge` take a signer;
  - `issue_and_send_member_vmc` takes separate credential and document signers.

## Tests
- A signed request verifies as the sender's `authentication` proof: it passes `proof_check` under `authentication` and is refused under `assertionMethod`.
- Changing the request's addressing breaks its proof.
- A capability list request is signed, dated and addressed, and has a unique id.
- The git-ns test now expects `authentication`.

Local checks all pass: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy with `-D warnings` (also with `--features dev-overrides`), `cargo doc -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace -- --include-ignored`, and `--no-default-features`.

## After merging `main`: one signing path

#390 on `main` and this PR both moved the same requests to the authentication key. #390 did it with purpose-taking variants beside the defaults, and the defaults stayed `assertionMethod`. This PR changes the defaults themselves. The merge keeps one path, and that path has no purpose to choose:
- `capabilities::sign_document`, `trust_task_doc::build_signed_value` and `vetting::wire::sign` always sign under `proofPurpose: authentication`, and callers pass the authentication key;
- #390's `sign_document_as`, `build_signed_value_as`, `wire::sign_as` and `sign_and_send_operational` are removed. Their callers use the single path: the capability toggle, the personhood challenge and assert, and the vetter profile and resend;
- `personhood::request_challenge(route, signer, subject_did)` keeps this PR's signature, and keeps #390's `build_challenge_request` split so the signing can be tested;
- both test sets are kept. A capability list request and a toggle are each signed for `authentication`. #390's personhood, resend and profile tests now go through the single path.

trust-tasks 0.23 signs for `authentication` by default and checks a proof's key against its purpose (`ProofPurposeResolver` / `PurposeBound`). That matches this PR. openvtc signs with `affinidi-data-integrity` and names the purpose explicitly.

After the merge, run locally: `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace` (1638 passed, 0 failed).

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] Finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1): unchanged
- [x] Retries bounded (R1.4): none added
- [x] Loops survive transient errors (R1.5): a persona whose key can't be read gets a clear status line, not a crash
- [x] Acks after handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] Wire types (R3.*): proof purpose change; breaking change flagged above
- [x] Fail-closed (R5.*): a request is never sent unsigned; an ask with no key is dropped
- [x] Logs claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations flagged: the anonymous pre-join HTTP manifest question stays unsigned

title: fix(openvtc): sign every Trust Task request as the persona, for authentication (#386)
body:
fix(openvtc): sign every Trust Task request as the persona, for authentication (#386)

* fix(openvtc-core): verify the proof on issued credentials

A credential a community delivers over credential-exchange/issue was
stored after checking only that its issuer matched the DIDComm sender.
Verify it before storing: resolve the issuer's DID document, require
every Data Integrity proof (eddsa-jcs-2022, mldsa44-jcs-2024) to verify
with a key of the issuer's own DID listed under assertionMethod, check
the validity window, and refuse a revoked credential via the existing
status-list check.

handle_credential_issue now takes a VerifiedIssuedCredential, which only
the verifier produces. Account recovery (rebuild::plan) applies the same
check to each membership it would restore, and the vault sync skips a
locally held credential that does not verify.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): admit a join only on a verified membership credential

An approved join status or an allow verdict is an unsigned reply; it no
longer activates the membership. It acknowledges the join, and the
membership becomes Active - and the reciprocal membership credential is
sent - only when the community's credential arrives and verifies.

Factor the proof check into proof_check (signer DID binding, relationship
per proof purpose, proof sets) so other signed messages can use it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): fail closed on credential status, and read proof-set status lists

A credential's revocation status must now be established: an unreachable
or unverifiable status list refuses the credential, with a message that
says to retry. The list is read by a new status_list module that
verifies it with proof_check, so a list signed with a proof set
(Ed25519 + ML-DSA-44) verifies. The vetter grant check uses the same
reader. StatusPolicy is removed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): activate only a pending join; bind verification methods to their controller

- a credential lands only on a Pending or Active membership, and only a
  Pending join is activated; an ended membership is not revived
- a proof's verification method must be controlled by the signer
- allow five minutes of skew on a proof's created, matching issuedAt
- cache fetched status lists for at most five minutes (or the list's
  validUntil/ttl), re-verifying on every use

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): check a delivered credential locally before fetching; keep status fetches on public hosts

- a credential-issue is checked against local state (issuer is the sender,
  subject is our persona, known kind, a live membership with the sender)
  before its proof is verified or its status list fetched, so a party we
  hold no membership with cannot make this client resolve or fetch
- status-list fetches refuse loopback, private, link-local and other
  non-public hosts: IP literals and special-use names in the URL, names by
  what they resolve to, and every redirect hop (affinidi-net-guard); no proxy
- a VRC's proof goes through proof_check: assertionMethod purpose, a method
  the issuer lists and controls

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): require proofs for relationship DIDs, removal notices and community answers

The transport sender is a routing hint, not an identity. Decisions that
turn on who said something now rest on a Data Integrity proof checked
against the party's DID document (proof_check):

- relationship request/accept carry didProof (and personaProof for an
  R-DID) binding the DID to the handshake thread and both personas, by
  authentication keys; accept, finalize and reject are matched by the
  thread id of a request in the right state from the right party, with
  no fallback to the sender
- a removal notice is acted on only as the community's signed Trust
  Task document
- a community's vetting answers are acted on only when signed by it, and
  a vetter role credential is kept only when its proof verifies
- document the sender sources in didcomm.rs as routing hints

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): operational documents need the authentication key, a recipient, freshness and no replay

Removal notices and a community's vetting answers are operational
documents (VTI-KEY-106/107). They are acted on only with a proof under
proofPurpose authentication by a key listed under authentication, a
recipient that is one of our personas, an issuedAt inside the kind's
window (and any expiresAt), and a document id not seen before. Seen ids
are persisted in the protected config until their window passes, and
recorded only after the proof verifies.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): bind operational documents before recording them; bound the replay set without eviction

verify_operational no longer records: the caller commits the verified
document only once it is bound (a removal notice from a community the
named persona belongs to; a community answer that matched something of
ours). A manifest from a community we have no business with is ignored.
The replay set is keyed by (issuer, id), ids are capped at 256
characters, and per-issuer and issuer quotas refuse rather than evict.
The dispatcher reports a change whenever the set changes, so it is
persisted.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): bind operational documents to their signed type, and relationship proofs to their side

- an operational document is acted on only as its own signed `type`: the
  handler's type must equal it, and the freshness window follows from it
  (OperationalKind::of), so a community's signed answer cannot be replayed
  as a removal notice or as the answer to another question
- the relationship DID binding statement names its role (request or
  accept), so a request's proof cannot stand as an accept's in the same
  handshake

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): authenticate capability and git-ns replies, invitations and join failures

- capability and git-ns success replies must be the community's signed
  operational document; a capability reply is taken only from the
  community the view asked
- an invitation credential is verified (proof, window, revocation) before
  it is stored, listed as usable, presented or used to prefill the
  community DID, at every ingest point
- a problem-report from a party we hold no membership with records
  nothing
- the credential status fetch is Send, so verification can run in a
  spawned job

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): require the community's proof on capability and git-ns refusals too

A trust-task-error refusal offered to the capability or git-ns view must
now be the community's signed operational document like a success reply;
an unsigned refusal is ignored with a log line. The check runs once per
message, so a refusal offered to both views is not read as a replay.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): sign-gate the join replies, profile answers and VRC rejections; record capability replies only from members

- join submit-receipt, verdict, status response and trust-task-error are
  acted on only as the community's signed operational document, and
  recorded only once they matched a pending join
- a DIDComm problem-report (unsignable) is surfaced for a community we
  hold a record with and never changes a record
- a community profile answer must be signed and answer a question we
  asked; a declared attributed default never replaces pairwise
- a VRC rejection closes only our VRC request to that party
- capability and git-ns replies are recorded only from communities we
  belong to

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(openvtc-core): keep send_community_profile_show's doc comment on it

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): refuse a community reply from a non-member before checking its proof

- capability, git-ns and join/profile replies from a party we hold no
  membership with (Pending included) are refused before anything is
  resolved (OperationalError::NoStanding), and never recorded
- each reply is verified as its own signed type

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): sign every Trust Task request as the persona, for authentication

A community requires a document proof bound to the sender on every Trust
Task request. Every request this client sends is now signed with the
persona's authentication key under proofPurpose authentication (issuer
the persona, recipient the community, issuedAt, a fresh id):

- the capability list, community-profile question and personhood
  challenge, which were unsigned, are signed
- the requests already signed (join submit/status, self-remove, member
  VMC, personhood assertion, capability toggles, git-ns, vetting
  documents) use the authentication key and purpose
- credentials (member VMC, vetting cards and statements) stay signed
  with the assertion key
- the unsigned document builders are removed

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vetting): sign the e2e manifest under its response type

The over-the-wire vetting test signed the community's manifest answer
with the request type (manifest/0.2) in the document while the message
carried manifest/0.2#response. #381's operational check correctly
refuses a document whose signed type differs from the type it is
handled as, so the applicant never learned the requirements. Sign it as
a VTC does, under the response type. The test is #[ignore]d and only
CI's coverage job (--include-ignored) runs it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): sign the statement delivery as the vetter persona

wire::credential_delivery sent the vetter's credential-exchange/issue
bare and unsigned, the one Trust Task document openvtc still sent
without a persona proof. It is now a Trust Task document from the
vetter persona to the applicant (fresh id and issuedAt, threaded on the
session) signed through wire::sign with the persona's authentication
key; the statement is its payload and keeps its own assertionMethod
proof.

On receipt the applicant claims an identity-vetting issue as before,
then opens it with wire::open (issuer bound to the sender, proof by the
sender) before reading the statement from the payload. A bare delivery
is still claimed, so it is refused rather than passed to the join
handler.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(tui): show break-glass git rights to administrators
body:
## What

The Repos panel now shows git-ns break-glass records: rights a member gave themselves with `git-ns/right/break-glass`, which another administrator has not yet ratified or revoked.

Spec PR: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#641 (see trust-tasks `feat/git-ns-break-glass`). VTI implementation: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1745, which serves `git-ns/view` 0.4, `right/break-glass`, `right/ratify` and `cnm git ratify`.

- **view 0.4.** `openvtc-core::git_ns::view` now re-exports the generated `git-ns/view/0.4` types instead of 0.1. In 0.4, right records carry `breakGlass`, and the VTC returns every unratified break-glass record to every community administrator and namespace admin of its namespace, and to the resource's owners and the subject.
- **Banner.** While the view holds any unratified break-glass record, every screen of the panel opens with a red banner. It shows how many records there are, and for each one (up to 5, then "… and N more"): who gave themselves which right, on what, and when; the time it takes effect if a policy delay applies; and the justification, sanitised. It also says how to ratify or revoke: in the admin console (Repos → Break-glass grants) or with:
  `cnm git ratify --subject=<did> --right=<r> --resource=<res> --break-glass-at=<rfc3339>` / `cnm git revoke --subject=… --right=… --resource=…`.
  Each value is quoted by `git_ns::shell_word`, the same rule as cnm's own, so the commands paste safely into sh, bash, zsh and fish. The subject of a record sees that another administrator must ratify it, and is not shown a ratify command.
- **Flag.** The People table shows `BREAK-GLASS` in red next to an unratified right, and `break-glass, ratified` in grey once it is ratified.
- **Who sees the banner.** The panel shows every record the view returns. The VTC decides that audience. The client cannot identify a community administrator who holds no git right; the VTC can, and returns the records to them.

## Behaviour changes

- The panel sends `git-ns/view/0.4`. A VTC that does not serve 0.4 yet refuses it, so the panel works only against a VTC with the VTI change.
- 0.4 pins `_shared/0.4`, which uses the DID-core `Did` pattern. An answer that contains a DID with a bidi override or a zero-width character now fails to parse, instead of being sanitised on screen. The sanitisation test checks that refusal and still checks the reason text.

## Needs

Nothing more. `main` is on trust-tasks 0.23 (#391), which ships `git-ns/view` 0.4 and grant/revoke 0.3, so this builds with no `[patch.crates-io]` override. The workspace resolves exactly one `trust-tasks-rs` (0.23.0). It still needs a VTC that serves view 0.4 and grant/revoke 0.3 (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1745).

## Grant and revoke at 0.3

The VTC now serves `git-ns/right/grant` and `git-ns/right/revoke` at 0.3 only (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1745, no compatibility window), so the Repos panel sends 0.3 and reads the 0.3 record, which carries `breakGlass`. A refused elevated self-grant (`git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`) is explained: ask another administrator, or break the glass from the admin console or with `cnm git break-glass`. Grant and revoke 0.3 ship in trust-tasks 0.23.

## Tests

- `openvtc-core` git_ns:
  - `only_unratified_break_glass_records_raise_the_banner`
  - `a_delayed_break_glass_says_when_it_takes_effect`
  - `people_carry_the_break_glass_flag`
  - `printed_commands_name_the_record_and_are_quoted`
  - `shell_words_survive_sh_bash_zsh_and_fish`: runs each shell that is installed
- `openvtc` repos_panel:
  - `no_banner_without_a_break_glass`
  - `an_administrator_sees_the_banner_with_the_commands`
  - `the_subject_is_told_someone_else_must_ratify`
  - `the_justification_is_sanitised_before_it_is_drawn`
  - `a_repo_view_flags_the_break_glass_right`
- `cargo test -p openvtc-core -p openvtc`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` passed with the patch before trust-tasks 0.23; see below for the run after the merge.
- After the 0.3 move: `cargo test -p openvtc-core --lib git_ns` (31) and `cargo clippy -p openvtc-core --tests -D warnings` pass with the patch.

## After merging `main`

Standalone on `main`; no merge order with other PRs. The merge was clean, and two things needed fixing after it:
- **One text for a refused self-grant.** `main`'s repo/create 0.3 (#391) added an arm for `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`, and this PR added one for grant. The two codes are the same string, so the create arm was unreachable and the new-repository form showed the grant text. Both now share one arm and one text: separation of duties; ask another community administrator; if nobody else can, break the glass (`cnm git break-glass`, or from the admin console), which is announced to every administrator and flagged until someone ratifies or revokes it. Both tests expect it.
- **`git-ns/view` 0.4 does not declare `proof` REQUIRED.** In 0.23, views 0.1–0.3 declare it. The merge took `main`'s expectation for view 0.1, so the test now expects 0.4's declaration. The view is signed anyway, like every request (`build_signed`).

After the merge, run locally: `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace` (1631 passed, 0 failed).
