title: fix(openvtc): authenticate capability and git-ns replies, invitations and join failures
body:
**Merge order:** #381 → #383 → #386 → #387. Each PR is based on the one before it; #381 is based on `main`.

**Up to date with `main`** (merge commits, no rebase): #380 (issued-credential proofs, the first part of this stack), #390 (personhood, capability and vetter profile/resend requests signed with the authentication key) and #391 (git-ns repo/create 0.3; trust-tasks 0.23, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.28.1, affinidi-tdk 0.18, vta-sdk 0.53, did-git-sign 0.5). The workspace resolves exactly one `trust-tasks-rs` (0.23.0).

## Summary

This covers the remaining places where openvtc took a reply on the sender's word.

**Capability replies**
- A capability success reply must now be the community's signed operational document. The check uses `openvtc_core::operational`, the same one #381 added:
  - signed with the community's `authentication` key;
  - addressed to the persona it arrived for;
  - fresh, and not a replay.
- `apply_capability_replies` accepts a reply only if its sender is the community the view is asking. A matching thread id alone is no longer enough.
- Refusals (`trust-task-error`) are held to the same rule: they must be the expected community's signed operational document. An unsigned refusal is ignored, with a log line. The check runs once per message, so a refusal offered to both the capability and the git-ns view is not treated as a replay. This relies on the VTC and VTA signing their error responses (VTI PR 3).

**git-ns replies**
- The same proof check now applies to success replies, on top of the existing sender and issuer binding in `repos_actions::apply_replies`.

**Invitation credentials (VIC)**
- The new `join::verify_invitation_credential` checks:
  - the shape;
  - the proof, against the DID document of the issuer the VIC names (`assertionMethod`, and every proof in a proof set);
  - the validity window;
  - the revocation status, which fails closed.
- It runs at every point a VIC comes in or gets used:
  - `--invitation` at startup;
  - a paste on the join entry and invitation pages;
  - the Add VIC panel, where it runs in the background job before the credential is stored in the vault;
  - the list of available invitations, where the vault's own `status` is no longer taken on trust;
  - the final check before presenting a VIC at join.
- **The community DID is no longer pre-filled from an unverified issuer.** On the entry page, the issuer is recorded only after the proof verifies.
- `validate_invitation_credential` is now documented as a shape check only.

**Join replies need the community's signed document.** The submit-receipt, verdict, status response and join `trust-task-error` are acted on only as the community's signed operational document. They are recorded in the replay set only after they matched a pending join. `confirm_request_id` therefore never takes an unsigned body.

**Problem-reports never change a record.** A DIDComm problem-report cannot be signed. It is surfaced in the activity log only for a community we hold a record with, and never rejects or acknowledges a join. `handle_join_problem_report` is replaced by the read-only `read_problem_report`.

**Community profile.** An answer is taken only when it is signed and answers a profile question we put to that community (outstanding questions are tracked in memory, answered once, expire after 10 minutes). A declared `attributed` default is never recorded over pairwise; the member chooses attributed per relationship.

**VRC rejection.** A rejection closes only our own `VRCRequestOutbound` task on that thread, to that counterparty (persona or relationship DID).

**Capability and git-ns replies** are recorded only from communities we belong to. A capability, git-ns, join or profile reply from a party we hold no membership with (Pending included) is refused **before** its proof is checked (`OperationalError::NoStanding`), so it never costs a resolve. Each reply is verified as its own signed `type`.

**Join problem-report, trust-task-error and submit-receipt (sender binding)**
- These handlers already correlate through `membership_by_pending_request(from_did, …)`, so they already require the expected community.
- The gap was the unclaimed problem-report path. It wrote an activity-log line whatever the sender. It now records nothing unless the sender is a community we hold a membership with.
- A new test checks that all three, from another party (even threaded on the real request id), change nothing and do not even acknowledge the request.

**Also**
- The status-list fetch inside `verify_issued_credential` now uses owned arguments, so the verification future is `Send` and can run in a spawned job.

## Rollout

Deploy together with VTI PR 3 (the VTC signing its operational documents and refusals with its `authentication` key). There is no compatibility window: these are test deployments, upgraded together. A VTC that still sends unsigned receipts, verdicts, status responses or refusals will see them ignored.

## Breaking changes

These target test deployments; there is no compatibility path.
- **Wire:** a VTC must sign capability and git-ns responses, refusals included, with an `authentication` key and include `recipient` and `issuedAt`.
- **Behaviour:**
  - an invitation that does not verify, including one whose status list cannot be reached, is refused at ingest;
  - the Add VIC panel reports why.

## Tests

- Capability replies:
  - a reply from another party on the right thread is ignored;
  - the right community's reply is applied.
- Invitations:
  - refused: an unsigned one, one signed by a DID other than its issuer, and a signed one whose status cannot be established;
  - an unsigned paste is refused and leaves no issuer behind to pre-fill from.
  - The existing paste tests now run through the post-verification path.
- Join failures from another party change nothing.
- A reply from a non-member is refused for standing before its proof is checked, and records nothing.

Checks run locally: `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings` (also with `--features dev-overrides`), `cargo doc -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace -- --include-ignored`, and `--no-default-features`. All pass.

## After merging `main`

This merged cleanly from #381's updated branch; no conflicts.

After the merge, run locally: `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace` (1637 passed, 0 failed).

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] Finite timeouts (R1.2): DID resolution takes 10 s at most; the status fetch uses `status_client`
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1): verification happens before any store, prefill or display
- [x] Retries bounded (R1.4): none added
- [x] Loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks after handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] Wire types (R3.*): the break is flagged above
- [x] Fail closed (R5.*)
- [x] Logs claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations flagged: none. Refusals need a proof too, which depends on the VTC and VTA signing their error responses (VTI PR 3)

title: fix(openvtc): authenticate capability and git-ns replies, invitations and join failures (#383)
body:
fix(openvtc): authenticate capability and git-ns replies, invitations and join failures (#383)

* fix(openvtc-core): verify the proof on issued credentials

A credential a community delivers over credential-exchange/issue was
stored after checking only that its issuer matched the DIDComm sender.
Verify it before storing: resolve the issuer's DID document, require
every Data Integrity proof (eddsa-jcs-2022, mldsa44-jcs-2024) to verify
with a key of the issuer's own DID listed under assertionMethod, check
the validity window, and refuse a revoked credential via the existing
status-list check.

handle_credential_issue now takes a VerifiedIssuedCredential, which only
the verifier produces. Account recovery (rebuild::plan) applies the same
check to each membership it would restore, and the vault sync skips a
locally held credential that does not verify.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): admit a join only on a verified membership credential

An approved join status or an allow verdict is an unsigned reply; it no
longer activates the membership. It acknowledges the join, and the
membership becomes Active - and the reciprocal membership credential is
sent - only when the community's credential arrives and verifies.

Factor the proof check into proof_check (signer DID binding, relationship
per proof purpose, proof sets) so other signed messages can use it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): fail closed on credential status, and read proof-set status lists

A credential's revocation status must now be established: an unreachable
or unverifiable status list refuses the credential, with a message that
says to retry. The list is read by a new status_list module that
verifies it with proof_check, so a list signed with a proof set
(Ed25519 + ML-DSA-44) verifies. The vetter grant check uses the same
reader. StatusPolicy is removed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): activate only a pending join; bind verification methods to their controller

- a credential lands only on a Pending or Active membership, and only a
  Pending join is activated; an ended membership is not revived
- a proof's verification method must be controlled by the signer
- allow five minutes of skew on a proof's created, matching issuedAt
- cache fetched status lists for at most five minutes (or the list's
  validUntil/ttl), re-verifying on every use

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): check a delivered credential locally before fetching; keep status fetches on public hosts

- a credential-issue is checked against local state (issuer is the sender,
  subject is our persona, known kind, a live membership with the sender)
  before its proof is verified or its status list fetched, so a party we
  hold no membership with cannot make this client resolve or fetch
- status-list fetches refuse loopback, private, link-local and other
  non-public hosts: IP literals and special-use names in the URL, names by
  what they resolve to, and every redirect hop (affinidi-net-guard); no proxy
- a VRC's proof goes through proof_check: assertionMethod purpose, a method
  the issuer lists and controls

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): require proofs for relationship DIDs, removal notices and community answers

The transport sender is a routing hint, not an identity. Decisions that
turn on who said something now rest on a Data Integrity proof checked
against the party's DID document (proof_check):

- relationship request/accept carry didProof (and personaProof for an
  R-DID) binding the DID to the handshake thread and both personas, by
  authentication keys; accept, finalize and reject are matched by the
  thread id of a request in the right state from the right party, with
  no fallback to the sender
- a removal notice is acted on only as the community's signed Trust
  Task document
- a community's vetting answers are acted on only when signed by it, and
  a vetter role credential is kept only when its proof verifies
- document the sender sources in didcomm.rs as routing hints

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): operational documents need the authentication key, a recipient, freshness and no replay

Removal notices and a community's vetting answers are operational
documents (VTI-KEY-106/107). They are acted on only with a proof under
proofPurpose authentication by a key listed under authentication, a
recipient that is one of our personas, an issuedAt inside the kind's
window (and any expiresAt), and a document id not seen before. Seen ids
are persisted in the protected config until their window passes, and
recorded only after the proof verifies.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): bind operational documents before recording them; bound the replay set without eviction

verify_operational no longer records: the caller commits the verified
document only once it is bound (a removal notice from a community the
named persona belongs to; a community answer that matched something of
ours). A manifest from a community we have no business with is ignored.
The replay set is keyed by (issuer, id), ids are capped at 256
characters, and per-issuer and issuer quotas refuse rather than evict.
The dispatcher reports a change whenever the set changes, so it is
persisted.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): bind operational documents to their signed type, and relationship proofs to their side

- an operational document is acted on only as its own signed `type`: the
  handler's type must equal it, and the freshness window follows from it
  (OperationalKind::of), so a community's signed answer cannot be replayed
  as a removal notice or as the answer to another question
- the relationship DID binding statement names its role (request or
  accept), so a request's proof cannot stand as an accept's in the same
  handshake

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): authenticate capability and git-ns replies, invitations and join failures

- capability and git-ns success replies must be the community's signed
  operational document; a capability reply is taken only from the
  community the view asked
- an invitation credential is verified (proof, window, revocation) before
  it is stored, listed as usable, presented or used to prefill the
  community DID, at every ingest point
- a problem-report from a party we hold no membership with records
  nothing
- the credential status fetch is Send, so verification can run in a
  spawned job

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): require the community's proof on capability and git-ns refusals too

A trust-task-error refusal offered to the capability or git-ns view must
now be the community's signed operational document like a success reply;
an unsigned refusal is ignored with a log line. The check runs once per
message, so a refusal offered to both views is not read as a replay.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): sign-gate the join replies, profile answers and VRC rejections; record capability replies only from members

- join submit-receipt, verdict, status response and trust-task-error are
  acted on only as the community's signed operational document, and
  recorded only once they matched a pending join
- a DIDComm problem-report (unsignable) is surfaced for a community we
  hold a record with and never changes a record
- a community profile answer must be signed and answer a question we
  asked; a declared attributed default never replaces pairwise
- a VRC rejection closes only our VRC request to that party
- capability and git-ns replies are recorded only from communities we
  belong to

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(openvtc-core): keep send_community_profile_show's doc comment on it

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): refuse a community reply from a non-member before checking its proof

- capability, git-ns and join/profile replies from a party we hold no
  membership with (Pending included) are refused before anything is
  resolved (OperationalError::NoStanding), and never recorded
- each reply is verified as its own signed type

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vetting): sign the e2e manifest under its response type

The over-the-wire vetting test signed the community's manifest answer
with the request type (manifest/0.2) in the document while the message
carried manifest/0.2#response. #381's operational check correctly
refuses a document whose signed type differs from the type it is
handled as, so the applicant never learned the requirements. Sign it as
a VTC does, under the response type. The test is #[ignore]d and only
CI's coverage job (--include-ignored) runs it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: fix(tui): stop adopting drift the panel cannot name a recipient for
body:
## Why

An adoption grants a right to whichever member linked the drift item's forge account. This panel sends `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1, and a 0.1 adopt does not name that member: the VTC picks the recipient from the account link as it stands when the task runs. If the account is relinked between the member reading the item and confirming, the right goes to someone the member never saw, and is published to the Trust Registry.

`git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.3 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#640) fixes this by naming the recipient (`subject`). VTI (companion draft PR, linked from #640's thread) serves 0.3 and refuses a 0.1 adopt with `unsupportedVersion`.

This panel cannot send a 0.3 adopt, because `git-ns/view` tells a member only their *own* account links. It cannot show who the recipient would be, so it cannot name them.

## What changed

- **`o` no longer arms an adoption.** It says the adoption would grant the projected right to the member who linked the account, that the panel can't see who that is, and where adopting works: the admin console, or `cnm git drift resolve … adopt --subject <DID>`.
  - When no right projects to the role, the existing "No git right corresponds…" message still comes first.
  - **Revert (`v`) is unchanged.**
- **Hints updated.** The key hint and the drift footer no longer offer `o adopt drift`. The footer says where to adopt instead.
- **openvtc-core** refuses to build a 0.1 adopt payload at all, so no future caller can send one by mistake.
- **Refusal message.** A VTC's refusal of a 0.1 adopt (`unsupportedVersion` naming drift/resolve 0.3) is now explained as exactly that. It no longer reads as "this community does not serve git namespaces".

## Behaviour change (deliberate, per the standing security/usability rule)

**This removes adopt from the TUI**, which #379 shipped. The choice was between keeping an adopt that could grant to someone the member never saw, and removing it with a pointer to the two places that can name the recipient. I removed it.

Bringing adopt back needs the member-to-account join visible to repository owners in `git-ns/view`. `git-ns/view` deliberately withholds that join today, so it's a separate privacy decision, raised on #640.

No dependency or version changes: this PR doesn't need the 0.3 types.

## Tests

- core: a 0.1 adopt is never built; the new refusal reads correctly; other `unsupportedVersion` refusals read as before.
- state: `o` arms nothing, names the right, and says where to adopt; `write` on an organisation still says "No git right".
- render: the hints offer revert only and point at the admin console or cnm for adopting.

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass locally.

## How to test

On a repository you own with a `roleAdded` drift item: highlight it and press `o`. Nothing is armed, and the status says where to adopt. `v` then `y` still reverts.

## After merging `main`

Standalone on `main`; no merge order with other PRs. The merge of `main` brought in #380, #390 and #391 (trust-tasks 0.23, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.28.1, affinidi-tdk 0.18, vta-sdk 0.53, did-git-sign 0.5) and merged cleanly. The workspace resolves exactly one `trust-tasks-rs` (0.23.0).

After the merge, run locally: `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace` (1622 passed, 0 failed).

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): nothing is sent for adopt
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): adopt fails closed
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(openvtc): require proofs for relationship DIDs, removal notices and community answers
body:
**Merge order:** #381 → #383 → #386 → #387. Each PR is based on the one before it; #381 is based on `main`.

**Up to date with `main`** (merge commits, no rebase): #380 (issued-credential proofs, the first part of this stack), #390 (personhood, capability and vetter profile/resend requests signed with the authentication key) and #391 (git-ns repo/create 0.3; trust-tasks 0.23, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.28.1, affinidi-tdk 0.18, vta-sdk 0.53, did-git-sign 0.5). The workspace resolves exactly one `trust-tasks-rs` (0.23.0).

## Summary

The sender a message arrives from is now treated as a **routing hint, not an identity**. Every decision that depends on *who said something* now requires a Data Integrity proof by that party, checked against their DID document with `proof_check` (added in #380).

### Relationships

**Proofs on request and accept.** Both now carry:
- `didProof`, made with an `authentication` key of the relationship DID;
- `personaProof`, made by the persona that names an R-DID.

Both sign `{role, did, persona, peer, thid}`, so a proof made for one handshake does not verify in another. `role` (`request` or `accept`) stops one side's proof standing as the other's within the same handshake. A request or accept whose proofs are missing or invalid is refused.

**Correlation by thread id only.** `Relationships::awaiting(thid, state, from)` matches accept, finalize and reject. It requires:
- our request's id, never empty;
- the right state: `RequestSent`, or `RequestAccepted` for finalize;
- the party the request went to.

The fallback that matched by sender alone is removed, so a reject can no longer end an established relationship.

**Other changes.**
- The request id is fixed before sending and written into the provisional record, so an accept that arrives early still matches.
- The unused `create_send_message_accepted`, which sent an accept with no proof, is removed.

### Operational documents (VTI-KEY-106 / VTI-KEY-107)

These are removal notices and a community's vetting answers (manifest, vetter list, profile, resend, withdrawal record). They are handled by the new `openvtc-core/src/operational.rs`, and acted on only if all of the following hold:
- `issuer` is the sending community;
- the document's signed `type` equals the type the handler handles. A community's signed answer therefore cannot be acted on as a removal notice, or as the answer to another question. The freshness window comes from that type (`OperationalKind::of`), so `verify_operational` takes the handled type rather than a kind;
- the proof has `proofPurpose: authentication`, by a key listed under `authentication`. An `assertionMethod` proof is **refused** for these;
- `recipient` is present and is one of our personas. For a removal notice it must also be the persona the payload removes;
- `issuedAt` is present and inside the kind's window: 30 days plus one for a removal notice (its delivery window), one day for an answer. Future-dated beyond a 5-minute skew, or an `expiresAt` in the past, is refused;
- the document `id` has not been acted on before.

**Replay store.** Ids go into `SeenDocuments`, which is persisted in the protected config and kept until each id's window passes, so a replay is refused across restarts too.
- `verify_operational` records nothing. It returns a `VerifiedOperational`, which the caller commits only once the document is **bound**: a removal notice from a community the named persona holds a membership with, or an answer that matched something of ours. A community's manifest is taken only from a community we asked, are applying to, or belong to. A party that can only sign with its own key never writes to the set.
- The set is keyed by `(issuer, id)`. Ids are capped at 256 characters.
- Quotas are 1024 ids per issuer and 256 issuers. At the bound they **refuse**; nothing is evicted before its window ends, so a flood cannot push out a genuine notice and replay it.
- The dispatcher reports a change whenever the set changes, so it is persisted even when a handler reports nothing else.

Membership and role credentials and vetter grants stay `assertionMethod`. A vetter grant is kept only when it verifies, including its revocation status, which fails closed.

### Sender sources

`dispatch_inbound`'s `from` selection, `authenticated_sender` and the dispatcher's `from_did` are now documented as routing hints, pointing to `proof_check`.

## Rollout

Deploy together with VTI PR 3 (the VTC signing operational documents, including refusals, with its `authentication` key, and including `recipient` and `issuedAt`). There is no compatibility window: these are test deployments, upgraded together. Until then, openvtc refuses the VTC's removal notices and vetting answers.

## Breaking changes

These are test deployments with no compatibility path.
- **Wire:**
  - relationship bodies gain `didProof`/`personaProof`, and both peers need this version;
  - a VTC must sign operational documents with an `authentication` key and include `recipient` and `issuedAt`.
- **Library:**
  - `verify_removal_notice(message, from, our_dids, resolver, seen, now)` and `handle_member_removal_notice(account, VerifiedRemovalNotice, from)`;
  - `vetting::inbound::handle(book, ctx, seen, message, sender)`, and `Context { did_resolver, .. }`;
  - new `ProtectedConfig::seen_documents`;
  - `create_send_message_accepted` removed.

## Tests

- **Relationship binding:**
  - a proven R-DID is accepted;
  - refused: missing DID proof, R-DID without a persona proof, a proof from another thread, a switch to a DID the sender does not control;
  - `awaiting` refuses: wrong sender, empty or unknown thread id, established relationship, wrong state.
- **Operational documents:**
  - a fresh, signed, addressed document is accepted once, and its replay is refused;
  - refused: an `assertionMethod` proof; an authentication-purpose proof by a key not under `authentication`; a missing or wrong recipient; a missing, old or future `issuedAt`; an expired document; a foreign issuer;
  - an unsigned copy does not burn the id;
  - a document is taken only as its own signed `type`: one without a type, or handled as another type, is refused.
- **Relationship binding role:** a request's proof does not verify as an accept's.
- **Removal notice:**
  - accepted once;
  - refused: `assertionMethod`, unsigned, bare, tampered, forged, wrong sender, unaddressed, misaddressed, stale.
- **Vetting:**
  - a community answer signed with the assertion key is refused, as is a replayed one or one addressed elsewhere;
  - a tampered grant is not kept, nor is a grant whose status list cannot be read.

## Checks

`cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings` (plus `--features dev-overrides`), `cargo doc -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace -- --include-ignored` (includes the mediator end-to-end tests) and `--no-default-features` all pass locally.

## After merging `main`

Only `CHANGELOG.md` conflicted: #380's entry is now on `main`, and this PR's entry sits after it. The code merged cleanly and needed no change for trust-tasks 0.23: the proof checks here go through `proof_check`, not the stock trust-tasks `Verifier`.

After the merge, run locally: `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace` (1635 passed, 0 failed).

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] Finite timeouts (R1.2): proof-check resolution 10 s
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)

title: fix(openvtc): require proofs for relationship DIDs, removal notices and community answers (#381)
body:
fix(openvtc): require proofs for relationship DIDs, removal notices and community answers (#381)

* fix(openvtc-core): verify the proof on issued credentials

A credential a community delivers over credential-exchange/issue was
stored after checking only that its issuer matched the DIDComm sender.
Verify it before storing: resolve the issuer's DID document, require
every Data Integrity proof (eddsa-jcs-2022, mldsa44-jcs-2024) to verify
with a key of the issuer's own DID listed under assertionMethod, check
the validity window, and refuse a revoked credential via the existing
status-list check.

handle_credential_issue now takes a VerifiedIssuedCredential, which only
the verifier produces. Account recovery (rebuild::plan) applies the same
check to each membership it would restore, and the vault sync skips a
locally held credential that does not verify.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): admit a join only on a verified membership credential

An approved join status or an allow verdict is an unsigned reply; it no
longer activates the membership. It acknowledges the join, and the
membership becomes Active - and the reciprocal membership credential is
sent - only when the community's credential arrives and verifies.

Factor the proof check into proof_check (signer DID binding, relationship
per proof purpose, proof sets) so other signed messages can use it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): fail closed on credential status, and read proof-set status lists

A credential's revocation status must now be established: an unreachable
or unverifiable status list refuses the credential, with a message that
says to retry. The list is read by a new status_list module that
verifies it with proof_check, so a list signed with a proof set
(Ed25519 + ML-DSA-44) verifies. The vetter grant check uses the same
reader. StatusPolicy is removed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): activate only a pending join; bind verification methods to their controller

- a credential lands only on a Pending or Active membership, and only a
  Pending join is activated; an ended membership is not revived
- a proof's verification method must be controlled by the signer
- allow five minutes of skew on a proof's created, matching issuedAt
- cache fetched status lists for at most five minutes (or the list's
  validUntil/ttl), re-verifying on every use

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): check a delivered credential locally before fetching; keep status fetches on public hosts

- a credential-issue is checked against local state (issuer is the sender,
  subject is our persona, known kind, a live membership with the sender)
  before its proof is verified or its status list fetched, so a party we
  hold no membership with cannot make this client resolve or fetch
- status-list fetches refuse loopback, private, link-local and other
  non-public hosts: IP literals and special-use names in the URL, names by
  what they resolve to, and every redirect hop (affinidi-net-guard); no proxy
- a VRC's proof goes through proof_check: assertionMethod purpose, a method
  the issuer lists and controls

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): require proofs for relationship DIDs, removal notices and community answers

The transport sender is a routing hint, not an identity. Decisions that
turn on who said something now rest on a Data Integrity proof checked
against the party's DID document (proof_check):

- relationship request/accept carry didProof (and personaProof for an
  R-DID) binding the DID to the handshake thread and both personas, by
  authentication keys; accept, finalize and reject are matched by the
  thread id of a request in the right state from the right party, with
  no fallback to the sender
- a removal notice is acted on only as the community's signed Trust
  Task document
- a community's vetting answers are acted on only when signed by it, and
  a vetter role credential is kept only when its proof verifies
- document the sender sources in didcomm.rs as routing hints

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): operational documents need the authentication key, a recipient, freshness and no replay

Removal notices and a community's vetting answers are operational
documents (VTI-KEY-106/107). They are acted on only with a proof under
proofPurpose authentication by a key listed under authentication, a
recipient that is one of our personas, an issuedAt inside the kind's
window (and any expiresAt), and a document id not seen before. Seen ids
are persisted in the protected config until their window passes, and
recorded only after the proof verifies.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): bind operational documents before recording them; bound the replay set without eviction

verify_operational no longer records: the caller commits the verified
document only once it is bound (a removal notice from a community the
named persona belongs to; a community answer that matched something of
ours). A manifest from a community we have no business with is ignored.
The replay set is keyed by (issuer, id), ids are capped at 256
characters, and per-issuer and issuer quotas refuse rather than evict.
The dispatcher reports a change whenever the set changes, so it is
persisted.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc): bind operational documents to their signed type, and relationship proofs to their side

- an operational document is acted on only as its own signed `type`: the
  handler's type must equal it, and the freshness window follows from it
  (OperationalKind::of), so a community's signed answer cannot be replayed
  as a removal notice or as the answer to another question
- the relationship DID binding statement names its role (request or
  accept), so a request's proof cannot stand as an accept's in the same
  handshake

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vetting): sign the e2e manifest under its response type

The over-the-wire vetting test signed the community's manifest answer
with the request type (manifest/0.2) in the document while the message
carried manifest/0.2#response. #381's operational check correctly
refuses a document whose signed type differs from the type it is
handled as, so the applicant never learned the requirements. Sign it as
a VTC does, under the response type. The test is #[ignore]d and only
CI's coverage job (--include-ignored) runs it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.23.0` → `0.23.1` | patch |

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.3.1`) | `0.3.0` → `0.3.1` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.3.0` → `0.3.1` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc): git-ns/account/unlink and cnm git unlink
body:
## Summary

Implements **`git-ns/account/unlink/0.1`** (spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#636): a member removes the link between their DID and their account on one forge. It uses the generated types, URI and error code from `trust-tasks-rs` 0.23, which main already takes. The branch is merged up to main, including #1742 (one forge account per member), #1745 (break-glass and separation of duties), reseat 0.3, drift resolve 0.3 and reproject.

### vtc-service
- A new `handle_unlink` → `ops::account_unlink`.
  - The binding is deleted in one edit of the member row, under the git-ns store lock that serialises link completion. So a link completing at the same moment is either unlinked (if it's the account named) or kept.
  - Optional `accountId` guard: `notLinked` if the account linked now is a different one.
  - Right after, `project_roles` queues the complete `desiredRoles` of every bridge-mode namespace on that forge. The account is in none of them, so the bridge withdraws the roles it gave it. No `removeAccounts`: a role the bridge didn't give stays and is reported as drift.
  - Audit: `gitNs.account.unlinked`, one row per affected namespace. It names the member and the forge, never the account.
- **Who may unlink.** Only the DID the account is linked to, as the spec says. The task has no subject, so nobody can unlink another member's account, and nobody can free an account for themselves.
  - Unlinking grants no right and no role: the next projection is simply computed without the account.
  - An administrator who needs a member's forge roles withdrawn revokes the rights or resolves the drift. To free a lapsed member's account, they remove the member, and the departure sweep deletes the binding.
  - An admin unlink with a `subject` is left to a later spec version.
- **Interaction with #1742.** A lapsed member keeps their account (nobody else may link it) but it projects nothing. They can still unlink it. After that, a current member who proves control of the account can link it.
- **Privacy.** Any caller with nothing linked, a non-member included, gets `notLinked`, so the answer doesn't reveal who is a member. Normal consent class.

### cnm-cli / vtc-client
- `cnm git unlink --forge <host> [--account-id <id>]`. It reads the linked account first (`git-ns/view/0.2`) and sends its id as the guard, so a re-link in between is never removed. For a lapsed member, whom `view` refuses, it prints how to pass `--account-id`.
- `vtc-client`: `git_ns_unlink_account`.
- `cnm git link --help` no longer says there is no unlink.

### Docs
`docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md` covers:
- unlinking, and the guard;
- how roles are withdrawn;
- the audit record;
- who may unlink, and what an administrator does instead.

### Console
The admin console can't sign as a member, so there is no Unlink button. The member's *Git rights* card (#1727) already names `cnm git unlink --forge <host>`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib git_ns` (193 passed), including:
  - `unlinking_drops_the_account_from_the_projection_and_only_that`, which covers:
    - the guard;
    - the binding goes and other members' stay;
    - the next `projectRoles` drops the account and keeps others, with no `removeAccounts`;
    - rights are unchanged;
    - the audit row names the forge and not the account id or login;
    - `notLinked` for a repeat, for another member's account, and for a non-member.
  - `an_account_on_a_forge_with_no_bridge_can_still_be_unlinked`
  - #1742's uniqueness test now also covers a lapsed member unlinking their own account, and another member then linking it.
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --test trust_task_manifest` (8 passed)
- [x] `cargo test -p cnm-cli git::` (23 passed)
- [x] admin-ui `npm run lint`, and vitest on `Members.test.tsx` and `RepoDetail.test.tsx` (39 passed)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p cnm-cli -p vtc-client --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`

## Summary

#642 made `proof` REQUIRED on `git-ns/view` 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3. - `specs/git-ns/view/0.4/spec.md`: `proofRequirement` is now `REQUIRED`, with 0.3's rationale. Nothing else in the specification discusses the proof, and the payload schema does not mention it.

## Audit

I compared every spec version added by #635–#643 and #646–#651 with the version before it. None of the others declares a weaker proof requirement than its predecessor. The specs #642 edited in place (`git-ns/account/link-status/0.1`, `vtc/members/personhood/challenge/0.1`, `vtc/vetting/vetters/profile/0.1`, `vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.1`) have no newer versions.

- `npm run check-bindings`

title: fix(vtc): one forge account per member, and only current members' accounts count
body:
## Summary

This comes out of the account-linking review: one forge account links to one member, and only a current member's account should count.

- **Uniqueness** (`git-ns/account/link` item 4) was already enforced: `complete_account_link` runs under the git-ns store lock, which serialises every link. As a belt to that, the check and the write are now one step under the member-row lock (`members::storage::edit_lock`). New regression test: a second member completing a link to an already-linked forge id ends `failed`, and the account stays with the first. This includes the case where the first member's access has lapsed.
- **Bug: a departed member's links could outlive them.** `sweep_departures` returns early when no departed member held a right, and the link deletion was after that return. So a member who linked an account but held no right kept the link after leaving, against the spec's "MUST delete it when the member leaves". Link deletion is now its own pass, `lifecycle::sweep_departed_links`, with a test.
- **Current members only.** `bridge::linked_accounts`, which feeds the role projection and drift adoption, now skips members who aren't current (ACL gone or expired) but haven't left. Such a member keeps the account, so no one else can link it, but it projects no forge role.
- **`GET /v1/git-ns/accounts` gains `memberCurrent`.** The Repos plugin's account index skips non-current members, so drift no longer offers *Adopt into VTC* for them. The daemon already refused that adoption. New UI test.

## Behaviour and API changes to flag

- `GitNsAccountRow` gains the required field `memberCurrent` (openapi.json and wire.ts regenerated). It is additive for JSON readers.
- A lapsed member's linked account no longer projects forge roles. Their rights were already revoked by the departure sweep, so in practice this only closes the window before the sweep runs.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib -- git_ns` (122 pass), including:
  - `a_forge_account_already_linked_to_a_member_cannot_be_linked_to_another`
  - `a_departed_member_with_no_rights_loses_their_linked_accounts`
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --test openapi_snapshot`, `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`
- [x] `npm run lint`, `npx vitest run` (401 pass), including *offers no adoption for an account whose member is no longer current*

title: feat(git-ns): move repo/create to 0.3, name owners, close the self-grant hole
body:
## Summary

- Moves `openvtc-core`'s `git-ns/repo/create` client from `0.1` to `0.3`. In `0.3` a namespace admin whose `git.repo.create` is only implied by `git.ns.admin` can no longer make themselves owner (and forge admin) of a repository they create — they must name another member in the new optional `owners` field, or the VTC refuses with `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`. Naming owners is itself a grant of `git.repo.own`, refused with `git-ns:escalation` without the authority to grant it.
- Adds an Owners field to the Repos panel's new-repository form (type to filter known members, Ctrl+A to add, Ctrl+D to paste a DID for someone not listed), and arms the change for confirmation once owners are named.
- `Refusal::explain()` shows the exact break-glass guidance for `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`.
- Updates existing `git-ns/repo/create` tests for the new `owners` field and adds tests for naming owners and for the `selfGrantNotAllowed` refusal, in both `openvtc-core` and the TUI (`repos_actions`, key mapping, rendering).

Pairs with [OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1745](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1745) and [trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#641](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/issues/641).

## Versions

The upstream releases are all published, so this now takes them directly (the temporary trust-tasks patch commit is reverted):

- `trust-tasks-rs` / `trust-tasks-proof` 0.23, `trust-tasks-capability-client` 0.23
- `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.28.1, `affinidi-tdk` 0.18, `affinidi-messaging-test-mediator` 0.11.1
- `vta-sdk` 0.53, `vta-service` 0.43 (dev), `did-git-sign` 0.5 (VGI v0.5.0)

`Cargo.lock` resolves **one** node each of `trust-tasks-rs`, `trust-tasks-proof`, `vta-sdk`, `affinidi-messaging-sdk` and `affinidi-tdk`.

trust-tasks 0.23 also makes a proof required on `git-ns/view` and `git-ns/account/link-status`, so those requests are now signed, and declares `git-ns:roleMapUnknown`, which the TUI explains.

Merge together with OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1745.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p openvtc-core git_ns` — 28 passed (pre-revert, against the temporary patch)
- [x] `cargo test -p openvtc` (repos-related + full suite) — all passed (pre-revert, against the temporary patch)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — all passed (pre-revert, against the temporary patch)
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean (pre-revert, against the temporary patch)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` — clean (pre-revert, against the temporary patch)
- [ ] Re-run the full test plan once `trust-tasks-rs` 0.23 is taken for real

title: feat(vtc/git-ns): separation of duties and break-glass for elevated git rights
body:
## What

This implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#641, the 2026-09-25 decision. An **elevated** git right (`git.ns.admin`, `git.repo.create`, `git.repo.own`) must be granted by someone other than its recipient. If nobody else is available, the member uses **break-glass**: an explicit self-grant that takes effect immediately and never expires. It is gated by a passkey, requires a written justification, and stays flagged in front of every other administrator until one of them ratifies or revokes it.

### Server (`vtc-service`, `vti-common`)
- **Fixed rule 7:** an elevated self-grant is refused with `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`, and the message names `cnm git break-glass …`. The rule applies to grant 0.3, to drift adopt (through `right_grant_via`), to `repo/adopt` when the adopter names themselves as owner, and to reseat to oneself. The actor is compared after console-key delegation. Self-grants of maintain and commit.sign still work. Bind is not a self-grant.
- **`git-ns/right/break-glass/0.1`** (`git_ns/break_glass.rs`):
  - **Who may use it:** someone with grant authority over the right, or a community admin taking `ns.admin` on a headless namespace (`notHeadless` otherwise).
  - **Passkey:** an **operation-bound passkey step-up is always required** (`acl::bound_step_up`, aal2 with user verification, the acting DID's own passkey). The spent mark now returns its evidence (credential id and bound digest) for the audit row.
  - **Admin gate:** it bypasses the `elevated_requires_admin` stand-in, because the real step-up applies.
  - **The record:** it takes effect immediately, has no expiry, and is flagged `breakGlass {by, at, justification, effectiveAt?, ratifiedBy?, ratifiedAt?}`.
  - **Audit failure:** if the critical audit row cannot be written, the break-glass is rolled back.
- **Ratify** (`git-ns/right/ratify/0.1`):
  - It is never allowed from the subject, and it is bound to the `breakGlassAt` the ratifier read.
  - A community admin can ratify, as can someone whose own grant authority is not itself an unratified break-glass.
  - It is gated like a grant of the same right.
- **Revoke:** any community admin may revoke an unratified break-glass, and no policy can refuse that. Unratified and expiring records never count toward the last-owner or last-admin invariants.
- **Visibility:**
  - `AuditEvent::GitNsBreakGlass` records the break-glass, and a new `AuditEvent::severity()` rates it as **Critical**. It carries the justification, the entitlement, the step-up evidence, the policy version and any notices that could not be delivered. The usual `GitNsOperation` row is still written.
  - Activity shows `gitNs.right.breakGlass`, `…BreakGlassRatified` and `…BreakGlassRevoked`.
  - A signed **`git-ns/right/break-glass-notice/0.1`** goes to every community admin and every live ns admin except the actor. It is sent through `AppState::send_to_member` (DIDComm through the VTC's mediator, guaranteed delivery), the same path as the removal notice.
  - `git-ns/view/0.4` returns the records, `GET /v1/git-ns/break-glass` is new, and the rights rows carry `breakGlass`. The registry projection is unchanged.
- **Policy** (`git_ns.rego` settings): `break_glass` (`enabled` by default, or `disabled`), `break_glass_delay_seconds` (up to a day, revocable meanwhile) and `break_glass_min_justification_chars`. The policy can also deny `right.breakGlass` or `right.ratify`. It cannot suppress the audit row, the notices or the surfaces.

- **`git-ns/repo/create/0.3`:** the creator owns the repository only when they hold `git.repo.create` **by explicit record**, either granted by someone else or recorded through break-glass. A `git.repo.create` that is only implied by `git.ns.admin` gives no creator ownership. That requester names another member in the new `owners`, or is refused `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed` with a message that names break-glass. Naming other owners counts as granting `own` (`git-ns:escalation`). A single-admin community breaks the glass once for `git.repo.create` on the namespace, not once per repository.
- **Members only (fixed rule 5):** an elevated right (own, repo.create, ns.admin) goes only to a current member with an ACL entry, and only from an actor who is one. This applies to grant, create, repo/adopt (including the reservation path), transfer, drift adopt and break-glass, and policy cannot waive it. A throwaway `did:key` the actor controls cannot stand in for a second person.

### `cnm`
- `cnm git break-glass --right=… --resource=… --justification=…`. On a step-up refusal it prints `<vtc>/admin/step-up#request=…`, waits for Enter, and resends the **identical** signed document.
- `cnm git ratify --subject=… --right=… --resource=… --break-glass-at=… [--statement=…]` and `cnm git break-glass-list`.
- `cnm git create --owner=<did>` (repeatable) sends repo/create 0.3. The generic `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed` help reads: "This would give you an elevated right (own, repo.create or ns.admin) on your own authority. Ask another community administrator to do it, or use break-glass (`cnm git break-glass`), which is audited and must be ratified."
- `cnm git view` shows a banner and flags each break-glass right. All printed commands are fish-safe.
- `grant` and `revoke` send 0.3 (`vtc-client`'s `git_ns_grant` and `git_ns_revoke` are now the 0.3 calls; the 0.1 methods and the `_v3` names are gone).

### Admin console
- A persistent banner on every page for every admin while anything is unratified or pending. It cannot be dismissed.
- **Repos → Break-glass grants**, with Ratify and Revoke. The grantee is never offered Ratify, and the page explains why.
- The flag chip next to every flagged right. The last-owner note follows the new invariants.
- Drift adopt never offers a viewer their own forge account as an elevated right: it hands the command to another administrator and names break-glass.
- The member page (`MemberGit.tsx`) flags a break-glass right with `BreakGlassChip`.
- When the viewer is the subject of an elevated grant, the grant and reseat forms don't offer it. They explain separation of duties and offer **Break glass…** instead, with the justification field and the consequences.
- `SignTaskDialog` answers a `stepUpRequest` refusal with the passkey and resends the same document. `/admin/step-up` finishes a step-up handed over from `cnm`.
- The create dialog takes an optional owner DID and sends repo/create 0.3. The hint explains that an empty owner makes the signer the owner, which works only on an explicit `git.repo.create`.
- Grant and revoke are sent as 0.3, and the `trust_task_manifest` census is updated. `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4` is allowlisted as a spine document.

## Deliberate breaks
- Self-grants of own, create and ns.admin that used to succeed are now refused, including drift adopts of your own forge role and reseating a namespace to yourself. A namespace admin creating a repository with no `owners`, on a `git.repo.create` that is only implied, is now refused as well.
- **repo/create is served at 0.3 only.** 0.1 is refused as an unknown task.
- Elevated rights to or from a DID with no ACL entry, which used to succeed for `own`, are now refused `git-ns:membersOnly`.
- **Grant and revoke are served at 0.3 only.** 0.1 is dropped with no compatibility window: a 0.1 client gets an unknown-task refusal. The pre-DID-core subject accommodation in revoke goes with it, because 0.3's schema holds every subject to DID-core. That is fine for test deployments, which are recreated rather than migrated. The openvtc TUI moves to 0.3 in OpenVTC/openvtc#384.
- A namespace admin with no passkey registered with the VTC cannot break the glass. They get the existing "register a passkey" refusal.

## Coordination
- #1729 (ns-admin projection): break-glass is how an ns admin gets an explicit `own`, and with it a forge role.
- The drift/resolve 0.3 recipient binding (trust-tasks #640) and reseat 0.3 (#635) should declare `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`.

## Merge order

**#1736 first, then #1735, then this PR.** This branch merges main and `feat/git-ns-reproject-role-map` (#1736). It does not depend on #1735. Where both touch drift adopt, the conflicts are small and in the same direction.

## trust-tasks-rs 0.23

Built on main's trust-tasks-rs 0.23, which carries #641 (break-glass, ratify, break-glass-notice, grant/revoke 0.3, repo/create 0.3, view 0.4). The local `[patch.crates-io]` is discarded, and Cargo.lock has one trust-tasks-rs (0.23). Reseat uses the generated `reseat::v0_3` (from #1736). The console's reseat form uses the generic separation-of-duties refusal and offers break-glass.

## With #1736's role map

- **Fixed rule 7 now asks `rules::elevated_on`**, which is `Right::is_elevated_in` under the target namespace's map. So grant 0.3, drift adopt and repo/adopt refuse a self-grant of `git.repo.maintain` where the map projects it to forge `admin`. They fail closed (refuse it too) while a bridge-mode namespace's map is unknown. A manual-mode namespace projects no forge role, so its elevated rights stay ns.admin, repo.create and own.
- Reseat (always ns.admin), repo/create (always own) and break-glass (only the three) are unchanged. The refusal for a right elevated only by the map points to another owner or administrator, not to break-glass.
- The console's `adoptStanding` hands over a self-adopt that the map makes elevated, without offering break-glass. The docs describe the rule.
- Two #1729 drift tests were adjusted: a namespace admin's own forge `admin` is now adopted by someone else, and one fixture reports the default map so the adopt reaches rule 7.

Rebased onto main after #1726, #1727, #1728, #1732, #1741 and #1747, and later merged with main (#1729, #1764) and #1736.

Local results: `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib git_ns` (139, including the repo/create 0.3 ownership and members-only sock-puppet tests, including the end-to-end drift-adopt self-grant refusal and a check that grant and revoke 0.1 and 0.2 are not served), `openapi_snapshot`, `trust_task_manifest`, the vti-common audit tests, the `cnm-cli` tests, and clippy `-D warnings` and fmt on the touched crates. Admin UI: `npx vitest run` (460) and `tsc -b`.

After the merges and 0.23: `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib git_ns` (182; after the two drift-test fixes `git_ns::tests::` re-run, 141 pass), `--test trust_task_manifest` (8), `cargo test -p cnm-cli git::` (21), clippy `-D warnings` (vtc-service, cnm-cli, vtc-client), `cargo fmt --check`, admin-ui `npm run lint` and `vitest run` (471) all pass locally.

The openvtc TUI banner is in OpenVTC/openvtc#384. Step-up passkeys for members who are not console users are a stacked follow-up.

title: feat(vtc/git-ns): separation of duties and break-glass for elevated git rights (#1745)
body:
feat(vtc/git-ns): separation of duties and break-glass for elevated git rights (#1745)

* feat(vtc-service): re-project git roles, and use the bridge's reported role map

Implements two follow-ups to the configurable bridge role map (VGI #84),
spec-first in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#639.

git-ns/bridge/event 0.3 (roleMapReported)
- Served beside 0.1 and 0.2; all three are read as 0.3 by one handler.
- The report is refused malformedRequest when a map is unordered
  (own >= maintain >= commit, commit <= write) or lists a repository
  twice, and permissionDenied when a repos/stale resource lies outside
  the namespace. Otherwise it is kept on the namespace (git_ns::role_map),
  and only while the same bridge DID serves it.
- Each stale active or orphaned repository has its roles digest
  forgotten, so the projector re-sends its complete desiredRoles without
  anyone asking. A repository leaves `stale` when a projectRoles job
  queued after the report succeeds.
- drift/resolve adopt derives the right from the map: the lowest right
  whose role is the observed one. A revert weighs as revoking own when
  the role is at or above the one own projects to. Without a report the
  default map is assumed. A namespace admin gets no forge role under any
  map.

git-ns/roles/reproject 0.1
- Open to a community administrator, or to git.ns.admin on the namespace
  by explicit record. A repository owner is refused. Covers a namespace
  (every active or orphaned repository) or one repository. Normal consent
  class, policy action roles.reproject, audited as
  gitNs.roles.reprojected. Refused with manualMode or noForgeAccess.
- `cnm git reproject <resource> [--reason]` and
  vtc-client git_ns_reproject.

Console (Repos)
- The namespace and repository rows carry the effective role map
  (roleMap, roleMapSource, roleMapStale).
- The people tables show each person's effective forge role, and "no
  forge role" for a namespace admin.
- Drift adopt and revert use projectedRight / driftRevertImpact over the
  repository's map. rightForForgeRole is removed.
- Stale repositories are flagged, and the namespace card and repository
  header gain a "Re-project roles" button.

Behaviour change: on a personal account a revert of collaborator write
(or above) now weighs as revoking own, because write is the role own
projects to there. Before, it weighed as revoking maintain.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* style(vtc-service): rustfmt the reproject test

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-service): owners re-project their own repository; an unknown role map after a bridge change

Follows trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#639 as revised.

- git-ns/roles/reproject: a repository resource is also admitted for
  `git.repo.own` on it, explicit or implied. A namespace still needs the
  community-administrator capability or `git.ns.admin` by explicit
  record. Entitlement is checked before the repository is looked up, so
  a caller entitled to nothing learns nothing about which names are
  recorded.
- git_ns::role_map adds Source::Unknown. A report held from a bridge DID
  that no longer serves the namespace is derived as the default map and
  exposed as `roleMapSource: "unknown"`. The namespace card shows a "Role
  map unknown" finding until the serving bridge reports.
- The console's re-project consent note distinguishes a namespace from a
  repository. cnm help and the docs say who may re-project.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc/git-ns): separation of duties and break-glass for elevated git rights

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#641.

- Fixed rule 7: no elevated self-grant (git.ns.admin, git.repo.create,
  git.repo.own) through grant 0.1/0.3, drift adopt, repo/adopt or reseat;
  refused git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed, naming cnm git break-glass.
- git-ns/right/break-glass/0.1: grant authority, or a community admin on a
  headless namespace; always an operation-bound passkey step-up
  (acl::bound_step_up, whose spent mark now yields its evidence); mandatory
  justification; immediate, no expiry; flagged breakGlass on the record.
- git-ns/right/ratify/0.1 and revoke 0.3: another administrator ratifies,
  bound to breakGlass.at; any community admin may revoke an unratified one,
  which policy cannot refuse. Unratified records do not count toward the
  last-owner and last-admin invariants.
- Visibility no policy can turn off: AuditEvent::GitNsBreakGlass at
  AuditSeverity::Critical with the step-up evidence, activity items, a signed
  git-ns/right/break-glass-notice/0.1 to every community admin and ns admin,
  view 0.4, GET /v1/git-ns/break-glass, and breakGlass on the rights rows.
- git_ns.rego settings: break_glass (enabled by default), a delay and a
  minimum justification; deny decisions on right.breakGlass and right.ratify.
- cnm: git break-glass, git ratify and git break-glass-list; git view flags
  break-glass rights; grant and revoke move to 0.3.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-admin-ui): break-glass banner, list, flags and passkey step-up

- A banner on every page for every administrator while any break-glass grant
  is unratified or pending; it clears only when one is ratified or revoked.
- Repos > Break-glass grants: ratify or revoke through the signed-task flow;
  the grantee is never offered Ratify. Hand-over commands are fish-safe.
- The break-glass flag next to every flagged right.
- An elevated self-grant is not offered; Break glass... is, with its
  justification and consequences stated.
- SignTaskDialog answers a stepUpRequest refusal with the passkey and
  re-sends the identical document; /admin/step-up completes a step-up
  handed over from cnm.
- Grant and revoke are sent as 0.3.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc/git-ns): serve grant and revoke at 0.3 only; refuse a self-adopt in the console

- git-ns/right/grant and git-ns/right/revoke are served at 0.3 only: 0.1 is
  dropped with no compatibility window, so no client reaches a grant that
  skips fixed rule 7 or a record answered without its breakGlass flag. The
  VTC's internals and the drift adoption use the 0.3 payload; vtc-client's
  git_ns_grant and git_ns_revoke are the 0.3 calls (the _v3 names and the
  0.1 methods are gone). Revoke's pre-DID-core subject accommodation goes
  with 0.1: 0.3's schema holds every subject to DID-core.
- Test: adopting drift on one's own linked forge account into git.repo.own
  is refused git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed, naming break-glass; nothing is
  written and the item stays outstanding.
- Test: grant and revoke 0.1 and 0.2 are not served.
- Console: adoptStanding never offers a viewer their own account as an
  elevated right; it hands the command to another administrator and names
  break-glass. The member page flags a break-glass right with
  BreakGlassChip.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-service): an unknown role map derives nothing, the newest report wins, a report names its ladder

git-ns/bridge/event 0.3 (trust-tasks-tf #639):

- no role map is assumed, the default included: until the bridge serving
  the namespace reports (after binding, after another bridge comes to
  serve it, or for good with a bridge before 0.3), drift adopt is refused
  with git-ns:roleMapUnknown and every role revert weighs as revoking
  git.repo.own;
- the report's issuedAt is kept, and one issued before the report held
  from the same bridge is acknowledged and ignored;
- a report names the forge's ladder: the VTC refuses a ladder that lists
  none or is out of order, a map role off it, and a ladder that is not the
  one it knows for a GitHub organisation, a GitHub personal account or
  Codeberg;
- a stale repository the VTC records neither active nor orphaned is not
  kept;
- Right::is_elevated_in: a right the namespace's map projects to forge
  admin is elevated there, and while the map is unknown git.repo.maintain
  is too;
- console: no map shown or derived while unknown; the drift revert task
  and dialog take the repository's map only.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc/git-ns): repo/create 0.3 and members-only elevated rights

Implements the review follow-ups in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#641.

- git-ns/repo/create is served at 0.3. The creator owns the repository
  only when they hold git.repo.create by explicit record (granted by
  someone else, or a break-glass). A git.repo.create implied by
  git.ns.admin gives no creator ownership: the requester names another
  member in the new owners, or is refused git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed, and
  the message names break-glass. Naming other owners is a grant of own
  (git-ns:escalation) to members only.
- Fixed rule 5: an elevated right (own, repo.create, ns.admin) goes only
  to a current member with an ACL entry, and only from an actor who is
  one, on grant, create, adopt, transfer, drift adopt and break-glass.
  Policy cannot waive it, so a throwaway did:key cannot stand in for a
  second person.
- cnm: git create --owner (repeatable); the generic selfGrantNotAllowed
  help names break-glass and ratification.
- Console: the create dialog takes an optional owner DID and sends 0.3.
- Tests: an implied-create self-own is refused and reserves nothing;
  naming another owner works and a non-member owner is refused; an
  explicit create owns; break-glass repo.create then create owns; the
  sock-puppet did:key is refused on grant, transfer and adopt. Tests where
  an ns admin creates a repository now name another member as owner.
- Docs and CLAUDE.md describe both rules. A fmt fix in vti-common.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(git-ns): reseat 0.3 and bridge job 0.4 use trust-tasks-rs 0.23's generated types

trust-tasks-rs 0.23 generates git-ns/namespace/reseat 0.3 and
git-ns/bridge/job 0.4, which #1729 spelled out ahead of the release.

- git_ns::reseat_v0_3 is gone: the handler takes reseat::v0_3::Payload
  through signed_handler!, ops::namespace_reseat reads v0_3's payload and
  refuses a self-reseat with the generated SELF_GRANT_NOT_ALLOWED, and
  vtc-client's RESEAT_TYPE_URI is v0_3's TYPE_URI. The module's own test
  (proof required, DID Core subject) moves to git_ns::tests.
- bridge::JOB_TYPE is job::v0_4's TYPE_URI, and acknowledgements are
  read as v0_4's Response.
- trust_task_manifest: the two UNPUBLISHED_CANONICAL_OK entries go back
  to zero, and the TODOs are resolved.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(git-ns): separation of duties counts a right the role map elevates

Fixed rule 7 (git-ns/right/grant 0.3) now asks rules::elevated_on, which
is Right::is_elevated_in (#1736) under the map of the namespace holding the
target. So every path through rules::grant_admitted (grant 0.3, drift
adopt, repo/adopt naming oneself) refuses a self-grant of
git.repo.maintain where the bridge's map projects maintain to forge
`admin`, and, while a bridge-mode namespace's map is unknown, fails closed
and refuses it too. A manual-mode namespace projects no forge role, so its
elevated rights stay ns.admin, repo.create and own. Reseat (always
ns.admin) and repo/create (always own) are unchanged, and so is
break-glass, which carries only the three. The refusal for a map-elevated
right therefore names another owner or administrator, not break-glass.

The console's adoptStanding hands over a self-adopt that the map makes
elevated, without offering break-glass. Docs describe the rule.

Tests: under a maintain->admin map an owner's self-grant of maintain is
refused with no break-glass pointer, commit.sign stays allowed, and an
administrator grants him maintain; with the map unknown the self-grant is
refused until the default map is reported. Console model test for the
hand-over.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(git-ns): #1729's drift-adopt tests under separation of duties

Two tests fail once main (#1729) and the role map (#1736) meet this
branch:

- a_namespace_admin_adopts_their_own_forge_admin_role_as_ownership had a
  namespace admin adopt `own` for themselves, which rule 7 refuses. It
  becomes a_namespace_admins_own_forge_admin_role_is_adopted_by_someone_else:
  the self-adoption is refused, another community administrator adopts it,
  and it is projected.
- drift_adopt_of_ones_own_account_into_an_elevated_right_is_a_self_grant ran
  before the bridge reported its role map, so it was refused
  git-ns:roleMapUnknown before it reached rule 7. The fixture now reports
  the default map.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: feat(git-ns): an adoption names the member who receives the right
body:
Spec first: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#640. Companion TUI change: OpenVTC/openvtc#382. (#1728, which this was stacked on, has merged.)

## Problem

A `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1 `adopt` does not name who receives the right. The VTC resolves the item's forge account to whoever has linked it **when the task runs**. If the account is relinked between the owner reading the item and signing, the owner's signed document grants a right, published to the Trust Registry, to someone the owner never saw.

## What changed

**Server (`vtc-service/src/git_ns`)**
- Serves `git-ns/drift/resolve` **0.3**. An adopt must carry `subject`, and a revert must not; either mistake is `malformedRequest`.
- Adopt step 3 refuses with the new **`git-ns/drift/resolve:subjectChanged`** when the account is linked to someone other than `subject`.
- **The link check is repeated in `right_grant_via`, under `store::write_lock`** (`GrantVia.linked_to`). Every link and unlink is written under that same lock: `bridge::handle_event` for `accountLinked`, and `lifecycle::sweep_departures`. So no relink can fall between the check and the write.
- 0.1 is still served for **revert**. A 0.1 **adopt** is refused with the framework's `unsupportedVersion` (new `OpError::UnsupportedVersion`), with a message naming 0.3. That follows the spec's SHOULD.

- **Adopt step 5 compares with the member's *projected* right** (`bridge::projected_repo_right`): the right the projector lists them at from rights in their own name, via `highest_repo_rights` with `git.ns.admin` rows left out. A namespace admin projects to no forge role, so one holding `maintain` can now have a forge `admin` adopted as `own`; before, their implied `own` made it unadoptable. The role-to-right side stays `drift::projected_right`, which #1736 generalises to the reported role map (no second implementation).
- **Adopt step 6, separation of duties** (trust-tasks #641 / #1745): an adoption that would record an elevated right (only `git.repo.own` is reachable here) for the resolver themselves is refused **`git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`**, before policy, with a message pointing to `git-ns/right/break-glass`. The actor is the DID after console-key delegation (`tasks::acting_as`). Adopting `maintain`/`commit.sign` for oneself stays allowed. `Right::is_elevated` is added verbatim as #1745 defines it, so the two merge cleanly.

**Admin console:** sends 0.3. `projectedRepoRank` replaces `heldRepoRank` (ns.admin no longer counts), and an adoption that would make the viewer an owner is handed over, naming break-glass, rather than offered. An adopt carries, as `subject`, the member its dialog already names, and the hand-over command gains `--subject=<DID>`, fish-safe.

**`cnm git drift resolve`:**
- New `--subject`: required to adopt, refused on revert, and validated as a DID Core DID before signing.
- Sends 0.3 through the new `vtc-client` `git_ns_drift_resolve_v3`.
- Explains `subjectChanged`.

**`vtc-client`:** `git_ns_drift_resolve` (0.1) is `#[deprecated]`, not removed, so the published API stays additive.

The `trust_task_manifest` census lists drift/resolve 0.3.

## Merge order

**#1736 first, then this PR, then #1745.** This branch merges main and `feat/git-ns-reproject-role-map` (#1736). If #1736 lands first, this PR's diff shrinks to its own changes.

## trust-tasks-rs 0.23

Built on main's trust-tasks-rs 0.23, which generates `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.3. A new commit reverts the `[patch.crates-io]` that 95f8f46c added. Cargo.lock has one trust-tasks-rs (0.23). 0.3 does not re-declare `git-ns:roleMapUnknown`, so `drift::ROLE_MAP_UNKNOWN` comes from 0.1's generated codes.

## With #1736's role map

- **Step 6 uses `Right::is_elevated_in(&ns, repo)`**, not `Right::is_elevated`. Where the bridge's map gives maintainers forge `admin`, adopting a forge `admin` as `git.repo.maintain` for oneself is refused `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`. The refusal points to another owner, not to break-glass, which does not carry `maintain`. The console mirrors this with `isElevatedIn(right, repo.roleMap)` in `adoptStanding`.
- Two #1729 tests asserted 0.2 behaviour and now test 0.3's:
  - A namespace admin's own forge `admin` is adopted by someone else. The self-adoption is refused.
  - A `roleChanged` over `maintain` is measured against the projected right, so it is a raise, and the self-adoption is refused by step 6.

## Behaviour changes (deliberate, per the standing security/usability rule)

- **A 0.1 adopt is refused.** Before, it granted to whoever held the link. This affects the openvtc TUI shipped in #379; #382 removes adopt there and says where to adopt instead.
- **`cnm git drift resolve … adopt` now requires `--subject`.**
- **Self-adopting `own` is refused** (`git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`), even by a community administrator; another owner adopts it or the resolver breaks the glass. The same goes for `maintain` where the role map projects it to forge `admin`, without the break-glass option.
- **`subjectChanged` is a new refusal.** A relinked account adopts nothing and must be read again.

## Tests

- server:
  - `drift_resolve_adopts_only_for_the_member_it_names`: a wrong `subject` is refused; a relink after reading is refused with no right recorded for anyone; naming the member it is linked to now adopts.
  - `an_adopted_grant_rechecks_the_link_where_it_is_written`: `right_grant_via` refuses a mismatched link (`subjectChanged`) and a vanished one (`accountNotLinked`) under the lock.
  - `a_namespace_admin_adopts_a_raise_over_their_own_name_right`: an ns admin holding `maintain` has a forge `admin` adopted as `own` by another admin.
  - `a_namespace_admin_alone_has_no_projected_right`
  - `an_adoption_never_grants_the_resolver_an_elevated_right`: self-adopting `own` is refused, signed directly or through a console key, recording nothing; an owner adopts `maintain` for himself.
  - `drift_resolve_0_1_reverts_but_does_not_adopt`
  - malformed: an adopt without `subject`, and a revert with one.
  - 0.3 is served.
- console: projected rank (ns.admin counts for nothing); self-adopt of `own` handed over naming break-glass; adopt payload, command and document carry `subject`; `subject` is shell-safe.
- cnm: payload building, `--subject` rules, and the `subjectChanged` hint.

`cargo test -p vtc-service --lib git_ns` (126 tests), `cargo test -p vtc-service --test trust_task_manifest`, `cargo test -p cnm-cli git::`, `cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p cnm-cli -p vtc-client --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, and admin-ui `npm run lint` + vitest (`model.test.ts`, `RepoDetail.test.tsx`) pass locally.

After the merges and 0.23: `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib git_ns` (168 pass), `--test trust_task_manifest` (8), `cargo test -p cnm-cli git::` (20), clippy `-D warnings` (vtc-service, cnm-cli, vtc-client), `cargo fmt --check`, admin-ui `npm run lint` and `vitest run` (433) all pass locally.
