  `RefreshTombstone` gains `cause` to record why a token was retired.
  `Superseded` is excluded from the innocent-retry grace window on purpose:
  that concession answers a lost rotation response, and a client that has
  just logged in holds its replacement. Honouring a replay there would have
  handed the new token to whoever replayed a pre-login theft — strictly worse
  than the gap being closed.

  Replaying a superseded token is refused and audited as
  `AuthAuditEvent::RefreshSuperseded` (`warn!`, `security_alert = true`), but
  the session is left running. Unlike reuse, the presented token is already
  dead — the login took its index — so revoking adds nothing against a thief,
  while the ordinary cause is a second device still holding what it was
  issued before the user signed in elsewhere. Killing the session there would
  sign out the client that is demonstrably current, and the re-login it
  forces would set the same trap again. The event still carries
  `security_alert` because a pre-login theft and a stale device are
  indistinguishable from the node's side; only an operator correlating them
  can say which it was.

  `cleanup_expired_sessions` now also sweeps `refresh:` entries that their
  session no longer names. Retirement fixes new logins but cannot reach
  entries already written, and those rows carry no TTL and are not inert: an
  orphan resolves again as soon as its DID has a session row, so it outlives
  a revocation and returns at the next login. The sweep is safe against a
  concurrent login or rotation because every writer stores the session row
  before its index entry, so an entry that disagrees with its row is stale
  rather than half-written.

  Also in this change: `RefreshReuseDetected` takes its `did` from the
  tombstone, so the alert names the account on the `SessionGone` path where
  the session row is absent by definition; the lost-response retry log
  carries `audit = true`, since a stable session id had left it
  indistinguishable from an ordinary rotation; and the module header no
  longer describes a delete-and-recreate the handler stopped doing.

  `refresh_reuse_grace` stays at 30s, now documented as a starting point
  rather than a ceiling — a client only discovers a lost response when its
  own HTTP timeout fires, so a deployment whose clients retry later than that
  may want 60s. It is a user-experience call, not a security one: the
  successor-unspent condition, not the clock, is what keeps the concession
  narrow. `0` still disables it entirely.

- **vta**: Session and consent operations are scoped to the caller's authority ([#1717](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1717))

Found by the scope sweep that followed FTL-29904 ([#1715](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1715)). Both surfaces
  checked the caller's role and never the subject or datum it acted on.

  Sessions (VTI-SES-043, VTI-ACL-050). Any admin could list every session on
  the VTA and end any of them, a super-admin's included, via
  `DELETE /auth/sessions?did=`, `DELETE /auth/sessions/{id}` and
  `auth/revoke-session`; initiators could list them all. Session management now
  follows ACL management: `operations::acl::may_manage_subject` answers "may
  this caller act on this subject" with the rule `acl/delete` applies (the
  caller itself, a super-admin, or a managing role that can see the subject's
  entry and is at least as privileged). A super-admin's entry names no context,
  so a scoped admin never reaches it; a subject with no entry belongs to no
  context and only a super-admin reaches it. `GET /auth/sessions` lists only
  the subjects the caller may manage. `auth/revoke-session` keeps its
  no-disclosure answer (revokedCount 0) and now also records a durable `denied`
  row when the session existed. `auth/sessions/list` was already self-only.

  Consent (VTI-CTX-001, VTI-CTX-002). Grants carried no context, so any admin
  could write a standing Allow for any subject (a decision with no challenge)
  or withdraw anyone's grant. `ConsentGrant` now records the context of the
  request it answers. `consent/revoke` needs authority over that context, or
  super-admin for a grant with none. A decision with no challenge writes a
  context-less grant and so needs a super-admin. A challenged decision with no
  bound approver and an empty request context now needs a super-admin, where it
  skipped the context check. `consent/request`'s `contextHint` must be a context
  the caller may act in.

  Every refusal is audited with outcome `denied` (VTI-AUD-003) and logged with
  `security_alert = true`.

- **workspace**: No type derives Debug over secret material ([#1711](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1711))

A derived `Debug` prints every field, so on a type holding a private key, a
  seed or mnemonic, a bearer or refresh token or a password it puts the secret
  into anything that formats the value — a `tracing` field, an `unwrap` or
  `expect` on an enclosing type, a test failure, a panic message. About 55 types
  across twelve crates did exactly that. It surfaced when `vtc-client` began
  holding an operator's key in a `HolderKey`, whose derived `Debug` printed it.

  Each now has a hand-written `Debug` that reports the secret as `<redacted>` —
  presence kept visible for an `Option` — and prints every other field as
  before, the idiom the workspace already used where someone had thought of it.
  Among them: `HolderKey`, `Session`, `ClientIdentity`, `CredentialBundle`,
  `SecretEntry`, `AgentConfig`, `AgentConnect`, `AuthResult`, the key-import and
  seed-rotation requests (mnemonic), `SeedRecord`, `MnemonicExportResponse`,
  `SecretsConfig` (seed, Vault token, AppRole secret id), `VaultSecret`, its
  `CustomField` values and secure notes, `TotpSeed`, the VTC install flow's
  ephemeral signing keys, setup tokens and install JWT, the VTC backup's signing
  bundle and password, mobile-core's X25519 and Ed25519 private keys, auth tokens
  and push tokens (including the Web Push auth secret), and vta-mcp's
  `--agent-key`/`--holder-key`/`--agent-secrets`.

  `Zeroizing<T>` is not a redaction — its `Debug` prints the inner value — so the
  fields wrapped in it were redacted too.

  `vta-sdk/tests/secret_debug_census.rs` keeps the class closed. It parses every
  workspace crate with `syn` and fails on a `#[derive(Debug)]` struct or enum
  whose field has a secret-sounding name (`*_key`, `*token*`, `*secret*`,
  `seed*`, `password`, `mnemonic`, `jwt`, and `secret_id` despite its `_id`)
  and a raw type (`String`, bytes, `Zeroizing<_>`, optionally in an `Option` or
  behind a reference). A field whose type is another workspace type inherits that
  type's `Debug`, which is checked where it is defined. What the name rule
  catches and is not a secret — a claim-type vocabulary token, a webvh path
  called `mnemonic`, the name of an entry in a secret store — is on a
  shrink-only list with what the field holds, and the census also refuses a
  stale entry and a walk that has stopped finding types.

  Not an API change: every type still implements `Debug`; only what it prints
  differs, and no test asserted on the old output.
</blockquote>

title: feat(vgi-bridge): several GitHub organisations on one bridge, one private App each
body:
**Merge order: #92, then this PR, then #95.** #89 (VTA mode) is in `main`. This branch has `main` (with #91's role-map report, event 0.3 and trust-tasks-rs 0.23) and `feat/bridge-job-0.4` (#92) merged in, so it merges cleanly whichever of the two lands first.

Design §5.7, "Several orgs: one private App per org, one bridge".

## What changes
- **`[[github]]` is keyed by `(host, app_owner)`.**
  - Each entry names its own `app_name`, since GitHub App names are unique per instance.
  - Validation refuses two entries for one owner on a host, a duplicate `app_name` on a host, an owner that is not a login, and a Forgejo host that is also a GitHub host.
- **An App serves its own `app_owner` only**, even when it is the host's only App. GitHub installs a private App only on its owner. A namespace whose owner has no entry fails its bind with `notCapable`.
- **Secrets are per App** at `github/<host>/<owner>/app`, in the sealed store or, in VTA mode, in the context's app-state.
  - The stored App records its `owner` (required), and an App stored under another owner is refused.
- **Each App has its own routes**, `/github/<host>/<owner>/{register,registered,setup,webhook}`, verified with that App's own webhook secret.
  - The manifest the bridge generates points the App at them.
  - A setup redirect must match the App that serves the namespace being bound.
  - There are no owner-less GitHub routes.
- **The bridge picks the App from a resource's host and owner** (`Adapters::for_resource`, `vgi_for`, `github_for`). This covers jobs, events, status reports, the bridge-posted check, the Dependabot re-sign and the role map.
- **Manifest flow:** one registration link per organisation, one click each.
- **VTC:** it still maps a forge host to one bridge DID (`[git_ns] bridges`, `vtc-service/src/git_ns/ops.rs`). No VTC change is needed.

## Breaking changes (no migration; test deployments are recreated)
- **A store in the single-App layout is refused at start.** That layout is `github/<host>/app` with owner-less routes. The error says to re-register: delete the App on GitHub, start on a fresh store (an empty `data_dir`, or a fresh VTA context), and register one App per organisation.
- The owner-less routes `/github/<host>/{register,registered,setup,webhook}` are gone. The proxy must forward `/github/<host>/<owner>/…`.
- A lone App no longer serves other owners on its host.
- Config: duplicate owners, or a duplicate `app_name`, on a host are refused.
- API: `Adapters::insert` takes the owner, `get(host)` is Forgejo-only, `get_github(host, owner)` is exact, `vgi(host)` becomes `vgi_for(resource)`, `github_app_secret` takes `(host, owner)`, and `StoredApp.owner` is required.

## Docs
- SETUP-GITHUB-VTC: removes "one namespace per bridge on github.com", and adds the second-org config example and the per-org registration.
- BRIDGE.md: routes, one App per org, and refusing a single-App store.
- RUNBOOK: troubleshooting row.

## Tests
`tests/multi_org.rs`:
- two orgs are each served by their own App (logins are case-insensitive);
- webhooks are routed per App and verified with that App's own secret; there is no owner-less route;
- per-org registration links and manifests carry their own routes, and one org's link is refused on another org's route;
- a single-App store is refused with re-register guidance;
- a lone App serves only its own owner;
- an App stored under the wrong owner is refused.

The existing suites moved to the owner routes. Bind tests for a second org register that org's own App. Personal-account tests use an App owned by that account. Config unit tests cover the keying.


## Security review follow-up (39cb210): an App acts only on its own organisation
An organisation's owners can set their App's webhook secret, so a delivery verified with that App's secret speaks for that organisation only. The verifying App's `(host, owner)` now scopes every delivery:
- An event naming a namespace or repository outside the owner is dropped and logged. A transfer must have one of its sides in the owner.
- Namespace and repository lookups are filtered by the scope. A forge id that another namespace records or manages is never detached, renamed or transferred on this App's word.
- An installation event must match the namespace's recorded installation id.
- Pushes (the Dependabot provenance ledger) are kept only for a repository this owner's namespace manages, matched by name and forge id. Check triggers for another owner's repository or forge id are dropped.
- A transfer between two served organisations is reported by each organisation's App for its own side.
- An account link's device-flow poll and redirect resolve their adapter from the namespace, not the host.

Regression tests from the probe are in `tests/multi_org.rs`. Each failed before the fix:
- another org's App cannot delete, rename or transfer this org's repository, whether it names the repository directly or by forge id;
- it cannot remove this org's installation, and a wrong installation id is ignored even through the org's own App;
- it cannot feed the provenance ledger or trigger checks.

## Re-review follow-up (08fe2fc): transfers only the new owner reports
- Another organisation's record of a repository no longer stops the new owner from reporting it `repoCreatedUnmanaged`.
- The old side is detached, and told `repoTransferred`, only once GitHub confirms the move: `GET /repositories/{id}` through the new owner's own installation must place the repository in the new namespace. An unconfirmed claim leaves the other organisation's state alone.
- New adapter read: `GitHubForge::repository_by_id`.
- Tests:
  - only the new owner reports: confirmed, old side detached, and a late old-owner delivery is harmless;
  - the old owner reports first: nothing to confirm;
  - an unconfirmed claim leaves the old side untouched.

## Merged with `main` (#91) and #92
- Role-map reports (event 0.3) are per organisation. A report picks its adapter with `Adapters::for_resource`, which finds the owner's App. It builds the map from `role_map`, which finds the owner's `[[github]]` entry.
- Fix: `role_map_repos` now finds the owner's `[[github]]` entry (`github_for`), not the first entry on the host. Before, a second organisation's configured repository maps were left out of its report. Test: `role_map_repos_are_the_owners_own`.
- trust-tasks-rs 0.23: the test resolver in `vta.rs` is main's `ProofPurposeResolver`. This PR adds no new signing path, so every bridge document is still signed through `BridgeIdentity::sign`, with `assertionMethod`.
- Job 0.4 and the rule that only `own` maps to admin come from #92 unchanged.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): query the Trust Registry over DIDComm as the bridge's own DID
body:
**Merge order: #92, then #90, then this PR.** This branch already contains #92 and #90, so until they merge its diff shows their changes too.

Bridge-posted checks can query the Trust Registry over DIDComm again. They go out as the bridge's own stable DID, on the mediator session the bridge already holds. HTTPS is the fallback. The bridge was HTTPS-only while the messaging SDK's reported authcrypt sender could not be trusted. That is fixed in affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.27.2 / affinidi-messaging-didcomm 0.15.9 (already in the lock via #94). This PR names those versions as explicit security floors.

## Commits
1. **build: require the messaging SDK that binds the authcrypt sender to its key.** Adds workspace floors `affinidi-messaging-sdk = "0.27.2"` and `affinidi-messaging-didcomm = "0.15.9"`, used by verify-trust and vgi-bridge. Also bumps delivery/core to 0.1.18 / 0.1.10 (the 0.27 SDK line). The lock change is minimal on top of #94.
2. **feat(vgi-bridge): query the registry over DIDComm as the bridge's own DID.** Brings back the `RegistryChannel` design removed in #88:
   - verify-trust gains `RegistryChannel` / `Registry::over_channel`.
   - The bridge gains `RegistryReplies` + `BridgeRegistryChannel`.
   - `Bridge::handle_inbound` offers each inbound document to the reply router first. The router takes a document only when both are true:
     - its sender is the registry's DID, and the transport **verified** it (`m.verified`, authcrypt);
     - its `threadId` matches a query in flight.
   - Everything else goes to the job path unchanged.

## Security
- Every query carries a fresh UUID v4 id, and the reply thread must match it. The first transport failure or timeout is latched for the rest of the check.
- verify-trust's own DIDComm transport keeps the #88 envelope check as defence in depth: `skid` == base64url-decoded `apu`, and the key belongs to the registry. On the bridge path the SDK hands over messages already unpacked, so the SDK floor above is what binds the sender there.
- A registry whose mediator refuses the bridge's DID fails closed (`registryUnavailable`).

## Config
`[verify_trust] transport` now also governs the bridge's own check:
- `auto` means DIDComm > HTTPS for the bridge's check. The bridge never uses TSP. For the written workflows `auto` still means TSP > DIDComm > HTTPS.
- `didcomm` / `https` apply to both.
- `tsp` is refused at startup while any GitHub forge has `bridge_checks` on.

## Tests
- `tests/registry_didcomm.rs` runs the bridge's real `DidcommLink` against an in-process mediator:
  - an honest registry reply is accepted through the router;
  - a **forged** reply (sealed with another DID's key, with party info naming the registry's key) never reaches the bridge, and the query times out.
- `registry_channel` unit tests:
  - a reply with the right thread but an unverified or wrong sender is not taken;
  - a late reply after a timeout is not taken;
  - if the link is down, the query fails at once.
- verify-trust channel transport tests: queries use distinct random ids, a reply to another thread is refused, and a failure is latched.
- Config: `tsp` is refused while `bridge_checks` is on.
- The #88 end-to-end check test is restored.

Local: `cargo test -p vgi-bridge --test registry_didcomm --test checks`, the vgi-bridge lib tests (`registry_channel`, `config`) and the verify-trust lib `registry` tests pass. `cargo clippy -p vgi-bridge -p verify-trust --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

## Coordination
Rebased on main after #94. It touches `vgi-bridge/src/{bridge,checks,config}.rs` and `docs/BRIDGE.md`, which the open drafts #89/#90/#91/#92 also edit. Expect small textual conflicts, whichever lands second.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): query the Trust Registry over DIDComm as the bridge's own DID (#95)
body:
feat(vgi-bridge): query the Trust Registry over DIDComm as the bridge's own DID (#95)

* feat(vgi-bridge): work off the VTC's VTA (VTA mode)

The bridge can now keep its identity, secrets and state in its own trust
context of the VTC's VTA, holding only a context-scoped credential on the
host (design §5.7, decided 2026-09-25):

- the context's did:webvh and its Ed25519 and X25519 keys are fetched
  into memory at start-up (never written to disk or logs); the bridge
  still signs as itself, never as the VTC;
- GitHub App credentials, webhook secrets and Forgejo tokens live in the
  context's app-state, sealed (AES-256-GCM) under a key derived from a
  dedicated context key, because app-state is documented as not a secret
  store; they are held in memory on the host, never in the redb file;
- namespaces, repositories, the provenance ledger and bookkeeping are
  mirrored to app-state with conditional writes; the local store is a
  cache, so a new host with a new credential rebuilds fully;
- a second writer on the context stops the mirror (fail closed), holds
  results and turns /healthz to 503;
- results and events go to the VTC only once the state they report is in
  the VTA; a rotated Forgejo token retires its predecessor only then;
- a key rotation in the VTA is picked up (interval on public keys, or
  SIGHUP), the new keys put in service and the old dropped;
- DID documents are cached for a bounded, configurable time (default
  60s), and a failed proof or unknown commit key is re-checked once
  against a fresh resolution before it is refused;
- `vgi-bridge vta setup` checks the context, the keys, app-state and
  that the credential reaches no other context.

The self-contained modes (sealed store, did:peer or imported bundle) are
unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): hold the keys the bridge's DID document lists through a rotation

In VTA mode the bridge's current DID document now decides which of its
keys it holds: every assertionMethod and keyAgreement key the document
lists, with the same public key. Private halves come from the VTA; one
the VTA no longer releases but the document still lists stays in memory.
The newest listed signing key the VTA releases signs.

Through a planned rotation the bridge therefore holds old and new keys
for the whole overlap (a job encrypted to either opens) and drops a key
only when the document stops listing it; no grace timer. A key whose id
the document lists with another public key is not used.

The refresh check compares the VTA's key list and the freshly resolved
document (public halves only) and exports again only on a change;
`vta setup` reports what the document lists; `identity show` reads the
context's DID without exporting.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge)!: reach the VTA over DIDComm only in VTA mode

The VTA releases a private key only over a channel confidential end to
end (VTI #1733 refuses keys/export-secret and vta/contexts/secrets over
REST and HTTPS, where the key would exist wherever TLS terminates). VTA
mode therefore always connects over DIDComm: `vta.mediator_did`
defaults to the bridge's own `mediator_did`, and `vta.url` is only the
DIDComm client's fallback for unauthenticated calls.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vgi-bridge): wait up to a minute for a check delivery

The bridge-posted check fetches from a local remote and verifies; on a
loaded machine that exceeded the helper's ten seconds and failed tests
that had nothing wrong.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vgi-bridge): VTA mode: the VTA is the authority on restart; bind secrets to their version

From the security review of #89:

- a stale host no longer resurrects what a recovery host deleted: each
  host records the version it mirrored each record at (a local-only
  table); on pull, a mirrored record the VTA no longer holds (tombstone,
  read through the change feed, or reaped) is dropped locally, only
  records never mirrored are written, and a remote version older than
  the one mirrored (rolled back or replayed) fails closed;
- a sealed secret's AAD binds its record version (predicted from the
  namespace counter and checked on the write), so an older ciphertext
  put back does not open and the start is refused;
- only a signing key the VTA still releases signs; with none listed the
  bridge refuses rather than falling back to a withdrawn key;
- evict-and-re-resolve after a failed proof or unknown commit key runs
  at most once per DID per 30 seconds;
- more than one active key under the sealing label is refused.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): switch the signing key only after the verifier cache horizon

The bridge now records when it first sees each signing key listed in its
DID document (mirrored to the VTA, so a restart or a new host keeps it),
and keeps signing with the oldest listed key it may use until a newer one
has been listed for vta.signing_switch_after_secs (default 86400, the
proposed 24-hour verifier cache cap; at least did_cache_ttl_secs), then
with the newest. An older key the document stops listing is gone at
once, so its successor signs immediately. Key-agreement keys: every
listed one is held, as before. The refresh loop re-evaluates when a
switch comes due even if nothing else changed.

A TODO points at VTI #638: switch at activatesAt once the VTA exposes
key-role states, and drop the heuristic.

Also: the resumed re-sign test waits up to a minute.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): report the effective role map to the VTC (git-ns/bridge/event 0.3)

- The bridge now sends `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.3 by default and, under it,
  `roleMapReported` for every bound namespace at start-up and right after a
  binding completes: the role map as the forge applies it (each right's
  configured role rounded onto the namespace's ladder), each configured
  repository whose map differs, and each managed repository whose roles
  were last projected under another map (`stale`), which the VTC
  re-projects. There is still no entry for git.ns.admin.
- RepoRecord keeps the map a fully successful projection applied
  (`roleMap`); a record without one is taken to be the default map.
- One outbox key per namespace, so a newer report replaces an
  unacknowledged one; sent after the start-up resend, so it is the last
  the VTC reads. The outside-namespace guard also covers `repos[].resource`
  and `stale`.
- BREAKING: `event_version` defaults to "0.3". A VTC that takes only 0.2
  needs `event_version = "0.2"` (or "0.1"), and is then told no role map.
- BridgeConfig::role_map_repos lists the repositories with a map layer.
- Docs: BRIDGE.md §6c and §7, RUNBOOK §8b and troubleshooting, the GitHub
  setup guide, the example config.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): report the role map whenever the bridge starts serving a namespace or its VTC link comes up

git-ns/bridge/event 0.3 now asks for a roleMapReported whenever the
bridge starts serving a namespace, whenever its link to the VTC is
established or re-established, and whenever its map changes.

- Bridge::link_up: resend everything unacknowledged except earlier
  role-map reports, then report every bound namespace afresh (one per
  namespace per link-up; the per-namespace outbox key replaces an
  unacknowledged report). Called at start-up (restore), on every new
  mediator session (the DIDComm supervisor in run), and when a send
  succeeds after sends failed, which covers a transport that came back
  without a signal: every send to the VTC goes through send_doc, which
  tracks a link-down flag and raises the background loop on recovery. A
  transport-signalled link-up clears the flag first, so it is not counted
  twice.
- Bridge::started_serving: report a namespace that became this bridge's
  to serve (after bindCompleted); a restored store is covered by restore.
- Tests: a cut link that comes back reports once per namespace and is not
  counted twice; a newly served namespace is reported. The test harness's
  link can be cut.
- BRIDGE.md §6c and RUNBOOK §8b say when reports are sent.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vgi-bridge): VTA mode: refuse a rolled-back VTA; one writer at a time

From the re-review of #89:

- a VTA restored to a snapshot from before some records existed is no
  longer read as those records being deleted: pull fails closed when the
  namespace counter is behind the highest version this host mirrored, or
  a mirrored key is missing above it (conflict, 503, nothing written);
- deletions pass their tombstone's version on, so the next sealed write
  predicts its version correctly;
- every writer of the bridge's app-state (the mirror for a pass,
  `secret set`, `vta setup`'s probe) holds a short lease record first,
  so a secret is sealed once to the version it lands at and is never
  left live and unopenable; a stray write that ignores the lease is
  sealed over again before put_sealed returns. The mirror takes the
  lease before its batch, so a pass given up while waiting loses nothing.

Tests: the rollback probe (ns_1@v1, ns_2@v2, remote restored to ns_1 at
watermark 1: refused, ns_2 kept), a secret after a deletion sealed once,
writers taking turns under the lease, a stray write resealed, and an
abandoned lease expiring.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* build: require the messaging SDK that binds the authcrypt sender to its key

affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.27.2 and affinidi-messaging-didcomm 0.15.9 bind
an authcrypt message's reported sender to the key its key agreement
actually used: `skid` must equal the `apu` party info, and the decrypted
sender key id must be that `skid`. #94 already resolves these versions;
this names both as security floors in verify-trust and vgi-bridge so a
later lock refresh cannot fall below them. The 0.26 SDK line cannot come
back: it declares didcomm "0.15", and against 0.15.9 its unpack calls the
deprecated `decrypt`, which refuses every authcrypt message.

The delivery layer and messaging core move to 0.1.18 / 0.1.10, the
versions on the 0.27 SDK line. No source change is needed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): query the registry over DIDComm as the bridge's own DID

Bridge-posted checks reach a registry that advertises DIDComm over the
bridge's existing mediator session, as the bridge's stable DID, before
falling back to HTTPS. They were HTTPS-only while the messaging SDK's
reported authcrypt sender could not be trusted. It can be now: the
previous commit requires the SDK release that binds the sender to the
key actually used.

The channel design from #88's first revision returns:
- verify-trust gains RegistryChannel and Registry::over_channel;
- the bridge gains RegistryReplies and BridgeRegistryChannel;
- Bridge::handle_inbound passes each inbound document to the reply
  router first. The router takes a document only when its sender is
  verified as the registry's DID and it answers a query in flight.
  Everything else goes to the job path unchanged.

The channel is hardened as well. verify-trust's channel transport sends
every query under a fresh UUID v4, requires the reply's thread to match
it, and latches the first transport failure or timeout for the rest of
the check, so later queries fail at once. The envelope header check from
#88 (`skid` == base64url-decoded `apu`, and the key belongs to the
registry) stays in verify-trust's own DIDComm transport. There the
packed frame is available, so the check still applies there as defence
in depth.

[verify_trust] transport now governs the bridge's own check too:
- auto means DIDComm, then HTTPS, for the bridge's check, with no
  fallback. For the written workflows auto still means TSP, then
  DIDComm, then HTTPS.
- didcomm and https apply to both.
- tsp applies to the workflows only. It is refused at start while any
  GitHub forge has bridge_checks on, because the bridge never speaks
  TSP.

Tests:
- ChannelTransport: queries are sent as the channel owner under
  distinct random ids; a reply to another thread is refused; a failure
  is latched and the second query is never sent.
- A tsp configuration is refused while bridge_checks are on.
- The #88 end-to-end check test, restored.
- A new tests/registry_didcomm.rs runs the bridge's real DidcommLink
  against an in-process mediator. An honest registry reply comes back
  through the router. A reply sealed with another DID's key, whose
  party info names the registry's key, never reaches the bridge: the
  SDK refuses it, and the query times out.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vgi-bridge): VTA mode: bound the lease by the VTA's clock; refuse a rollback the counter hides

- A lease's expiry is its holder's `until` capped at the VTA's own
  `updatedAt` plus the TTL, so no writer (a wrong clock, or on purpose)
  keeps others out past one TTL after its last write. The holder counts its
  own lease on the monotonic clock from before the write was sent, never
  renews one that ran out, and renews before every sealed-secret attempt.
- Listings say whether they are the change feed from the start (every
  deletion present) or a snapshot (tombstones reaped). From the feed, a
  record this host mirrored with no tombstone was lost, not deleted: the
  start is refused even when the counter has moved past the restore point.
  Only a snapshot takes it for deleted.
- Every app-state request is given up after 20s (checked at compile time
  to be well under half the lease), so a write is never still in flight
  once the lease it was sent under could have run out.
- A refused state (rollback, replay, a secret that does not open) is a
  typed error the start does not retry: it fails at once with the reason.
- /healthz answers 503 once changes have waited five minutes with every
  pass failing (the VTA away, or the lease kept by someone else), with the
  number waiting, instead of "ok" while nothing reaches the VTA.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): several GitHub organisations on one bridge, one private App each

GitHub installs a private App only on the account that owns it, so a
community binding several organisations needs one App per organisation
(design §5.7, "Several orgs: one private App per org, one bridge").

- [[github]] entries are keyed by (host, app_owner); each names its own
  app_name (App names are unique per GitHub instance). A host with a
  single entry keeps serving every owner there, as before.
- App credentials are stored per App at github/<host>/<owner>/app, with
  the owner recorded; an App stored for another owner is refused. A
  single-App release's github/<host>/app is moved at start to the entry
  it belongs to (the only one, or the one whose app_name is the App's),
  or the start is refused naming the fix.
- Each App has its own routes, /github/<host>/<owner>/{register,
  registered,setup,webhook}, verified with its own webhook secret. The
  owner-less routes stay for Apps registered before: a webhook there goes
  to the host's only App or to the one GitHub names in
  X-GitHub-Hook-Installation-Target-ID.
- The bridge picks the App from a resource's host and owner; the
  manifest flow offers one registration per organisation.

The VTC still maps a forge host to one bridge DID; nothing changes there.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge)!: one App per owner, no single-App layout or owner-less routes

Security first, no compatibility layer (test deployments are recreated):

- a lone GitHub App serves only its own app_owner; an owner without an
  entry has no App, and its bind fails notCapable;
- a store in the single-App layout (github/<host>/app) is refused at
  start with re-register guidance, and nothing is moved or read; the
  stored App's owner is required;
- the owner-less /github/<host>/{register,registered,setup,webhook}
  routes and the X-GitHub-Hook-Installation-Target-ID fallback are gone;
  every App has only its own routes, verified with its own secret, and a
  GitHub bind completes only on its App's setup route;
- account links (device flow and redirect) resolve their adapter from
  the namespace, not the host.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vgi-bridge): a GitHub App's webhooks act only on its own organisation

From the security review of #90 (blocking): a delivery verified with one
organisation's App secret could act on another organisation's namespace,
since the handlers dropped the verifying App's owner. An organisation's
owners can set their App's webhook secret, so that is one organisation
forging events about another.

The verifying App's (host, owner) now scopes every delivery:

- an event naming a namespace or repository outside the owner is dropped
  and logged (a transfer must have one side in the owner);
- namespace and repository lookups are filtered by the scope, and a
  forge id another namespace records or manages is never detached,
  renamed or transferred on this App's word;
- an installation event must match the namespace's recorded
  installation id;
- pushes (the Dependabot provenance ledger) are kept only for a
  repository this owner's namespace manages, by name and forge id; check
  triggers for another owner's repository or forge id are dropped;
- a transfer between two served organisations is reported by each
  organisation's App for its own side.

Regression tests from the probe in tests/multi_org.rs.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vgi-bridge): confirm a transfer with GitHub before detaching the other organisation

From the re-review of #90: when only the new owner's App delivered a
transfer between two served organisations, the repository was not
reported to the new namespace (another organisation's record of it
blocked the report) and the old namespace kept a stale managed record.

- another organisation's record of a repository no longer stops the new
  owner from reporting it repoCreatedUnmanaged;
- the old side is detached (and told repoTransferred) only once GitHub
  confirms the move: GET /repositories/{id} through the new owner's own
  installation must place it in the new namespace. An unconfirmed claim
  leaves the other organisation's state alone.

Tests cover both delivery orders and an unconfirmed claim.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vgi-bridge): review follow-ups for the DIDComm registry channel

- registry_didcomm: the fake registry asserts the mediator accepted each
  reply, and after a forged reply sends an honest canary; the forged-reply
  test now requires the canary to surface authenticated as the registry
  and nothing else to surface, so it cannot pass vacuously.
- registry_channel: a query's pending entry is held by a drop guard, so an
  exchange future dropped mid-wait (abort, shutdown) unregisters it.
- verify-trust: document RegistryChannel and Registry::over_channel as a
  security-critical contract: deliver only replies whose transport-verified
  sender is the registry DID.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): take git-ns/bridge/job 0.4 only, and answer trust-task-discovery

git-ns/bridge/job 0.4 (trust-tasks #635) sends a namespace admin with no
right of their own on a repository as git.ns.admin, which maps to no role,
never as the git.repo.own it implies. Before 0.4 the two could not be told
apart, so the bridge now takes 0.4 only:

- A job of 0.1, 0.2 or 0.3 is refused unsupportedVersion.
- projectRoles requires repo: there is no namespace-level role job, so one
  without repo is malformedRequest (it was notCapable).
- desiredRoles may name an account once, matched by forge and id.
- removeAccounts may name an account desiredRoles lists at git.ns.admin
  (no role either way); any other overlap is still malformedRequest.
- trust-task-discovery/0.2 from the VTC is answered with the 0.4 type URI,
  which is how the VTC learns it may send 0.4 (the spec forbids sending it
  to a bridge that has not shown it takes it).

0.4 payloads are read with the generated 0.3 types, which have the same
shape, until a trust-tasks-rs release carries 0.4's. The lockfile moves
trust-tasks-rs to 0.22.7 for job::v0_3.

No backwards compatibility: every deployment is a test instance.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(vgi-bridge): mark the hand-written job 0.4 type for the trust-tasks release

JOB_TYPE and the job::v0_3 alias stand in for the generated job::v0_4
until a trust-tasks-rs release carries trust-tasks #635. Say so with a
TODO at both.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vgi-forge): only own may map to the forge admin role

A role map giving maintain or commit the admin role would let a member make
themselves a repository administrator on the forge by self-granting a
non-elevated right. RoleMap::new and deserialisation now refuse such a map,
so the bridge fails to start with an error naming the layer, and RoleMap's
fields are private so no map can be changed afterwards to one they refuse.
The docs and example config no longer suggest maintainers as admins.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): report the forge's ladder, and build every role-map report afresh

git-ns/bridge/event 0.3 (trust-tasks-tf #639):

- a roleMapReported event names the namespace's `ladder`, which the VTC
  holds every map to;
- a report is built afresh at each send, a resend of an unacknowledged
  one included, so a later `issuedAt` never carries an older map;
- a map that the adapter rounds unordered is logged and not reported,
  and not recorded as the map a repository was projected under;
- a pending report is dropped once the bridge speaks an event version
  below 0.3, rather than sent under a version without the type.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(vgi-bridge): take trust-tasks-rs 0.23 for the published git-ns/bridge/event 0.3

git-ns/bridge/event 0.3 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#639) is now
published, so the local trust-tasks-rs patch this branch developed
against is no longer needed: bump to the real 0.23 release.

trust-tasks-proof 0.23 also changed sign_trust_task's default
proofPurpose from assertionMethod to authentication (matching the
Trust Task spec's own examples). This bridge and the VTC-side checks
it faces still require assertionMethod on both sides of the wire, so
BridgeIdentity::sign now passes it explicitly instead of relying on
the library default.

trust-tasks-proof 0.23 also replaced VerificationMethodResolver with
a purpose-aware ProofPurposeResolver; the test-only Published resolver
in vta.rs moves onto it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(vgi-bridge): take trust-tasks-rs 0.23 for the generated git-ns/bridge/job 0.4

git-ns/bridge/job 0.4 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#635) is now
published (trust-tasks-rs 0.23): the bridge takes the generated
specs::git_ns::bridge::job::v0_4 types in place of the generated 0.3
ones it read 0.4's wire-identical payload with, and JOB_TYPE is now

title: feat(vgi-bridge): take git-ns/bridge/job 0.4 only, and answer trust-task-discovery
body:
## What

The bridge side of `git-ns/bridge/job` 0.4 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#635). Under 0.4 a namespace admin gets no role on the forge.

This PR does **not** keep backwards compatibility: every deployment is a test instance and will be recreated.

- **Only 0.4 is taken.** A job of 0.1, 0.2 or 0.3 is refused with `unsupportedVersion` ("this bridge takes git-ns/bridge/job 0.4 only"). Before 0.4, a VTC sent a namespace admin as `git.repo.own`, and the bridge could not tell them from a real owner.
- **`projectRoles` requires `repo`.** There is no namespace-level role job any more, so a job without `repo` is refused `malformedRequest`. Before, it was refused `notCapable` in `admit`.
- **One entry per account in `desiredRoles`**, matched by `forge` and `id`. Before, it was matched by `id` only.
- **`removeAccounts` may name an account that `desiredRoles` lists at `git.ns.admin`.** Both mean no role. Any other overlap is still `malformedRequest`. `apply_roles` already sets such an account to no role.
- **Discovery.** The bridge answers `trust-task-discovery/0.2` from its VTC with the 0.4 type URI, if the patterns select `git-ns/bridge/job`. The VTC asks before sending, because 0.4 forbids sending 0.4 to a bridge that has not shown it takes it. A pre-0.4 bridge refuses discovery with `unsupportedType`, and the VTC then sends it nothing and tells the operator to upgrade.
- **ns.admin mapping:** `git.ns.admin` maps to no role, as #84 already does.
- **Only `own` may map to admin.** `RoleMap::new` and deserialisation refuse a map that gives `maintain` or `commit` the forge `admin` role, so the bridge fails to start with an error naming the layer. `RoleMap`'s fields are now private (read through `own()`, `maintain()`, `commit()`), so no map can be changed afterwards to one that `new` would refuse. The docs and example config no longer suggest maintainers as admins.

### Implementation notes

- Code changes are confined to `wire.rs`, `jobs.rs` (comments only), and one dispatch branch in `bridge.rs::handle_inbound` for discovery and old versions. The docs (BRIDGE, RUNBOOK, SETUP-GITHUB-VTC, README) and tests are updated.

## VTC side

OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1729 sends 0.4 only, after discovery.

## trust-tasks-rs 0.23

`git-ns/bridge/job` 0.4 is now published (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#635, trust-tasks-rs 0.23), so this PR takes it instead of reading 0.4's wire-identical payload with the generated 0.3 types:

- `trust-tasks-rs` / `trust-tasks-proof` bumped to 0.23 in the workspace `Cargo.toml`, same three-node split as #91 (see the comment above `trust-tasks-rs`).
- `wire.rs`'s `job` alias moves from `specs::git_ns::bridge::job::v0_3` to `::v0_4` (source-only swap; the two are structurally identical). `JOB_TYPE` is now sourced from the generated `Payload::TYPE_URI` instead of hand-written.
- `BridgeIdentity::sign` now passes `assertionMethod` explicitly: trust-tasks-proof 0.23 changed `sign_trust_task`'s default `proofPurpose` to `authentication`, but this bridge and the VTC-side checks it faces still require `assertionMethod` on both sides of the wire (see #91's `proofPurpose` follow-up).
- The test-only `Published` resolver in `vta.rs` moves onto trust-tasks-proof 0.23's `ProofPurposeResolver` (replaces `VerificationMethodResolver`).

**Merged with #91** (`git-ns/bridge/event` 0.3, role-map reporting) to resolve the Cargo.toml/lock conflict between the two ahead of either landing, since both took 0.23 independently. That merge also surfaced two incompatibilities between the two branches' independent work, both fixed here:
- #91's `role_map.rs` tests set `[forgejo.role_map] maintain = "admin"` and stored a repo record's role map with `maintain: "admin"` directly — both now refused by this branch's new "only `own` may map to admin" rule. Changed to `maintain = "write"` in both places; the tests still exercise the same staleness/ladder behaviour with a value the rule allows.
- #91's `role_map.rs` called a `send_job_0_2` test helper this branch removed (job 0.2 support is gone). Swapped to `send_job`, which sends the same payload as a 0.4 job.

Until #91 lands on `main`, this branch's diff includes #91's commits too.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p vgi-bridge`: 187 tests pass (85 lib, 102 across the integration suites, including the merged role-map and VTA-mode suites from #91).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` pass.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): report the effective role map to the VTC (git-ns/bridge/event 0.3)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #84 (configurable role map): the VTC could only assume the default map, so its console showed forge roles the bridge did not give, drift adopt derived rights from the wrong map, and a map change reached a repository only at its next unrelated role projection.

- **`git-ns/bridge/event` 0.3** (spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#639) is now the default. Under it the bridge sends `roleMapReported`, one per namespace, whenever it **starts serving** a namespace (at start-up — the only time its config, and so its map, can change — and right after a binding completes, `Bridge::started_serving`) and whenever its **link to the VTC comes up** (`Bridge::link_up`, see below):
  - `roleMap` — the map as the forge applies it: each right's configured role rounded onto the namespace's ladder (GitHub personal account: `write`/`write`/`none`; Forgejo's `maintain` is the adapter's own rung, `write` + merge allow-list);
  - `repos` — configured repositories whose map differs;
  - `stale` — managed repositories whose roles were last projected under another map. The VTC re-projects these itself (and `cnm git reproject` / console "Re-project roles" do it by hand).
  - No entry for `git.ns.admin`: a namespace admin still gets no forge role.
- `RepoRecord.roleMap` records the map a **fully** successful projection applied (a partly failed one leaves the repo stale); a record without one is taken to be the default map, the only one a released bridge applied.
- **Link-up triggers.** `Bridge::link_up` resends everything unacknowledged except earlier role-map reports, then reports every bound namespace afresh. It runs (1) at start-up from `restore`, (2) on every new mediator session in the DIDComm supervisor (`run`), and (3) when a send succeeds after sends had failed — every send to the VTC goes through `send_doc`, which keeps a link-down flag and wakes the background loop on recovery, covering a transport that comes back without a signal. Debounced to one report per namespace per link-up: a signalled link-up clears the flag before sending, so its own sends do not count as a second one.
- One outbox key per namespace (`event:roleMap:<ns>`), so a newer report replaces an unacknowledged one rather than piling up. `outside_namespace` also checks `repos[].resource` and `stale`.
- **Review follow-ups (#639 latest):**
  - every report carries `ladder`, the namespace's levels lowest first without `none` (GitHub org `read…admin`, personal account `write`, Forgejo `read`/`write`/`maintain`/`admin`); the VTC refuses a map off it;
  - **newest wins:** the VTC ignores a report issued before the one it holds, so every send of a report — a resend of an unacknowledged one included — is rebuilt from the map applied at that moment (`Bridge::send_outbox` → `refresh_role_map_entry`), never the content first queued under a new `issuedAt`;
  - a map the adapter rounds **unordered** is logged at error and not reported (`effective_for` returns `None`), and is not recorded as the map a repository was projected under;
  - a pending role-map outbox entry is **dropped** once `event_version` is below 0.3, rather than sent under a version without the type.
- Docs: BRIDGE.md §6c/§7, RUNBOOK §8b + troubleshooting, SETUP-GITHUB-VTC, example config.

## Breaking

- **`event_version` defaults to `"0.3"`.** A VTC that serves only `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.2 refuses every event as an unsupported type until it is updated or the bridge is set to `event_version = "0.2"` (or `"0.1"`); under 0.1/0.2 no role map is reported (logged once at info).

## trust-tasks-rs 0.23

`git-ns/bridge/event` 0.3 is now published (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#639, trust-tasks-rs 0.23). The branch is off the local `[patch.crates-io]` it was built and tested against and takes the real release: `trust-tasks-rs` and `trust-tasks-proof` bumped to 0.23 in the workspace `Cargo.toml`, `cargo update`d, no other dependency changes.

Two things broke on the bump, both fixed:

- trust-tasks-proof 0.23 changed `sign_trust_task`'s default `proofPurpose` from `assertionMethod` to `authentication` (matching the Trust Task spec's own examples). This bridge and the VTC-side checks it faces still require `assertionMethod` on both sides of the wire (see **Follow-up** below), so `BridgeIdentity::sign` now passes it explicitly instead of relying on the library default — otherwise every event the bridge signs would have silently switched purpose and the VTC's own `assertionMethod` check would start refusing them.
- trust-tasks-proof 0.23 replaced `VerificationMethodResolver` with a purpose-aware `ProofPurposeResolver`; the test-only `Published` resolver in `vta.rs` moves onto it.

The rest of the workspace (`vta-sdk` 0.51, `verify-trust`, and `trql-client` below them) is still on the 0.22 and 0.21 lines respectively, so `cargo tree -i trust-tasks-rs` now shows three nodes rather than two — a wider but still bounded, `publish = false` split; see the comment above `trust-tasks-rs` in the root `Cargo.toml`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p vgi-bridge`: a cut link that comes back reports once per namespace and is not counted twice by a signalled link-up; a newly served namespace is reported; new tests for the effective map (GitHub org default, personal account, Forgejo default and `maintain = "admin"`), repository overrides listed only when they differ, `stale` incl. a record with no map, a successful projection clearing it, one outbox entry per namespace, the start-up report, the report after `bindCompleted`, nothing sent under `event_version = "0.2"`, and the outside-namespace guard for `repos`/`stale`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] review follow-ups: a resend carries the map applied now; a pending report is dropped under `event_version = "0.2"`; an adapter that rounds unordered reports nothing; the ladder in every report
- [x] trust-tasks-rs 0.23: dependency bumped off the local patch, `cargo test -p vgi-bridge` green (82 lib + 17 + 2 integration tests), clippy and fmt clean
- [ ] Against a VTC with the matching change: restart the bridge with a changed `role_map` and see the VTC re-project the stale repositories

## Follow-up

- **`proofPurpose`.** The spec's examples sign bridge events with `proofPurpose: "authentication"`; this bridge still signs with `assertionMethod` and still requires `assertionMethod` on the jobs the VTC signs (`wire.rs`). Moving both sides together is left for a separate change, so neither refuses the other in between.

title: fix(vta-service)!: close the key-material follow-ups from the export audit
body:
Stacked on #1733 (base `fix/vta-key-export-authz`). Review that PR first.

## Summary

This PR fixes the follow-ups found while writing #1733.

1. **`keys/export-secret` returns the spec's own codes.**
   - An internal key is refused with `keys/export-secret:neverExportable`.
   - A key marked non-exportable is refused with `keys/export-secret:notExportable`. It used to return `permissionDenied` in both cases.
   - The refusals stay typed (`KeyExportRefusal`) from the operation up to the Trust-Task handler.
   - They are reached only after the `key-export` capability, the channel and the caller's scope have all passed, so an unentitled caller never sees them. This is the spec's "after establishing entitlement and before assembling a response".
   - REST, DIDComm and the other callers keep a 403 carrying the same message.
2. **`vault/release` writes a durable `vault.secret_release` audit row before the sealed secret leaves.** If the row cannot be written, the release is refused, as `key.secret_export` is.
   - This applies to every kind of vault secret, including passkey and SSH private keys.
   - The row names the holder, the entry id, the context, the transport (`trust-task/<binding>`) and `kind=<secretKind>`.
   - It never contains the secret, the entry's label or its site.
3. **The TEE mnemonic export is sealed to the requester, and a bearer token alone never releases it.**
   - **New Trust Task:** `spec/vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0` (payload `{clientDid, nonce, label?}`). Spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#649. Until that ships in trust-tasks-rs, the URI is listed in `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS`.
   - **Signed by the caller, on every path.** The request's proof is made for `authentication` and verifies as `issuer`. `issuer` is the session DID, `recipient` is this VTA's DID, and `issuedAt` is fresh. The caller is a super admin holding `key-export`.
   - **End-to-end path (DIDComm authcrypt, TSP).** `clientDid` is the requester's ephemeral key, from `pnm bootstrap request`.
   - **Signed first-boot path (Trust Tasks on HTTPS).** A freshly booted TEE VTA may have no DIDComm or TSP endpoint yet. Over HTTPS the export is allowed only when `clientDid` is **exactly** the signing caller's DID, so the words are sealed to a key only the caller holds. A TLS terminator holding the bearer JWT cannot sign as the caller, so it can neither make its own request nor change the seal recipient in the caller's. The spine's replay guard refuses a second use of the document `id`.
   - **Everything else over hop-by-hop is refused** with `permissionDenied`, including a `clientDid` that differs from the signer and an unsigned request. Every refusal happens before the guard is touched, so a refused request does not spend the one-time release.
   - **The replay guard never keeps a secret-bearing response.** A task classified `Discloses::Secret` has its duplicate absorbed with no body. So a replayed mnemonic export is never answered with the bundle, and the record never holds it.
   - **`POST /attestation/mnemonic` is refused** with 403 for every caller (after the `key-export` check), with a message naming the Trust Task. REST is hop-by-hop, and for a TEE, TLS terminates outside the enclave.
   - **Sealed answer:** an armored bundle carrying a new additive `SealedPayloadV1::SeedMnemonic` variant, sealed to `clientDid` under an `Attested` producer assertion. The quote binds `SHA256(client_ed25519 || nonce || producer_ed25519)`. The response also carries the bundle's digest. Open the bundle with `pnm bootstrap open --expect-digest`.
   - **Two-phase export:** `MnemonicExportGuard::reserve` and `commit` are the only way to read the words. The plaintext one-shot `MnemonicExportGuard::export()` and `MnemonicExportResponse` are removed from the public API. The entropy is zeroed only after the bundle is built and the audit row is written, so a failed seal cannot lose the root seed, and a concurrent second export is refused.
   - **`SeedMnemonicBundle` zeroizes its mnemonic on drop**, on every path: opened, sealed, or dropped on an error.
   - **Audit:** the `seed.mnemonic_export` row records the actor, the recipient `did:key`, the transport and the bundle digest.
4. **The VTA's own use of a key is recorded as `key.internal_use`.** `get_key_secret_internal` used to log it as `key.secret_export`, so every VC issuance and webvh publish looked like an export.
5. **Stored P-256 public keys are multicodec-prefixed (`p256-pub`).**
   - `create_key` and `import_key` stored a bare SEC1 point, which named no algorithm (VTI-KEY-012) and differed from what custody publishes for the same key on export. The same was true of imported X25519 keys and of the offline `vta keys` export.
   - No boot migration. These are test deployments, so a record written by an earlier build is recreated, not rewritten. (`migrate_unprefixed_public_keys` and its test are removed.)

The spec side of the capability is trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#643, which registers `keyExport` in the shared `Capability` enum.

## Breaking changes

- **`POST /attestation/mnemonic`** is refused (403). Use `spec/vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0`: over DIDComm or TSP, or at first boot over HTTPS, signed by the caller with `clientDid` set to the caller's own DID. It returns `{bundle, digest, windowRemainingSecs}`. The request must carry the caller's `authentication` proof.
- **A duplicate of a secret-disclosing Trust Task** (for example `keys/export-secret`) is answered with an empty body rather than a replay of the first response.
- **`MnemonicExportGuard::export()` and `MnemonicExportResponse`** are removed. Use `reserve()` / `commit()`.
- **`SealedPayloadV1`** gains the variant `SeedMnemonic`. It is additive, but any exhaustive `match` must add an arm. Every in-tree match has been updated.
- **Audit consumers** that counted `key.secret_export` rows will see the VTA's internal loads move to `key.internal_use`.
- **Stored P-256 and imported X25519 key records** written by an earlier build keep the bare encoding. Recreate the deployment.
- **`vault/release`** fails when the audit sink is unavailable.

## Tests

- `refusals_about_the_key_carry_the_declared_codes` (trust task)
- `an_uncommitted_reservation_releases_the_export` (vta-tee)
- `seed_mnemonic_roundtrips_and_redacts` (vta-sdk)
- `internal_use_is_not_recorded_as_an_export`
- `p256_record_and_export_agree_on_the_multicodec_public_key`
- `a_mnemonic_export_over_an_end_to_end_channel_is_sealed_to_the_requester`: only the requester's key opens the bundle, it holds 24 words, the words are not in the response, and the release is one-time.
- `a_signed_first_boot_export_over_https_is_sealed_to_the_signer`: first boot over HTTPS, signed, `clientDid` == signer. The export is released, only the caller's key opens it, and it is one-time.
- `over_https_a_client_did_other_than_the_signer_is_refused`
- `an_unsigned_request_is_refused` (HTTPS and end-to-end)
- `a_request_signed_by_another_did_is_refused`
- `a_proof_made_for_another_purpose_is_refused`
- `a_non_super_admin_is_refused` (HTTPS and end-to-end)
- `a_replayed_first_boot_request_is_refused_the_bundle`: the same document is sent twice through the dispatch spine. The replay is not answered with the bundle.
- In each refusal test the guard is still available afterwards.
- `the_rest_mnemonic_export_is_refused`
- The existing export, vault and guard tests pass.
- Local: `cargo test -p vta-service --features tee --lib`: 1330 passed, 1 ignored. `cargo clippy -p vta-service --features tee --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: fix(vta-service)!: close the key-material follow-ups from the export audit (#1743)
body:
fix(vta-service)!: close the key-material follow-ups from the export audit (#1743)

* fix(vta-service): apply the key-export and sign capability checks on every transport

The KeyExport capability was checked only by the keys/export-secret
Trust-Task handler, so GET /keys/{id}/secret and DIDComm get-key-secret
released private keys to an admin whose entry was narrowed without
key-export. Capability::Sign was checked nowhere.

Both checks now live in the operation layer (VTI-VTA-003, VTI-VTA-007):

- get_key_secret requires key-export before any lookup, refuses a
  hop-by-hop channel (keys/export-secret/0.1 requires a channel
  confidential to the two parties), keeps the internal-key and
  non-exportable refusals, and writes the key.secret_export audit row
  durably before releasing the material, refusing if it cannot.
- The Trust-Task binding (https, didcomm, tsp) is recorded at the three
  entry points and named in the export's audit channel.
- vta/contexts/secrets and provision-integration use the same gate.
- sign_payload requires sign for opaque caller bytes; derive-and-sign
  and derive-and-sign-document require sign.
- The legacy REST and DIDComm key routes now consult the policy gate
  with the matching Trust-Task URI.
- The TEE mnemonic export writes a durable audit row before release.

BREAKING CHANGE: private keys are no longer released over REST or the
HTTPS Trust-Task binding; use DIDComm, TSP or the on-host CLI. Entries
narrowed without key-export or sign lose export, provisioning and
generic signing respectively.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service)!: gate backup export on key-export and a confidential channel

A backup carries the seed, so it is an export of every key the VTA holds
(VTI-VTA-003).

- export_backup requires the key-export capability, read from the caller's
  ACL entry, on every path (REST, DIDComm, both initiate-export versions).
- The backup.export and backup.initiate-export audit rows are written
  durably before the envelope or descriptor is returned; a failed write
  refuses the export and aborts the bundle.
- POST /backup/export is refused, and initiate-export is refused over a
  hop-by-hop transport: the sealing password would exist in plaintext
  wherever TLS terminates, next to the bundle. DIDComm and TSP work.
- POST /attestation/mnemonic requires key-export.
- keys/export-secret and keys/sign check the caller's scope before they
  say whether a key exists, so an out-of-scope caller gets one refusal for
  both and learns neither the key's context nor its existence.
- Revoked keys are neither exported nor loaded with InternalAuthority.
- The non-exportable refusal message no longer carries a run of spaces.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): the admin key-export gate test expects the scoped refusal

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service)!: refuse backup import over REST and HTTPS Trust Tasks

The import carries the backup and the password that opens it, which
together are every key the backup holds. Over a hop-by-hop channel both
exist in plaintext wherever TLS terminates.

- POST /backup/import always answers 403.
- initiate-import and finalize-import (1.0 and 1.1) are refused over the
  HTTPS binding, after the super-admin check and before a slot is minted
  or the password is used. DIDComm and TSP still work, as does DIDComm
  backup-import.
- This implements the vta/backup Channel requirement proposed in
  trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#646, which also covers initiate-export.
- The pnm --use-rest-legacy help and the backup docs say DIDComm or TSP.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): close the key-material follow-ups from the export audit

- keys/export-secret answers keys/export-secret:notExportable and
  :neverExportable (typed KeyExportRefusal), reached only after the
  key-export, channel and scope checks.
- vault/release writes a durable vault.secret_release row (holder,
  entry, context, transport, kind; never the secret) before the sealed
  secret leaves, and refuses if it cannot.
- POST /attestation/mnemonic seals the mnemonic to the caller's did:key
  (new additive SealedPayloadV1::SeedMnemonic, Attested assertion)
  instead of returning plaintext; the guard is two-phase so a failed
  seal cannot lose the root seed.
- get_key_secret_internal records key.internal_use, not
  key.secret_export.
- P-256 (and imported X25519) public keys are stored multicodec-
  prefixed, matching custody; a boot migration re-encodes old records.

BREAKING CHANGE: POST /attestation/mnemonic takes a BootstrapRequest and
returns a sealed bundle; SealedPayloadV1 gains SeedMnemonic; internal
key loads are audited as key.internal_use.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service)!: release the TEE mnemonic only sealed, over an end-to-end channel

- New Trust Task spec/vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0 (specced at
  trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#649): super admin with key-export, the
  mnemonic sealed to the requester's did:key under an Attested assertion,
  dispatched over DIDComm and TSP. Over Trust Tasks on HTTPS it is refused
  with permissionDenied after entitlement and before the guard is touched,
  as the backup export is.
- POST /attestation/mnemonic is refused (403) and names the task: REST is
  hop-by-hop, and for a TEE TLS terminates outside the enclave.
- SeedMnemonicBundle zeroizes its mnemonic on drop.
- MnemonicExportGuard::export() and MnemonicExportResponse are removed:
  reserve/commit is the only way to read the words.
- The boot migration migrate_unprefixed_public_keys and its helper are
  removed; test deployments are recreated, not migrated.

BREAKING CHANGE: the mnemonic export moves from POST /attestation/mnemonic
to spec/vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0 over DIDComm or TSP; the
plaintext guard export is gone; unprefixed P-256 records are no longer
rewritten at boot.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): a signed first-boot mnemonic export over HTTPS

A freshly booted TEE VTA may have no DIDComm or TSP endpoint yet, and its
export window is short. The end-to-end-only rule left it with no way to take
the backup. spec/vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0 now defines a signed
first-boot path (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#649).

- Both paths require the request to be the caller's own signed document:
  - the proof is made for authentication and verifies as issuer;
  - issuer is the session DID;
  - recipient is this VTA's DID (a VTA without one is refused);
  - issuedAt is inside the dispatch freshness bound.
- Over Trust Tasks on HTTPS the export is allowed only when clientDid is
  exactly the signing caller's DID, so the words are sealed to a key only the
  caller holds. A TLS terminator holding the bearer JWT cannot sign as the
  caller, so it can neither make its own request nor change the seal
  recipient in the caller's.
- A clientDid other than the signer is refused over hop-by-hop, and so is an
  unsigned request, on every path. All refusals happen before the guard is
  touched.
- The dispatch replay guard no longer keeps a response whose task discloses
  a secret. A replayed mnemonic export is absorbed with no body, never
  answered with the bundle.
- POST /attestation/mnemonic stays 403, and names both paths.
- The durable audit row before release and the one-shot guard are
  unchanged.
- test_support::sign_as_for signs for a chosen proofPurpose.
- deploy/nitro/README.md documents the first-boot path.

Tests:
- first boot over HTTPS, signed, clientDid == signer: released, and only the
  caller's key opens it;
- clientDid != signer over HTTPS: refused;
- unsigned: refused;
- signed by another DID: refused;
- proof made for assertionMethod: refused;
- non-super-admin: refused;
- a replayed document through the dispatch spine: not answered with the
  bundle.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix: classify the mnemonic export for the MCP guard, and name its sealed request schema apart

vta/attestation/mnemonic-export is Sensitive, like keys/export-secret. The sealed-transfer BootstrapRequest schema is published as SealedBootstrapRequest so it no longer collides with the provision-integration BootstrapRequest in the OpenAPI document.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix: the mnemonic export body carries ext, and the manifest counts its unpublished URI

MnemonicExportBody denies unknown fields, so it takes the SPEC §4.5.1 ext member like every other such wire type. vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0 is bound ahead of the trust-tasks-rs this workspace takes (it is specified in 0.23), so the vta/ unpublished count is 7 until the workspace moves to 0.23.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta): drop the mnemonic-export debt now that 0.23 publishes it

vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0 (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#649) is
published in trust-tasks-rs 0.23, taken by #1764:

- trust_task_manifest.rs's vta/ unpublished-URI count goes back to 6,
  and the entry drops out of vta-service's UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS.
- the mnemonic-export handler takes the generated
  trust_tasks_rs::specs::vta::attestation::mnemonic_export::v1_0
  payload type in place of the hand-written MnemonicExportBody, which
  is now unused and removed.

title: security(vta-sdk)!: verify a proof's key against its proofPurpose (VTI-KEY-022)
body:
## What

A Data Integrity proof now verifies only when the signer's DID document lists its `verificationMethod` under the relationship named by its `proofPurpose` (VTI-KEY-022). This matches W3C Controlled Identifiers v1.0 §3.3, *Retrieve Verification Method*, steps 10 and 11. The check is strict and has no escape hatch.

## Why

Every verifier in the workspace looked the method up in `verificationMethod` and nowhere else. A key published only for `keyAgreement`, or authorised only to authenticate, could therefore make an `assertionMethod` proof over a credential.

## Changes

**vta-sdk** (`trust_task_proof::purpose`, new)
- `ProofPurpose` covers the four signing relationships. `parse` refuses `keyAgreement`, an empty value and unknown values.
- `PurposeVmResolver` resolves a method for one purpose.
- `PurposeBound` binds that resolver to one proof's purpose, as the upstream `VerificationMethodResolver` that `DataIntegrityProof::verify` takes.
- `authorised_method` requires three things:
  1. the resolved document's `id` is the DID;
  2. the method is listed under the purpose's relationship, by absolute DID URL, by `#fragment` or embedded. A reference resolves only against the top-level `verificationMethod` set, never to a method embedded under another relationship;
  3. the method's `controller` is the DID.
- **`TrustTaskVmResolver`** implements `PurposeVmResolver` and no longer implements the purpose-unaware trait.
  - For did:key, only `did:key:<id>#<id>` is accepted, and it is valid for every signing purpose. An X25519 did:key signs for nothing.
  - For did:peer, the document's own relationships apply: V keys are valid for `authentication` and `assertionMethod`, and E keys for nothing.
- `verify_trust_task_proof_with` and vetting's `verify_attached_proof` verify through `PurposeBound`.
- Refusals name the rule that failed. They contain no DID or key material.

**vtc-service**
- `DidVmResolver` delegates to `TrustTaskVmResolver` for a purpose. `resolve_ed25519`, `resolve_verifying_key` and `resolve_bbs_g2` each take the purpose.
- `check_issuer_binding` compares exact strings and requires a non-empty fragment.
- **Proof sets** (`proof_set`):
  - `accept_any` is replaced by `accept_all`: every proof present must verify, and there must be at least one.
  - A proof whose `cryptosuite` this build does not implement is skipped. A set with nothing verifiable left is refused.
  - `require_suites` lets policy require particular suites. No caller uses it yet.
  - `verify_one` checks that the proof declares the purpose the document is relied on for: `assertionMethod` for credentials and invitations, `authentication` for presentations and holder bindings.
- The credential, VP, VMC, VEC, VRC, recognition, personhood, invitation and audit paths all verify through the resolver above.
- `LocalSigner::verify_vc` checks each proof against the key that proof names.
- `assertion_method_id` returns `did:key:<id>#<id>` for a did:key issuer.

**vta-service**
- A did:key VTA signs as `did:key:<id>#<id>` instead of the store's `#key-0` (`vta_signing_vm`). This covers VC issuance, provision-integration and the rooms responses.
- `derive-and-sign-document` refuses a `proofPurpose` that no verifier accepts.
- Room invitations must declare `assertionMethod`.

**vti-rooms-dtg**: `VerificationKeys::public_key` takes the purpose. Room credentials must declare `assertionMethod`.

**vta-mcp**: the default holder fragment follows the DID method: the key id for did:key, `key-1` for did:peer, and `key-0` otherwise.

**Collapses #1757 onto this check.** #1757 added a separate relationship check for approver decisions: `ProofRelationship` and `TrustTaskVmResolver::requiring`. That check is gone, and so are the resolver's `relationship` field and `ProofRelationship::lists`/`require`. `verify_approval_proof_with` now refuses any `proofPurpose` other than `assertionMethod` (`WrongPurpose`). It then verifies through the general verifier, which binds the resolver with `PurposeBound` to `assertionMethod`, including on the retry after a DID-cache refresh (#1737's `resolve_for_vm` and `refresh_if_cached`). The public API is unchanged: `verify_approval_proof`, `verify_approval_proof_with` and `APPROVAL_PROOF_PURPOSE`. No caller outside vta-sdk used `ProofRelationship`. In `derive-and-sign-document`, #1733's `Sign` capability check runs first, then the purpose validation, both before any key is derived.

## Breaking changes

| Change | Who is affected | Migration |
|---|---|---|
| `TrustTaskVmResolver` no longer implements `VerificationMethodResolver` | callers of `DataIntegrityProof::verify` with it | `PurposeBound::for_proof(&resolver, &proof)?` |
| `VerificationKeys::public_key(vm, purpose)` | room hosts implementing it | pass the proof's purpose |
| A proof whose key is not listed under its purpose is refused | signers using a key under another relationship | sign with a key listed for the purpose |
| One failing proof refuses a proof set | documents carrying a stale or bad extra proof | drop it |
| A did:key method other than `#<id>` is refused | anything signing a did:key as `#key-0` | sign as `did:key:<id>#<id>` |

These are test deployments, so there is no migration path.

## Signer audit

**Now fails:**
- **openvtc personhood presentations.** `openvtc/src/state_handler/runtime_actions.rs:576` passes the persona's `keys.signing` key (`#key-1`) to `personhood::build_presentation`, which signs with `proofPurpose: authentication` (`openvtc-core/src/personhood.rs:316`). `create_initial_webvh_did` lists `#key-1` under `assertionMethod` only (`openvtc-core/src/config/did.rs`), so the VTC refuses the VP. Fix in openvtc: sign with `keys.authentication`.
- **did:key signers naming `#key-0`.** A did:key VTA or VTC did this; both are fixed here. So were the mock VTA in `vta-service/src/test_support.rs` and the test fixtures in `vtc-service/tests/{join_requests,invitations}.rs`.

**Pass today, will break when the VTC moves trust-task documents to `authentication`:**
- **VGI bridge.** `crates/vgi-bridge/src/wire.rs:257` refuses any inbound VTC document whose `proofPurpose` is not `assertionMethod`. No git-ns spec requires that. It must change in step with the VTC. The VTC keeps signing with `assertionMethod` for now, so nothing breaks today.

**Pass:**
- **VTC.** `LocalSigner` signs `assertionMethod` with `#key-0`, which is listed under both relationships. The hybrid ML-DSA `#key-2` is under `assertionMethod` only. That is fine for credentials, but `#key-2` could not sign an `authentication` proof.
- **VTA.** `#key-0` is listed under both relationships. The step-up, consent, credential and trust-task response signers all emit `assertionMethod`.
- **Bridge.** Its own signatures pass: the did:peer `#key-1` is listed under authentication and assertionMethod, and the did:key `#<id>` is valid for every purpose.
- **openvtc capability documents.** They are signed `assertionMethod` with `#key-1`. Under the key-roles rule they should move to the authentication key.
- **Trust Registry.** It has no DI signer.

**Verifiers outside this repo that still resolve without a purpose:** Trust Registry (trust-tasks-proof 0.21) and the bridge (0.22). Both need the next trust-tasks-proof release to get the strict check. Both compile unchanged. The in-flight bridge branches `bridge-vta` and `bridge-multi-org` implement `VerificationMethodResolver` for `Published` and pass it to `Verifier::with_resolver`, so they will need a `ProofPurposeResolver` instead.

**Not changed:** vta-vault and vta-mobile-core verify against did:key-derived or pinned keys. For those the did:key rule already holds.

## Companion changes

- Framework spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#24
- trust-tasks-proof: OpenVTC/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#637

This PR does not depend on either one; it carries its own resolver.

## Tests

- **vta-sdk**: purpose unit tests, and did:key / did:peer / wrong-purpose end-to-end tests through `verify_trust_task_proof_with`.
- **vtc-service `proof_set`**:
  - a failing proof refuses the set;
  - an unsupported suite is skipped, and a set with only unsupported suites is refused;
  - a proof with no suite is not skipped;
  - `require_suites`;
  - real did:key proofs for both purposes, a wrong purpose, and a foreign fragment.
- **Run locally**:
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`;
  - `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --features bbs --all-targets -D warnings`;
  - `cargo test -p vtc-service --tests` (all integration binaries);
  - targeted `vtc-service`, `vta-service`, `vta-sdk`, `vti-rooms-dtg` and `vta-mcp` tests.
