title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): show members' git rights and linked forge accounts
body:
## Summary

Test-guide item **UI-13** / design §7.1 ("Member detail gains a *Git rights* section and the linked GitHub account").

- **Members list**: a new *Git* column — the member's strongest recorded right, `+N` for the rest (all listed on hover), and their linked forge logins (`@login`, forge id on hover; the id is authoritative, the login display only).
- **Member detail**: a *Git rights* card — each recorded right with resource (repositories link to `/repos/repo/…`), granter (named; flagged *departed*; role-derived v0.1 grants marked as configuration), grant date and expiry (flagged within 14 days); and *Linked forge accounts* with forge id and link date, or a hint to link with `cnm git link --forge <host>` (#1726).
- Implied rights (own ⇒ maintain ⇒ commit, ns.admin ⇒ own) are not records and are not repeated; the card says so.
- Reads `GET /v1/git-ns/rights` and `GET /v1/git-ns/accounts` once per page under the Repos plugin's query keys, so both pages share a cache. Those projections need a community administrator: for a context-scoped admin the column is dropped and the page says why, rather than showing empty cells.

No server change; both endpoints already exist.

## Test plan

- [x] New `src/plugins/Members.test.tsx`: the Git column shows strongest right, count and logins; a 403 drops the column with the reason; the detail card orders rights strongest first, links repositories and not namespaces, and shows the linked account and its id
- [x] `npm run lint` (wire check + `tsc`), `npx vitest run` (385 pass), `vite build`
- [ ] Manual (UI-13): as a community admin open **Members**, check the Git column against **Repos**; open a member who linked an account and check the *Git rights* card; sign in as a context-scoped admin and check the column is replaced by the notice

title: feat(cnm-cli): cnm git link — link a forge account to the profile's DID
body:
## Summary

Closes the "no `cnm` account-link command" gap from the git-namespaces test guide.

- `cnm git link --forge <host>` sends `git-ns/account/link/0.1`, signed as the community profile's DID, prints where to authorise (and GitHub's device code), then polls `git-ns/account/link-status/0.1` every 5 s (the spec's SHOULD) until `linked` / `expired` / `failed`.
- `cnm git link --status <linkId>` follows a link begun earlier; `--no-wait` prints and returns.
- `cnm git link --list` lists the accounts linked to this DID, from `git-ns/view/0.2`'s `accounts`.
- Refusals print the fix: `git-ns/account/link:unsupportedForge`, `git-ns/account/link-status:unknownLink`, and the non-member `permissionDenied`.
- `vtc-client` gains `git_ns_link_status`.
- `docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md` gets a *Linking a forge account* section.

### Review follow-ups (second commit)

- **Exit status is the same in both modes.** Anything but `linked` exits non-zero: `failed`, `expired`, a state this client doesn't know, and still pending when waiting stops. In `--json` mode the last answer is still the only thing on stdout.
- **`failed` wording** covers both causes: the forge refused (the member declined, or the bridge job failed), or the account is already linked to another member.
- **Security:**
  - `terminal_safe` (shared by every refusal and printed value in `cnm git`) now also replaces Unicode format characters (category Cf: bidi overrides and isolates, zero-width characters, the BOM, tag characters).
  - The authorisation URL is parsed and refused unless it is `https`, with a host and no credentials. It is printed in parsed form: IDNA host, percent-encoded path. So neither a lookalike host nor an embedded bidi override can disguise it.
- The link id is polled as the VTC returned it, and sanitised only for display.

No server change: link, link-status and view/0.2 already exist in `vtc-service` `git_ns`.

## Behaviour change to flag

`cnm --json git link …` used to exit 0 on `failed` / `expired` / still-pending; it now exits non-zero, as text mode does. A script that relied on exit 0 plus parsing `state` still gets the same JSON on stdout.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p cnm-cli --bins` (79 pass). Tests cover:
  - following a link to a final state, and stopping past the deadline plus grace
  - stdout purity and exit status in both modes
  - bidi and zero-width characters
  - refused URLs (`http`, `javascript:`, `file:`, credentials, no host)
  - IDNA display of a lookalike host
  - argument parsing
  - error hints
- [x] `cargo clippy -p cnm-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`
- [ ] Manual, against a VTC with a bridge-mode namespace: `cnm git link --forge github.com`, authorise at the printed URL, see `Linked github.com account …`, then run `cnm git link --list`

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): adopt drift through git-ns/drift/resolve
body:
## What

A follow-up to #1725. **Adopt** on a drift item used to build a plain `git-ns/right/grant`. It now sends `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1 with `action: "adopt"`, carrying the same selector as Revert: `type`, the account (`forge` + `id`, `login` for display) and the `observed` value read. The VTC then:
- adopts nothing if the forge has changed since it was read (`driftNotFound`);
- records the right as the resolver's own grant (`right_grant_via`, `via: drift.adopt`);
- takes the item off the outstanding drift itself, which a plain grant never did.

An optional reason becomes the right's `reason`.

**Review fix.** The right is now the one the server projects. Adopt used `rightForForgeRole`, which mapped `write`/`push` to `git.commit.sign`, so on a personal-account namespace `write` said "No git right corresponds" when the VTC would project maintainer. It now uses `projectedRight`, which mirrors `git_ns::drift::projected_right`. `rightForForgeRole` had no other caller and is removed.

### Server rules, mirrored
`adoptStanding` (`repos/model.ts`) follows `git_ns::drift::adopt`, in order:
1. the repository is active or orphaned;
2. the signer holds `git.repo.own` there, explicit or implied by `git.ns.admin`, which is the same visibility as Revert;
3. the item is `roleAdded` or `roleChanged` (`notAdoptable` otherwise);
4. a member linked the account (`accountNotLinked`);
5. a right projects to the observed role (`noMatchingRight`);
6. for `roleChanged`, the projected right is a raise over what the member already holds on the repository, explicit or implied and unexpired (`heldRepoRank`). A lowering is `notAdoptable`, and the fix is to revoke the right;
7. the consent class: `right_grant_via` gates it as `right.grant`, so adopting owner is elevated and needs a community administrator (`elevated_requires_admin`, assumed on as for every elevated task).

When a viewer can't adopt but someone else could, they see why and the `cnm git drift resolve <resource> adopt --type=… --account-id=… --account-login=… --observed=… [--reason=…]` command, quoted fish-safe (#1723). When no one could adopt the item as it stands, it says why and offers no command. Revert is unchanged and stays on offer beside it.

`RevertDriftDialog` is now `DriftResolveDialog`, serving both actions. For adopt it names the member who receives the right, and the sign dialog lists them as "Receives the right".

## Behaviour changes (deliberate)

This PR follows the standing rule for this work: stronger security and better usability win over keeping existing behaviour.

- **Organisation `write` / `push` roles are no longer adoptable as committer.** The old button granted `git.commit.sign` for them with a plain grant. The VTC's own projection maps `write` to nothing on an organisation, because a committer is not necessarily given `write`, so drift/resolve refuses it with `noMatchingRight`. Adopting it would record a right the projection does not produce. The page now says so and points at the two safe paths: Revert, or grant the right with Add person and then revert the role.
- **Adopt no longer tolerates a stale read.** A plain grant went through whatever the forge showed by then. Now the VTC refuses it (`driftNotFound`) when the forge changed after the page was read.
- **Adopt checks more before sending.** A lowering (`roleChanged` no higher than what the member holds), an unlinked account, and an owner-level adopt from a non-community-administrator are no longer offered. Each shows why, and where someone else could do it, the command to hand over. Previously these were offered and then refused, or in the lowering case granted.
- **The hand-over command changed** from `cnm git grant …` to `cnm git drift resolve <resource> adopt …`. It needs a `cnm` with `git drift` (#1703) and a VTC that serves drift/resolve. The console ships inside `vtc-service`, so the console and the VTC always match.
- **The fixed reason is gone.** The grant used to carry "Adopted from a role added on the forge". The reason is now whatever the operator types, or none. The VTC tags the grant `via: drift.adopt` for policy and audit anyway.
- **`roleChanged` raises are now adoptable.** Previously only `roleAdded` was.

## Review follow-up (second commit)

- **Adopt waits for the rights listing.** While the listing is still loading, the list shows "Reading who holds what here before offering to adopt…" and no button. Before, it ranked against an empty list, so a `roleChanged` lowering could be offered as a raise.
- **`heldRepoRank` now matches the server's `effective_on`.** The namespace's admins (`ns.admins`) count as owners of every repository, with or without a row. `roleDerived` rows are ignored, because they are v0.1 hook-relay grants merged from the registry and never held in the git-ns store.
- **Tests:** a loading-window test (it fails without the gate), plus ranking tests for an admin with no row and for a `roleDerived` row.

## Tests

- actions:
  - adopt payload, command and party
  - normal class for maintainer, elevated for owner
  - shell safety for the resource, account, observed and reason
- model: `adoptStanding` covers
  - an owner adopting maintain
  - personal-account `write` → maintainer, while on an organisation `write` projects nothing
  - personal-account `admin` projects nothing
  - a lowering refused, and a raise from committer accepted
  - `roleRemoved` refused, and an unlinked account refused
  - hand-over to non-holders, elevated adopt only for a community administrator, a namespace admin allowed
  - `heldRepoRank`: explicit, implied and expired rights
- RepoDetail:
  - an owner adopts through the form, and the sign dialog shows the exact command and drift/resolve document without sending anything
  - personal-account `write` offers "Adopt into VTC as maintainer"
  - organisation `write` offers nothing, with the reason
  - a `roleChanged` lowering offers no adopt but keeps Revert
  - a non-holder, and a viewer with no whoami, get the command instead of the button
  - an owner-level adopt is hidden from an owner who is not a community administrator and shown as Elevated to one who is

`npx tsc -b --noEmit`, `npm run wire:check` and `npx vitest run` (416 tests) pass. No Rust changed: drift/resolve is already in the `trust_task_manifest` census (#1725).

## How to test (ROLE-13, adopt side)

1. Bridge-mode namespace. On the forge, give a collaborator role to an account a member has linked. Wait for the drift report.
2. Admin console → Repos → the repository. As an owner or namespace admin, **Adopt into VTC as …** → optional reason → **Build the adopt** → sign.
3. The member now holds the projected right, the drift item is gone without a separate revert, and `gitNs.drift.resolved` appears in the activity.
4. On a personal-account namespace, a `write` collaborator adopts as maintainer.
5. When the forge shows a role no higher than the member already holds (`roleChanged`), the page says to revoke instead and offers only Revert.

title: Retry each verification check while a deployment propagates
body:
## Summary

The preview job for #7 failed twice in a row, on a different set of files each time: first `/dtg/vsc` with `Accept: application/ld+json`, then the home page, the endorses definition by its direct path, and `release.json`. Every failing URL answered 200 when fetched moments later, and the failing responses were Pages' own `text/html` 404s without the worker's CORS header, so the asset store was still filling in when the checks ran. The wait for `release.json` added in 6dfed92 does not cover this: the second run saw `release.json` pass the probe and then fail its check seconds later.

## Change

`infra/verify.mjs` now runs each check through a `check()` helper that retries with a short backoff (1 s, 2 s, ... capped at 5 s) until the check passes or its own deadline runs out, 60 s by default and settable with `--retry <seconds>`. A check that passes on a later attempt reports the attempt count. A check that never passes reports the last attempt's problems and the attempt count, so a real defect (wrong content type, missing header, wrong body) still fails and is still diagnosable. The initial wait for `release.json` stays, since it also covers DNS and TLS not being ready and gives a clear message when a deployment never appears.

The check list and the expectations are unchanged. `expect()` is split into `problemsWith()`, which computes the mismatches, and `check()`, which loops.

## Verification

- `docker compose run --rm shell -c 'node infra/verify.mjs https://36570ae3.dtgwg-vsc-registry.pages.dev'` against the second failed preview: all 17 checks pass.
- With `--wait 3 --retry 2` against a base that has no `release.json`, the wait loop still fails with its message and exit code 1.
- `docker compose run --rm test`: 22 tests pass.

The retry path itself was not exercised against a live propagating deployment, since that needs a fresh deploy; the first PR preview job after this merges is the real test.

title: Add the DTG credential context as v1, and the rules for contexts
body:
Add the DTG credential context as v1, and the rules for contexts

Lands PLAN.md section 1.8 step 3 as a draft for the credential
specification's editors to review: contexts/v1.jsonld, the JSON-LD 1.1
context the spec's Base Structure requires, transcribed from
specification 0.5.0. It defines DTGCredential and the seven concrete
subtypes, taskContext and taskDigestMultibase, and the type-specific
members of the VSC (predicate as @id, object.value as @json,
witnessContext), the VDC (delegation) and the VAC (authority). Every
term is @protected and carries a full IRI under the unversioned
namespace https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/credentials#.
digestMultibase is inherited from the W3C VC 2.0 context and not
redefined.

Terms are defined at the top level rather than under type-scoped
contexts, because a type-scoped context does not propagate into
credentialSubject and would leave predicate and its siblings undefined.
delegation and authority carry property-scoped contexts so that the
JSON key scope expands to a different IRI in each: a set of acts in a
delegation, one resource identifier in an authority.

GOVERNANCE.md gains section 3.1: the specification is the authority
over a context's content and over when a new version is minted; a
published context is byte-frozen; changes under contexts/ follow the
specification's editorial process and land with the matching
specification change. Section 2.5 reserves /dtg/credentials and section
6 gains the review rows.

The context IRI itself is decided in cred-spec #48, not here. Refs #4.

title: feat(register)!: serve only listed controller VTAs
body:
feat(register)!: serve only listed controller VTAs

`push/register` is anonymous and names its `controllerVtaDid`, so any DID
a caller holds could be made the controller of a handle. The gateway now
serves only the controller VTAs its operator lists in
`GATEWAY_ALLOWED_CONTROLLERS` (comma/space separated DIDs, exact match):

- a registration naming an unlisted controller is refused with
  `permissionDenied`, before a sender is selected or anything stored;
- a provision by a controller no longer on the list is refused the same
  way, without spending a replay record (covers handles restored from a
  snapshot taken under a wider list);
- unset or empty lists nothing, so every registration is refused, and
  startup logs an error saying so;
- `*` alone is an explicit open mode: any controller may register, a
  startup warning is logged, and the per-controller, per-handle and
  fair-share limits all still apply;
- a malformed list (a non-DID entry, a fragment, a pattern, or `*`
  mixed with DIDs) stops startup. Patterns are deliberately not
  supported: one would admit every DID anyone can mint under it.

BREAKING CHANGE: a gateway must be configured with the VTAs it serves;
without `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_CONTROLLERS` it refuses every registration. The
`test-wake` helpers register under a throwaway controller and so need a
local gateway in open mode.

title: fix(replay): budget the record per handle and fairly overall
body:
fix(replay): budget the record per handle and fairly overall

`push/register` is anonymous and names its controller freely, so anyone
can become the "authorised" controller of handles naming DIDs they hold
and send them signed provisions. A handful of such controllers could fill
the replay record's global bound, after which every issuer was refused.
A registration-time proof from the controller would not prevent it (the
attacker is that controller), so the record's budgets now carry it:

- a provision that re-applies the stored allowlist changes nothing and
  is answered without spending a record (`Store::allowlist_is`);
- records are charged to the handle as well as the issuer, and one handle
  holds at most 512 in the window, shared by its controller and every
  trigger acting on it;
- at the global soft bound (65536) an issuer is admitted only while it
  holds less than its fair share (soft bound / issuers holding records),
  so invented controllers cannot lock out one that is not flooding; a
  hard bound of twice the soft bound caps memory;
- one controller DID holds at most 4096 live handles
  (`GATEWAY_MAX_HANDLES_PER_CONTROLLER`), and an unprovisioned handle is
  swept after 1 h instead of 24 h.

The reviewer's probe is a regression test (three self-registered
controllers flooding fresh provisions; a legitimate wake is still
admitted), with tests for the no-op provision, the per-handle budget,
the fair share and the per-controller cap. The README specifies who can
spend the record.

title: fix(inbound): believe a task-consent outcome only from the executor it answers
body:
> **Blocked on a release:** needs `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` **0.12.0** (OpenVTC/vti-didcomm-js#27) published to npm. `packages/core/package.json` asks for `^0.12.0`, but `package-lock.json` still resolves 0.11.0, so `npm ci` and CI fail until then. After publishing, run `npm install -w @openvtc/pnm-core @openvtc/vti-didcomm-js@^0.12.0` and commit the lockfile here.

## What changes

When the executor answers a `task-consent/decision`, a refusal raises "The VTA refused your approval" and drops the pending decision (`awaitingDecisions`). Until now that reply was believed whenever the message's `from` named *any* enrolled executor, and `from` is plaintext the sender writes. The wallet now keys on the sender the **transport authenticated**:

- **Transport → handler.** vti-didcomm-js 0.12 passes a `VerifiedSender` (the authcrypt `skid`'s DID) to `onInbound`, and `connectMediatorSession` passes it through. `MediatorConnection.waitFor` accepts the library's `from` filter. On the TSP path the sender is the one `unpackInboundTsp` proved.
- **Handler → pipeline.** `onInboundMessage` → `handleInbound` → `dispatchInbound` carry `senderDid`, and `PendingInbound` persists it. A message re-driven after an MV3 teardown is therefore attributed the same way it was on arrival.
- **`parseTaskConsentOutcome(message, { senderDid, expectedExecutorDid })`** (now async):
  - the authenticated sender must be **the executor the decision was sent to**. That executor is recorded as `AwaitingDecision.executorDid` at send time; when the thread is no longer remembered, the session's own VTA is used. Another enrolled executor is **not** accepted;
  - an in-band `issuer` naming anyone else → dropped;
  - if the reply carries a Data Integrity proof, it must verify (`assertionMethod`) as that executor, with `issuer` equal to it. The VTA signs its success responses but not its error documents (their proof is RECOMMENDED), so a missing proof is not a refusal in itself; the authenticated sender is the evidence then;
  - `message.from` is not consulted.
- **`parseTaskConsentGranted(message, vtaDid, senderDid)`** requires the authenticated sender to be the session's VTA. A missing sender is no longer tolerated.
- **Replies to this wallet's own requests** are accepted only from the peer each request went to. `DidcommMessageBridge.sendAndAwaitReply` now takes a **required** `from`, and `MediatorSessionBridge` hands it to the session's `waitFor` filter, so a frame on the thread from any other sender is never returned as the answer. Call sites:
  - `DidcommVtaTransport` → the VTA, plus the forwarding mediator when one is configured (its refusal of the hop is an answer the caller already maps);
  - `MediatorClient` → the mediator;
  - `loginViaDidcomm` → the RP.

  `InMemoryDidcommBridge` enforces the same rule.
- `taskConsentOutcomeThread()` lets the caller look up the awaiting decision (and its executor) before the reply is trusted.
- **Adapts to 0.12's exact-`skid` key selection.** `connectMediatorSession` seeds the VTA key with its `kid`, and `resolveSender(did, skid)` resolves that exact keyAgreement key (`resolveX25519KeyAgreementKey`).
- CLAUDE.md gains a section on this invariant and on the new `^0.12.0` floor.

## Breaking changes

- `parseTaskConsentOutcome` changed shape (async; `{ senderDid, expectedExecutorDid }` replaces `{ enrolledExecutorDids }`).
- `parseTaskConsentGranted` takes a third argument.
- `PendingInbound` has a required `senderDid`. Per this repo's no-compat-folds rule there is no migration for stored records: a record written by an older build re-drives with `senderDid` undefined, so its outcome or granted notice is dropped rather than believed. Request prompts are unaffected, because they are proof-verified.
- `MediatorConnection.onInbound`'s handler gets a third `sender` argument.
- `DidcommMessageBridge.sendAndAwaitReply`'s options, including `from`, are required. Any other bridge implementation must honour `from`.

## Tests

- `inbound.task-consent-outcome.mjs`:
  - refusal with `from` = VTA but a different authenticated sender (the forged notice) → `null`;
  - reply from another enrolled executor → `null`;
  - no authenticated sender → `null`;
  - a missing `from` doesn't matter when the sender is proven;
  - contradicting `issuer` → `null`;
  - signed response from the executor → believed;
  - proof by another key → `null`;
  - signed reply edited after signing → `null`;
  - thread lookup.
- `inbound.task-consent.mjs`: granted notice keyed on the authenticated sender, not `from`; no sender → dropped.
- `inbound.pending.mjs`: `senderDid` persists.
- `vta.bridge-peer.mjs` (new): `MediatorSessionBridge` passes `from` to `waitFor`; a VTA request names the VTA as its only peer; a mediator request names the mediator; the in-memory bridge refuses a reply from an unnamed peer. `rp-login.didcomm.mjs`: the login names the RP.
- `inbound.consent-schema.mjs`: updated to the new options.
- Run locally against a packed 0.12.0 tarball of vti-didcomm-js#27: `npm run lint` and `npm run build` are clean, and `npm test` passes (core 705/705, plus the other workspaces). `inbound.ack-ordering.mjs` still passes, so R1.6 ordering is unchanged.

## Release ordering

1. Merge vti-didcomm-js#27 and publish 0.12.0.
2. Refresh this PR's lockfile; CI goes green.
3. Merge this.

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — proof verification resolves did:webvh via the existing resolver
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — persist still precedes resolve; senderDid is written in the same put
- [ ] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire change; depends on vti-didcomm-js 0.12
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no sender → dropped
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — inbound log shows the authenticated sender
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — senderDid is persisted with the message
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```

title: ci(vtc-admin-ui): run the admin console's unit tests
body:
## Summary

CI never ran the admin console's tests. `cargo build -p vtc-service` runs `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`), which only proves the console compiles. The vitest suite (400 tests in 35 files) and the `openapi.json` -> `src/lib/wire.ts` drift check only ever ran on a developer's machine.

### New job: `Test (VTC admin UI)`
- `actions/setup-node` (pinned SHA), node version from `vtc-service/admin-ui/.nvmrc`, `cache: npm` keyed on the lockfile
- `npm ci` (exact lockfile, and it fails if the lockfile disagrees with `package.json`)
- `npm run wire:check` (lint: generated wire types match `openapi.json`)
- `tsc -b --noEmit` (typecheck)
- zsh and fish installed (bounded, best-effort apt) so that the `shellQuote` round-trip tests in `src/plugins/repos/actions.test.ts` actually run. Without them the runner has only sh and bash, and those 6 tests were skipped without anyone noticing.
- `vitest run`
- No Rust, no system packages, no secrets. `timeout-minutes: 10`. Gated on the VTC closure (`affects.vtc_tests`), the same as `Test (VTC)`.

I checked the rest of the repo: this is the only JS/TS package with tests. `examples/vta-auth-demo` and `vtc-service/website-default` are static files with no package.json, and `vti-rooms-wasm` is a Rust crate that `Mobile build` already builds.

### `Test (VTC)` robustness (the #1725 timeout)
Across the 34 runs before this change, the job took 11-16 min: disk freeing 0.6-2.5 min, `cargo test` 8-12 min, and the no-op guard about 2 min. The run that timed out on #1725 was on a slow runner where every step took 2-3x as long (disk freeing 7.4 min, tests 21.1 min), and the 30-minute ceiling ran out during the no-op guard.
- **Disk freeing only runs when needed.** The job links two crates, and the image has about 100 GB free even after the removal, so about 80 GB before it. The `rm -rf` of Android, .NET and GHC now only runs when less than 30 GB is free.
- **The no-op guard (#1243) is fast now.** It re-runs the test step's own build with `--no-run` (one settle build, then the check) so it reuses that step's artifacts. title: feat(unpack)!: bind an authcrypt message's `from` to its sender key
body:
## What changes

**`unpack` binds an authcrypt message's `from` to the key that authenticated it.** It already required `apu == skid`, which pins the sender *key*. Nothing tied that key to the plaintext `from`, and consumers read `from`. DIDComm v2 requires `from` on an authcrypt message and requires `skid` to be a key of it; both are now enforced. A message whose `from` is missing, is a DID URL, or names any DID other than `DID(skid)` throws `SenderMismatchError` (`code: "E_SENDER_MISMATCH"`, R3.7).

**The authenticated sender is passed to consumers directly**, so none of them has to read `from`:

| API | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `unpack()` | `{ message, senderKid, authenticated, legacyKekUsed }`; anoncrypt `senderKid: undefined` | adds `senderDid`; anoncrypt `senderKid` and `senderDid` are both `null` |
| `onMessage` / `onMediatorMessage` | `(message, thid)` | `(message, thid, sender)`, where `sender` is a frozen `VerifiedSender { did, kid }` |
| `waitFor(thid, ms)` | resolves `message` | `waitFor(thid, ms, { from })` resolves `{ message, sender }`. Given `from` (a DID or a list of DIDs), only a reply authenticated as one of them claims the waiter; anyone else's frame on that thread goes to other waiters or the listener |
| `VtaMediatorClient.sendAndWait` | any reply on the thread | only a reply authenticated as its VTA; still returns the message |
| `unpackInbound` | — | also returns `senderDid` |

**Sender key selected by the exact `skid`.** `unpackInbound` now matches a `senderKeys` entry only when its `kid` equals the `skid`, so the reported `senderKid` is the key the envelope was actually authenticated with. A relative `#fragment` is resolved against the DID, and an entry without a `kid` matches nothing. `resolveSender` is called as `(did, skid)` and held to the same rule. `connectVtaViaMediator` uses the new `resolveX25519KeyAgreementKey(did, kid)`, which requires the key to be listed under `keyAgreement`.

**Refused frames are acked and dropped.** A frame that decrypts and is then refused for good (`E_SENDER_MISMATCH`, or anoncrypt carrying a `skid`, which returns the new `E_UNAUTHENTICATED_FRAME`) is logged via `onError` and acked, so it isn't redelivered forever. Other unpack failures, which may be transient, are still left queued.

JSDoc, the generated `types/`, and the README now call `message.from` sender-asserted plaintext, and say to authorise on `senderDid` / `sender.did`.

## Breaking changes (0.11.0 → 0.12.0)

- `waitFor` resolves `{ message, sender }` instead of the bare message.
- Anoncrypt `senderKid` is `null` (was `undefined`).
- Authcrypt with no `from`, or with a `from` that doesn't match, no longer unpacks. Through `MediatorSession` such a frame goes to `onError` and is not acked, like any other frame that fails to unpack.
- `senderKeys` entries need `kid`; `resolveSender` receives `(did, skid)` and must return that key.
- Consumer: **pnm-browser-plugin** (`connectMediatorSession` wraps `waitFor` and `onMessage`). Its adaptation is a separate draft PR, which needs this published first. CHANGELOG has migration notes.

## Tests

- `test/sender-binding.test.js` (13 tests, now timer-free: every wait is on the event asserted), including exact-skid selection (wrong kid, no kid, relative kid, resolver asked for the skid) and ack-and-drop of a forged-`from` frame and of an anoncrypt-with-skid frame. Original cases:
  - unpack: genuine authcrypt returns `senderDid`/`senderKid`; a forged `from` with a mismatched `skid` is refused with `E_SENDER_MISMATCH` (the attacker's key, the victim's DID); a missing `from` is refused; a DID-URL `from` is refused; anoncrypt gives a `null` sender whatever `from` says.
  - session: a genuine frame reaches `onMessage` with its verified sender and is acked; a forged-`from` frame is never delivered and never acked; `waitFor` resolves `{ message, sender }`; a waiter bound with `from` ignores an attacker's frame on its thread, which falls through to the listener, and still gets the genuine reply; a malformed `from` throws `TypeError`.
- Existing fixtures updated to the new shapes. Authcrypt fixtures that had no `from` now carry one.
- `npm test`: 304 tests, 297 pass, 7 skipped, 0 fail (the Rust round-trip suite skips locally and runs in CI). `npm run build:types` is clean.

## Release

Publish **0.12.0** after merge, because the plugin resolves from npm. `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and the CHANGELOG are bumped in this PR.

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — n/a
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — a refused frame is reported via onError; the loop continues
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — unchanged; a refused frame is never acked
- [ ] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire change; the JS consumer (pnm-browser-plugin) is updated in its own PR
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no opt-out
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — n/a
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```

title: fix(didcomm): claim the replay record only for an authorised, unexpired document
body:
fix(didcomm): claim the replay record only for an authorised, unexpired document

Follow-ups to the document admission added in the previous commit:

- An already-expired document (`expiresAt` in the past, `issuedAt` in
  the window) was accepted, and because its record was retained only
  until `expiresAt` it re-executed on every delivery. `validate_basic`
  now refuses `expiresAt <= now` before anything is claimed.
- The record was claimed before authorisation, so any self-signed
  did:key could create entries and push legitimate ones out of the
  bounded record, making them replayable. The claim now runs inside the
  dispatch core (`AdmitOnce`), after the per-DID rate limit and after the
  controller/allowlist check (`Store::check_controller` for provision).
  A refused caller leaves no entry.
- The record (`src/replay.rs`, `ReplayRecord`) is keyed by (issuer, id)
  and partitioned per issuer: one issuer cannot evict another's entries
  or take an id another will use. At its bounds (8192 per issuer, 65536
  total) it refuses instead of evicting.
- A transient push failure releases the claim, so a retry of the same
  document is attempted instead of answered with the failure.
- Retention now runs to the last instant the window accepts the document
  (`issuedAt + max_age + skew`, or `expiresAt` if sooner) plus 1 s.
  Previously it stopped `skew` short of that.
- The proof's verification method is refused when `revoked` is set or
  `expires` has passed (or does not parse), and a resolved DID document
  over 64 KiB is refused.

title: fix(vti-common)!: bind the authcrypt sender key id to the key used, before trusting a DIDComm sender
body:
Bind the authcrypt sender key id to the key used, before trusting a DIDComm sender.

An authcrypt (ECDH-1PU) JWE names its sender key twice in the protected header: `skid`, and `apu` (the PartyUInfo the key derivation is bound to). A conforming packer writes the same key id into both. The direct-unpack callers now require that they agree, and that the key the unpack metadata reports is that same key, before a sender is trusted.

## Changes

- **`vti_common::auth::verify_authcrypt_header(raw_jwe)`** (new). Reads the outer JWE (JSON or compact serialization), decodes the protected header, and for an ECDH-1PU layer requires: `skid` is a string DID URL with a `#fragment`, `apu` is present, and `BASE64URL-decode(apu)` is exactly the `skid` bytes (canonical encoding only). Returns the `skid`. Any other `alg` is refused, so authcrypt nested inside anoncrypt is not accepted on these paths.
- **`vti_common::auth::bind_authcrypt_sender(raw_jwe, message, metadata)`** now takes the raw envelope as well. It requires: the header check passes; the unpack wrapping is `authcrypt(plaintext)` or `authcrypt(sign(plaintext))` (never `anoncrypt(authcrypt(plaintext))`); `metadata.encrypted_from_kid == Some(skid)`; and `DID(from) == DID(skid)`.
- `AuthcryptError` gains variants for these cases and becomes `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- Every caller is updated: VTA `POST /auth/` and `/auth/refresh`, VTC `POST /v1/auth/`, `/wallet/auth/` and their refresh routes, and VTA vault unseal (`vault/upsert` with a `didcomm-authcrypt` sealed secret).
- New `vti-common` feature `test-support` (`auth::authcrypt_test_support`) that builds authcrypt envelopes with a caller-chosen protected header. The `test-support` features of `vta-service` and `vtc-service` turn it on. Never enabled in a production build.

## Breaking changes

- **API:** `bind_authcrypt_sender` takes a new first argument, `raw_jwe: &str`. `AuthcryptError` has new variants and is now `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- **Wire:** the direct-unpack routes above now refuse:
  - a bare-DID `skid` (no `#fragment`);
  - an authcrypt header missing `skid` or `apu`, or whose `apu` does not encode `skid`;
  - authcrypt wrapped in anoncrypt (`anoncrypt(authcrypt(plaintext))`) posted directly to these routes.

  The messaging SDK's packer writes `skid = apu = <DID URL of the key-agreement key>` in every in-repo client, so the SDK login and refresh used by pnm, cnm, vta-sdk and vtc-client are unchanged. Third-party packers that emit any of the refused shapes will now get a 401.

## Tests

- `vti-common` unit tests cover: a `skid`/`apu` split; `skid` or `apu` missing; a non-string `skid`; a bare-DID `skid`; a near-miss or non-canonical `apu`; the compact serialization; an anoncrypt outer layer and nested authcrypt; a metadata key other than `skid`; and a `from` mismatch. One case runs a real envelope through the messaging library's decryptor, to show it decrypts before the header check refuses it.
- `vta-service/tests/auth_authcrypt_sender_binding.rs` and `vtc-service/tests/auth_authcrypt_sender_binding.rs` drive the real routes: `/auth/` on the VTA, and `/v1/auth/` and `/wallet/auth/` on the VTC. They use an offline ATM that decrypts real envelopes. Each test gets a challenge for an enrolled admin DID and answers it with a JWE whose `skid` names another party's key while `apu` and `from` name the admin. That is refused with 401, no token is issued, and the session stays unauthenticated. The same tests cover a missing `skid`, a missing `apu`, a bare-DID `skid`, and a consistent key whose `from` names a different DID. A genuine envelope packed by the library still logs in and gets tokens.

The check is local to VTI and does not depend on what the messaging library verifies, so it stays in place as defence in depth.

title: refactor(vti-common): move the task-consent core out of vta-policy so the VTC can share it (VTI-APV-014)
body:
First of four PRs for **VTI-APV-014** at the VTC. The requirement: creating an entry with unrestricted act scope, or widening an entry to it, needs consent from a party other than the requester. The design is in `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-operation-bound-step-up.md` §4.

The VTC is to use the same `task-consent/*` ceremony the VTA runs (VTI-VTC-020: one model, not a parallel one). The ceremony's data layer lives in `vta-policy`, which the VTC cannot depend on. This PR moves it to `vti-common` so the VTC can reuse it instead of copying it. It is a move only, with no behaviour change.

## What moves

| From | To |
|---|---|
| `vta-policy/src/consent.rs` | `vti_common::task_consent` |
| `vta-policy/src/effects.rs` | `vti_common::task_consent::effects` |

- Both files are moved with `git mv`, so their history follows.
- `vta_policy::{consent, effects}` re-export the new modules, so every existing path still resolves.
- `vta-policy` no longer needs `multibase` or `serde_json_canonicalizer`, and `vti-common` gains `serde_json_canonicalizer`.

## One copy of the digest

The VTC's operation-bound step-up (`vtc-service/src/acl/bound_step_up.rs`) carried a byte-for-byte copy of the digest function, differing only in its domain tag (`vtc/step-up/v1\0`). The construction is now public as `domain_digest(domain, type_uri, payload, salt)`, and the step-up calls it.

## Evidence that no digest changed

- `digest_matches_its_pinned_vectors` pins the task-consent digest and the step-up digest, salted and unsalted, against vectors computed independently in Python.
- That matters because the digest keys stored pendings, grants and step-up marks, and it is what approvers sign. A pending or mark in flight across an upgrade still resolves.
- The `vta/task-consent/v1\0` tag is kept for the same reason. It separates this digest from other digests, not one node from another, because a pending never leaves the node that minted it.

## Checks

- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 4913 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 2158 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

## Next in the series

2. The VTC consent gate and ceremony on `acl/grant` and `acl/change-role`, with the per-community threshold.
3. Attrition checks, plus two paths that confer unrestricted admin today without any check: `vtc/admin/invites/create`, and an `acl/grant` rewrite that narrows an unrestricted admin.
4. A co-admin at install, and audit rows for the offline ACL writers.

title: fix(vta): a DIDComm reply is accepted only from the peer it was asked of
body:
fix(vta): a DIDComm reply is accepted only from the peer it was asked of

`DidcommMessageBridge.sendAndAwaitReply` correlated a reply by thread
id alone. A thread id is the id of a message this wallet sent through
the mediator, not a secret, so any authenticated sender that learned
it could have its frame returned as the answer.

`sendAndAwaitReply` now takes a required `from` — the DID(s) the reply
must be authenticated as — and `MediatorSessionBridge` hands it to the
session's `waitFor` filter (vti-didcomm-js 0.12), which leaves anyone
else's frame on the thread unclaimed. Each call site names its
addressee:

- `DidcommVtaTransport`: the VTA, plus the forwarding mediator when one
  is configured (its refusal of the hop is an answer the caller maps);
- `MediatorClient`: the mediator;
- `loginViaDidcomm`: the RP.

`InMemoryDidcommBridge` enforces the same rule, failing fast on a reply
from an unnamed peer.

title: feat(didcomm)!: authentication-purpose proofs, bounded by time of issue and id
body:
feat(didcomm)!: authentication-purpose proofs, bounded by time of issue and id

`push/provision` and `push/wake` are the caller's own operational
messages, not attestations. Per VTI-KEY-106 they are signed with the
caller's operational key under `proofPurpose: authentication`, and the
verification method must be listed under `authentication` in the
issuer's DID document. An `assertionMethod` proof — reserved for
attestation artefacts — is now refused. The exact
verificationMethod/controller/issuer binding is unchanged.

An `authentication` proof carries no challenge, so the document itself
binds it to one delivery (VTI-KEY-107):

- `recipient` is required on a signed document (and must be this
  gateway, as before);
- `issuedAt` is required and must lie within the acceptance window —
  at most 5 minutes old, at most 60 s in the future (VTI-OPS-024,
  `FreshnessPolicy::consequential`);
- the document `id` is claimed in a replay record held in `AppState`
  and retained for exactly that window (VTI-OPS-026). A second delivery
  of an accepted document is answered with the first response and not
  executed again; a different document under an accepted id gets
  `idConflict`; an unavailable record fails closed.

BREAKING CHANGE: the VTA must sign these messages with its operational
key under `authentication`, and include `recipient`, `issuedAt` and a
unique `id`. No dual acceptance of `assertionMethod`.

title: fix(inbound): believe a task-consent outcome only from the executor it answers
body:
fix(inbound): believe a task-consent outcome only from the executor it answers

The executor's answer to a `task-consent/decision` is read by
`parseTaskConsentOutcome`, and a refusal both raises "The VTA refused
your approval" and drops the decision the wallet is waiting on. It was
believed when the message's `from` named any enrolled executor, and
`from` is plaintext the sender writes.

It now keys on the sender the transport authenticated:

- `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` 0.12 delivers a `VerifiedSender` (the
  authcrypt `skid`'s DID) to `onInbound` handlers; `connectMediatorSession`
  passes it through, and its `waitFor` takes the library's `from` filter.
  The TSP path uses the sender `unpackInboundTsp` proved.
- `onInboundMessage` → `handleInbound` → `dispatchInbound` carry that
  `senderDid`, and `PendingInbound` persists it, so a message re-driven
  after an MV3 teardown is attributed exactly as it was on arrival.
- `parseTaskConsentOutcome(message, { senderDid, expectedExecutorDid })`
  requires the authenticated sender to be the executor the decision was
  sent to (`AwaitingDecision.executorDid`, recorded at send time; the
  session's VTA when the thread is no longer remembered). Another
  enrolled executor is not accepted. An in-band `issuer` that names
  someone else is dropped, and a reply that carries a Data Integrity
  proof must verify as that executor. Error documents are unsigned by
  the executor, so a missing proof is not itself a refusal. It is now
  async; `taskConsentOutcomeThread` exposes the thread lookup.
- `parseTaskConsentGranted` takes the authenticated sender and no
  longer tolerates a missing one.

`@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` is raised to `^0.12.0`. That release is not
yet published, so the lockfile still resolves 0.11.0 and must be
refreshed once it is.

title: feat(verify-trust): query the Trust Registry over TSP or DIDComm; REST is optional
body:
## What

verify-trust no longer needs the Trust Registry's REST interface. It queries over the binding the registry's DID document advertises, preferring **TSP, then DIDComm, then HTTPS**. There is **no fallback**: if the chosen binding fails, the run fails. A blocked mediator never downgrades the check to HTTPS.

### Choosing the binding
- **CLI:** `--transport <auto|tsp|didcomm|https>`.
  - `auto` is the default and uses the strict preference order above.
  - Naming a binding the registry doesn't advertise, or one this build can't speak, fails closed and names what each side offers.
  - `https` uses the `#rest` endpoint from the DID document.
  - `--registry-url` stays the explicit HTTPS override and implies `https`. Combining it with `tsp` or `didcomm` is an error.
- **Action:** a `transport` input, validated, and passed to the CLI only when it is not `auto`.
- **Workflows the bridge writes, and `vgi repo init`:** `[verify_trust] transport` and `--verify-trust-transport`. The input is written into the workflow only when it isn't `auto`, so existing workflows don't drift.

### CI runs (GitHub required and in-repo workflows, Forgejo workflow, local CLI)
- **Per-run identity:** each run generates a fresh `did:peer:2` in memory. It is never written to disk or logs, and its keys are removed from the resolver when the run ends. Its service entry names the registry's mediator, so replies route back.
- **Accepting a DIDComm reply:** the envelope is read packed and checked before it is unpacked. The sender key id must be bound to the key the key agreement actually used:
  - the envelope is authcrypt (`ECDH-1PU`);
  - `skid` and `apu` are both present, and `apu` decodes to exactly `skid`;
  - the key belongs to the registry's DID;
  - neither member appears outside the protected header.

  After unpacking, the message's sender must be that key and `from` must name the registry. A signature by anyone else refuses the reply. The registry does not sign its replies today, so authcrypt is the proof of origin.
- **Accepting a TSP reply:** the sender VID whose signature was verified must be the registry DID. The run forms a relationship with the registry (Rev 3 §7.2.2) before the first query.
- **Query ids:** every query goes out under a fresh random UUID v4, and the reply's thread must match it.
- **Failing closed:** each of these makes that signer's commits `registryUnavailable`:
  - the mediator refuses the run's DID;
  - the registry or its mediator sends a problem report whose sender passes the same check;
  - no proven answer arrives within 30 seconds.

  A problem report from an unproven sender is ignored and does not end the run.

### Bridge-posted checks
These use the registry's `#rest` endpoint (HTTPS) **until the messaging SDK's authcrypt fix is released**. The bridge's mediator session delivers replies already unpacked, so it can't run the envelope check above. The bridge's DIDComm registry channel from the first revision of this PR is removed for now. A follow-up PR will re-enable bridge-DID DIDComm registry queries on the fixed SDK and keep this PR's header check as defence in depth. Until then, the registry must publish `#rest` for bridge-posted checks.

The bridge's job path is unaffected: a job is accepted only on a Data Integrity proof by a key of the VTC DID, which must also be the document's issuer.

### Also
- `UNKNOWN-KEY` now names the usual cause: the signer rotated their key, so the commit needs re-signing with the current key. It includes the re-sign recipe.
- The RUNBOOK now says to re-sign the commits in your open pull requests after rotating your signing key.

## Breaking changes / release note
- **CI binding change:** a registry that advertises `#tsp` or `#didcomm` is now queried over it, not over `#rest`. For that to work, the registry's mediator must admit unknown DIDs:
  - `mediator_acl_mode = explicit_deny`;
  - a `global_acl_default` with an open inbox; the narrowest that works is `DENY_ALL,LOCAL,SEND_MESSAGES,RECEIVE_MESSAGES,SEND_FORWARDED,RECEIVE_FORWARDED,MODE_EXPLICIT_DENY`.

  The mediator's shipped default gives a new DID a closed inbox, so runs fail `registryUnavailable` until this is changed. To keep today's HTTPS behaviour, set `transport: https`. The release note text is in the RUNBOOK.
- **Library API:**
  - new: `Registry`, `TransportSelector`, `verify_prepared_with`, and `authcrypt_sender_kid`;
  - `VerifyTrustArgs` gains `transport`;
  - `discover_registry_route` takes a selector.
- **Bridge config:** `[verify_trust] transport` is new. A `[checks] transport` key is rejected.

## Dependencies
- `didcomm` and `tsp` are default features of verify-trust. `--no-default-features` builds an HTTPS-only verifier.
- TSP adds `affinidi-tsp` and its crypto dependencies.
- `trust-tasks-trql` is an alias for the trust-tasks-rs 0.21 node that trql-client already resolves, so no new version enters the tree.
- Dev-only: `affinidi-messaging-test-mediator` 0.9.17 and `sha2`.

## Tests
- **Unit tests:**
  - binding selection, including named transports, bindings the registry doesn't advertise, bindings this build can't speak, and `--registry-url` with a conflicting transport;
  - the reply rule;
  - the authcrypt binding: a `skid`/`apu` mismatch in either direction, a missing `skid` or `apu`, anoncrypt, and sender members outside the protected header;
  - query ids are random UUID v4s;
  - the run identity;
  - failing closed.
- **Against an in-process mediator:**
  - DIDComm and TSP round trips;
  - a correlated reply from another DID is ignored;
  - a reply sealed with another DID's key whose party info names the registry's key is never believed. Disabling the binding check makes this test fail with `authorized: true`.
  - an `ExplicitAllow` mediator and a mediator on the shipped ACL default both fail closed.
- **Workflow templates and bridge config:** the transport input and the config option.
- **Local runs:** fmt, clippy with warnings as errors (workspace, plus the verify-trust feature subsets), `cargo test --workspace`, and the 1.95 MSRV check all pass.

title: feat(verify-trust): query the Trust Registry over TSP or DIDComm; REST is optional (#88)
body:
feat(verify-trust): query the Trust Registry over TSP or DIDComm; REST is optional (#88)

* feat(verify-trust): query the Trust Registry over TSP or DIDComm

The registry's REST interface is now optional. Discovery takes the
highest-preference binding the registry's DID document advertises and
this build speaks — TSP, then DIDComm, then HTTPS — instead of bailing
on a registry that advertises no #rest service.

Over the mediator bindings each run queries as a fresh did:peer:2,
minted in memory on the first query (never written to disk, logs or the
environment) with a DIDComm service naming the registry's mediator so
the reply routes back. The verdict rests on the registry's key: a reply
is believed only when the binding authenticated it as the registry DID
(authcrypt sender key and `from`, or the TSP-verified sender VID) and it
answers the query asked. verify-trust implements these transports itself
because trql-client's route replies by threadId alone.

A mediator that refuses the run's DID, a problem report, or no proven
answer within 30s fails the signer's commits as registryUnavailable and
the session stops asking for the rest of the run. A range with nothing
to ask about never opens a session.

--registry-url stays as the explicit HTTPS override and behaves exactly
as before. `didcomm` and `tsp` are default features; HTTPS-only builds
use --no-default-features. The library gains `Registry` (HTTPS, an
ephemeral sender, or a caller-owned `RegistryChannel`) and
`verify_prepared_with`; `verify_prepared` and `resolve_registry_endpoint`
keep their HTTPS meaning.

Tests cover selection for TSP-only and DIDComm-only documents, the reply
rule, the run identity, fail-closed on an unreachable mediator, and —
against an in-process mediator — DIDComm and TSP round trips, a
correlated reply from another DID being ignored, and ExplicitAllow and
shipped-default-ACL mediators failing closed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): query the registry as the bridge's DID over DIDComm

The bridge-posted check now reaches a registry that advertises DIDComm
over the bridge's existing mediator session, as the bridge's own stable
DID, preferring it to HTTPS. It does not open a second session: the
mediator permits one websocket per DID, and a second would take the job
link's slot.

Replies arrive on the same inbound stream as jobs. Bridge::handle_inbound
offers each document to RegistryReplies::route first, which takes it only
when authcrypt proved it came from the registry's DID and it answers a
query in flight; everything else goes to the job path unchanged. A link
that is down, a refusal, or no proven answer in 30s is
registryUnavailable. The start-up git.commit.sign grant probe uses the
same binding.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs: the registry's REST interface is optional for the commit check

verify-trust README, RUNBOOK, BRIDGE.md, the top-level README and the
action's registry-url input now describe binding selection, the per-run
did:peer, what the registry's mediator must allow for it (explicit_deny,
an open-inbox global_acl_default, and the forwarded bits for DIDComm),
fail-closed behaviour, the absence of an automatic HTTPS fallback, and
the bridge querying as its own DID.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat: explicit registry transport selector; no fallback

verify-trust gains --transport <auto|tsp|didcomm|https>. auto keeps the strict
TSP > DIDComm > HTTPS preference with no fallback; a named binding the
registry does not advertise, or this build cannot speak, fails closed naming
both sides. https uses the DID document's #rest endpoint; --registry-url
implies https and refuses tsp/didcomm.

The action takes a matching transport input (validated, passed only when not
auto). The workflows the bridge and vgi repo init write carry it from
[verify_trust] transport / --verify-trust-transport, written only when not
auto so existing workflows do not drift. The bridge-posted check takes
[checks] transport (auto = DIDComm > HTTPS; tsp is refused).

UNKNOWN-KEY now names the usual cause, a key rotated since signing, and how to
re-sign; the runbook says to re-sign open pull requests after rotating a key
and carries the release note for the behaviour change.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(verify-trust): bind the authcrypt sender key id to the key actually used

A DIDComm reply was believed on the unpacked sender the messaging SDK
reports. That sender comes from the envelope's party info (`apu`), while
the key the SDK looks up comes from `skid`, and nothing tied the two
together. The DIDComm transport now reads each envelope packed and checks
its protected header before unpacking: it must be authcrypt (ECDH-1PU),
with both `skid` and `apu` present, `apu` decoding to exactly `skid`, the
key belonging to the registry DID, and neither member repeated outside
the protected header. The unpacked sender must then be that key, `from`
must name the registry, and a signature by anyone else refuses the reply.
The registry does not sign replies today, so authcrypt remains the proof
of origin.

Every mediated query now goes out under a fresh UUID v4 from the OS
CSPRNG, whatever id the client chose (trql-client falls back to a clock
and counter id in the build verify-trust uses), and the reply must carry
that id as its thread.

A problem report ends a query only if its sender passes the same check
and is the registry or its mediator. Unauthenticated DIDComm frames on a
TSP session are ignored. Neither can latch the session any more.

The bridge-posted check goes back to HTTPS only. The bridge's mediator
session hands it replies already unpacked, so it cannot check the
binding above and cannot prove a reply came from the registry. The
bridge's DIDComm registry channel, and the inbound hook that fed it, are
removed. The bridge's job path is unaffected: it accepts a document only
if a Data Integrity proof verifies against a key of the VTC DID, which
must also be the document's issuer. The authcrypt sender is an extra
refusal condition on that path, never a reason to accept.

Tests: the binding is exercised on crafted headers (a mismatch in either
direction, missing skid or apu, anoncrypt, sender members outside the
protected header), and query ids are checked to be random. A regression
test against the in-process mediator sends a reply sealed with another
DID's key whose party info names the registry's key: the query times out
and is never answered.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(unpack)!: bind an authcrypt message's `from` to its sender key
body:
feat(unpack)!: bind an authcrypt message's `from` to its sender key

`unpack` already required `apu == skid`, which pins the key an authcrypt
envelope was made with. Nothing tied that key to the `from` the plaintext
carries, and consumers read `from`. Both halves of DIDComm v2's rule are
now enforced: an authcrypt message whose `from` is missing, is a DID URL,
or names another DID than the `skid`'s is refused with
`SenderMismatchError` (`code: "E_SENDER_MISMATCH"`).

The authenticated sender is also handed to consumers directly, so none
has to read `from`:

- `unpack` returns `senderDid` beside `senderKid`; both are `null` for
  anoncrypt (previously `senderKid` was `undefined`).
- `MediatorSession` passes a frozen `VerifiedSender` `{ did, kid }` as a
  third argument to `onMessage` / `onMediatorMessage`.
- `waitFor` resolves `{ message, sender }` and takes `{ from }`, a DID or
  list of DIDs a reply must be authenticated as; a message on the thread
  from anyone else is left for other waiters and the listener.
- `VtaMediatorClient.sendAndWait` only accepts a reply from its VTA.

`from` is documented as sender-asserted plaintext throughout (JSDoc,
generated types, README).

BREAKING CHANGE: `waitFor` resolves `{ message, sender }` instead of the
message; anoncrypt `senderKid` is `null`; authcrypt without a matching
`from` no longer unpacks. Release 0.12.0 (+ CHANGELOG, with migration
notes).

title: feat(didcomm)!: authenticate provision and wake by the document's proof
body:
feat(didcomm)!: authenticate provision and wake by the document's proof

The HTTPS adapter authenticates `push/provision` and `push/wake` by a
signature over the request body. The DIDComm adapter authorised them on
the envelope's `from`, so the two transports did not ask the caller for
the same evidence. They now do: over DIDComm the Trust Task document
carries an `eddsa-jcs-2022` Data Integrity proof, and the caller is the
document's `issuer` once that proof binds it to one of the issuer's own
keys (src/proof.rs):

- the proof is `eddsa-jcs-2022` with `proofPurpose: assertionMethod`;
- the DID of `proof.verificationMethod` is the `issuer`;
- the issuer's DID document lists that method, its `controller` is the
  issuer, and it is referenced (or embedded) under `assertionMethod`;
- the signature verifies over the raw document without `proof`.

`push/provision` then requires that issuer to be the handle's
controller VTA and `push/wake` requires it to be on the allowlist,
through the unchanged dispatch core.

The envelope sender is never authorising on its own. A document with no
proof reaches the core as anonymous, so `push/register` works as before
and provision/wake answer `proofRequired`. When the envelope does name a
sender it must be the proven issuer (`identityMismatch` otherwise), and a
document addressed to another `recipient` gets `wrongRecipient`.

Proof DIDs resolve through a resolver built from the same tuning and
host policy as the listener's, since inbound documents choose them.

BREAKING CHANGE: a controller VTA or trigger that sends
`push/provision` / `push/wake` over DIDComm without a document proof is
now refused with `proofRequired`. vta-service's `provision_gateway`
(trust_tasks/device.rs) and `trigger_gateway_wake`
(trust_tasks/step_up.rs) send them unsigned today and need to attach a
proof with the VTA's assertionMethod key (`attach_proof_in_place`) before
this ships. The HTTPS path is unchanged.

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): revert drift on a repository through git-ns/drift/resolve
body:
## What

The repository Drift card listed what the bridge reported but the only way to revert was "remove the role on the forge by hand". The VTC already serves `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1 (`vtc-service/src/git_ns/drift.rs`, #1703) and `cnm git drift resolve` already signs it. This PR adds the console action. No server change.

- **Revert action** (`repos/RepoDetail.tsx`): every drift item gets a **Revert to the VTC's state** button. It opens `RevertDriftDialog` (`repos/dialogs.tsx`), which shows the item, says what the bridge will do, and takes an optional reason. That builds `driftRevertTask` (`repos/actions.ts`):
  - payload `{ resource, action: "revert", drift: { type, account?, observed? }, reason? }`. The item is selected as the spec selects it: by `type`, by account (`forge` + `id`, with `login` for display) for the role types, and by the `observed` value read here. If the forge has changed since, the VTC refuses with `driftNotFound` instead of reverting a state nobody looked at.
  - command `cnm git drift resolve <resource> revert --type=… [--account-id=… --account-login=…] [--observed=…] [--reason=…]`, with every value quoted by the fish-safe `shellQuote` from #1723.
  - what the bridge does, per type: `roleAdded` removes the role (bridge job 0.2 `removeAccounts`), `roleRemoved`/`roleChanged` re-project roles, `requiredCheckMissing`/`protectionWeakened` re-apply the ruleset and required check, and `bootstrapMissing` re-runs the bootstrap plan.
- **Shown only to roles the VTC accepts** (`revertStanding` in `repos/model.ts`). It mirrors `drift_resolve` + `revert`:
  - the namespace is in bridge mode (manual mode answers `notRevertible`)
  - the repository is active or orphaned
  - the session's DID holds `git.repo.own` on the repository, explicitly (an owner) or implied (a namespace admin). A console key acts as that DID (`acting_as`).
  - a revert that weighs as revoking `own` (taking an `admin` role off an org repository) also needs a community administrator, as `consent_gate` requires under `elevated_requires_admin`. The console already assumes that setting is on for every elevated task.

  Anyone else sees why they can't revert, plus the `cnm` command to hand to an owner.
- **Consent mirror**: the server gates a revert as `consent_gate("right.revoke", impact)`, so `consentClass("drift.resolve", impact)` classes it the same way: elevated for `own`, normal otherwise. `projectedRight` and `driftRevertImpact` mirror `projected_right`, including personal accounts, where `write` is maintain and `admin` projects nothing.
- `useViewerDid()` (`lib/viewer.ts`) reads the session subject from the shell's whoami cache. It is the same observe-only query as `useIsSuperAdmin`.
- The `git-ns/drift/resolve/0.1` URI is added to `trust_task_manifest`'s `SIGNED_DOCUMENT_TYPES`, and the activity feed now names `gitNs.drift.resolved`.

Adopt is unchanged: it still builds a `right/grant`.

## Tests

- actions:
  - payload and command for a role item and for a ruleset item (no account)
  - elevated class for an `admin` role, normal for re-projection and on a personal account
  - shell safety for the resource, account id, login, observed and reason
- model:
  - `projectedRight` for org and personal accounts
  - `revertStanding` for owner, namespace admin, non-holder, unknown viewer, the elevated case, manual mode, and archived vs orphaned repositories
  - consent mirror
- RepoDetail:
  - an owner reverts through the form, and the sign dialog shows the exact command and document without sending anything
  - a non-holder, and a viewer with no whoami, get no button but do get the command
  - an `admin`-role revert is hidden from an owner who is not a community administrator, and shown to one who is, as elevated

`npx tsc -b --noEmit`, `npm run wire:check` and `npx vitest run` (400 tests) pass, as do `cargo test -p vtc-service --test trust_task_manifest` and `cargo fmt --check`.

## How to test (test guide ROLE-13)

1. Bridge-mode namespace, active repository. On the forge, weaken the ruleset or remove the required check, or add a collaborator role. Wait for the bridge to report drift.
2. Admin console → Repos → the repository. The Drift card lists the item.
3. Signed in as an owner or namespace admin: **Revert to the VTC's state** → optional reason → **Build the revert**. Sign in the browser (console key), or run the `cnm git drift resolve …` command shown.
4. The item leaves the outstanding drift (sync `pending`), the bridge re-applies the state, and the follow-up inspect returns it to `in sync`. `gitNs.drift.resolved` appears in the activity.
5. Signed in as an admin who holds no git right on the repository: no button. You see the reason and the command.

title: feat(tui): resolve drift from the Repos panel (revert or adopt)
body:
## What

On a repository screen the TUI listed drift but said "a namespace admin adopts or reverts drift from the admin console". An owner of the repository, or a namespace admin, can now resolve it in the panel (test guide **TUI-10**) with `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1, which the VTC already serves (VTI `vtc-service/src/git_ns/drift.rs`, #1703):

- **`v` revert**: the bridge re-applies what the community's rights call for, and no right changes. Per item type:
  - `roleAdded`: takes the unprojected forge role off
  - `roleRemoved` / `roleChanged`: re-projects roles
  - `requiredCheckMissing` / `protectionWeakened`: re-applies the ruleset and required check
  - `bootstrapMissing`: re-runs the bootstrap plan
- **`o` adopt (accept)**: records a role added or raised on the forge as the right it projects. On an organisation `admin` becomes owner and `maintain` becomes maintainer; on a personal account `write` becomes maintainer. The VTC records it as the resolver's own grant. Whether the account is linked to a member is the VTC's call (`accountNotLinked`).

### Selection and consent
- Drift rows now render after the people and take the highlight: ↓ past the last person reaches them, marked `▸`. An item is selected as the spec selects it: `type`, the account (`forge` + `id`, `login` for display) for role items, and the `observed` value read. If the forge has changed since, the VTC refuses with `driftNotFound` instead of acting on a state nobody looked at.
- Both keys arm a confirmation and send only on `y`. The consent class follows what the VTC gates each action as:
  - a revert is gated as the revocation it amounts to, which is elevated when it takes an owner-level (`admin`) role off
  - an adopt is gated as the grant it records

  When only a community administrator may do it (`elevated_requires_admin`), the confirmation says so.
- The actions are offered only to an owner or namespace admin (`governs`), and a revert only where the namespace has a bridge (manual mode would answer `notRevertible`). Each declared refusal code (`driftNotFound`, `notAdoptable`, `accountNotLinked`, `noMatchingRight`, `notRevertible`) gets an explanation with the key to try next.

### Code
- `openvtc-core::git_ns` gains `Request::DriftResolve`, `Reply::DriftResolved`, `DriftRef`, `DriftAction` and `DriftAccount`. It also gains `projected_right`, `adoptable_right`, `revert_weighs_as` and `has_bridge`, which mirror the VTC's `git_ns::drift::{projected_right, revert}`. The payload goes through the generated `drift::resolve::v0_1::Payload`, so the schema is checked before sending. An adopt without `observed` is refused locally.
- **Dependency**: `trust-tasks-rs` and `trust-tasks-capability-client` (and so `-didcomm`, `-https`, `-proof` and `-tsp`) move from 0.22.3 to 0.22.7. This is a patch on the same line, and the one the VTI workspace is on; 0.22.4 is the first to generate `git-ns/drift/*`. The `Cargo.toml` note is updated. `cargo tree -d -e normal,build,dev` still shows one `trust-tasks-rs`.

**No VTI crate release is needed**: nothing here depends on a new VTI crate. The community's VTC must be running a build with #1703 (`git-ns/drift/resolve`). An older one answers `unsupportedType`, and the panel already explains that.

## Tests

- core:
  - a drift item read as its selector
  - payload for a role revert (with a trimmed reason) and for a ruleset revert (no account, blank reason dropped)
  - an adopt without `observed` is refused before sending
  - projected, adoptable and weighted rights for organisation and personal accounts, plus the consent class
  - typed `DriftResolved` reply
  - every `drift/resolve` declared code is explained
- state:
  - the highlight runs from the people into the drift
  - a non-owner is refused
  - an owner arms a normal revert of a ruleset item, and adopt is refused for it
  - taking an `admin` role off is armed as elevated and names the community administrator
  - a `maintain` role adopts as maintainer, and `write` on an organisation adopts nothing
  - a manual namespace has no bridge to revert with
  - the reply reports success and triggers a fresh read
- keys: `v` / `o` are mapped on a repository and not on the list
- render: drift rows show the highlight and the `v revert drift   o adopt drift` hints, and no longer point at the admin console

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` pass locally.

## How to test (TUI-10)

1. Use a bridge-mode namespace with a repository you own (or a namespace you admin). On the forge, add a collaborator role or weaken the ruleset, and wait for the drift report.
2. Communities → the community → `r` → the repository. The *Drift from the forge* section lists the item.
3. Press ↓ past the people to highlight it, then `v`. The confirmation says what the bridge will do. Press `y`. The status reads "Reverted: …"; press `r` to see the item gone and, after the bridge's inspect, the repository back in sync.
4. For a role added on the forge whose account a member has linked, press `o` then `y`. The member now holds the projected right.
5. As a member who only commits there, `v` and `o` explain that it is an owner's decision.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): the send reuses the existing DIDComm path and its 30 s reply window
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): nothing is patched locally; the view is read again after the reply
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retry, and a timeout says to refresh before trying again
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): generated types from trust-tasks-rs 0.22.7
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): "Reverted" is said only on the VTC's response, and it says the bridge is re-applying, not that it is done
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): the VTC is the record; a lost reply times out and asks for a refresh
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(vgi-forge): review follow-ups for #84
body:
Follow-ups from the review of #84 (merged before these landed).

## Changes
- **EffectiveRights serde round trip (published crate).** Before this, serialisation wrote every held right, including the ones implication adds, and deserialisation ran `from_granted` over that list. So `[git.ns.admin]` came back as a value that projects `own`, i.e. repo `admin`.
  - It now serialises the canonical grants (`EffectiveRights::granted()`): `ns.admin`, or else `repo.create`, plus the highest repository right granted in its own name.
  - A round trip is now the identity. Equality holds exactly when the canonical grants are equal: `[ns.admin]` and `[ns.admin, own]` are different values.
  - **Wire change:** implied rights are no longer listed. For example, `[maintain]` now serialises as `["git.repo.maintain"]`.
- **Quoted `runs-on:`** in the Forgejo workflow, so labels such as `-`, `null`, `true`, `1` and `1.5` stay YAML strings.
- **Docs** (the `desired_roles` comment and BRIDGE.md §6c):
  - An account listed with no role loses *any* direct collaborator role, including one given by hand on the forge.
  - The namespace-admin guarantee only holds end to end once the VTC sends `git.ns.admin` for namespace admins. Today it sends them as `git.repo.own`; a VTI fix is in progress.

## Tests
- Serde round trips for `[]`, `[NsAdmin]`, `[NsAdmin, RepoOwn]`, `[NsAdmin, RepoMaintain]` and more.
- The runner label parses as a YAML string for tricky labels.
- A namespace admin's hand-given repo admin role is DELETEd by a projection.
- The Forgejo merge allow-list:
  - `maintain = "admin"`: admin, and on the list
  - `maintain = "write"`: write, and the list is not touched
  - default: write, and on the list

The Forgejo test bridge moved into `tests/common` so both test files can use it.

`cargo test --workspace`, clippy (`-D warnings`, all features) and fmt pass locally.

title: fix(vgi-bridge): guard identity mint --replace (review follow-ups for #85)
body:
Review follow-ups for #85. That PR merged before these fixes landed.

## Changes

1. **`identity mint --replace` is guarded.** Replacing the identity isn't a key rotation: the new DID is a different bridge. The guards apply to `mint --replace` and to an `identity import` of a *different* DID.
   - **Backup required.** `--backup <file>` must be given. The current identity's bundle is written there (0600, `O_EXCL`) before it is replaced, and the old DID is printed.
   - **Explicit confirmation.** The command refuses, and lists the namespaces (id, resource, state), while the store holds namespaces bound or being bound to the current DID. It also refuses when the current DID wasn't minted by the bridge (a VTA-provisioned `did:webvh`). `--abandon-current-did` overrides both.
   - **Consequences printed.** Every replace, and every refusal, says what a new DID breaks:
     - the VTC's `[git_ns] bridges` must change;
     - the VTC accepts a namespace's results and events only from the DID it bound;
     - the registry's `git.commit.sign` service grant is held by the old DID, so Dependabot commits the new one re-signs fail the check;
     - with no re-attach yet, re-binding needs an unbind, which revokes every right in the namespace.
   - **Mismatch error reordered.** Setting `mediator_did` back to the DID's mediator is now the first fix offered. It is the only one that keeps bound namespaces working.
2. **`identity export` writes the stored bundle verbatim.** An imported bundle's keys are all exported, including a P-256 key, which used to fail the export with a misleading error. A `did:key` seed is still exported as its two keys.
3. **No partial file after a failed export.** If writing or syncing the export fails, the partial file is removed, so a retry isn't refused over it.

Docs: BRIDGE.md §2 gets a paragraph on replacing the identity. The `mint --replace` references in BRIDGE.md, SETUP-GITHUB-VTC.md and RUNBOOK.md now include `--backup <file>`.

## Behaviour change (from #85, noted here)

`identity import`, and `run`, now refuse a `did:peer` whose document doesn't name the configured `mediator_did` as its `DIDCommMessaging` endpoint. A hand-made `did:peer` imported with an `https` endpoint, or with several services where the DIDComm one names another mediator, is refused. Before #85 it would have been accepted. `did:webvh` identities are not checked this way; their host publishes the document.

## Tests

- `run_refuses_a_did_peer_that_names_another_mediator`
- `export_refuses_to_write_through_a_symlink` (nothing is written to the link target)
- `a_did_peer_advertises_didcomm_through_its_mediator` now also checks that the resolved `keyAgreement` is the X25519 secret's id (`#key-2`) and that `assertionMethod` is `#key-1`, and that the mismatch error offers `mediator_did` first
- `mint_replace_refuses_while_namespaces_are_bound_to_the_did`: the refusal names the namespace, writes no backup and keeps the identity. With `--abandon-current-did` it replaces, and the backup holds the old DID.
- `a_vta_provisioned_did_exports_verbatim_and_is_not_replaced_unasked`: a did:webvh bundle with Ed25519, X25519 and P-256 keys exports byte-for-byte as imported, and replacing it needs the flag
- The existing CLI flow checks that `--backup` is required, that the consequences are printed, and that the backup restores the old DID through `import`.
