| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.22.3` → `0.22.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.22.3` → `0.22.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.22.3` → `0.22.4` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.20.4` → `0.20.5` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.2.5`) | `0.2.4` → `0.2.5` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.2.4` → `0.2.5` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(ui): the QR button reaches the DIDs drawn outside `Did`
body:
Follow-up to #275. That PR gave every DID drawn by the shared `Did` component a "Show QR code" button. About two dozen places draw a DID in their own markup, so they had no button. Each one someone would want to scan now has the same `DidQrButton` beside its text. None of them was converted to `Did`, so their appearance doesn't change.

## Now with the button

- **Consent window.** In `DidField`, beside Show full and Copy. That covers "Relying party" and "Sign in as / Acting as / Approving as".
- **Popup.**
  - The VTA line in the header.
  - The "advertises no transports" warning.
  - The vault entry's "acts as" DID.
- **Options and onboarding.**
  - The approver DID, beside Copy DID.
  - The newly onboarded holder DID.
  - The confirmed "Connecting to" DID.
- **Console.**
  - Persona cards and persona detail.
  - Disclosure history ("To" and "As").
  - Outdated disclosures.
  - The persona editor's DID.
  - A face's usage list.
  - A new room's identity.

## Deliberately left without one

- **`<select>` options** (the persona and host pickers). An option can't contain a button.
- **The retired holder DID** in the "Re-onboarding required" banner, and **the "Previously:" relying party** in the consent mismatch warning. A code there would invite someone to use a DID the screen is replacing or warning about.
- **The DID in the DIDs table's delete preview**, and **the trust graph's SVG labels**.

None of the new sites sits inside a `<button>`, `<a>` or `<label>`; each was checked before editing. `DidQrButton` already stops its clicks from reaching an enclosing clickable card or row.

## Testing

- **New render test:** it opens the code from one of these sites (a persona's DID in `FaceHistory`'s usage list) and checks the SVG encodes that DID.
- **Full suite:** `npm test` across all workspaces passes (1,655 tests), and `tsc -b` is clean.
- **Build:** `npm run build -w packages/extension` succeeds, and CI's eight bundle-confinement assertions pass locally.
- **Not done:** I haven't clicked through the unpacked extension in Chrome or scanned a code with a phone.

| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.20.3` → `0.20.4` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.2.4`) | `0.2.3` → `0.2.4` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.2.3` → `0.2.4` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: fix(git-ns/right/grant): publish the implied commit right of a namespace admin
body:
Follow-up to #621, which merged moments before this landed on its branch.

A namespace admin implies `git.repo.own` on every repository in the namespace, and so `git.commit.sign` on each. But the projection rule in `git-ns/right/grant` named only recorded `own` and `maintain` rights, so an admin's commits would fail every verify-trust check.

The rule now also publishes an admin's `git.commit.sign` on the namespace resource. A bridge that sets up a repository's check must configure the namespace as the check's fallback resource, so that record counts.

This changes spec prose only: no schema, example or generated-binding changes. `npm run validate` and `npm run check-bindings` pass.

title: feat(pnm): show the VTA's DID as a QR code with `pnm vta qr`
body:
`pnm vta qr` prints the active VTA's DID as a terminal QR code, for a phone (Keyring) to scan instead of retyping it. It's the pnm counterpart of the VTC landing-page QR code (#1698).

## Usage

```console
$ pnm vta qr                          # the default VTA's DID
$ pnm --vta work vta qr               # another configured VTA
$ pnm vta qr --did did:webvh:…        # any DID
$ pnm vta qr --out vta-did.svg        # also write the code as an SVG
```

It runs offline and reads the DID from this machine's config, so there's no connection or authentication. A VTA with no stored DID gets an error naming `pnm setup continue <slug>` and `--did`. A `--did` value that doesn't start with `did:` is refused.

## Choices

- **Bare DID.** The code carries the DID and nothing else, so it's safe on a shared screen. A DID is already a URI with scheme `did`, so there's no `did://` or app-specific wrapper, the same choice as #1698.
- **Dark on white, always.** Each line paints its own colours, black modules on bright white, because on a dark theme the terminal's defaults draw the code inverted and many phone cameras refuse an inverted code. The four-module quiet zone is part of the output.
- **Shared renderer.** `vta_cli_common::qr::{terminal_lines, svg}` holds the rendering, so `cnm` can adopt it without copying code. `qrcode` 0.14 is added with the `svg` feature only.
- **No PNG.** PNG output would need the `image` crate. SVG covers files.

## Testing

- `vta-cli-common` has three unit tests. One unpacks the half blocks back into a module grid and checks every module, quiet zone included, against the encoder's.
- `pnm-cli` has five unit tests: the CLI parse, the default VTA, a `--did` override with no config, a non-DID, and an unknown `--vta`.
- I ran `pnm vta qr --out …` against a real config. It drew the default VTA's DID and wrote the SVG. I didn't scan it with a phone.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast` was still running when this PR opened. I'll add the result as a comment.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): report forge status to the VTC in ext
body:
## What

The VTC's admin console (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1694) shows bridge-known status that the `git-ns/*` payloads don't carry. The VTC reads it from `payload.ext["org.openvtc.git-ns"]` of `git-ns/bridge/result` and `git-ns/bridge/event`, shaped `{"namespace": {...}, "repo": {...}}`. This PR makes the bridge send it.

Every result and event now carries the report whenever the bridge has something to say:

| `namespace` member | Source |
|---|---|
| `installationId` (string) | the binding's GitHub App installation id |
| `appName` | `[[github]].app_name` |
| `appSlug` | the registered App's slug |
| `appRegistration` | `registered` / `pending` (an open manifest link) / `unregistered` |
| `missingPermissions` (array, omitted when empty) | what the installation lacks (`name:level`, `event:<name>`) |
| `permissionUpgradePending` (bool) | something is missing, or the bridge-posted check is wanted but the installation isn't ready; omitted until probed |
| `orgRulesets` (bool) | org rulesets on the owner's plan, as probed; omitted until probed |
| `requiredWorkflow` (bool) | the adapter's capability in force |
| `bridgePostedCheck` (bool) | the adapter's capability in force (configured, installation ready, no required workflow) |

| `repo` member | Source |
|---|---|
| `guard` | the guard in force from the last inspection: `requiredWorkflow`, `codeOwnerReview`, `bridgePostedCheck`, `protectedFiles` (Forgejo), or `none` (a solo repository, or a guard whose source protection has drifted) |
| `lastCheck` | `{sha, conclusion, at}` for the last check the bridge posted |

## When it goes

- Every result gets the namespace report and, when the job reached a repository, the repo report. That covers bind, inspect, create, bootstrap, archive and projectRoles.
- Every event gets the namespace report, plus the repo report when it names a `forgeId` (for example `protectionChanged` or `repoRenamed`).
- Create and bootstrap read the repository back once they finish, so their result carries the guard they set up.
- After a check it posts on a managed repository, the bridge records it, inspects the repository, and sends a `protectionChanged` with the full drift and `lastCheck`. This is throttled to one per repository per minute, and a report that is waiting picks up the newest check.
- When an installation accepts new permissions, the bridge probes it again and now also refreshes its missing-permission list (`GitHubForge::detect_installation`).

## Framework rules

`ext` is the payload-level member from SPEC §4.5.1, which both generated payload types declare. It has reverse-DNS keys and at least one property, and it is signed with the rest of the payload. The payload with `ext` is checked against the generated type before it is sent. If it doesn't fit, it is dropped, but the document still goes. If there is nothing to report, `ext` is left out entirely, and a member the bridge doesn't know is never sent as `null`.

## Tests

The fake-VTC protocol tests check the report on each document type:
- inspect: exact `ext` on both the `protectionChanged` and the result, and a tampered `ext` fails the proof
- unprobed namespace: `permissionUpgradePending`, `orgRulesets` and `repo` are left out, with no nulls
- bind: `bindCompleted` and the result carry the installation, the missing events, org rulesets and the pending upgrade
- create: the result's `repo.guard`
- bridge-posted check: `protectionChanged` carries `lastCheck` and `guard`
- installation re-probe: the missing list is refreshed
- unit test: the guard mapping

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace` all pass locally.

title: feat(ui): every DID can be shown as a QR code for a phone to scan
body:
Every DID drawn by the shared `Did` component now has a small QR button after it. The button opens a popover with "Scan with Keyring", the QR code, the full DID and **Copy DID**, so a phone can take a DID by scanning instead of retyping it.

This is the wallet counterpart of the VTC landing-page QR code (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1698) and `pnm vta qr` (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1700). All three encode the bare DID, so one scanner reads them all.

## Where it appears

- **Through `Did`, `DidNamed` and `MailDid`**, about 32 places: the console panes, the Mediator Lens, setup/network, and disclosure consent.
- **The popup:** beside the VTA DID, the holder DID, and each configured VTA.
- **Not yet:** about 25 places draw a DID without `Did`, including `confirm.tsx`'s `DidField`, the persona screens, onboarding and the popup's warning banners. Moving them onto `Did` also changes how they look, and the consent window is a security prompt, so that's a follow-up rather than part of this.

## Decisions

- **A button beside the DID, not a click on it.** In the DIDs table and the lens, clicking a DID already opens its log or its mail, and the QR code mustn't take that over.
- **The bare DID, UTF-8 bytes, level M, four-module quiet zone.** A DID is already a URI with scheme `did`, so there's no `did://` or app wrapper.
- **Black on white in every theme.** This is the one colour literal outside `theme.ts`, and it's commented as such. A token would invert the code in dark mode, and many phone cameras refuse an inverted code.
- **The popover is portalled to `document.body`, and clicks stop at the component.** React bubbles a portal's events through the component tree, so without the stop, dismissing the popover also clicked the row behind it. A test pins this.
- **`qr={false}`** is for a DID inside another control, where a nested button is invalid: the DIDs table's open button and the did-create checkbox label. The DIDs table puts its QR button beside the open button instead.
- **`qrcode-generator` ^2.0.4** (MIT, no dependencies) builds the module grid. `did-qr.ts` turns it into one run-length SVG path. The QR code adds about 20 KB to the popup/options chunk and to `manager.js`.

## Testing

- `tests/did-qr.test.mts`:
  - A did:webvh is a version-5 code.
  - The path, repainted module by module, is exactly the library's grid inside the quiet zone, with no module drawn twice.
  - The finder patterns are in place.
  - Non-ASCII input is encoded as UTF-8.
- `tests/did-qr.render.test.mts`, in happy-dom:
  - The button opens the popover with the code and full DID, and Escape closes it.
  - Opening, and dismissing with an outside click, never reaches the enclosing row.
  - `qr={false}` inside a button renders no nested button.
- `npm test` across all workspaces passes (1,654 tests), and `tsc -b` is clean.
- `npm run build -w packages/extension` succeeds, and CI's bundle-confinement assertions pass locally:
  - The worker is a single bundle.
  - Admin, persona and mediator task URIs stay confined.
  - `manager.js` is a single bundle.
- **Not done:** I haven't loaded the unpacked extension in Chrome or scanned a code with a phone.

title: feat(persona): read one attribute by name, and call an arrangement a world
body:
Takes **vta-sdk 0.51**, which needed `did-git-sign` 0.4.13 first (OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#71): `vta-sdk` is 0.x, so a consumer on 0.51 beside a `did-git-sign` asking for `^0.50` held two copies, and `TrustTask<Value>` crosses between `openvtc` and `openvtc-core` — a build failure, not an untidy graph.

The workspace now holds **one** each of `vta-sdk`, `trust-tasks-rs`, `affinidi-messaging-sdk` and `affinidi-tdk`.

### `pool::reveal` reads one attribute

It was a `typePrefix` listing filtered here by id, because the family had no by-id read. To show one email address the agent decrypted **every** email address the holder has and sent them all, and its audit trail recorded a listing of the pool rather than a decision about one value.

`persona/attribute/get` is that read (spec dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#616). The claim type is gone from the signature — it existed only to build the prefix.

### A facet is a world

`persona/world/*`, `worldId`, and the Rust types to match. The screen has said "world" since the Worlds tab existed; `face` and `facet` share a stem while naming different things, and code saying one word while the UI says another is the collision the rename exists to end.

The retired `persona/facet/*` spellings still answer for a release, so this could have waited — but the alias window is for moving, not for staying.

### A face made in a context claims no provenance

The SDK's `LocalInlineValue` has no `provenance` member, because the schema has none and refuses one. This code sent it, and every "make a face here" write was refused at the agent; now it does not compile. Same defect as OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#271 and VTI#1676.

CI set run locally: fmt, both clippy runs, doc, tests with `--include-ignored` (1518), `--no-default-features` (1499), `-p openvtc --features dev-overrides` (682), bench build.

title: feat(vtc): show the community DID as a QR code on the landing page
body: A wallet (Keyring first) can now add a community by scanning its DID off the default landing page instead of retyping it. This is the "VTC landing page" row of the Keyring QR proposal: public, carries nothing secret. ## What changes - **`GET /v1/community/did-qr.svg`**: new public, unauthenticated route (classified in `PUBLIC_UNGOVERNED` beside `public-profile`). It renders the profile's `communityDid` as a black-on-white SVG QR code (ECC level M, 4-module quiet zone) and returns 404 until the profile is initialised. The response carries `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'` and `nosniff`. - **Landing page (`website-default/`)**: a pass card in the hero shows the QR code, "Scan with Keyring", and the DID with Copy. The Community DID row moves out of the Daemon card into it. - The code stays hidden until it loads, so there is no broken image before setup. - It stays dark on white in the dark theme, because inverted codes fail on many scanners. - On a touch device the caption says to copy the DID instead, since a phone can't scan its own screen. - The DID text now comes from `public-profile`, the same source as the QR, so the two can't disagree. `/health` covers only the window before the profile exists. - **Docs**: `docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md` covers the endpoint, including how an operator site under `website.root_dir` can show the same code with one `` tag. - **Dependency**: `qrcode` 0.14, `svg` feature only (MIT/Apache, no extra dependencies). - `admin-ui/openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are regenerated for the new documented route. ## What the QR carries The bare DID, exactly what Copy copies. A DID is already a URI with scheme `did`, so there is no `did://` or app-specific wrapper. A phone's camera hands the scan to whichever app registers the `did` scheme. Signalling intent to a wallet ("join this community") is still the open "format to agree" item in the Keyring proposal, and a bare DID can't conflict with whatever format that becomes. ## Testing - `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: no failures, including `openapi_snapshot`, `openapi_response_census` and the unauthenticated-route classification test. Two new unit tests cover the renderer. - `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `npm run wire:check`: clean. - Previewed the new page files in Chrome against a running VTC's `/health` and `public-profile`, with the QR rendered by the same `qrcode` code. The stacked phone layout was not checked in a browser, and the code was not scanned with a phone.

title: feat(vtc): the admin console signs its Trust Task documents
body:
Client side of #1684, against the design note merged in #1685 (Option A) and
the server half merged in #1692. The admin console had **no signing primitive
at all** — no `eddsa-jcs-2022`, no Ed25519, no `crypto.subtle.sign` — and that
is the single reason every bearer route #1641 would retire is still mounted
(#1681 §"the bearer routes stay"). It has one now.

## The key, and the flag

```ts
const kp = await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: "Ed25519" }, false, ["sign", "verify"]);
```

**The `false` is load-bearing and is not a typo to tidy up.** It governs the
*private* key only; WebCrypto sets `publicKey.[[extractable]]` unconditionally
for a generated pair, so `exportKey("raw", publicKey)` still returns the 32
bytes needed to derive `did:key:z6Mk…`, while `true` would hand the private
half to any script in the origin. That is exactly the defect found in
`did-hosting-ui/lib/session-key.ts` — the file this design says to lift — and
fixed in affinidi-webvh-service#210. So the reason is stated in the code, and
`console-key.test.ts` asserts `privateKey.extractable === false` *and* that
`exportKey("pkcs8"|"jwk", privateKey)` throws, so it cannot quietly flip back.

The `CryptoKey` objects go into IndexedDB as objects, never as bytes; the
structured-clone round trip preserves non-extractability. Where IndexedDB is
unavailable (a private window, an embedded webview, jsdom) the fallback is an
in-memory record that loses the key on reload — the honest degradation, since
nothing writes key material anywhere weaker.

## What is signed, and where

One seam, `src/lib/api.ts::postSignedTrustTask`, as #1692 asked and as
`pnm-browser-plugin` does it (signing belongs to the channel, not to 116 call
sites). It builds `{id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, payload}`, attaches
the proof, and POSTs to `/v1/trust-tasks`.

```
hashData   = SHA-256(JCS(proofConfig)) || SHA-256(JCS(document minus "proof"))
signature  = Ed25519(hashData)                    // via crypto.subtle.sign
proofValue = "z" + base58btc(signature)
```

`issuer` is the **console key's own `did:key`**, not the operator's admin DID:
SPEC §4.7 binds the proof to the in-band issuer, and the delegation is resolved
server-side from the signer. `created` is back-dated 60 s, matching the plugin.

**Lifted**: the JCS canonicaliser and base58btc, near-verbatim from
`pnm-browser-plugin`'s `packages/core/src/trust-tasks/canonical.ts` and
`did-hosting-ui/lib/session-key.ts` (the same code in both). **Written**:
everything around them — the custody, the enrolment, the seam, the fallback,
and the timestamp rule below. Zero new dependencies; the CSP stays
`script-src 'self'`.

### The bug the Rust fixture caught

**Timestamps go out at whole-second precision, and that is not cosmetic.** The
VTC does not verify the proof over the bytes it received: it parses them into a
`trust_tasks_rs::TrustTask`, strips `proof`, and re-serialises *that*.
`issuedAt` is a `chrono::DateTime<Utc>`, whose serde writes `SecondsFormat::
AutoSi` — **no** fractional digits when the sub-second part is zero.
`Date.prototype.toISOString()` always writes three.

So a document stamped on a whole second went out as `…:00.000Z`, came back from
the parser as `…:00Z`, canonicalised to different bytes, and the proof failed —
while every other document that second verified. One request in a thousand,
never reproducible, and indistinguishable at the client from a revoked
delegation. The first run of `vtc-service/tests/console_signed_document.rs`
failed on exactly this. Nothing on the TypeScript side could have found it,
which is the argument for the fixture.

## Does a signed document verify against the real service?

**Yes.** `vtc-service/tests/console_signed_document.rs` verifies a document
produced by `admin-ui/src/lib/console-key.ts` through
`vta_sdk::trust_task_proof::verify_trust_task_proof` — the `did:key`-only
verifier `POST /v1/trust-tasks` reaches via
`trust_tasks/helpers.rs::verify_trust_task_proof`. Three tests: it verifies,
the proven signer is the document's `issuer` (SPEC §4.7), and tampering with
either the payload or the `recipient` breaks it. Regenerate the fixture with
`cd vtc-service/admin-ui && npx vite-node scripts/write-rust-fixture.ts`.

## Which calls now sign

| call | task | door |
|---|---|---|
| member credentials | `vtc/members/credentials/0.1` | **signed**, bearer fallback |
| admin-remove | `vtc/members/admin-remove/0.1` | **signed**, bearer fallback |
| purge | `vtc/members/purge/0.1` | **signed**, bearer fallback |

That is three of the four #1681 tasks. The fourth, `vtc/members/update/0.1`, is
**not reachable from any console screen** — the Members panel promotes through
`acl/change-role` and has no metadata editor — so there is nothing to move.

### The 64 KiB verdict for `members/update`

Checked rather than assumed, as #1684 asks. `UNAUTH_BODY_SIZE = 64 * 1024`
(65536 bytes, `DefaultBodyLimit` on the governed chain, a 413 refusal not a
truncation); `MEMBER_EXTENSIONS_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024` (16384 bytes, measured
on `serde_json::to_vec(&extensions)`). `extensions` is embedded as JSON in the
payload rather than as a string, so nothing is re-escaped and the bag costs its
own size. A document carrying a maximal bag, a 256-character label and every
other optional member comes to **under 18 KiB** — roughly 47 KiB of headroom.
Pinned by a test in `console-key.test.ts` so a later field addition has to
re-do the sum rather than discover it.

## Everything else still uses a bearer route, and why

No bearer route is retired in this PR. Beyond the three above, every console
call still uses one, for three distinct reasons:

1. **No signed door exists yet.** The rest of #1641's 49 are still on the
   bearer surface; each needs its own `DISPATCHED_URIS` binding in a #1641
   batch. This PR unblocks them but does not do them.
2. **A signed document cannot spend a step-up.** `admin_signer` builds claims
   with `session_id: ""`, so `require_fresh_step_up` always fails on that door.
   Anything gated on a live passkey gesture — `acl/grant`, `acl/change-role`,
   console-key enrolment itself — must stay on the session-bearing path until
   that interaction is designed. Worth stating as a design fact, not an
   oversight: the design note (§6f) wants the step-up to stay exactly where
   #1658 put it.
3. **Three routes have no published task at all** — `/v1/admin/console-keys`
   itself, which is why it uses the `*Exempt` helpers.

**Before the bearer routes can be retired**, in order: (a) this ships and
operators enrol; (b) `vtc-client` gets the same path for the three of the four
it reaches (it has `vta_sdk::trust_task_sign` already, so it is small); (c) the
step-up-over-signed-documents question above is answered for the verbs that
need one; (d) then the routes, their OpenAPI entries and the transitional
descriptions come out and `openapi.json` + `wire.ts` regenerate.

## Fallback behaviour

`signedOrBearer(typeUri, payload, bearer)` catches `SigningUnavailableError`
and **nothing else**. Two causes produce it: no WebCrypto Ed25519 (below Chrome
137 / Firefox 130 / Safari 17, detected by an actual `generateKey` since
nothing advertises the curve synchronously), or no key enrolled in this
browser. Both fall through to the existing call, unchanged.

A signed call that is *refused* propagates. Retrying it over a bearer token
would use the session as the authority the signed door exists to stop relying
on, and would hide a revocation from the operator who just performed it.

## The Signing keys screen

Beside **My passkeys**, because it is the same kind of thing. Lists the
caller's keys with the server's own `active` (not re-derived — the two
disagreeing is how a page shows a key as working after it stopped), marks the
row this browser holds, labels a new one, and revokes. Revoking this browser's
own key also forgets the local copy, so it cannot sit there signing documents
the daemon refuses. It handles: already enrolled, a browser with no key yet, a
browser whose key was revoked (a fresh one is generated — a revoked console DID
is tombstoned and can never be re-enrolled), a refused passkey, and a browser
that cannot sign at all.

## One finding, deliberately not fixed here

#1692 introduced an OpenAPI **schema-name collision**. utoipa keys
`components.schemas` by the bare Rust type name, and `routes/admin/
console_keys.rs` declares `ListResponse` and `RevokeResponse` — names already
used by `routes/admin/passkeys.rs` and by four other routes. The console-key
shapes won, so the published document now has `GET /v1/admin/passkeys` pointing
at a schema describing `{consoleKeys}`. Nothing noticed because
`myPasskeys.tsx` carries a local interface.

The fix is `#[schema(as = ConsoleKeyListResponse)]` / `…RevokeResponse` plus a
regenerate, and it is server-side, so it is not smuggled into a console PR.
`wire-types.ts` records it where the stale `PasskeyListResponse` alias was, and
`console-keys-api.ts` deliberately does not read the revoke response body. The
`RevokeResponse` collision predates #1692.

## Tests

`npm run lint` (wire:check + tsc) passes — `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are
untouched, which is the check that this PR only consumes the API.
`npx vitest run`: **222 passed, 27 files**, of which 50 across five new files are new. They assert on
the document that would go on the wire, not on "we called fetch": the envelope
member by member, the proof's six members, and an independent recomputation of
`hashData` from the serialised document verified against the public key.

Covered: the private key does not export while the public key does; the derived
`did:key` *is* the public key; a page reload restores the same key still
non-extractable; the JCS rules the signature rests on (key order, presence
sensitivity, non-ASCII); whole-second timestamps; the signature verifies; the
fallback on both causes; the non-fallback on refusal; enrolment order (gesture
before write) and that a refused passkey writes nothing; revocation with and
without the local key; and the screen's states, including that a successful
enrolment updates it without a reload (checked to fail without the fix, so it
is not a vacuous assertion).

`cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`, run without
`VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD` so the admin UI builds as part of it and
`openapi_snapshot` would catch an unintended API change.

That run found one thing, in a second commit. `trust_task_manifest.rs::
every_admin_ui_task_is_enforced_by_a_route` scans **every** file under
`admin-ui/src` — tests included — and treats each spec URI as a `Trust-Task`
header the console sends. `signed-door.test.ts` mocks the daemon's *error*
document, whose type is `trust-task-error/0.5`: a framework type no route
binds and no client ever sends. The guard called it a dead page. The scan now
skips `*.test.ts(x)`, which is the rule `collect_prefixed_in_file` already
records for the other side of the same comparison — a URI in a fixture is not
wiring — and it still fails on an orphan added to a non-test file, checked
rather than assumed.
`cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
are clean; the only Rust in this PR is the new test and its fixture.

Refs #1684, #1641.

title: chore(deps)!: messaging-sdk 0.27.1 + trust-tasks-rs 0.22.3; answer a mutual TSP cancel the SDK could not (Keyring VTI-38)
body:
## What

Moves VTI onto **affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.27.1** and **trust-tasks-rs 0.22.3**, with exactly one copy of each in the graph. Also adapts the TSP control path to the SDK's new meaning of `reply_expected`, which is what closes **Keyring VTI-38** (mutual TSP cancellation left unanswered) on the VTI side.

#1690 already moved main to trust-tasks 0.22.1 / SDK 0.27.0 / tdk 0.17 / test-mediator 0.10 / mediator-admin 0.2. This PR raises the floors and makes the SDK pin structural:

| Crate | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `affinidi-messaging-sdk` | `0.27.0` (five per-crate literals) | `0.27.1` (**workspace table**, floor) |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | 0.22.1 | **0.22.3** (floor: first release with the `git-ns` family, `trust_tasks_rs::specs::git_ns`) |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | 0.22 | 0.22.3 (floor) |
| `trust-tasks-{https,tsp,capability-client,didcomm}` | 0.22.x | resolve to 0.22.3 |

No `version =` field of a workspace crate is touched; release-plz owns those.

### Why the others have to move with it

`trust_tasks_rs` types cross the public API of six upstream crates: `affinidi-messaging-sdk` (`MediatorAcl` among them), `affinidi-messaging-mediator` (via test-mediator), `affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin`, and `trust-tasks-{proof,https,tsp,capability-client}`. If any one of them stays on its 0.21-line release, the graph holds two `trust-tasks-rs` and fails with `expected X, found a different X`. `mediator-admin`/`-tui` 0.1 and `test-mediator` 0.9 were the non-obvious ones: 0.1 still pinned SDK 0.26 and 0.9 pulled mediator 0.26.

### The SDK pin moves into the workspace table

`affinidi-messaging-sdk` was a hand-written literal in `vta-sdk`, `vta-service`, `vti-common`, `room-host` and `tests/e2e`. A literal that falls behind the others still resolves, so nothing catches it until `affinidi-tdk` moves a minor and the graph splits. It is now one workspace entry, `{ version = "0.27.1", default-features = false }`. Members inherit it and add their own features. `tests/e2e` asks for `default` explicitly, so its feature set is the same as before.

## Breaking changes adapted to

1. **affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.27.1: `reply_expected` has a new meaning** (tdk #887, Keyring VTI-38). `TspOps::record_incoming_control` now sends the §7.3 answer to a mutual cancellation itself. `reply_expected` (and `InboundKind::RelationshipControl::reply_expected`) now means *the answer is still owed*: it is `true` only when the SDK's own send failed. For a cancellation, `thread_digest` is now the relationship digest the peer named.
   - Before this PR, when `decide_control` returned `ControlDecision::Cancel`, the VTA's and VTC's `handle_tsp_control` called `cancel_relationship`. By then the relationship is already `None`, so that call refuses `SendCancel` out of `None`. That refusal is the VTI-38 failure itself, and it was still reachable on the retry path.
   - Both now call **`TspOps::answer_cancellation(profile, sender_vid, thread_digest)`**, which sends without running the state machine. `vta-service/src/messaging/{service.rs,tsp_inbound.rs}` and `vtc-service/src/messaging.rs` are updated, including the `ControlDecision::Cancel` docs and the §7.3 comments.
   - `decide_control` is unchanged. Its unit tests (VTA + VTC) are renamed and re-documented for the new semantics: `false` now also covers "already answered", and answering then would send twice. title: feat(vgi-bridge): re-sign Dependabot pull requests on push provenance
body:
## What

The GitHub bridge re-signs Dependabot pull requests with its own DID, so they pass the commit-trust check without a human step (design §9, "Dependabot re-sign bot"). Since #68, verify-trust exempts a `web-flow`-signed commit only when it is a clean merge, so Dependabot's single-parent commits fail as `platformSignedEdit`.

The bridge decides from **signed `push` webhooks, never from commit authorship.** Any writer can get GitHub to write and sign a commit with `author: dependabot[bot]` through the Contents API.

### Provenance ledger
- The App now subscribes to `push`. It's delivered under Contents, which the App already has, so no new permission. Every verified push to a `dependabot/*` branch is recorded in a new `branches` table: before, after, sender login and numeric id, the `created`/`forced` flags, and the delivery id. Deleting a branch clears its record. A creation starts it again.
- A branch is **clean** up to head `H` when both hold:
  - walking back from `H` through the recorded `after → before` links reaches a creation by Dependabot, with no gap;
  - every recorded push came from `dependabot[bot]` (login **and** id: `dependabot_login` / `dependabot_id`, default id 49699333), or is a push the bridge recorded as its own (exact before/after) before sending it.

  A foreign push, a gap (the bridge was down), a missing creation or an overflow each mean not clean. GitHub doesn't guarantee delivery order, so the chain is rebuilt from before/after.

### Trigger
- Runs on `pull_request` opened / synchronize / reopened. It also runs when a push arrives for a branch whose pull request it has already seen, because the PR delivery can come before the push.
- Everything is re-read from `GET /pulls/{n}`. The PR must be open and opened by Dependabot (login and id). Its head must be a `dependabot/*` branch in the **same repository**, and its base must be the default branch.
- The namespace must have `resign_dependabot` on (`[github.namespaces.<owner>]`, default true) and a platform keyring configured. With no keyring, nothing is re-signed.

### Re-sign
- Each commit in `base...head` must meet all of these, or nothing is re-signed:
  - one parent, continuing the range;
  - only the standard headers;
  - a `web-flow` PGP signature that verifies against the configured keyring (verify-trust's `ExemptKeyring`);
  - Dependabot's noreply author.
- Each new commit keeps the **same tree** and the author line byte for byte. The committer is the bridge (`[resign] committer_name/email`, dated now). The message gets a `Signed-by-DID: <bridge DID>#<key>` trailer. The commit is signed with an sshsig (namespace `git`) made with vgi-core's encoder and the bridge's Ed25519 DID key, the same key that signs its Trust Task documents. The first new commit keeps the original base parent.
- The trailer is placed by `git interpret-trailers --if-exists doNothing`, as did-git-sign's hook does, **plus `--no-divider`**. Dependabot messages contain a `---` line (the `updated-dependencies` YAML), and without that flag git inserts the trailer *above* it, where the `git log`-style reader verify-trust uses doesn't look. Before signing, the result is read back with vgi-core's `signer_did` / `conflicting_signer_dids`.
- The push is `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<old head>` with a contents:write token for that one repository. It goes over the same hardened git as the check: cleared env, no config, hooks at `/dev/null`, https only, token in `http.extraHeader` from the environment. The push is recorded in the ledger as the bridge's own before it's sent.
- **Idempotent:** Ed25519 is deterministic, so a head whose commits already carry the bridge's signature is detected exactly and left alone.
- A failing check on a Dependabot PR now says in its summary whether the bridge is re-signing it. If it isn't, the summary gives the reason and what a maintainer can do: re-sign per runbook §5, or have Dependabot start the branch over.

### Fetching and pushing without the blobs
The check's `tree:0` clone can't be pushed from, because git walks the trees it must not send. The re-sign fetches with `blob:none` at depth n+1. Before pushing, it lists the objects git will want to send (`rev-list --objects --missing=print new ^old`) and fetches those blobs by id, bounded. In practice that's the files the change touched. It then pushes with `--no-thin`: a thin pack would use blobs the clone doesn't hold as delta bases.

### VTC side
The re-signed commits pass only if the VTC grants the bridge DID `git.commit.sign` on the namespace. That grant is being added to vtc-service separately; this PR documents it in BRIDGE.md §6a. The bridge queries the registry at start, and two minutes after a bind, and logs a warning if the grant is missing. The query goes through a new `CommitVerifier::commit_sign_granted`, using TRQP via trql-client. The DID document has to publish the signing key as a verification method (`publicKeyMultibase`). `did:key` always does, and a VTA-provisioned `did:webvh` does for the key in its bundle. This is documented.

## Tests
- **Ledger (unit):** a clean branch, including out-of-order arrival; a foreign push fails even when it's later overwritten; a matching login with the wrong id fails; a gap, a missing creation, a creation by someone else and an overflow each fail; the bridge's own push is accepted only for its exact before/after.
- **End to end:** mock GitHub via wiremock, plus a local repository standing in for the remote that is fetched from and force-pushed to.
  - A Dependabot PR with two web-flow-signed commits (PGP fixture as in the verify-trust e2e) is re-signed. The trees and author lines are unchanged, the committer and trailer are the bridge's, the trailer is the final trailer after the `---` block, and parents chain from the base.
  - The **real `VerifyTrustVerifier`**, with a stub registry granting the bridge DID on the namespace, returns `trusted` for both new commits. The originals fail.
  - A second run after the bridge's own push webhook skips with "already re-signed".
  - The PR webhook arrives before the pushes: the check fails with the hint, then the late pushes resume the re-sign.
  - If the head moves after GitHub reports it, force-with-lease refuses the push (`stale info`) and the branch keeps what landed.
  - Nothing is re-signed for: a non-Dependabot author, or `dependabot[bot]` with the wrong id; a foreign pusher; a missed push; no keyring; a commit whose platform signature doesn't verify; a namespace with the re-sign off.
  - Pushes to other branches aren't recorded. A repeat delivery changes nothing, a deletion clears the record, and an unsigned push is refused with 401.
- **Adapter:** `push` in the manifest events; `parse_push`, including forged and malformed deliveries; PR authorship and head repo; the push token is exactly contents:write on one repository.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace` all pass locally.

## Open / assumed
- **Checked against GitHub:** `dependabot[bot]` is user id 49699333, type `Bot` (`GET /users/dependabot[bot]`). That id and login also appear as `user` on this repo's Dependabot PRs and as the actor on Dependabot `PushEvent`/`CreateEvent`s in the repo's Events API. The shape of a push for a new branch (`before` all zeros, `created: true`, `sender{login,id}`) comes from octokit/webhooks' captured examples.
- **Assumed:** that the webhook `push` for Dependabot's *branch creation* is delivered with `sender = dependabot[bot]`. I found no captured Dependabot push payload, and the Events API shows the creation only as a `CreateEvent`. If GitHub reported another sender, branches would never be clean, which fails safe.
- **Upgrade:** Apps registered before this change must subscribe to `push` by hand (BRIDGE.md §3). Branches created before that have no record of their creation and are never re-signed.
- `@dependabot recreate` after a foreign push only helps if Dependabot re-creates the branch. A force-push keeps the foreign push in the record. The hint says so.
- did-git-sign's hook had the same `---` trailer placement problem; #72 (now on main) fixed it separately.


## Review follow-ups (b52403f, rebased on main)
- **Workflow changes are never re-signed.** A commit that changes anything under `.github/workflows/` stops the re-sign. Changed paths come from `diff-tree` over the fetched trees; if they cannot be read, nothing is re-signed. The App gets no `workflows` permission. The check tells the maintainer to re-sign by hand (runbook §5).
- **Missed own push.** If the bridge missed the webhook for its own push, the chain walk still steps through its own push record, on an exact before/after match only. A later Dependabot force-push is then still clean.
- **Bounds.** At most 64 branches are tracked per repository; the oldest untouched is evicted, and an evicted branch is never clean. Re-signs run under a `checks.concurrency` semaphore.
- **Replays.** The bridge uses the signed `repository.pushed_at`: it does not record a delivery older than 6 days. Only a delivery at least as new as every recorded one may reset or clear a ledger.
- **Nits:** ledgers record when they were last touched, hints get the real protected branch, and `forced` is no longer stored. A foreign `Signed-by-DID` trailer is now a skip rather than an error.
- **New tests:** fork head, non-default base, two parents, extra headers, foreign trailer, late creation or deletion after a foreign push, replay window, missed own push followed by a Dependabot rebase, the workflow exclusion and its hint, and the branch cap.

title: fix(did-git-sign): write Signed-by-DID into the final trailer block past `---` lines
body:
## Problem

did-git-sign's `commit-msg` hook added the `Signed-by-DID:` trailer with `git interpret-trailers` in its default mode. In that mode a `---` line counts as the start of a patch, so the trailer went into the paragraph above it. A commit message has no patch. `git log --format='%(trailers)'` and verify-trust (vgi-core `signer_did`) both read the message's final paragraph and treat `---` lines as ordinary text. So on any message with a `---` line (every Dependabot commit, and some templates):

- the claim was never read, and the commit failed `noSignerDid`; or
- if the final paragraph already held a `Signed-by-DID`, that stale claim was verified instead of the one the hook wrote.

Reproduced before the fix. On the Dependabot-shaped message, `git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Signed-by-DID)'` printed nothing, and the new tests failed.

A second problem showed up in the new differential test. `--if-exists doNothing` matches trailer keys **by prefix**. A final block containing `Signed-by: ...` or `S: ...` counted as an existing claim, so the hook wrote none.

## Fix

- The hook passes `--no-divider` to every `interpret-trailers` call. The flag exists since git 2.20 (backported to 2.19.2), below the repo's git >= 2.40 floor.
- The hook checks for an existing claim using the exact key (`interpret-trailers --parse --no-divider`, then a case-insensitive `^Signed-by-DID:`). It only adds a trailer when there is none, using `--where end --if-exists add`. An existing `Signed-by-DID` trailer in the final block is still kept, so amend and rebase behave as before.
- vgi-core's parser needed no change: it already follows git's commit view, which ignores dividers. The differential test now also covers `---` shapes and confirms this.

## Existing installs

Hooks are only replaced when the user re-runs `init`. The hook now carries a `# did-git-sign-hook-version: 2` line. `did-git-sign health` finds the commit-msg hook git will actually run (`git rev-parse --git-path hooks/commit-msg`, which follows `core.hooksPath`; outside a repo it uses the global `core.hooksPath`). It reports the hook as one of:

- `OK`
- `OUTDATED`, with a prompt to re-run `did-git-sign init`
- `NEWER`
- `NOT did-git-sign`
- `MISSING`

A hook with no version line is v1. This is documented in the crate README (new "Upgrading" section) and in the RUNBOOK (setup section and the `noSignerDid` row).

## Tests

- `did-git-sign` unit tests run `git commit` through the real hook on these messages: Dependabot-style, `---` followed by a diff body, a trailing `---`, an existing claim past a divider, and prefix keys (`Signed-by:`, `S:`, `Signed-by-DIDX:`). In each case both git's trailer view and `vgi_core::signer_did` must name the DID. The divider and prefix tests fail on the old hook. There are also tests for the hook-version classification and a `core.hooksPath` lookup test.
- New `crates/did-git-sign/tests/hook_trailer_differential.rs` runs the real hook script, after `git stripspace --strip-comments`, over fixed and proptest-generated messages that include `---` lines. It requires vgi-core and `git log %(trailers)` to agree on the claim. When the message had no claim, the claim must be the hook's own.
- `vgi-core` `trailer_differential`: adds `---` fixed cases and generated divider lines. The `interpret-trailers` oracle is now `--parse --no-divider`, the view that matches a commit object.
- `verify-trust`: a claim above `---` gives `NoSignerDid`, and a claim at the end gives `Valid`.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace --all-targets` (MSRV) all pass locally.

The Cargo.lock diff adds `proptest` as a dev-dependency of did-git-sign, and nothing else.

title: chore(deps): vta-sdk 0.51, and 0.4.13 to carry it
body:
A **follow, not a choice** — the sixth time, and the note beside the pin has been counting them: this crate is the reason OpenVTC cannot move.

`vta-sdk` is 0.x, so `"0.50"` excludes 0.51. A consumer that takes 0.51 while `did-git-sign` asks for 0.50 gets two copies of `vta-sdk` in its graph, and they do not unify — the workspace stops building. That is exactly where OpenVTC is now:

```
error[E0308]: mismatched types
  expected `TrustTask<Value>`, found a different `TrustTask<Value>`
  note: there are multiple different versions of crate `trust_tasks_rs`
```

**Nothing here needs 0.51.** This crate reaches the VTA through `connect_auto` and takes display names; 0.51's changes are all in the persona family — `persona/facet/*` renamed to `persona/world/*`, `correlation/analyze` 1.1, and a new `persona/attribute/get`. No API this crate touches moved, and there is no source change in this PR.

Version 0.4.12 → **0.4.13**, a patch, following what the last five of these took (0.4.11 took `vta-sdk ^0.39`, 0.4.12 took `^0.42`).

Ran locally: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (440), and `cargo test -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass` (73). All pass.

Once this is tagged and published, OpenVTC can take `vta-sdk` 0.51 and drop the workaround that reads one attribute by listing every attribute sharing its type prefix.

body:
Takes the latest TSP fixes on the messaging line the VTI stack is built on:

| Crate | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| `affinidi-messaging-sdk` | 0.26.22 | 0.26.27 |
| `trust-tasks-rs` / `-proof` / `-capability-client` | 0.21.18 | 0.21.21 |
| `affinidi-messaging-core` | 0.1.9 | 0.1.10 |
| `affinidi-messaging-mediator-common` | 0.16.21 | 0.16.23 |
| `affinidi-messaging-mediator` (dev, via test-mediator) | 0.28.32 | 0.28.36 |
| `affinidi-messaging-test-mediator` (dev) | 0.9.13 | 0.9.17 |

Unchanged: `vta-sdk` 0.49.0, `vta-service` 0.39.0, `affinidi-tdk` 0.16.0, `affinidi-tsp` 0.2.1.

**Why.** Two TSP fixes, both from Keyring findings:
- 0.26.26 (VTI-39): `TspOps::send_raw` made one attempt, so a keep-alive connection closed under it (ngrok, a load balancer) lost the message silently. It now re-POSTs the identical bytes up to twice when no HTTP answer came back; the mediator's hash-keyed store makes that idempotent.
- 0.26.27 (VTI-41): a TSP relationship across two mediators never completed, because the peer's accept was refused with a 403 at its own mediator. The profile's mediator is now put in front of such a route, and `send_control` routes via a known foreign peer mediator.

**Why not 0.27 / TDK 0.17 / trust-tasks 0.22.** Every published `vta-sdk`, 0.50 included, still declares `affinidi-messaging-sdk ^0.26.12` and `trust-tasks-rs ^0.21`. Taking 0.27 would put a second messaging sdk and a second `trust-tasks-rs` in the graph. It moves when `vta-sdk` does. Nothing here needs porting for 0.27.1's cancellation change: `record_incoming_control` answering a mutual cancel only matters to a consumer that answers `reply_expected` itself, and this repo answers no relationship control yet (`dispatch_inbound` records and drops; WS5).

**Second `vta-sdk` 0.42.1: still present, and it predates this PR.** `did-git-sign` 0.4.12 (latest release) requires `^0.42`. VGI main is already on `vta-sdk 0.50` (VGI #63) but has not published it. `cargo tree -d -e normal,build,dev --all-features` shows no other stack duplicate: 0.42.1 resolves onto the same messaging sdk, messaging-core, trust-tasks and dtg-credentials. The root manifest's `did-git-sign` note said this was closed, which stopped being true at #369; this PR corrects it.

**Source changes:** none. Manifest floors move to `affinidi-messaging-sdk = "0.26.27"` and `trust-tasks-rs = "0.21.20"` (what sdk 0.26.25+ declares). The pin commentary in `Cargo.toml` and `openvtc-core/Cargo.toml` is updated to match. The lockfile moves only through targeted `cargo update -p`.

**Verification** (locally, after rebasing on #375):
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets --all-features`: ok
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`: 1498 passed, 0 failed, 19 ignored. After the rebase, `cargo test -p openvtc --bin openvtc`: 683 passed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`: clean

### Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide.md §9)
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): N/A, no source change. The sdk adds a 30 s per-request timeout on TSP sends
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): N/A, no source change
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): N/A
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): the new sdk retry is bounded (2 retries, 100/400 ms), on identical bytes, and idempotent at the mediator
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): N/A
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): N/A
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): N/A, no wire type change on this line
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed (R5.*): N/A
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): N/A
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): N/A, no mutation touched
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: vta-service-v0.41.0
body:
### Added

- **persona**: Worlds on the wire, and a narrow read of one attribute ([#1690](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1690))

Takes trust-tasks-rs 0.22, which has been unreachable since 0.21.21:
  affinidi-messaging-sdk required ^0.21.20 and `MediatorAcl` crosses that
  SDK's API, so a graph holding both versions failed to compile rather than
  merely carrying a duplicate. affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#885 moved the
  messaging crates; this takes the line they are now on. One
  `trust-tasks-rs`, one `affinidi-messaging-sdk`, one `affinidi-tdk`.

  **Worlds.** `persona/facet/*` is `persona/world/*`, `facetId` is
  `worldId`, and `correlation/analyze` takes a 1.1 for its three renamed
  members. `face` and `facet` shared a stem while naming different things —
  a projection of the pool, and an arrangement of those projections — and
  every UI had already resolved it by saying "world" on screen, which left
  the collision live for anyone reading both.

  The retired spellings stay routable for a release and answer in their own
  words: `facetId` for `worldId`, `facets` for `worlds`, `crossesFacets`
  for `crossesWorlds`. A document already issued against one still
  validates, and refusing it would break a caller for a rename that costs
  it nothing. The whole alias is marked for deletion in one commit.

  **`persona/attribute/get`.** Reading one value meant
  `persona/attribute/list` with a type prefix, filtered by the caller — so
  revealing one email address decrypted every email address the holder has,
  and the audit row recorded a listing of the pool rather than a decision
  about one fact. `PersonaStore::get_attribute` applies exactly what a
  listing applies: visibility, retention, credential re-derivation.
  `versionPurged` is distinct from `notFound` because the attribute is
  still there, and `retainedVersions` lets a holder see what purging would
  take away rather than deciding blind.

  Two latent defects, both found by the new tests:

  - `correlation/analyze/1.0` was already answering with 1.1's member
    names. Nothing noticed because 1.1 did not exist.
  - A world with no faces and no attributes serialised without `faceIds`
    and `attributeIds`, which its own response schema requires, so listing
    an empty one returned a 500. `skip_serializing_if` on a required
    member; no test had made an empty one.

  The `pf:` storage prefix is unchanged — it is an opaque key prefix, not
  the noun, and renaming it would orphan every world already stored.



### Fixed

- **vtc**: A Trust Task over DIDComm rides the binding envelope only (Keyring VTI-42) ([#1687](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1687))

The DIDComm binding (bindings/didcomm/0.2 §2-§5) makes the envelope
  https://trusttasks.org/binding/didcomm/0.1/envelope the only carriage for a
  Trust Task, and requires a consumer to refuse any other type at the DIDComm
  layer with no trust-task-error.

  The VTC router still carried twelve task-typed arms beside the envelope arm
  (join-requests submit/manifest 0.1+0.2/status, members/self-remove,
  members/vmc, six vtc/vetting URIs). Every other served verb answered
  'unsupported message type' when typed as itself. Two of the arms
  (self-remove, vmc) parsed bespoke bodies and bypassed
  dispatch_trust_task_core, so they skipped freshness, recipient and proof
  checks. All twelve are removed. Every one of these URIs is dispatched by the
  spine via the envelope.

  The VTC and VTA fallbacks now answer a https://trusttasks.org/spec/ type
  with a threaded problem-report that names the envelope type.

  Parity tests walk each dispatcher's own list (VTC DISPATCHED_URIS +
  ROOMS_DISPATCHED_URIS; VTA dispatched_uris()). An enveloped request is never
  answered 'unsupported message type'. A task-typed one gets the
  envelope-naming problem-report. The VTA's two remaining task-typed arms
  (acl/swap-key/0.1, provision/integration/0.3) are pinned in a shrink-only
  list.

title: fix(join): say when a pasted invitation cannot be presented, and present it when it can
body:
Fixes #373.

## What was wrong

When a join minted a persona, the flow cleared the loaded invitation (`join_flow.rs`, both the first-join path and `✦ Be someone new`) and the join went out as an open request. Meanwhile the entry page still said `✓ … it will be presented to the community`. The only sign of the drop came after the request had been sent.

## Why the invitation can't always just be presented

The VTC's holder-binding check (`vtc-service/src/credentials/invitation_verify.rs`) accepts an invitation only from its subject, or from a presenter the subject vouches for with a `subjectLinkage` proof. `build_subject_linkage` can sign that proof only when the subject is one of this account's personas. Two consequences:

- **First join:** there's no persona to sign with, so a new persona can't present the invitation. Presenting it anyway would get a refusal, not an admission.
- **An invitation naming a DID that isn't one of our personas:** no persona can present it.

## Fix

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Invitation names a DID that isn't one of our personas (incl. every first join) | Entry page: "✓ will be presented"; silently dropped | Entry page warns **before Enter**, names the DID, says the join will be an open request and how to get invited properly. The invitation is still vaulted, and the progress page says why it went unused |
| `✦ Be someone new`, invitation names one of our personas | Dropped | Presented with a subject-linkage proof, as the reuse path already did. The progress page notes that the community will see the two personas are linked |
| Reuse a persona, loaded invitation names a DID that isn't one of our personas | Offered on the invitation step; presenting it earned a refusal | Not offered. Falls to the open-request path with the reason |

`mint_can_present` also requires the invitation to be for this community and unexpired. Otherwise the sequence would fall back to any matching vault invitation, which a new persona was never meant to present.

**For review:** presenting through a linkage proof on `Be someone new` links the new persona to the invited one in the community's eyes. That's the point of the linkage proof, and the reuse path already does it for a hand-loaded invitation, so this PR keeps the two paths consistent and says so on screen. If `Be someone new` should instead mean "never linked", the alternative is to drop the invitation there with an entry-page warning.

## Tests

- `a_first_join_names_the_invitation_it_cannot_present`
- `a_new_persona_presents_an_invitation_one_of_ours_can_vouch_for` (including the wrong-community case)
- `an_invitation_for_a_stranger_is_foreign_to_every_persona`
- `an_invitation_for_someone_else_is_not_promised` (entry-page rendering)

`cargo test -p openvtc --bin openvtc`: 685 passed. `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `fmt --check` are clean.

## Pre-merge checklist

Rendering and client-side join decisions only. No new outbound client, wire shape or persisted state, so the networking and wire rules don't apply. A subject DID taken from a pasted credential is `sanitize_display`d before it's shown.

title: Join drops a pasted invitation (VIC) when the join mints a new persona
body:
## What happens

On the **Join a community** page, pasting an invitation credential (VIC) shows `✓ Invitation credential loaded — it will be presented to the community.` The page also says the invitation "rides along with the join request" (`openvtc/src/ui/pages/join_flow/vtc_enter_did.rs:256`).

If the join then mints a new persona, the loaded invitation is thrown away and the request goes out as an open request. The only sign is on the progress page, after the choice is made: `Joining without an invitation — submitting an open request (awaiting approval).` and `Invitation: None · open request (awaiting approval)` in the result.

This happens on two paths:

- **The account has no personas yet (a first join).** `continue_join` sets `state.invitation_credential = None` before `offer_contexts` (`openvtc/src/state_handler/join_flow.rs:1819`). The comment there reads "A new persona can't hold an existing invitation."
- **The account has personas, and the user picks `✦ Be someone new to this community`.** The `JoinIdentityChoose` mint branch does the same (`openvtc/src/state_handler/join_flow.rs:1012`).

The first path is the one a new user hits: they have been handed a VIC, they have no persona, and the entry page tells them to paste it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Complete `openvtc setup` on a fresh profile, so the account has no personas.
2. From **Communities**, press `j`.
3. Paste a valid VIC for the community. The page confirms it is loaded and fills in the community DID.
4. Press **Enter**, then accept `✦ A context of its own` on **Where should this community live?**
5. The progress page reports an open request, and the result shows `Invitation: None`.

## Expected

One of:

- The invitation is presented on the mint path too. `open_invitation_choice` already accepts a hand-loaded VIC whatever its subject, with `build_linkage_proof` covering a subject that isn't the presenting persona, so it isn't clear the mint path needs to be different.
- If a VIC really can't be presented by a freshly minted persona, the TUI says so before anything is sent. For example, the entry page or the context/identity step could warn that the loaded invitation will be dropped, and suggest creating a persona under **My Identity** first so the community can issue an invitation bound to it.

## Found at

`main` at 5453239. Found while checking the developer "Joining a Community" tutorial in `vti-setup` against the TUI. That tutorial now tells VIC holders to create their persona before joining, as a workaround.

title: vta-cli-common-v0.23.0
body:
### Added

- **persona**: Worlds on the wire, and a narrow read of one attribute ([#1690](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1690))

Takes trust-tasks-rs 0.22, which has been unreachable since 0.21.21:
  affinidi-messaging-sdk required ^0.21.20 and `MediatorAcl` crosses that
  SDK's API, so a graph holding both versions failed to compile rather than
  merely carrying a duplicate. affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#885 moved the
  messaging crates; this takes the line they are now on. One
  `trust-tasks-rs`, one `affinidi-messaging-sdk`, one `affinidi-tdk`.

  **Worlds.** `persona/facet/*` is `persona/world/*`, `facetId` is
  `worldId`, and `correlation/analyze` takes a 1.1 for its three renamed
  members. `face` and `facet` shared a stem while naming different things —
  a projection of the pool, and an arrangement of those projections — and
  every UI had already resolved it by saying "world" on screen, which left
  the collision live for anyone reading both.

  The retired spellings stay routable for a release and answer in their own
  words: `facetId` for `worldId`, `facets` for `worlds`, `crossesFacets`
  for `crossesWorlds`. A document already issued against one still
  validates, and refusing it would break a caller for a rename that costs
  it nothing. The whole alias is marked for deletion in one commit.

  **`persona/attribute/get`.** Reading one value meant
  `persona/attribute/list` with a type prefix, filtered by the caller — so
  revealing one email address decrypted every email address the holder has,
  and the audit row recorded a listing of the pool rather than a decision
  about one fact. `PersonaStore::get_attribute` applies exactly what a
  listing applies: visibility, retention, credential re-derivation.
  `versionPurged` is distinct from `notFound` because the attribute is
  still there, and `retainedVersions` lets a holder see what purging would
  take away rather than deciding blind.

  Two latent defects, both found by the new tests:

  - `correlation/analyze/1.0` was already answering with 1.1's member
    names. Nothing noticed because 1.1 did not exist.
  - A world with no faces and no attributes serialised without `faceIds`
    and `attributeIds`, which its own response schema requires, so listing
    an empty one returned a 500. `skip_serializing_if` on a required
    member; no test had made an empty one.

  The `pf:` storage prefix is unchanged — it is an opaque key prefix, not
  the noun, and renaming it would orphan every world already stored.

title: vti-common-v0.24.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: A console signing key is a credential of the operator's admin DID ([#1692](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1692))

Server side of #1684, against the design note merged in #1685
  (`vtc-console-signing.md`, Option A). The admin console cannot author a signed
  Trust Task document, which is what keeps every bearer route #1641 would retire
  mounted — 34 of the 49 are console-reachable, including all four #1681 kept.

  A console signing key is a credential of the operator's existing admin DID, the
  way a passkey is. Not an identity of its own and not an ACL row: giving a
  console key its own admin row is self-promotion by a longer path, and #1658's
  `Invariant::SelfPromotion` (VTI-OPS-050) refuses it. What the VTC stores is a
  delegation — "console key K may act as admin DID D" — which confers no role.
  Authority remains D's ACL row, read at execution time, so the property #1681
  established (`admin_signer` never consults `sessions_ks`) survives intact.

  - `console_keys` keyspace, `console_key:<consoleDid>` → the delegation, and
    EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP. That exclusion is a security decision rather than
    housekeeping: a restore into a rebuilt host, a staging clone or different
    hands must not hand a browser profile the ability to sign as an administrator
    again.
  - Enrolment behind `AdminAuth` plus `acl::elevation::verified`, which reads the
    session row — a stolen session alone cannot leave a signing key behind. The
    subject is the proven caller and the body cannot name it, so self-targeted is
    the only case this surface can express. That inverts `acl/grant`'s rule
    deliberately: a delegation confers nothing, so there is nothing to promote,
    and it is a credential of your own identity.
  - `admin_signer` gains one step. A signer with no ACL row of its own may be a
    delegated console key, in which case the delegating admin's row is resolved,
    at execution time, as before. A signer that has a row is answered by that row,
    including when it refuses — tighter than the note's sketch, so a stale
    delegation cannot route around a demotion.
  - List and revoke on the passkey management model. Revocation tombstones the row
    (a burned key cannot be re-enrolled), takes effect on the next document, and
    needs no second factor: an operator who suspects a browser should not have to
    find their authenticator before disowning it.
  - `AdminConsoleKeyEnrolled` / `AdminConsoleKeyRevoked` audit events.

  No published Trust Task covers this. `device/register/0.1` registers a device as
  a consumer in its own right, with a granted `Capability` set — the shape
  VTI-OPS-050 refuses here — and `auth/passkey/*` is WebAuthn end to end. So the
  three routes are mounted without a Trust-Task binding, the same exemption
  `relationships::{suspend,restore}` carries, and `routes/admin/console_keys.rs`
  records what the upstream `auth/signing-key/{enroll,list,revoke}` family should
  be. The bodies here are already those payloads.

  it nothing. The whole alias is marked for deletion in one commit.

  **`persona/attribute/get`.** Reading one value meant

title: fix(verify-trust): pin merge recomputation to no attributes
body:
Follow-ups from the review of #68, which is already merged.

## Pin the merge recomputation to no attributes (medium)

`git merge-tree` ran in the checked-out repository, so it applied `.gitattributes`. A `merge=union` attribute in the worktree turned a conflict into a "clean" merge that matched a resolution written by hand, so the merge counted as `exempt`.

The recomputation now reads attributes from the empty tree (`--attr-source`) and sets `core.attributesFile=/dev/null`.

- **New git floor.** `--attr-source` needs git **2.40**, up from 2.38. On an older git the run fails with an error that names the requirement; it never falls back to an unpinned check. GitHub-hosted runners ship a newer git. The runbook (§4, §4a), the verify-trust README and the action input description now state the requirement.
- **Side effect.** A repository whose real merges rely on committed merge attributes now gets `platformMergeAltered` for those merges. This fails closed.
- **Test.** A `merge=union` attribute in the worktree does not make a conflicting merge exempt. With the pinning removed, this test fails.

## Re-sign recipe (medium, docs)

`--exec` over the whole branch breaks on a PR with commits from more than one person. A commit another contributor already signed keeps their `Signed-by-DID:` trailer, and did-git-sign then refuses to sign it as you.

- **Runbook §5** now re-signs only the refused commits: `rebase -i`, with an `exec` line after each refused pick.
- **Foreign trailers.** A refused commit whose message already carries someone else's trailer needs that trailer removed first.
- **Bridge bot.** One line notes that a bridge bot to re-sign Dependabot PRs is planned.
- **Hint.** The `platformSignedEdit` message printed by `verify-trust` matches the new recipe.

## Smaller fixes

- **Non-UTF-8 messages.** Commit headers are now split on bytes before decoding, so a non-UTF-8 message no longer leaves a merge with zero parents. A unit test covers this.
- **Wording.** The rebase-and-merge note no longer says GitHub "drops" signatures; it says GitHub rewrites the commits, so their DID signatures are lost.

## New tests

- a merge of conflicting parents is refused (merge-tree exit 1)
- an octopus merge is refused
- a parent that is outside the range and not on its boundary is refused (shallow clone)
- a platform merge that skewed dates list before its parent merge still settles as `exempt` (covers the fixpoint)
- git version parsing

Locally: fmt, clippy (`-D warnings --all-targets`), workspace tests and the MSRV 1.95 check all pass.

This is not marked breaking because the public API is unchanged. The new git 2.40 floor for platform-merge checks is called out in the docs.

title: Implementation Guide: the explanatory chapters, extracted from the specification (WG-13)
body:
The companion **DTG ZKP Implementation Guide**: a navigation companion to the compressed specification. It explains where each construction record fits, how the records compose, and how to read their evidence. It defines nothing; the specification is authoritative. The explanatory chapters are extracted from the specification, as the chair's Round 1 position asked (spec PR #11, refine 2) and WG-13 records.

**Chapters**
- **Reading this guide:** three reading paths, how to read a record part by part, and an outcome-to-record index linked into the specification.
- **From a Trust-Graph Outcome to a Proof:** the six implementation steps.
- **Trust-Graph Operations:** the life cycle, ADR-001, and admission.
- **Construction walkthroughs:** every record family in plain terms (what it proves, how its clauses fit, where its limits lie), each entry linking to its record.
- **Reading the evidence:** formal models, circuit proofs, runtimes and policy enforcement kept apart; evidence states; formal blocks; proving routes as a map; reading a mapping to a paper.
- **Cryptographic Background**, and **Attribution and maintenance**.

Working-group notes, call narrative, dated research entries, the SIROS review pack and the verification worklist are **not** in the guide. The open decisions are tracked in the specification's appendix; the working material is kept in the evidence repository.

**Also in this PR:** `.github/workflows/guide.yml` renders and checks the guide on pull requests and uploads a preview artifact (it does not deploy Pages; publication is a maintainer decision), and `README.md` points to the guide.

**Merge order:** this first. [dtgwg-zkp-spec PR #12](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-zkp-spec/pull/12) replaces the moved chapters with pointers here.

Local check: 8 chapters, internal links resolved, render clean from a clean checkout; all 18 record links resolve against the rendered specification.

title: fix(tui): stop the vetting desk's text running together
body:
## Problem

On **Vetting → Vetting desk**, text ran together:

- The header padded the community name to a fixed 30 columns. A community known only by its DID is shortened to 48 characters, so the grant ran straight into it: `did:webvh:QmZM…VxW1:webvh.storm.ws:pcs-vtcuntil 2027-09-23`.
- The Requests view put the selected request's own keys and the desk's keys on one long line: `o: open session  x: decline  p: your vetter profile  g: …  Tab: Applications`.

## Fix

- The header's name column is now as wide as the longest name, with a three-space gap after it, so a grant never touches its name. With more than one community, the grants line up.
- Requests now puts its own keys on one line and the desk keys on the next, which is how Tickets and Issued already do it. When there are no requests, it shows the full desk key line instead of just `p`.

This changes rendering only: no state, protocol or network code.

## Tests

- `the_desk_header_keeps_a_long_name_apart_from_its_grant`: a 48-character DID next to a short name; checks for the gap and that the grants line up.
- `a_request_keeps_its_keys_apart_from_the_desks`: the request's keys appear on their own line.
- `cargo test -p openvtc --bin openvtc`: 681 passed. clippy (`--all-targets`) and rustfmt are clean.
